وليس للمرتهن ولا للراهن أخذه من يده
فإن قضاه الدين قيل له: سلم الرهن إليه
فليس للراهن عزله عنها
أن يطالب الراهن ويحبسه به
cards.why: The lender carries the loss, neither side may take it from the trusted person, the agent stays, and the lender may still demand his debt; once it is paid, the pledge goes back.

lessons.title: Selling, damaging and caring for the pledge

cards.title: The owner sells the pledge
cards.ar: وإذا باع الراهن الرهن بغير إذن المرتهن فالبيع موقوف فإن أجازه المرتهن جاز وإن قضاه الراهن دينه جاز البيع
cards.en: If the owner sells the pledge without the lender's permission, the sale is mawquf: on hold. It goes through if the lender approves it, or if the owner pays off his debt.

cards.ask: Zaid has pledged his bike to Omar. Without asking Omar, Zaid sells it to Bilal. Then Zaid pays Omar the whole debt. What about the sale?
options: It is void and must be made again
It was always valid from the start
cards.source: فالبيع موقوف فإن أجازه المرتهن جاز وإن قضاه الراهن دينه جاز البيع
cards.why: The sale was on hold. Paying the debt frees the pledge, so the sale goes through.

cards.title: Freeing a pledged slave
cards.ar: وإن اعتق الراهن عبد الرهن نفذ عتقه فإن كان الدين حالا طولب بأداء الدين وإن كان مؤجلا أخذ منه قيمة العبد فجعلت رهنا مكانه حتى يحل الدين وإن كان الراهن معسرا استسعي العبد في قيمته فقضى بها دينه
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time, if the owner freed a pledged slave, the freeing took effect. If the debt was due, he had to pay it. If it was due later, the slave's value was taken from him as the pledge instead. If he was too poor, the freed man worked to earn his value, and that paid the debt.

cards.title: When the pledge is destroyed
cards.ar: وكذلك إذا استهلك الراهن الرهن وإن استهلكه أجنبي فالمرتهن هو الخصم في تضمينه ويأخذ القيمة فتكون رهنا في يده
cards.en: If the owner destroys the pledge, it is the same: he must replace it. If a stranger destroys it, the lender is the one who takes him to court; he takes its value, and that value becomes the pledge in his hands.

cards.ask: Yusuf holds Ali's TV as a pledge. A neighbour drops it and smashes it. Who sues the neighbour, and what happens to the money?
options: Yusuf sues; the money becomes the pledge
Ali sues and keeps the money
Nobody: the debt is simply paid off
cards.source: وإن استهلكه أجنبي فالمرتهن هو الخصم في تضمينه ويأخذ القيمة فتكون رهنا في يده
cards.why: The lender is the one who claims from a stranger, and the value he takes stays as the pledge.

cards.title: Harm done to and by the pledge
cards.ar: وجناية الراهن على الرهن مضمونة وجناية المرتهن عليه تسقط من دينه بقدرها وجناية الرهن على الراهن وعلى المرتهن وعلى مالهما هدر
cards.en: Jinaya means harm or damage. If the owner damages the pledge, he must make it good. If the lender damages it, that much drops off his debt. If the pledge itself (an animal, say) harms the owner, the lender or their property, it is hadar: nothing is owed.

cards.ask: Hamza holds Karim's camel as a pledge for £1000. Hamza carelessly injures it, cutting £200 off its value. What happens?
options: Hamza owes nothing: it is his to hold
cards.source: وجناية المرتهن عليه تسقط من دينه بقدرها
cards.why: Damage by the lender is taken off his debt by its amount, so Karim now owes £800.

cards.title: Who pays to keep it
cards.ar: وأجرة البيت الذي يحفظ فيه الرهن على المرتهن وأجرة الراعي ونفقة الرهن على الراهن ونماؤه للراهن فيكون رهنا مع الأصل
cards.en: The rent of the place where the pledge is stored is on the lender. The shepherd's wage and the upkeep (feeding) of the pledge are on the owner. What the pledge produces, like milk or young, belongs to the owner, and it is pledged along with the original.

cards.ask: Who pays?
items: Rent of the room where it is stored
Rent of the barn it is kept in
cards.source: وأجرة البيت الذي يحفظ فيه الرهن على المرتهن وأجرة الراعي ونفقة الرهن على الراهن
cards.why: Keeping it safe (storage) is on the lender. Keeping it alive (shepherd, food) is on the owner.

cards.title: When the original or its young is lost
cards.ar: ويقسم الدين على قيمة الرهن يوم القبض وقيمة النماء يوم الفكاك فما أصاب الأصل سقط من الدين وما أصاب النماء افتكه الراهن به
cards.en: If the growth (say, a lamb) is lost, it is lost for nothing. If the original is lost and the growth remains, the debt is split by the original's value when handed over and the growth's value on redemption day. The original's share falls off the debt; the owner pays the growth's share to take it back.

cards.ask: Owing £90, Musa pledges a sheep worth £60 on the day he hands it over. It gives birth to a lamb, then the sheep dies. On redemption day the lamb is worth £30. What must Musa pay to take the lamb back?
source: وإن هلك الأصل وبقي النماء
ويقسم الدين على قيمة الرهن يوم القبض وقيمة النماء يوم الفكاك فما أصاب الأصل سقط من الدين وما أصاب النماء افتكه الراهن به
cards.why: The £90 debt splits 60 : 30. The sheep's £60 share falls off; the lamb's £30 share is what Musa pays to redeem it.

cards.ask: Which are true of dealing with a pledge?

options.text: A sale of the pledge without the lender's permission is on hold
If the pledge's young dies, it is lost for nothing
If the pledged animal kicks the lender, the owner must pay
The owner pays for the pledge's food
The milk of a pledged animal belongs to the lender

source: فالبيع موقوف
فإن هلك هلك بغير شيء
وجناية الرهن على الراهن وعلى المرتهن وعلى مالهما هدر
ونفقة الرهن على الراهن ونماؤه للراهن
cards.why: The sale waits, the young is lost for nothing, the owner feeds it and owns its growth. Harm done by the pledge itself is hadar.

lessons.title: Adding to it, keeping it, and death

cards.title: Adding to the pledge
cards.ar: وتجوز الزيادة في الرهن ولا تجوز في الدين عند أبي حنيفة ومحمد ولا يصير الرهن رهنا بهما
cards.en: More may be added to the pledge for the same debt. But more debt may not be added onto the same pledge, say Abu Hanifa and Muhammad: the pledge does not become security for both. Note: Abu Yusuf says adding to the debt is allowed too.

cards.title: One pledge, two lenders
cards.ar: وإذا رهن عينا واحدة عند رجلين بدين لكل واحد منهما جاز وجميعها رهن عند كل واحد منهما والمضمون على كل واحد منهما حصة دينه منهما فإن قضى أحدهما دينه كانت كلها رهنا في يد الآخر حتى يستوفي دينه
cards.en: One thing may be pledged to two people who are each owed a debt. All of it is pledged to each of them, but each carries the risk only for his own share. If one is paid off, the whole thing stays pledged with the other until he is paid too.

cards.ask: Ibrahim owes Ali £500 and Hasan £500, and pledges one car to both. He pays Ali in full. What happens to the car?
options: All of it stays pledged with Hasan until he is paid
Half is returned to Ibrahim, and half stays with Hasan
Ali keeps half until Hasan is paid
cards.source: فإن قضى أحدهما دينه كانت كلها رهنا في يد الآخر حتى يستوفي دينه
cards.why: The whole car was pledged to each lender, so it all stays with Hasan until his debt is paid.

cards.title: A sale on condition of a pledge
cards.ar: لم يجبر عليه وكان البائع بالخيار: إن شاء رضي بترك الرهن وإن شاء فسخ البيع إلا أن يدفع المشتري الثمن حالا أو يدفع قيمة الرهن رهنا مكانه
cards.en: If someone sells on condition that the buyer pledges a particular thing for the price, and the buyer refuses to hand it over, he cannot be forced. The seller may then accept going without the pledge, or cancel the sale, unless the buyer pays the price at once or gives the pledge's value as a pledge instead.

cards.ask: Tariq sells his car to Yahya on credit, on condition that Yahya pledges his gold watch. Yahya then refuses to hand over the watch. What may Tariq do?
options: Accept without the pledge, or cancel the sale
Force Yahya to hand over the watch
Take any other item from Yahya
source: ومن باع عبدا على أن يرهنه المشتري بالثمن شيئا بعينه فإن امتنع المشتري من تسليم
لم يجبر عليه وكان البائع بالخيار: إن شاء رضي بترك الرهن وإن شاء فسخ البيع
cards.why: The buyer is not forced, so the seller chooses: go without the pledge or cancel. Unless Yahya pays now or gives the watch's value as a pledge.

cards.title: Who may keep it for the lender
cards.ar: وللمرتهن أن يحفظ الرهن بنفسه وزوجته وولده وخادمه الذي في عياله وإن حفظه بغير من في عياله
cards.en: The lender may look after the pledge himself, or by his wife, his child, or his servant who live in his household. If he has it kept by someone outside his household, or deposits it with someone, he is liable for it.

cards.ask: Who may the lender have look after the pledge without becoming liable?

options.text: Himself
His wife
His son who lives with him
A friend in another town
A neighbour, as a deposit

cards.source: وللمرتهن أن يحفظ الرهن بنفسه وزوجته وولده وخادمه الذي في عياله
cards.why: He and the people of his household may keep it. Anyone outside it makes him liable.

cards.title: Misuse, and lending it back to the owner
cards.ar: بجميع قيمته وإذا أعار المرتهن الرهن للراهن فقبضه خرج من ضمان المرتهن فإن هلك في يد الراهن هلك بغير شيء وللمرتهن أن يسترجعه إلى يده فإذا أخذه عاد الضمان
cards.en: If the lender misuses the pledge, he must pay its whole value, like someone who took it by force. If he lends it back to the owner, it leaves his risk: if it is lost with the owner, it is lost for nothing and the debt stays. The lender may take it back, and then the risk returns to him.

cards.ask: Owing £400, Adam pledged his laptop to Khalid. Khalid lends it back to Adam for a week, and it breaks while Adam has it. What does Adam owe now?
cards.source: فإن هلك في يد الراهن هلك بغير شيء
cards.why: While lent back, the pledge is out of the lender's risk, so its loss changes nothing: the debt stays £400.

cards.title: When the owner dies
cards.ar: وإذا مات الراهن باع وصيه الرهن وقضى الدين فإن لم يكن له وصي نصب القاضي له وصيا وأمره ببيعه
cards.en: If the owner dies, his wasi (the person he named to handle his affairs after death) sells the pledge and pays the debt. If he has no wasi, the judge appoints one and orders him to sell it.

cards.ask: Salim dies leaving a pledged necklace and no one named to handle his affairs. How is the debt paid?
options: The judge appoints someone and orders him to sell it
The lender simply keeps the necklace in place of the debt
The heirs must pay before anything is sold
cards.source: فإن لم يكن له وصي نصب القاضي له وصيا وأمره ببيعه
cards.why: With no wasi, the judge appoints one to sell the pledge and pay the debt.

cards.ask: The pledge is lost. Does the loss fall on the lender, or is it lost for nothing?
items: He misused it and it was ruined
He had lent it back to the owner, and it was lost there
He gave it to a friend outside his home to keep
His wife was keeping it, and it was lost without fault
source: وإذا تعدى المرتهن في الرهن ضمنه
فإن هلك في يد الراهن هلك بغير شيء
وإن حفظه بغير من في عياله
دخل في ضمانه
فإن هلك هلك بغير شيء
cards.why: Misuse, a keeper outside the household, and ordinary loss in his household all fall on the lender. Lent back to the owner, or the pledge's young, it is lost for nothing.

lessons.title: The child, the slave and the insane

cards.title: Three causes
cards.ar: الأسباب الموجبة للحجر ثلاثة: الصغر والرق والجنون
cards.en: Hajr means restriction: a person is stopped from dealing freely with money and contracts. Al-Quduri gives three causes: being a child, being a slave (in his time), and insanity.

cards.ask: How many causes of restriction (hajr) does al-Quduri give?
cards.source: الأسباب الموجبة للحجر ثلاثة
cards.why: The causes are three: childhood, slavery and insanity.

cards.ask: Which of these are al-Quduri's causes of restriction?

options.text: Being a child
Old age
Being a slave
Illness
Insanity

cards.source: الأسباب الموجبة للحجر ثلاثة: الصغر والرق والجنون
cards.why: The three are childhood, slavery and insanity. Old age and illness are not on his list.

cards.title: With permission, or not at all
cards.ar: ولا يجوز تصرف الصغير إلا بإذن وليه ولا تصرف العبد إلا بإذن سيده ولا يجوز تصرف المجنون المغلوب على عقله بحال
cards.en: A child's dealings count only with the permission of his wali (guardian). A slave's dealings counted only with his master's permission. Someone insane, whose mind is overcome, cannot deal at all.

cards.ask: Hamid is insane, his mind overcome. His guardian gives him permission to sell his car, and he sells it. Does the sale count?
options: No: the insane cannot deal at all
Yes, if the price was fair to him
cards.source: ولا يجوز تصرف المجنون المغلوب على عقله بحال
cards.why: A child or a slave may deal with permission, but someone whose mind is overcome cannot deal in any way.

cards.title: The guardian decides
cards.ar: ومن باع من هؤلاء شيئا أو اشتراه وهو يعقل البيع ويقصده فالوالي بالخيار: إن شاء أجازه إذا كان فيه مصلحة وإن شاء فسخه
cards.en: If one of them buys or sells something while understanding what a sale is and meaning to do it, the guardian may choose: approve it if it is good for him, or cancel it.

cards.ask: Musa, aged 10, understands buying and selling. Without asking his father, who is his guardian, he sells his bike for £80. What happens?
options: His father may approve it or cancel it
The sale is binding, because he understood it
The sale is void and cannot be approved
cards.source: وهو يعقل البيع ويقصده فالوالي بالخيار: إن شاء أجازه إذا كان فيه مصلحة وإن شاء فسخه
cards.why: A child who understands the sale has made a deal that waits on his guardian, who approves it if it helps him or cancels it.

cards.title: Words, not deeds
cards.ar: وهذه المعاني الثلاثة توجب الحجر في الأقوال دون الأفعال فالصبي والمجنون لا تصح عقودهما ولا إقرارهما ولا يقع طلاقهما ولا عتاقهما
cards.en: These three causes restrict what a person says (contracts, admissions, divorce), not what he does. So a child or an insane person cannot make contracts or admissions, and their divorce or freeing of a slave does not happen. But if they destroy something, they must pay for it.

cards.ask: Eight-year-old Adam kicks a ball through a shop window. Must the damage be paid for from his money?
options: Yes: restriction covers words, not deeds
No: a child is restricted, so nothing is owed
source: توجب الحجر في الأقوال دون الأفعال
وإن أتلفا شيئا
cards.why: Breaking things is a deed, and restriction does not cover deeds, so he owes for the window.

cards.ask: Does it take effect for a child?
items: He sells his phone with no guardian's permission
He admits he owes someone money
He says he divorces a wife
source: فالصبي والمجنون لا تصح عقودهما ولا إقرارهما ولا يقع طلاقهما
وإن أتلفا شيئا
cards.why: His words (contracts, admissions, divorce) have no effect alone. What he destroys must be paid for.

cards.title: The slave's words
cards.ar: وأما العبد فأقواله نافذة في حق نفسه غير نافذة في حق مولاه فإن أقر بمال لزمه بعد الحرية ولم يلزمه في الحال وإن أقر بحد أو قصاص لزمه في الحال وينفذ طلاقه
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time, a slave's words counted against himself but not against his master. If he admitted owing money, it bound him only after he was freed. If he admitted something carrying a hadd (a fixed punishment) or qisas (equal retaliation), it bound him at once. His divorce took effect.

cards.ask: In al-Quduri's time, a slave admits he owes a man 100 dirhams. When must he pay?
options: At once, from his master's wealth
Never: his words count for nothing
cards.source: فإن أقر بمال لزمه بعد الحرية ولم يلزمه في الحال
cards.why: An admission of money touches his master's rights, so it waits until he is free.

cards.ask: Which are true of restriction?

options.text: Childhood, slavery and insanity are the three causes of restriction
An insane person may deal with his guardian's permission
A slave's divorce takes effect
A child who destroys something owes nothing
A guardian may approve a child's sale if it is good for him

source: الصغر والرق والجنون
ولا يجوز تصرف المجنون المغلوب على عقله بحال
وينفذ طلاقه
إن شاء أجازه إذا كان فيه مصلحة
cards.why: The insane cannot deal at all, and restriction does not cover a child's deeds. The other three are al-Quduri's words.

cards.title: No restriction on the adult spendthrift
cards.ar: على السفيه إذا كان بالغا عاقلا حرا وتصرفه في ماله جائز وإن كان مبذرا مفسدا يتلف ماله فيما لا غرض له فيه ولا مصلحة
cards.en: A safih is a spendthrift: someone who wastes his money. Abu Hanifa said: a spendthrift who is adult, sane and free is not restricted. His dealings with his money are valid, even if he squanders it on things with no purpose or benefit.

cards.ask: Tariq is 30, sane and free, and wastes his money on things of no use. His family asks the judge to restrict him. According to Abu Hanifa?
options: He is not restricted: his dealings stand
He is restricted until he is sensible
He is restricted until he turns 40
cards.source: على السفيه إذا كان بالغا عاقلا حرا وتصرفه في ماله جائز
cards.why: Abu Hanifa does not restrict an adult, sane, free spendthrift.

cards.title: Until twenty-five
cards.ar: إلا أنه قال: إذا بلغ الغلام غير رشيد لم يسلم إليه ماله حتى يبلغ خمسا وعشرين سنة
cards.en: Rashid means sensible with money. Abu Hanifa said: if a boy comes of age not sensible, his wealth is not handed to him until he reaches twenty-five.

cards.title: Before and at twenty-five
cards.ar: فإن تصرف فيه قبل ذلك نفذ تصرفه فإذا بلغ خمسا وعشرين سنة سلم إليه
cards.en: If he deals with that wealth before then, his dealing still goes through. When he reaches twenty-five, it is handed to him, even if he still has not shown good sense.

cards.ask: Complete Abu Hanifa's rule.
cards.ar: لم يسلم إليه ماله حتى يبلغ ____ سنة
cards.source: لم يسلم إليه ماله حتى يبلغ خمسا وعشرين سنة
cards.why: خمسا وعشرين: twenty-five. Eighteen and fifteen are ages of coming of age, not of handing over wealth.

cards.ask: Yahya came of age not sensible with money. He is now 22, and his wealth has not been handed to him, but he sells a field from it. According to Abu Hanifa, is the sale valid?
options: Only if the judge approves it
cards.source: فإن تصرف فيه قبل ذلك نفذ تصرفه
cards.why: The wealth is held back until 25, but if he deals in it before then, his dealing goes through.

cards.ask: According to Abu Hanifa, Hamid came of age not sensible with money. He is now 26 and still careless. What happens to his wealth?
options: It is kept from him until he is sensible
The judge spends it for him
cards.source: فإذا بلغ خمسا وعشرين سنة سلم إليه
cards.why: At twenty-five the wealth is handed over, even if good sense has not been seen in him.

cards.title: The view of Abu Yusuf and Muhammad
cards.ar: ويمنع من التصرف في ماله فإن باع لم ينفذ بيعه فإن كان فيه مصلحة أجازه الحاكم وإن أعتق عبدا نفذ عتقه وكان على العبد أن يسعى في قيمته وإن تزوج امرأة جاز نكاحه فإن سمى لها مهرا جاز منه مقدار مهر مثلها وبطل الفضل
cards.en: Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say the spendthrift IS restricted. His sale holds only if the judge approves it. If he frees a slave, it takes effect, but the slave works off his value. If he marries, only the usual mahr (bride gift) for a woman like her counts. And his wealth is kept until good sense is seen.

cards.title: Zakat, family, Hajj and bequests
cards.ar: فإن أراد حجة الإسلام لم يمنع منها ولا يسلم القاضي النفقة إليه ويسلمها إلى ثقة من الحاج ينفقها عليه في طريق الحج فإن مرض وأوصى بوصايا في القرب وأبواب الخير جاز ذلك في ثلث ماله
cards.en: Zakat is still paid from the restricted spendthrift's wealth, and his wife, children and dependent relatives are supported from it. He is not stopped from his obligatory Hajj, but the judge gives the money to a trustworthy pilgrim to spend on him. Bequests for good causes in his illness are valid within a third of his wealth.

cards.ask: A spendthrift is under restriction. Which of these still happen?

options.text: Zakat is paid from his wealth
His wife and children are supported from it
He goes on his obligatory Hajj
The judge hands him the Hajj money himself
His bequests for good causes go beyond a third

source: وتخرج الزكاة من مال السفيه
وينفق منه على أولاده وزوجته
فإن أراد حجة الإسلام لم يمنع منها ولا يسلم القاضي النفقة إليه
جاز ذلك في ثلث ماله
cards.why: Zakat and his family's support still come from his wealth, and he goes on Hajj, but a trustworthy pilgrim spends the money on him. Bequests are valid within a third.

cards.title: A boy comes of age
cards.ar: وبلوغ الغلام الاحتلام والإحبال والإنزال إذا وطئ فإن لم يوجد ذلك فحتى يتم له ثماني عشرة سنة عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: Bulugh is coming of age (puberty). A boy comes of age by a wet dream, or by being able to father a child. If none of these signs appears, then when he completes eighteen years, according to Abu Hanifa.

cards.title: A girl comes of age
cards.ar: وبلوغ الجارية بالحيض والاحتلام والحبل فإن لم يوجد ذلك فحتى يتم لها سبع عشرة سنة
cards.en: A girl comes of age by her period, a wet dream, or pregnancy. If none of these appears, then when she completes seventeen years. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say a boy and a girl are both of age at fifteen.

cards.ask: A sign for a boy or for a girl?
items: Being able to father a child
source: وبلوغ الغلام الاحتلام والإحبال والإنزال
فحتى يتم له ثماني عشرة سنة
وبلوغ الجارية بالحيض والاحتلام والحبل فإن لم يوجد ذلك فحتى يتم لها سبع عشرة سنة
cards.why: Period and pregnancy are a girl's signs, fathering a child a boy's. With no sign: 18 for a boy, 17 for a girl.

cards.ask: Zayd has shown none of the signs of coming of age. At what age is he counted an adult, according to Abu Hanifa?
cards.source: فإن لم يوجد ذلك فحتى يتم له ثماني عشرة سنة عند أبي حنيفة
cards.why: With no sign, a boy comes of age when he completes eighteen years.

cards.ask: Maryam has shown none of the signs. When is she counted an adult?
cards.source: فإن لم يوجد ذلك فحتى يتم لها سبع عشرة سنة
cards.why: For a girl with no sign, it is seventeen.

cards.title: Taking their word
cards.ar: الغلام والجارية وأشكل أمرهما في البلوغ وقالا: قد بلغنا فالقول قولهما وأحكامهما أحكام البالغين
cards.en: When a boy or girl is near the age and it is unclear whether they have come of age, and they say "We have come of age", their word is accepted, and they are treated as adults.

cards.ask: Thirteen-year-old Idris is near the age of puberty and says, "I have come of age." Nothing shows otherwise. What is the ruling?
options: He must wait until he turns 18
cards.source: وقالا: قد بلغنا فالقول قولهما وأحكامهما أحكام البالغين
cards.why: Near the age and unclear, their own word is accepted.

cards.ask: Which are true of coming of age?

options.text: A wet dream is a sign for both boys and girls
A girl with no sign comes of age at 17
A boy with no sign comes of age at 15, according to Abu Hanifa
A child near the age who says he has come of age is believed
Pregnancy is not a sign of coming of age

source: وبلوغ الغلام الاحتلام
والاحتلام والحبل
فحتى يتم لها سبع عشرة سنة
فحتى يتم له ثماني عشرة سنة عند أبي حنيفة
فالقول قولهما
cards.why: The wet dream is in both lists, 17 is for girls, and their word is accepted. Abu Hanifa's age for a boy is 18, and pregnancy is a sign.

lessons.title: The debtor who will not pay

cards.title: No restriction for debt
cards.ar: وقال أبو حنيفة: لا أحجر في الدين: وإذا وجبت الديون على رجل وطلب غرماؤه حبسه والحجر عليه لم أحجر عليه
cards.en: Abu Hanifa said: I do not restrict for debt. If a man has debts, and his creditors (the people he owes) ask for him to be imprisoned and restricted, I do not restrict him.

cards.title: Prison until he sells
cards.ar: لم يتصرف فيه الحاكم ولكن يحبسه أبدا حتى يبيعه في دينه
cards.en: If he has property, the judge does not deal with it himself. Instead he keeps him imprisoned until he sells it himself for his debt.

cards.ask: Rashid owes £20,000 and owns a plot of land, but refuses to sell it. According to Abu Hanifa, what does the judge do?
options: Imprisons him until he sells it himself
Restricts him and shares the land among the creditors
cards.source: لم يتصرف فيه الحاكم ولكن يحبسه أبدا حتى يبيعه في دينه
cards.why: The judge does not sell his property for him; he keeps him in prison until he sells it.

cards.title: When he has the same money
cards.ar: ودينه دراهم قضاها القاضي بغير أمره وإن كان دينه دراهم وله دنانير باعها القاضي في دينه
cards.en: But if he has dirhams (silver coins) and owes dirhams, the judge pays the debt from them without his order. If he owes dirhams and has dinars (gold coins), the judge sells the dinars for his debt.

cards.ask: Umar owes 500 dirhams and has 800 dirhams at home, but refuses to pay. What does the judge do, according to Abu Hanifa?
options: Pays the 500 from his dirhams without his order
cards.source: ودينه دراهم قضاها القاضي بغير أمره
cards.why: Dirhams owed and dirhams held: the judge simply pays the debt from them.

cards.title: The view of Abu Yusuf and Muhammad
cards.ar: القاضي عليه ومنعه من البيع والتصرف والإقرار حتى لا يضر بالغرماء وباع ماله إن امتنع من بيعه وقسمه بين غرمائه الحصص فإن أقر في حال الحجر بإقرار لزمه ذلك بعد قضاء الديون
cards.en: Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say that if the creditors of a muflis (bankrupt) ask, the judge restricts him from selling, dealing and making admissions, sells his property if he refuses, and shares it among the creditors. An admission made while restricted binds him only after the debts are paid.

cards.title: His family is still provided for
cards.ar: وينفق على المفلس من ماله وعلى زوجته وأولاده الصغار وذوي أرحامه
cards.en: From the bankrupt's own wealth, he is still provided for, and so are his wife, his young children and the relatives he must support.

cards.ask: Ziyad is bankrupt and owes many creditors. Are he, his wife and his young children still provided for from his wealth?
options: Yes: they are provided for from it
No: every coin goes to the creditors
Only once all the debts are paid
cards.source: وينفق على المفلس من ماله وعلى زوجته وأولاده الصغار وذوي أرحامه
cards.why: The bankrupt, his wife, his young children and the relatives he must support are still provided for from his wealth.

cards.title: Which debts mean prison
cards.ar: وإن لم يعرف للمفلس مال وطلب غرماؤه حبسه وهو يقول لا مال لي حبسه الحاكم في كل دين التزمه بدلا عن مال حصل يده كثمن مبيع وبدل القرض وفي كل دين بعقد كالمهر والكفالة ولم يحبسه فيما سوى ذلك
cards.en: If he has no known wealth and says "I have nothing", the judge still imprisons him for a debt taken on in exchange for wealth he received (a price, a loan), or by a contract (a mahr, or kafala: standing surety). For other debts, like injury compensation, he is not imprisoned unless there is proof he has wealth.

cards.ask: He says "I have nothing" and there is no proof he has wealth. May the judge imprison him for this debt?
items: The price of a car he bought
A debt he guaranteed for a friend
Compensation for an injury he caused
source: حبسه الحاكم في كل دين التزمه بدلا عن مال حصل يده كثمن مبيع وبدل القرض وفي كل دين بعقد كالمهر والكفالة ولم يحبسه فيما سوى ذلك
إلا أن تقوم البينة أن له مالا
cards.why: Debts for wealth he received (price, loan) or by contract (mahr, surety) mean prison. Others, like injury compensation, do not without proof of wealth.

cards.ask: Nabil owes 1000 dirhams and has 100 dinars. He will not pay. According to Abu Hanifa, what does the judge do?
options: Sells the dinars for the debt
Waits until Nabil sells them himself
source: وإن كان دينه دراهم وله دنانير باعها القاضي في دينه
وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد: إذا طلب غرماء المفلس
cards.why: Owing dirhams and holding dinars, the judge sells the dinars to pay. Restricting him is the view of Abu Yusuf and Muhammad, not of Abu Hanifa.

lessons.title: Release, the sinner, and goods left with a bankrupt
lessons.arabic: ومن أفلس وعنده متاع لرجل بعينه

cards.title: Two or three months
cards.ar: وإذا حبسه القاضي شهرين أو ثلاثة يسأل عن حاله: فإن لم ينكشف له مال خلى سبيله وكذلك إذا أقام البينة أنه لا مال له
cards.en: When the judge has imprisoned him for two or three months, he asks about his situation. If no wealth comes to light, he lets him go. The same if he brings proof that he has nothing.

cards.ask: Sami has been in prison for his debts for three months. The judge asks around and finds no wealth. What happens?
options: He stays until the debt is paid
cards.source: فإن لم ينكشف له مال خلى سبيله
cards.why: After two or three months, if no wealth appears, the judge releases him.

cards.title: After release
cards.ar: ولا يحول بينه وبين غرمائه بعد خروجه من الحبس ويلازمونه
cards.en: After his release, the judge does not stand between him and his creditors: they may follow him around. But they cannot stop him from dealing or travelling. They take what he earns beyond his needs and share it by their shares.

cards.ask: After release, Saeed earns £300 more than he needs. He owes Ali £2000 and Omar £1000. How is the £300 shared?
options: All £300 to Ali, the bigger creditor
cards.source: من التصرف والسفر ويأخذون فضل كسبه فيقسم بينهم بالحصص
cards.why: The extra earnings are shared by their shares of the debt, 2 : 1, so £200 and £100.

cards.title: The view of the two companions
cards.ar: وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد: إذا فلسه الحاكم حال بينه وبين غرمائه
cards.en: Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say that once the judge declares him bankrupt, he keeps the creditors from following him, unless they bring proof he has gained wealth.

cards.title: The sinner who manages well
cards.ar: ولا يحجر على الفاسق إذا كان مصلحا لماله والفسق الأصلي والطاريء سواء
cards.en: A fasiq is someone who openly commits sins. He is not restricted if he looks after his money well. It makes no difference whether he was always like that or became so later.

cards.ask: Karim neglects his prayers, but he runs his shop carefully and saves well. Is he restricted?
options: No: he manages his money well
Only if he became a sinner after coming of age
cards.source: ولا يحجر على الفاسق إذا كان مصلحا لماله
cards.why: Sin alone is not a cause of restriction when he manages his wealth well, whenever the sin began.

cards.title: Your goods with a bankrupt
cards.ar: ومن أفلس وعنده متاع لرجل بعينه ابتاعه منه فصاحب المتاع أسوة الغرماء فيه
cards.en: If someone goes bankrupt while he still has the very goods he bought from a seller (and has not paid), the seller has no special claim: he is equal with the other creditors in it.

cards.ask: Hassan sold a carpet to Bilal on credit. Bilal goes bankrupt with the carpet still at home and owes others too. What can Hassan do?
options: Share with the other creditors, equal to them
Be paid first, before the others
cards.source: فصاحب المتاع أسوة الغرماء فيه
cards.why: The seller is equal with the other creditors; he has no right to take the carpet back.

cards.ask: Which are true of a restricted debtor?

options.text: A debtor imprisoned two or three months with no wealth found is released
After release, the creditors may stop him travelling
Creditors share his spare earnings by their shares
A sinner who manages his money well is restricted
A seller is equal with other creditors in goods left with a bankrupt

source: شهرين أو ثلاثة يسأل عن حاله: فإن لم ينكشف له مال خلى سبيله
من التصرف والسفر ويأخذون فضل كسبه فيقسم بينهم بالحصص
ولا يحجر على الفاسق إذا كان مصلحا لماله
فصاحب المتاع أسوة الغرماء فيه
cards.why: He is released, the creditors follow him and share his spare earnings but cannot stop his travel, the careful sinner is not restricted, and the seller is one creditor among many.

lessons.title: Admitting a debt, even a vague one
lessons.arabic: إذا أقر الحر البالغ العاقل بحق لزمه

cards.title: An admission binds
cards.ar: إذا أقر الحر البالغ العاقل بحق لزمه إقراره مجهولا كان ما أقر به أو معلوما ويقال له: بين المجهول
cards.en: Iqrar is an admission: saying that you owe someone something. When a free, adult, sane person admits a right, his admission binds him, whether the thing is vague or clear. If it is vague, he is told: explain it.

cards.title: "I owe him something"
cards.ar: فإن قال لفلان على شيء لزمه أن بين ماله قيمة والقول فيه قوله مع يمينه إن ادعى المقر له أكثر من ذلك
cards.en: If he says "I owe so-and-so something", he must name a thing that has value. His word is accepted, with his oath (yamin: swearing by Allah), if the other person claims more.

cards.ask: Ali says, "I owe Omar something." Asked to explain, he says it is 5 dirhams. Omar claims it is 100. Whose word is taken?
options: Neither: the admission is void because it was vague
cards.source: والقول فيه قوله مع يمينه إن ادعى المقر له أكثر من ذلك
cards.why: A vague admission still binds. The one who admitted explains it, and swears if the other claims more.

cards.title: Wealth, great wealth, dirhams
cards.ar: فالمرجع في بيانه إليه ويقبل قوله في القليل والكثير فإن قال: له علي مال عظيم لم يصدق في أقل من مائتي درهم وإن قال: دراهم كثيرة لم يصدق في أقل من عشرة دراهم وإن قال: دراهم فهي ثلاثة إلا أن يبين أكثر منها
cards.en: If he says "I owe him wealth", it is for him to explain, and a little or a lot is accepted. "Great wealth" cannot be less than 200 dirhams. "Many dirhams" cannot be less than 10. Just "dirhams" means 3, unless he says more.

cards.ask: Hamza admits, "I owe Zaid many dirhams." What is the least he can be held to?
cards.source: وإن قال: دراهم كثيرة لم يصدق في أقل من عشرة دراهم
cards.why: "Many dirhams" cannot be less than ten.

cards.ask: Complete the rule for "great wealth".
cards.ar: فإن قال: له علي مال عظيم لم يصدق في أقل من ____ درهم
cards.source: فإن قال: له علي مال عظيم لم يصدق في أقل من مائتي درهم
cards.why: مائتي: two hundred dirhams for "great wealth". Ten is for "many dirhams", three for "dirhams".

cards.title: "So-and-so many dirhams"
cards.ar: وإن قال: له علي كذا كذا درهما لم يصدق في أقل من أحد عشر درهما
cards.en: If he says "I owe him kadha kadha dirhams" ("so-many so-many", two numbers run together, like eleven), it cannot be less than eleven. The next sentence in this copy gives twenty-one, for the form joined by "and" (kadha wa kadha), like twenty-one.

cards.ask: Sufyan says, "I owe him kadha kadha dirhams." What is the least he can be held to?
cards.source: وإن قال: له علي كذا كذا درهما لم يصدق في أقل من أحد عشر درهما
cards.why: Two numbers run together without "and" are read as eleven at the least.

cards.title: "On me" or "with me"
cards.ar: فقد أقر بدين وإن قال: عندي أو: معي فهو إقرار بأمانة في يده
cards.en: "He has on me" ("alayya") is an admission of a debt. "I have it" or "It is with me" is an admission of an amana: something of his kept in trust in my hands.

cards.title: Replies that admit
cards.ar: وإن قال له رجل لي عليك ألف فقال اتزنها أو انتقدها أو أجلني بها أو قد قضيتكها فهو إقرار
cards.en: If a man says "You owe me a thousand" and he replies "Weigh it", "Check the coins", "Give me time for it" or "I have already paid it", that is an admission.

cards.ask: Someone says, "You owe me 1000." Which replies are an admission?

options.text: "Weigh it out"
"Give me more time to pay it"
"I have already paid you"
"I owe you nothing"
"Prove it"

cards.source: فقال اتزنها أو انتقدها أو أجلني بها أو قد قضيتكها فهو إقرار
cards.why: Weighing it, asking for time, or saying it was paid all accept that the debt existed.

cards.ask: Yusuf admits, "I owe Bilal £500, due next year." Bilal agrees about the debt but says it is due now. What is the ruling?
options: The debt is due now, and Bilal swears about the date
It is due next year, as Yusuf said, and Yusuf swears to it
The admission is void because they disagree
source: ومن أقر بدين مؤجل فصدقه المقر له في الدين وكذبه في التأجيل لزمه الدين
ويستحلف المقر له في الأجل
cards.why: Yusuf admitted the debt, and the delay is a separate claim. So the debt is due now, and Bilal takes an oath about the delay.

cards.ask: Rami says, "Sami has 100 with me (‘indi)." What has he admitted?
options: That he holds 100 of Sami's in trust
A debt of 100 owed to Sami
Nothing, because he gave no reason
cards.source: وإن قال: عندي أو: معي فهو إقرار بأمانة في يده
cards.why: "With me" admits a trust held in his hands, not a debt.

cards.title: An exception said straight away
cards.ar: ومن أقر واستثنى متصلا بإقراره صح الاستثناء ولزمه الباقي سواء استثنى الأقل أو الأكثر فإن استثنى الجميع لزمه الإقرار وبطل الاستثناء
cards.en: If he admits something and adds an exception straight away, in the same breath ("except..."), the exception is valid and he owes the rest, whether he takes out less or more than half. If he takes out all of it, the whole admission binds him and the exception is void.

cards.ask: Faris says, "I owe Ziyad 100 dirhams except 30." What does he owe?
cards.source: صح الاستثناء ولزمه الباقي
cards.why: The exception was joined to the admission, so he owes what is left: 70.

cards.ask: Faris says, "I owe Ziyad 100 dirhams except 100." What does he owe?
cards.source: فإن استثنى الجميع لزمه الإقرار وبطل الاستثناء
cards.why: Taking out everything cancels the exception, not the admission. He owes all 100.

cards.title: Except a dinar
cards.ar: وإن قال: له علي مائة درهم إلا دينار أو: إلا قفيز حنطة لزمه مائة درهم إلا قيمة الدينار أو القفيز
cards.en: If he says "100 dirhams except a dinar" or "except a qafiz of wheat" (a measure of grain), he owes 100 dirhams minus the value of the dinar or of the wheat.

cards.title: "A hundred and a dirham"
cards.ar: وإن قال: له علي مائة ودرهم فالمائة كلها دراهم
cards.en: "I owe him a hundred and a dirham": the hundred are all dirhams. But "a hundred and a garment" means one garment, and it is for him to explain what the hundred are.

cards.ask: Qasim says, "I owe him a hundred and a garment." What does he owe?
options: One garment, and he explains what the hundred are
100 dirhams and a garment, as with "a hundred and a dirham"
cards.source: مائة وثوب لزمه ثوب واحد والمرجع في تفسير المائة إليه
cards.why: The garment is one garment. Unlike with a dirham, the hundred is not taken to be garments: he explains it.

cards.title: In sha' Allah, and an option
cards.ar: ومن أقر بحق وقال إن شاء الله متصلا بإقراره لم يلزمه الإقرار ومن أقر وشرط الخيار لزمه الإقرار وبطل الخيار
cards.en: If he admits something and says "in sha' Allah" (if Allah wills) straight after it, the admission does not bind him. If he admits something but adds an option to take it back (khiyar), the admission binds him and the option is void.

cards.ask: Does the admission bind him?
items: "I owe him 50, in sha' Allah", said straight away
"I owe him 50, and I have three days to take it back"
source: وقال إن شاء الله متصلا بإقراره لم يلزمه الإقرار
ومن أقر وشرط الخيار لزمه الإقرار وبطل الخيار
فإن استثنى الجميع لزمه الإقرار
صح الاستثناء ولزمه الباقي
cards.why: Only "in sha' Allah" joined to it stops an admission. An option is void, a total exception is void, and a part exception leaves the rest (30).

cards.title: The house and its building
cards.ar: فللمقر له الدار والبناء وإن قال: بناء هذه الدار لي والعرصة لفلان فهو كما قال
cards.en: If he admits a house is someone's but takes out its building for himself, the other person gets the house and the building. But if he says "The building of this house is mine and the 'arsa (the bare land) is so-and-so's", it is as he said.

cards.ask: Jamal says, "This house belongs to Nadir, except its building, which is mine." What does Nadir get?
source: ومن أقر بدار
فللمقر له الدار والبناء
cards.why: The building is part of the house, so it cannot be taken out: Nadir gets both.

cards.ask: Which are true of exceptions in an admission?

options.text: An exception must be joined to the admission
Taking out everything cancels the whole admission
"100 except a dinar" means 100 dirhams minus the dinar's value
"The building is mine and the land is his" is taken as he said
Adding an option lets him take the admission back

source: ومن أقر واستثنى متصلا بإقراره صح الاستثناء
فإن استثنى الجميع لزمه الإقرار وبطل الاستثناء
لزمه مائة درهم إلا قيمة الدينار
فهو كما قال
لزمه الإقرار وبطل الخيار
cards.why: A joined exception works and a total one fails; the option is void. The dinar is valued and taken off, and building-and-land is as he said.

cards.title: Dates in a basket, an animal in a stable
cards.ar: ومن أقر بتمر في قوصره لزمه التمر والقوصرة ومن أقر بدابة في إصطبل لزمه الدابة خاصة
cards.en: If he admits "dates in a basket" (qawsara, a basket woven from palm leaves), he owes the dates and the basket. If he admits "an animal in a stable", he owes only the animal.

cards.title: A garment in a garment
cards.ar: وإن قال: غصبت ثوبا في منديل لزماه جميعا وإن قال: له علي ثوب في ثوب لزماه وإن قال: له علي ثوب في عشرة أثواب لم يلزمه عند أبي حنيفة وأبي يوسف إلا ثوب واحد
cards.en: "I took a garment in a cloth wrapper by force": he owes both. "A garment in a garment": both. But "a garment in ten garments" means only one garment, say Abu Hanifa and Abu Yusuf. Note: Muhammad says eleven.

cards.ask: What does he owe?
items: A garment in a cloth wrapper
source: لزمه التمر والقوصرة ومن أقر بدابة في إصطبل لزمه الدابة خاصة
غصبت ثوبا في منديل لزماه جميعا وإن قال: له علي ثوب في ثوب لزماه
لم يلزمه عند أبي حنيفة وأبي يوسف إلا ثوب واحد
cards.why: A basket and a wrapper are carried with what they hold, and so is a garment wrapped in a garment. A stable is not, and ten garments cannot wrap one.

cards.title: Bringing back a damaged one
cards.ar: وجاء بثوب معيب
cards.en: If he admits he took a garment by force and then brings back a damaged one, his word is taken with his oath. The same if he admits dirhams and says they are zuyuf (poor-quality coins).

cards.ask: Murad admits he took Tahir's coat by force. He brings back a torn coat and says, "This is the one." Tahir says it was a good one. Whose word is taken?
options: Neither: Murad pays a new coat's price
source: وقال محمد: يلزمه أحد عشر ثوبا
وجاء بثوب معيب
مع يمينه وكذلك لو أقر بدراهم وقال: هي زيوف
cards.why: The one who admitted describes what he took, so his word is taken with an oath, as with bad coins.

cards.title: Five in five
cards.ar: وإن قال: له علي خمسة في خمسة يريد الضرب والحساب لزمه خمسة واحدة وإن قال: أدرت خمسة مع خمسة لزمه عشرة
cards.en: If he says "I owe him five in five", meaning multiplication, he owes just five. If he says "I meant five with five", he owes ten.

cards.ask: Asad says, "I owe Rafi five in five," meaning five times five. What does he owe?
cards.source: وإن قال: له علي خمسة في خمسة يريد الضرب والحساب لزمه خمسة واحدة
cards.why: Multiplying does not add to what he owes: it is five.

cards.ask: Complete the rule.
cards.ar: خمسة مع خمسة لزمه ____
cards.source: خمسة مع خمسة لزمه عشرة
cards.why: عشرة: "five with five" adds them, so ten.

cards.ask: Which are true of admitting things inside things?

options.text: Admitting dates in a basket means owing the basket too
Admitting an animal in a stable means owing the stable too
"Five in five", meaning multiplication, is five
"Five with five" is ten
Bringing back a damaged garment, his word is never accepted

source: لزمه التمر والقوصرة
لزمه الدابة خاصة
لزمه خمسة واحدة
خمسة مع خمسة لزمه عشرة
مع يمينه
cards.why: The basket comes with the dates but the stable does not; five in five is five, five with five is ten; and his word about the damaged garment is taken with an oath.

lessons.title: From one to ten, and "the price of..."

cards.title: From one to ten
cards.ar: وإن قال: له علي من درهم إلى عشرة لزمه تسعة عند أبي حنيفة فيلزمه الإبتداء وما بعده
cards.en: "I owe him from one dirham to ten": he owes nine, says Abu Hanifa. He owes the start and what follows, but the end point drops. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say all ten.

cards.ask: Anwar says, "I owe Halim from one dirham to ten." According to Abu Hanifa, how many dirhams does he owe?
cards.source: لزمه تسعة عند أبي حنيفة
cards.why: The first and everything after it count; the last, the end point, drops: nine.

cards.title: The price of a named item, not yet received
cards.ar: وإذا قال: له علي ألف درهم من ثمن عبد اشتريته منه ولم أقبضه فإن ذكر عبدا بعينه قيل للمقر له: إن شئت فسلم العبد وخذ الألف وإلا فلا شيء لك
cards.en: Al-Quduri's example from his time: "I owe him 1000 dirhams as the price of a slave I bought from him and have not received." If he names a particular one, the other is told: hand it over and take the 1000, or else you get nothing. If it was "this one", nothing is owed until it is handed over.

cards.ask: Majid says, "I owe him 1000, the price of this item I bought from him and haven't received." The seller never hands it over. What does Majid owe?
options: Nothing, until the item is handed over
cards.source: لم يلزمه حتى يسلم العبد فإن سلم العبد لزمه الألف وإن لم يسلمه لم تلزمه
cards.why: An admission tied to "this" item's price only binds when the item is handed over.

cards.title: Not naming which
cards.ar: وإن قال: له علي ألف من ثمن عبد ولم يعينه لزمه الألف في قول أبي حنيفة
cards.en: If he says it was the price of one he does not identify, he owes the 1000, according to Abu Hanifa: his addition does not cancel the admission.

cards.title: "The price of wine"
cards.ar: ولو قال: له علي ألف من ثمن خمر أو خنزير لزمه الألف ولم يقبل تفسيره
cards.en: If he says "I owe him 1000 for wine or pork", he owes the 1000 and his explanation is not accepted: he is trying to take back his admission with a reason that would cancel it.

cards.ask: Kamal admits, "I owe Tamim 1000, the price of some wine." What is the ruling?
options: He owes nothing, since a wine sale is void
cards.source: لزمه الألف ولم يقبل تفسيره
cards.why: He admitted the 1000, and the explanation that would cancel it is not accepted.

cards.title: "The price of goods, in bad coins"
cards.ar: ولو قال: له علي ألف من ثمن متاع وهي زيوف
cards.en: If he says "I owe him 1000 for some goods, and they are bad coins", and the other disagrees, he owes good coins, according to Abu Hanifa.

cards.title: A ring, a sword, a canopy
cards.ar: ومن أقر لغيره بخاتم فله الحلقة والفص وإن أقر له بسيف فله النصل والجفن والحمائل وإن أقر بحجلة فله العيدان والكسوة
cards.en: Admitting a ring is someone's gives him the band and the stone. A sword: the blade, the sheath and the straps. A hajala (a canopy over a bed): the poles and the cloth cover.

cards.ask: Faisal admits a sword belongs to Zaid. What does Zaid get?

options.text: The blade
The sheath
The carrying straps
Only the blade
The shield that hangs beside it

cards.source: وإن أقر له بسيف فله النصل والجفن والحمائل
cards.why: A sword includes its blade, sheath and straps; nothing more.

cards.ask: Which are true of admitting sums?

options.text: "From one to ten" is nine, according to Abu Hanifa
"1000 for wine" means he owes nothing
A ring includes its stone
"1000 for goods, in bad coins" means he owes good coins, according to Abu Hanifa
A canopy means only its cloth

source: لزمه تسعة عند أبي حنيفة
لزمه الألف ولم يقبل تفسيره
فله الحلقة والفص
لزمه الجياد في قول أبي حنيفة
فله العيدان والكسوة
cards.why: Nine, the stone, good coins. The wine excuse is rejected so he owes 1000, and a canopy includes its poles.

lessons.title: The unborn, and admissions in the last illness

cards.title: Owing an unborn child
cards.ar: وإن قال: لحمل فلانة علي ألف فإن قال أوصى به له فلان أو مات أبوه فورثه
cards.en: If he says "I owe the unborn child of such-and-such woman 1000" and explains "so-and-so left it to him in a will" or "his father died and he inherited it", the admission is valid. Note: if he gives no reason, Abu Yusuf says it is not valid.

cards.title: Admitting what is in the womb
cards.ar: وإذا أقر بحمل جارية أو حمل شاة لرجل صح الإقرار ولزمه
cards.en: If he admits that the unborn young of an animal (a sheep, say), or, in al-Quduri's time, of a slave woman, belongs to a man, the admission is valid and binds him.

cards.ask: Rashid says, "I owe Hind's unborn child 1000, because its father died and it inherited from him." Is the admission valid?
options: Yes: he gave a reason that makes sense
No: an unborn child can't be owed anything
Only after the child is born and names him
source: وإن أبهم الإقرار لم يصح عند أبي يوسف
أو مات أبوه فورثه
cards.why: Inheriting is a way an unborn child can own something, so the admission is valid.

cards.title: Debts from health come first
cards.ar: وإذا أقر الرجل في مرض موتته بديون وعليه ديون في صحته وديون لزمته في مرضه بأسباب معلومة فدين الصحة والدين المعروف بالأسباب مقدم على غيره
cards.en: If a man in his final illness admits debts, while he has debts from when he was healthy and debts he took on in his illness for known reasons, then the health debts and the debts with known reasons come first. Anything left over goes to what he admitted while ill.

cards.title: With no health debts
cards.ar: كان فيما أقر به في حال المرض وإن لم يكن عليه ديون في صحته جاز إقراره وكان المقر له أولى من الورثة
cards.en: If he has no debts from his time of health, his admission in illness is valid, and the person he admitted to comes before the heirs.

cards.ask: Jafar dies of an illness. He owed £1000 from when he was healthy, and while ill he admitted owing a friend £500. His estate is £1200. What does the friend get?
cards.source: فدين الصحة والدين المعروف بالأسباب مقدم على غيره
cards.why: The £1000 health debt is paid first; the £200 left goes to what he admitted while ill.

cards.title: Admitting to an heir
cards.ar: وإقرار المريض لوارثه باطل إلا أن يصدقه فيه بقية الورثة
cards.en: An admission by a dying man to one of his heirs is void, unless the rest of the heirs agree with it.

cards.ask: In his final illness, Mansur admits he owes his son Ilyas £5000. His other children say it isn't true. Must the £5000 be paid to Ilyas?
options: No: the other heirs do not agree
Yes, but only from a third of the estate
cards.source: وإقرار المريض لوارثه باطل إلا أن يصدقه فيه بقية الورثة
cards.why: Ilyas is an heir, and the other heirs do not agree, so the admission is void.

cards.title: A stranger who turns out to be a son
cards.ar: ومن أقر لأجنبي في مرضه ثم قال هو ابني ثبت نسبه وبطل إقراره له
cards.en: If in illness he admits a debt to a stranger and then says "He is my son", the lineage (nasab) is established and the admission is cancelled, since the son is an heir. But if he admits to a woman who is a stranger and then marries her, the admission stays valid.

cards.title: The wife divorced in illness
cards.ar: ومن طلق زوجته في مرضه ثلاثا ثم أقر لها بدين ومات فلها الأقل من الدين ومن ميراثها منه
cards.en: If he divorces his wife three times (a final divorce) in his illness, then admits a debt to her and dies, she gets whichever is less: the debt, or what she would have inherited from him.

cards.ask: In his final illness, Imran divorces his wife finally, then admits he owes her £3000, and dies. Her share as an heir would have been £2000. What does she get?
cards.source: فلها الأقل من الدين ومن ميراثها منه
cards.why: She gets the lesser of the debt (£3000) and her inheritance (£2000): £2000.

cards.ask: A man admits a debt in his final illness. Valid or void?
items: To a woman, whom he then marries
To a stranger, whom he then says is his son
To his son, and the other heirs deny it
To a friend, and he has no debts from his health
To his son, and all the other heirs agree
source: ثم تزوجها لم يبطل إقراره لها
ثم قال هو ابني ثبت نسبه وبطل إقراره له
وإقرار المريض لوارثه باطل إلا أن يصدقه فيه بقية الورثة
جاز إقراره وكان المقر له أولى من الورثة
cards.why: Admissions to heirs fail unless the other heirs agree. A wife married after the admission keeps it, and a non-heir comes before the heirs.

lessons.title: Admitting a relative
lessons.arabic: ومن أقر بغلام يولد مثله لمثله

cards.title: Claiming a son
cards.ar: ومن أقر بغلام يولد مثله لمثله وليس له نسب معروف أنه ابنه
cards.en: If a man says a boy is his son, the boy is old enough to be his child, he has no known lineage (nasab: who his father is), and the boy agrees, the lineage is established, even if the man is ill. The boy then shares in the inheritance with the other heirs.

cards.ask: A man says a boy is his son. What is needed for the lineage to be established?

options.text: The boy could be his child, given their ages
The boy has no known father
The boy agrees
The man must be healthy
Two witnesses

source: ومن أقر بغلام يولد مثله لمثله وليس له نسب معروف أنه ابنه
ثبت نسبه منه وإن كان مريضا ويشارك الورثة في الميراث
cards.why: Possible by age, no known lineage, and his agreement. It holds even if the man is ill, with no witnesses needed.

cards.title: Whom men and women may claim
cards.ar: ويجوز إقرار الرجل بالوالدين والولد والزوجة والمولى ويقبل إقرار المرأة بالوالدين والزوج والمولى ولا يقبل بالولد إلا أن يصدقها الزوج أو تشهد بولادتها قابلة
cards.en: A man may admit a parent, a child, a wife, or a mawla (a tie of clientship, from freeing a slave in al-Quduri's time). A woman may admit a parent, a husband or a mawla, but not a child, unless her husband agrees or a qabila (midwife) testifies she gave birth.

cards.ask: Salma says a young boy is her son. Her husband agrees. Is her claim accepted?
options: No: a woman can never admit a child
Only if the boy is over 15
cards.source: ولا يقبل بالولد إلا أن يصدقها الزوج أو تشهد بولادتها قابلة
cards.why: A woman's claim to a child is accepted when her husband agrees or a midwife testifies.

cards.title: A brother or an uncle
cards.ar: ومن أقر بنسب من غير الوالدين والولد والزوج والزوجة والمولى - مثل الأخ والعم - لم يقبل إقراره في النسب فإن كان له وارث معروف قريب أو بعيد فهو أولى بالميراث من المقر له وإن لم يكن له وارث استحق المقر له ميراثه
cards.en: Claiming anyone else, like a brother or an uncle, does not establish lineage. If he has a known heir, near or distant, that heir comes first in inheritance. If he has no heir, the person he claimed inherits from him.

cards.ask: A man admits this relative. Is lineage established?
source: ويجوز إقرار الرجل بالوالدين والولد والزوجة والمولى
مثل الأخ والعم - لم يقبل إقراره في النسب
cards.why: Parents, children, a wife and a mawla are accepted. A brother or an uncle is not.

cards.ask: Nuh has no heirs at all. He says, "Hadi is my brother," and dies. What happens to his estate?
options: Nothing goes to Hadi, since lineage is not established
cards.source: وإن لم يكن له وارث استحق المقر له ميراثه
cards.why: The lineage is not established, but with no other heir the one he named takes the inheritance.

cards.title: A son claims a brother
cards.ar: ومن مات أبوه فأقر بأخ له لم يثبت نسب أخيه ويشاركه في الميراث
cards.en: If a man's father dies and he says someone is his brother, the brother's lineage is not established, but he shares the inheritance with him.

cards.ask: Bilal's father dies, leaving Bilal as his only known son. Bilal says, "Saad is my brother." What is the ruling?
options: No lineage, but he shares Bilal's share
Saad becomes Bilal's brother in every way
cards.source: لم يثبت نسب أخيه ويشاركه في الميراث
cards.why: Admitting a brother does not establish lineage, but Bilal must share his inheritance with him.

cards.ask: Aisha says, "Amina is my daughter." Her husband denies it and no midwife testifies. What is the ruling?
options: Accepted: a mother knows her child
cards.source: ولا يقبل بالولد إلا أن يصدقها الزوج أو تشهد بولادتها قابلة
cards.why: A woman's claim to a child needs her husband's agreement or a midwife's testimony. Here there is neither.

lessons.title: What hire is, and making it known

cards.title: A contract on benefits
cards.ar: الإجارة: عقد على المنافع بعوض
cards.en: Ijara is hire: renting a thing or hiring a person. It is a contract on the benefits (the use or the work) of something, for a payment. You don't buy the house; you buy living in it for a time.

cards.ask: What is ijara?
options: Buying a thing outright, for a price
A contract on benefits, for a payment
Giving the use of a thing, for nothing
cards.source: الإجارة: عقد على المنافع بعوض
cards.why: Hire is a contract on the benefits of something, in return for a payment.

cards.title: Both sides must be known
cards.ar: ولا تصح حتى تكون المنافع معلومة والأجرة معلومة وما جاز أن يكون ثمنا في البيع جاز أن يكون أجرة في الإجارة
cards.en: Hire is valid only when the benefit is known and the ujra (the wage or rent) is known. Anything that can be a price in a sale can be the wage in a hire.

cards.ask: Imran rents a flat to Jalal "for some money, we'll see how much." Is the hire valid?
options: No: the rent must be known
Yes: they can agree the amount later
cards.source: ولا تصح حتى تكون المنافع معلومة والأجرة معلومة
cards.why: Hire needs a known benefit and a known wage. "Some money" is not known.

cards.ask: Complete the rule.
cards.ar: وما جاز أن يكون ثمنا في البيع جاز أن يكون ____ في الإجارة
cards.source: وما جاز أن يكون ثمنا في البيع جاز أن يكون أجرة في الإجارة
cards.why: أجرة: whatever can be a price in a sale can be a wage in a hire.

cards.title: Known by time
cards.ar: والمنافع تارة تصير معلومة بالمدة كاستئجار الدور للسكنى والأرضين للزراعة فيصح العقد على مدة معلومة أي مدة كانت
cards.en: The benefit becomes known in three ways. First, by a period of time, like renting houses to live in or land to farm. The contract is valid for any known period, however long.

cards.ask: Rafiq rents a field to Sulayman for 30 years at a known rent. Is the period allowed?
options: Yes: any known period is valid
No: the limit is one year
cards.source: فيصح العقد على مدة معلومة أي مدة كانت
cards.why: Al-Quduri says any known period, whatever its length.

cards.title: Known by the work
cards.ar: وتارة تصير معلومة بالعمل والتسمية كمن استأجر رجلا على صبغ ثوب أو خياطته أو استأجر دابة ليحمل عليها مقدارا معلوما أو يركبها مسافة سماها
cards.en: Second, by naming the work: hiring a man to dye or sew a garment, or hiring an animal to carry a known load or to ride a named distance.

cards.title: Known by pointing
cards.ar: وتارة تصير معلومة بالتعيين والإشارة كمن استأجر رجلا لينقل له هذا الطعام إلى موضع معلوم
cards.en: Third, by pointing to it: hiring a man to carry "this food" to a known place.

cards.ask: In how many ways does al-Quduri say the benefit becomes known?
source: والمنافع تارة تصير معلومة بالمدة
وتارة تصير معلومة بالعمل والتسمية
وتارة تصير معلومة بالتعيين والإشارة
cards.why: Three ways: by a period of time, by naming the work, and by pointing.

cards.ask: How is the benefit made known?
items: Renting a house for a year
Hiring a tailor to sew a shirt
Hiring a porter to carry these boxes to the station
Hiring a horse to ride 20 miles
source: والمنافع تارة تصير معلومة بالمدة
وتارة تصير معلومة بالعمل والتسمية
وتارة تصير معلومة بالتعيين والإشارة
cards.why: Houses and land go by a period; sewing and a named distance by the work; "these boxes" by pointing.

cards.ask: Which are true of a hire contract?

options.text: Hire is a contract on benefits, for a payment
The wage may be left unknown if both agree
A benefit can be made known by a period of time
A benefit can be made known by pointing
Hire buys the thing itself

source: الإجارة: عقد على المنافع بعوض
والأجرة معلومة
تصير معلومة بالمدة
تصير معلومة بالتعيين والإشارة
cards.why: Hire is on benefits, not the thing itself, and the wage must be known. Time and pointing are two of the three ways.

cards.title: Houses and shops
cards.ar: ويجوز استئجار الدور والحوانيت للسكنى وإن لم يبين ما يعمل فيها وله أن يعمل كل شيء إلا الحداد والقصار والطحان
cards.en: Houses and shops may be rented to use, even without saying what will be done in them. The tenant may do anything there except be a blacksmith, a qassar (a fuller, who beats and washes cloth) or a miller: heavy work that damages the building.

cards.ask: Sami rents a shop without saying what it's for. What may he do there?

options.text: Sell clothes
Store his books
Live in it
Set up a blacksmith's forge
Run a grain mill

cards.source: وله أن يعمل كل شيء إلا الحداد والقصار والطحان
cards.why: Anything is allowed except a blacksmith, a fuller or a miller.

cards.title: Land for farming
cards.ar: ويجوز استئجار الأراضي للزراعة ولا يصح العقد حتى يسمي ما يزرع فيها أو يقول: على أن يزرع فيها ما شاء
cards.en: Land may be rented to farm, but the contract is valid only if he names what he will grow, or says "on condition that he grows whatever he likes."

cards.ask: Ahmad rents a field "for farming" but they don't say what he will grow, and he doesn't say "whatever I like." Is the hire valid?
options: No: the crop must be named
cards.source: ولا يصح العقد حتى يسمي ما يزرع فيها أو يقول: على أن يزرع فيها ما شاء
cards.why: Different crops treat the land differently, so it must be named, or left open by saying so.

cards.title: Building and planting on rented land
cards.ar: ويجوز أن يستأجر الساحة ليبني فيها أو يغرس فيها نخلا أو شجرا فإذا انقضت مدة الإجارة لزمه أن يقلع البناء والغرس ويسلمها فارغة
cards.en: He may rent an open plot to build on, or to plant palms or trees. When the period ends, he must pull up the building and the trees and hand the land back empty.

cards.title: The landowner's choice
cards.ar: إلا أن يختار صاحب الأرض أن يغرم له قيمة ذلك مقلوعا فيملكه أو يرضى بتركه على حاله فيكون البناء لهذا والأرض لهذا
cards.en: Unless the landowner chooses to pay him what the building or trees are worth once pulled up, and own them, or agrees to leave them as they are, so the building belongs to one and the land to the other.

cards.ask: Amir rented a plot for 10 years and planted trees. The 10 years are over, and the owner says nothing special. What must Amir do?
options: Pull up the trees and hand the land back empty
Leave the trees; they now belong to the owner
Keep using the land while the trees stand
cards.source: فإذا انقضت مدة الإجارة لزمه أن يقلع البناء والغرس ويسلمها فارغة
cards.why: At the end of the hire he must clear the land, unless the owner chooses otherwise.

cards.ask: The landowner wants to keep Amir's trees. What does he pay?
options: Their value standing in the ground
Nothing: they are on his land
cards.source: أن يغرم له قيمة ذلك مقلوعا فيملكه
cards.why: He pays what they are worth pulled up (مقلوعا), and then owns them.

cards.ask: Allowed in the rental, or not?
items: Living in a house rented without saying what for
Running a blacksmith's forge in a rented house
Renting land "to grow whatever he likes"
Renting farmland without naming the crop at all
Renting a plot to build a shed on
source: للسكنى وإن لم يبين ما يعمل فيها
إلا الحداد والقصار والطحان
أو يقول: على أن يزرع فيها ما شاء
ولا يصح العقد حتى يسمي ما يزرع فيها
ويجوز أن يستأجر الساحة ليبني فيها
cards.why: Use of a house is open except heavy trades. Farmland needs a named crop or "whatever he likes", and building on a plot is allowed.

cards.title: A named rider
cards.ar: ويجوز استئجار الدواب للركوب والحمل فإن قال: على أن يركبها فلان أو يلبس الثوب فلان فأركبها غيره أو ألبسه غيره كان ضامنا إن عطبت الدابة أو تلف الثوب وكذلك كل ما يختلف باختلاف المستعمل
cards.en: Animals may be hired to ride or to carry loads. If it was "for so-and-so to ride" (or a garment "for so-and-so to wear") and he lets someone else, he is damin (must pay for it) if the animal dies or the garment is ruined. The same goes for anything that changes with who uses it.

cards.ask: Yusuf hires a horse "for Yusuf to ride." He lets his cousin ride it instead, and the horse dies on the way. Must Yusuf pay for it?
options: Yes: he let another person ride
No: a hired animal is a trust with him
Only if the cousin was heavier
cards.source: فأركبها غيره أو ألبسه غيره كان ضامنا إن عطبت الدابة
cards.why: Riding changes with the rider, so using someone else makes him liable when it dies.

cards.title: Houses don't change with the user
cards.ar: وأما العقار وما لا يختلف باختلاف المستعمل فلا ضمان عليه فإذا شرط سكنى واحد فله أن يسكن غيره
cards.en: But 'aqar (land and buildings) and things that don't change with who uses them carry no liability. If the hire said one person would live there, he may let someone else live there.

cards.ask: Aisha rents a flat "for Aisha to live in." She moves away and lets her sister live there instead. Is that allowed?
options: Yes: a home is the same for any user
No: only the named person may live there
cards.source: فإذا شرط سكنى واحد فله أن يسكن غيره
cards.why: Living in a home is the same whoever does it, so naming one person doesn't stop another.

cards.title: Like the named load, or lighter
cards.ar: وإن سمى نوعا أو قدرا يحمله على الدابة مثل أن يقول: خمسة أقفزة حنطة فله أن يحمل ما هو مثل الحنطة في الضرر أو أقل كالشعير والسمسم وليس له أن يحمل ما هو أضر من الحنطة كالملح والحديد
cards.en: If he names a kind or amount to load, like "five qafiz of wheat", he may carry something as easy on the animal as wheat, or easier, like barley or sesame. He may not carry something harder on it, like salt or iron.

cards.ask: Tariq hired a camel to carry five qafiz of wheat. May he carry this instead?
cards.source: فله أن يحمل ما هو مثل الحنطة في الضرر أو أقل كالشعير والسمسم وليس له أن يحمل ما هو أضر من الحنطة كالملح والحديد
cards.why: Barley and sesame are no harder on the animal than wheat; salt and iron are.

cards.title: Cotton, iron, and a second rider
cards.ar: فليس له أن يحمل مثل وزنه حديدا وإن استأجرها ليركبها فأردف معه رجلا فعطبت ضمن نصف قيمتها ولا يعتبر بالثقل
cards.en: If he hired it to carry a named amount of cotton, he may not carry the same weight in iron (iron presses on one spot). If he hired it to ride and takes another man behind him, and it dies, he pays half its value, whatever their weights.

cards.ask: Hamid hires a camel worth £900 to ride. He takes a friend up behind him, and the camel dies. How much must he pay?
cards.source: فأردف معه رجلا فعطبت ضمن نصف قيمتها ولا يعتبر بالثقل
cards.why: With a second rider he pays half its value, £450, without weighing the riders.

cards.title: Loading more than agreed
cards.ar: وإن استأجرها ليحمل عليها مقدرا من الحنطة فحمل أكثر منه فعطبت ضمن ما زاد الثقل
cards.en: If he hired it to carry a set amount of wheat, loads more, and it dies, he pays for the share of the extra weight.

cards.title: Pulling and beating
cards.ar: وإذا كبح الدابة بلجامها أو ضربها فعطبت ضمن عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: If he yanks the animal back with its bridle or beats it, and it dies, he pays for it, according to Abu Hanifa.

cards.ask: Bashir hires a donkey to carry 100 kg of wheat, loads 120 kg, and it collapses and dies. What does he pay?
options: Only the share that the extra weight caused
Nothing, since it was mostly the agreed load
cards.source: فحمل أكثر منه فعطبت ضمن ما زاد الثقل
cards.why: He pays for what the extra weight added, not the whole animal.

cards.ask: Which are true of hiring animals and houses?

options.text: Letting an unnamed rider ride makes him liable if it dies
A house rented for one person may be lived in by another
Hired for wheat, he may load salt
A second rider makes him pay half if it dies
Beating a hired animal to death costs nothing, according to Abu Hanifa

source: كان ضامنا إن عطبت الدابة
فله أن يسكن غيره
كالملح والحديد
ضمن نصف قيمتها
أو ضربها فعطبت ضمن عند أبي حنيفة
cards.why: A named rider, a house for anyone, half for a second rider. Salt is harder than wheat, and beating it to death makes him pay.

cards.title: Common and private workers
cards.ar: والأجراء على ضربين: وأجير مشترك وأجير خاص فالمشترك: من لا يستحق الأجرة حتى يعمل كالصباغ والقصار
cards.en: Workers are of two kinds. The ajir mushtarak (common worker) works for anyone who brings a job, like a dyer or a fuller, and earns his wage only by doing the work. The ajir khass (private worker) is hired for a period.

cards.ask: Into how many kinds does al-Quduri divide hired workers?
cards.source: والأجراء على ضربين
cards.why: Two kinds: the common worker (ajir mushtarak) and the private worker (ajir khass).

cards.ask: Which of these are al-Quduri's kinds of hired worker?

options.text: The common worker (ajir mushtarak)
The partner
The private worker (ajir khass)
The agent

cards.source: والأجراء على ضربين: وأجير مشترك وأجير خاص
cards.why: His two kinds are the common worker and the private worker. A partner and an agent are not hired workers.

cards.title: The goods are a trust with him
cards.ar: والمتاع أمانة في يده: إن هلك لم يضمن شيئا عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: The goods with a common worker are a trust: if they are lost (without his fault), he owes nothing, according to Abu Hanifa. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say he must pay.

cards.ask: A dry-cleaner's shop is robbed, through no fault of his, and Nasir's suit is taken. According to Abu Hanifa, must the cleaner pay?
options: No: the goods were a trust in his hands
Yes: a worker always pays for what he loses
cards.source: والمتاع أمانة في يده: إن هلك لم يضمن شيئا عند أبي حنيفة
cards.why: For Abu Hanifa the goods are a trust, so a loss without fault is not paid for.

cards.title: Damage from his own work
cards.ar: وما تلف بعمله كتخريق الثوب من دقة وزلق الحمال وانقطاع الحبل الذي يشد به المكاري الحمل وغرق السفينة من مدها مضمون إلا أنه لا يضمن به بني آدم
cards.en: But what is ruined by his own work he must pay for: a garment torn by his beating, a porter slipping, the hirer of animals' rope snapping, a boat sinking from his rowing. Except people: he does not pay for a person who drowns in the boat or falls off the animal.

cards.ask: A fuller beats Layla's cloth to clean it and tears it. Must he pay?
options: Yes: it was ruined by his own work
No: the cloth was a trust
Only if he did it on purpose
cards.source: وما تلف بعمله كتخريق الثوب من دقة
cards.why: Damage caused by the worker's own work is paid for.

cards.ask: A boatman's boat sinks from his rowing. Goods are lost, and a passenger drowns. What does the boatman pay for?
options: Both the goods and the person
source: وغرق السفينة من مدها مضمون إلا أنه لا يضمن به بني آدم
فمن غرق في السفينة أو سقط من الدابة
cards.why: Goods ruined by his work are paid for, but a person who drowns is not paid for in this way.

cards.title: The bloodletter and the vet
cards.ar: وإذا قصد الفصاد أو بزغ البزاغ ولم يتجاوز الموضع المعتاد فلا ضمان عليه فيما عطب من ذلك
cards.en: A fassad (bloodletter, who opens a vein) or a bazzagh (who lances an animal) who does not go beyond the usual spot is not liable if the patient or animal dies from it.

cards.title: The private worker
cards.ar: ولأجير الخاص: الذي يستحق الأجرة بتسليم نفسه في المدة وإن لم يعمل كمن استؤجر شهرا للخدمة أو لرعي الغنم ولا ضمان على الأجير الخاص فما تلف في يده ولا ما تلف من عمله
cards.en: The private worker earns his wage by making himself available for the period, even if no work is given him, like someone hired for a month to serve or to herd sheep. He owes nothing for what is lost in his hands, or even what is ruined by his work.

cards.ask: Common or private worker?
items: A dyer who takes cloth from anyone
A shepherd hired for a month
A fuller with a shop in the market
A servant hired for a month
source: فالمشترك: من لا يستحق الأجرة حتى يعمل كالصباغ والقصار
كمن استؤجر شهرا للخدمة أو لرعي الغنم
cards.why: Dyers and fullers work for all comers; those hired for a month are private workers.

cards.ask: Sadiq is hired for a month to herd Hamza's sheep. While herding, one breaks its leg and dies. Must Sadiq pay?
options: No: a private worker isn't liable even for his work
Yes: it happened during his own work, so he must pay
cards.source: ولا ضمان على الأجير الخاص فما تلف في يده ولا ما تلف من عمله
cards.why: Unlike a common worker, the private worker owes nothing, even for what is ruined by his work.

cards.title: Bad conditions spoil it
cards.ar: والإجارة تفسدها الشروط كما تفسد البيع
cards.en: Hire is made fasid (spoiled, invalid) by improper conditions, just as a sale is.

cards.ask: Complete the rule.
cards.ar: والإجارة تفسدها الشروط كما تفسد ____
cards.source: والإجارة تفسدها الشروط كما تفسد البيع
cards.why: البيع: conditions spoil hire just as they spoil a sale.

cards.title: Hired to serve, not to travel
cards.ar: ومن استأجر عبدا للخدمة فليس له أن يسافر به إلا أن يشترط ذلك
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time, someone who hired a slave for service could not take him on a journey, unless that was a condition of the hire. Service at home is lighter than service on a journey.

cards.ask: In al-Quduri's time, Munir hires a slave of Zaid's to serve in his house, and says nothing about travel. Then he wants to take him on a trip. May he?
options: No, unless it was a condition
cards.source: فليس له أن يسافر به إلا أن يشترط ذلك
cards.why: Travel was not part of what was hired, so he needs it as a condition.

cards.title: A camel for a litter and two riders
cards.ar: ومن استأجر جملا ليحمل عليه محملا وراكبين إلى مكة جاز وله المحمل المعتاد وإن شاهد الجمال المحمل فهو أجود
cards.en: He may hire a camel to carry a mahmil (a covered litter seat) and two riders to Makkah. He gets the usual kind of litter. If the camel owner sees the litter first, that is better.

cards.ask: Harun hires a camel to Makkah for a litter and two riders. The owner never sees the litter. Is the hire valid?
options: Yes, with the usual kind of litter
No: the litter must be seen
cards.source: جاز وله المحمل المعتاد وإن شاهد الجمال المحمل فهو أجود
cards.why: It is valid with the usual litter; seeing it first is only better.

cards.title: Eating the provisions on the way
cards.ar: وإن استأجر بعيرا ليحمل عليه مقدارا من الزاد فأكل منه في الطريق جاز له أن يرد عوض ما أكل
cards.en: If he hires a camel to carry a set amount of provisions (food for the journey) and eats some on the way, he may put back the same amount to replace what he ate.

cards.ask: Ihsan hires a camel to carry 100 kg of food for his journey. By halfway he has eaten 20 kg. May he buy 20 kg more and load it?
options: Yes: he may replace what he ate
No: he may only carry what is left
cards.source: فأكل منه في الطريق جاز له أن يرد عوض ما أكل
cards.why: The hire was for that amount, so he may replace what he ate.

cards.ask: Which are true of conditions in a hire?

options.text: Improper conditions spoil a hire as they spoil a sale
Someone hired to serve at home may be taken travelling without a condition
A camel may be hired for a litter and two riders to Makkah
Eaten provisions may be replaced
The camel owner must see the litter or the hire is void

source: والإجارة تفسدها الشروط كما تفسد البيع
فليس له أن يسافر به إلا أن يشترط ذلك
ليحمل عليه محملا وراكبين إلى مكة جاز
جاز له أن يرد عوض ما أكل
وإن شاهد الجمال المحمل فهو أجود
cards.why: Conditions spoil it, travel needs a condition, the litter hire is valid without seeing it, and eaten food may be replaced.

cards.title: Not by the contract alone
cards.ar: والأجرة لا تجب بالعقد وتستحق بأحد معان ثلاثة: إما بشرط التعجيل أو بالتعجيل من غير شرط أو باستيفاء المعقود عليه
cards.en: The wage is not owed just by making the contract. It becomes due in one of three ways: a condition to pay in advance, paying in advance without a condition, or receiving the benefit that was hired.

cards.ask: In how many ways can the wage become due?
cards.source: وتستحق بأحد معان ثلاثة
cards.why: Three: a condition to pay in advance, paying in advance anyway, or receiving the benefit.

cards.ask: Which of these make the wage due?

options.text: A condition that it is paid in advance
Paying in advance anyway
Receiving the benefit that was hired
Signing the contract, and nothing more
The worker asking for it before starting

cards.source: إما بشرط التعجيل أو بالتعجيل من غير شرط أو باستيفاء المعقود عليه
cards.why: Those are the three ways. The contract alone does not make it due.

cards.title: Day by day, stage by stage
cards.ar: ومن استأجر دارا فللمؤجر أن يطالبه لأجره كل يوم إلا أن يبين وقت الاستحقاق بالعقد ومن استأجر بعيرا إلى مكة فللجمال أن يطالبه بأجرة كل مرحلة
cards.en: A landlord may ask for each day's rent, unless the contract set a time for payment. The camel owner on the road to Makkah may ask for the wage of each stage of the journey.

cards.ask: Kamil rents a house, and the contract says nothing about when rent is paid. After three days the landlord asks for three days' rent. May he?
options: Yes: he may ask for each day's rent
No: only at the end of the month
No: only at the end of the hire
cards.source: فللمؤجر أن يطالبه لأجره كل يوم إلا أن يبين وقت الاستحقاق بالعقد
cards.why: Each day's use is received, so each day's rent is due, unless the contract set another time.

cards.title: Craftsmen wait until done
cards.ar: وليس للقصار والخياط أن يطالب بالأجرة حتى يفرغ من العمل إلا أن يشترط التعجيل
cards.en: A fuller or a tailor may not ask for the wage until he finishes the work, unless paying in advance was a condition.

cards.ask: A tailor has sewn half of Rashid's suit and asks for half the wage. Must Rashid pay now?
options: No: not until the work is finished
Yes: half the work, half the wage
cards.source: وليس للقصار والخياط أن يطالب بالأجرة حتى يفرغ من العمل
cards.why: A tailor earns his wage only when the work is done, unless advance payment was agreed.

cards.title: The baker and the cook
cards.ar: ومن استأجر خبازا ليخبز له في بيته قفيز دقيق بدرهم لم يستحق الأجرة حتى يخرج الخبز من التنور ومن استأجر طباخا ليطبخ له طعاما للوليمة فالغرف عليه
cards.en: A baker hired to bake a qafiz of flour in someone's house for a dirham earns nothing until the bread comes out of the oven. A cook hired for a walima (a wedding feast) must also serve the food out into the dishes.

cards.title: The brick-maker
cards.ar: ومن استأجر رجلا ليضرب له لبنا استحق الأجرة إذا أقامه عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: A man hired to make mud bricks earns his wage once he has stood them up to dry, according to Abu Hanifa. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say not until he stacks them.

cards.ask: Wasim hires a baker to bake his flour at home for one dirham. When has the baker earned it?
options: When the bread comes out of the oven
When he has kneaded the dough and lit the oven
cards.source: لم يستحق الأجرة حتى يخرج الخبز من التنور
cards.why: The work is done only when the bread comes out of the oven.

cards.ask: Faruq hires a cook for his walima. The food is cooked, and the cook says, "Serving it out is not my job." Who is right?
cards.source: ومن استأجر طباخا ليطبخ له طعاما للوليمة فالغرف عليه
cards.why: Serving out the food is on the cook hired for a walima.

lessons.title: Two prices, and month by month
lessons.arabic: إن خطت هذا الثوب فارسيا فبدرهم

cards.title: One price or another
cards.ar: وإذا قال للخياط: إن خطت هذا الثوب فارسيا فبدرهم وإن خطته روميا فبدرهمين جاز وأي العلمين عمل استحق الأجرة
cards.en: He may tell a tailor: "If you sew this in the Persian style, one dirham; in the Roman style, two." That is valid, and he earns the wage for whichever he does.

cards.ask: Hasan tells a tailor, "Persian style, one dirham; Roman style, two." The tailor sews it Roman style. What is he owed?
cards.source: وأي العلمين عمل استحق الأجرة
cards.why: Both offers were valid, and he earns the wage named for the one he did.

cards.title: Today or tomorrow
cards.ar: وإن قال: إن خطته اليوم فبدرهم وإن خطته غدا فبنصف درهم فإن خاطه اليوم فله درهم وإن خاطه غدا فله أجر مثله عند أبي حنيفة ولا يتجاوز به نصف درهم
cards.en: "Sew it today for a dirham, tomorrow for half." If he sews it today he gets a dirham. If tomorrow, he gets ajr al-mithl (the usual wage for such work), but not more than half a dirham, according to Abu Hanifa.

cards.ask: The usual wage for this sewing is one dirham. The tailor finishes tomorrow. According to Abu Hanifa, what does he get?
cards.source: وإن خاطه غدا فله أجر مثله عند أبي حنيفة ولا يتجاوز به نصف درهم
cards.why: He gets the usual wage, but capped at half a dirham, so half.

cards.title: Perfumer or blacksmith
cards.ar: وإن قال: إن سكت في هذا الدكان عطارا فبدرهم في الشهر وإن سكنته حدادا فبدرهمين جاز وأي الأمرين فعل استحق المسمى فيه عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: "If you use this shop as a perfumer, one dirham a month; as a blacksmith, two." Abu Hanifa says that is valid, and the rent named for whichever he does is due. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say this hire is fasid.

cards.title: "A dirham each month"
cards.ar: ومن استأجر دارا كل شهر بدرهم فالعقد صحيح في شهر واحد فاسد في بقية الشهور إلا أن يسمي جملة شهور معلومة
cards.en: Renting a house "at a dirham each month" is valid for one month and fasid for the rest, unless a known total number of months is named.

cards.ask: Huda rents a room "at a dirham each month" and names no number of months. For how long is the contract sound?
options: No time at all: it is fasid
cards.source: فالعقد صحيح في شهر واحد فاسد في بقية الشهور إلا أن يسمي جملة شهور معلومة
cards.why: It is sound for the first month only, unless a known total of months is named. Each later month is fasid until she begins it.

cards.title: An hour into the next month
