cards.ar: فإن سكن ساعة من الشهر الثاني صح العقد فيه ولزمه ذلك الشهر ولم يكن للمؤجر أن يخرجه منها إلى أن ينقضي وكذلك كل شهر يسكن في أوله
cards.en: If he lives there for an hour of the second month, the contract becomes valid for that month: he owes it, and the landlord cannot put him out until it ends. The same for every month he begins.

cards.ask: Zubair rents a room "at £300 each month," with no number of months. He stays into the first day of month two. The landlord wants him out on day ten. May he?
options: No: month two is now binding until it ends
Yes: only the first month was valid
Yes, if he refunds the rent
cards.source: صح العقد فيه ولزمه ذلك الشهر ولم يكن للمؤجر أن يخرجه منها إلى أن ينقضي
cards.why: Living into the second month makes that month binding on both.

cards.title: A year for ten
cards.ar: وإذا استأجر دارا سنة بعشرة دراهم جاز وإن لم يسم قسط كل شهر من الأجرة
cards.en: Renting a house for a year at ten dirhams is valid, even without saying how much of it is for each month.

cards.ask: Complete the rule.
cards.ar: وإذا استأجر دارا سنة بعشرة دراهم جاز وإن لم يسم ____ كل شهر من الأجرة
cards.source: وإذا استأجر دارا سنة بعشرة دراهم جاز وإن لم يسم قسط كل شهر من الأجرة
cards.why: قسط: the share of each month need not be named.

cards.ask: Which are true of hire with two prices or month by month?

options.text: "Persian style one dirham, Roman style two" is valid
"A dirham each month" is valid for every month
A year's rent need not be split into months
Sewn tomorrow, he gets at most half a dirham, according to Abu Hanifa
The landlord may evict him in the middle of a month he has started

source: إن خطت هذا الثوب فارسيا فبدرهم وإن خطته روميا فبدرهمين جاز
فالعقد صحيح في شهر واحد فاسد في بقية الشهور
وإن لم يسم قسط كل شهر من الأجرة
ولا يتجاوز به نصف درهم
ولم يكن للمؤجر أن يخرجه منها إلى أن ينقضي
cards.why: Two styles and a yearly rent are valid; tomorrow is capped at half. "Each month" holds only for the first month and each month begun, which cannot be cut short.

lessons.title: What may be hired, and the wet nurse

cards.title: Allowed and not allowed
cards.ar: ويجوز أخذ أجرة الحمام والحجام ولا يجوز أخذ عسب التيس ولا يجوز الاستئجار على الأذان والإقامة والحج والغناء والنوح
cards.en: A fee may be taken for a public bath, and by a hajjam (a cupper, who draws blood for treatment). But not a fee for a male goat to mate with someone's herd. Nor may anyone be hired for the adhan, the iqama, Hajj, singing or wailing for the dead.

cards.ask: May a wage be taken for this?
items: A male goat mating with a herd
cards.source: ويجوز أخذ أجرة الحمام والحجام ولا يجوز أخذ عسب التيس ولا يجوز الاستئجار على الأذان والإقامة والحج والغناء والنوح
cards.why: The bath and the cupper are allowed. A stud fee and acts of worship like the adhan and Hajj are not.

cards.title: A shared property
cards.ar: ولا تجوز أجارة المشاع عند أبي حنيفة إلا من الشريك وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد: إجازة المشاع جائزة
cards.en: A mushaa' share (an undivided share of something owned jointly) may not be rented out, says Abu Hanifa, except to the partner who owns the rest. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say it is allowed.

cards.ask: Idris and his brother own a house jointly, undivided. Idris rents his half to a stranger. According to Abu Hanifa, is that allowed?
options: No, only to his brother, the partner
Yes, if the stranger lives in one room
cards.source: ولا تجوز أجارة المشاع عند أبي حنيفة إلا من الشريك
cards.why: For Abu Hanifa, an undivided share may only be rented to the partner.

cards.title: The wet nurse
cards.ar: ويجوز استئجار الظئر بأجرة معلومة ويجوز بطعامها وكسوتها وليس للمستأجر أن يمنع زوجها من وطئها
cards.en: A zi'r is a wet nurse: a woman hired to breastfeed a baby. She may be hired for a known wage, or for her food and clothing. The family who hired her may not keep her husband from his married life with her.

cards.title: Her duties
cards.ar: فإن حبلت كان لهم أن يفسخوا الإجارة إذا خافوا على الصبي من لبنها وعليها أن تصلح طعام الصبي وإن أرضعته في المدة بلبن شاة فلا أجر لها
cards.en: If she becomes pregnant, the family may end the hire if they fear her milk will harm the baby. She must prepare the baby's food. If she fed him goat's milk for the period instead of nursing him, she gets no wage.

cards.ask: A family hires a wet nurse in return for her food and clothing, with no money. Is the hire valid?
options: Yes: food and clothing may be her wage
No: the wage must be in money
Only if the amounts are written down
cards.source: ويجوز استئجار الظئر بأجرة معلومة ويجوز بطعامها وكسوتها
cards.why: Al-Quduri allows hiring a wet nurse for her food and clothing.

cards.ask: A wet nurse is hired for six months, but she feeds the baby goat's milk the whole time. What wage is she owed?
options: The full wage: the baby was fed
cards.source: وإن أرضعته في المدة بلبن شاة فلا أجر لها
cards.why: She was hired to nurse him; feeding goat's milk is not that work, so she has no wage.

cards.ask: Which are true of what may be hired?

options.text: A cupper may take a fee
A man may be hired to call the adhan
If the nurse becomes pregnant, the family may end the hire if they fear for the baby
The nurse must prepare the baby's food
A stud fee for a male goat is allowed

source: ويجوز أخذ أجرة الحمام والحجام
ولا يجوز الاستئجار على الأذان
كان لهم أن يفسخوا الإجارة إذا خافوا على الصبي من لبنها
وعليها أن تصلح طعام الصبي
ولا يجوز أخذ عسب التيس
cards.why: The cupper's fee, ending the hire out of fear for the baby, and preparing his food are in the text. The adhan and the stud fee are not allowed.

lessons.title: Holding the goods, helpers and disputes

cards.title: Holding the goods until paid
cards.ar: وكل صانع لعمله أثر في العين كالقصار والصباغ فله أن يحبس العين بعد الفراغ من عمله حتى يستوفي الأجرة
cards.en: Any craftsman whose work leaves a mark on the thing itself, like a fuller or a dyer, may keep the item after finishing until he is paid. Someone whose work leaves no mark on it, like a porter or a boatman, may not keep the item for his wage.

cards.ask: May he keep the item until he is paid?
items: A dyer, after dyeing a scarf
A porter, after carrying a trunk
A boatman, after carrying goods across
source: وكل صانع لعمله أثر في العين كالقصار والصباغ فله أن يحبس العين
ومن ليس لعمله أثر
كالحمال والملاح
cards.why: Dyeing and fulling leave a mark on the item; carrying it does not.

cards.title: "Do it yourself"
cards.ar: وإذا شرط على الصانع أن يعمل بنفسه فليس له أن يستعمل غيره فإن أطلق له العمل فله أن يستأجر من
cards.en: If the craftsman was told to do the work himself, he may not use anyone else. If the work was left open, he may hire someone to do it.

cards.ask: Lubna tells a tailor, "Sew this dress yourself." He gives it to his apprentice. Was he allowed?
options: No: he had to do it himself
Yes: he is responsible either way
Yes, if the apprentice is skilled
cards.source: وإذا شرط على الصانع أن يعمل بنفسه فليس له أن يستعمل غيره
cards.why: The condition was his own work, so he may not hand it to someone else.

cards.title: Disagreeing about what was asked
cards.ar: وإذا اختلف الخياط وصاحب الثوب فقال صاحب الثوب: أمرتك أن تعمله قباء وقال الخياط: قميصا أو قال صاحب الثوب للصباغ: أمرتك أن تصبغه أحمر فصبغته أصفر فالقول قول صاحب الثوب مع يمينه فإن حلف فالخياط ضامن
cards.en: If the owner says "I told you to make a qaba' (a long open robe)" and the tailor says "a shirt", or the owner tells the dyer "I said red and you dyed it yellow", the owner's word is taken with his oath. If he swears, the tailor must pay for the cloth.

cards.ask: Maryam says she asked the dyer for red; he dyed it yellow and says she asked for yellow. Whose word is taken?
cards.source: فالقول قول صاحب الثوب مع يمينه
cards.why: The owner knows what she gave permission for, so her word is taken with an oath.

cards.title: "You did it for free"
cards.ar: وإذا قال صاحب الثوب: عملته لي بغير أجرة وقال الصانع: بأجرة فالقول قول صاحب الثوب مع يمينه عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: If the owner says "You did it for me without a wage" and the craftsman says "for a wage", the owner's word is taken with his oath, according to Abu Hanifa.

cards.title: The other views
cards.ar: أبو يوسف: إن كان حريفا له فله الأجرة وإن لم يكن حريفا له فلا أجرة له وقال محمد: إن كان الصانع معروفا بهذه الصنعة أن يعمل بالأجرة فالقول قوله أنه عمله بأجرة
cards.en: Note: Abu Yusuf says if the craftsman is his regular (someone he usually deals with), he gets a wage; if not, he doesn't. Muhammad says if the craftsman is known for doing this work for pay, his word is taken that it was for a wage.

cards.ask: According to Abu Hanifa: a tailor says Bilal agreed to pay for a shirt; Bilal says it was a favour, for free. Whose word is taken?
options: The tailor's: tailors work for pay
The tailor's, if he swears first
cards.source: فالقول قول صاحب الثوب مع يمينه عند أبي حنيفة
cards.why: For Abu Hanifa, the owner's word is taken with his oath.

cards.ask: A dyer has finished dyeing Hind's curtains, and she has not paid. He refuses to hand them over until she does. Is he allowed?
options: Yes: his work left a mark on them
No: he must hand them over and claim later
Only if the contract said so
cards.source: وكل صانع لعمله أثر في العين كالقصار والصباغ فله أن يحبس العين بعد الفراغ من عمله حتى يستوفي الأجرة
cards.why: A dyer's work shows in the item, so he may hold it until he is paid.

lessons.title: Spoiled hire, ruin, death and excuses

cards.title: A spoiled hire
cards.ar: والواجب في الأجارة الفاسدة أجر المثل لا يتجاوز به المسمى
cards.en: In a fasid (spoiled) hire, what is owed is the usual wage, but not more than the amount that was named.

cards.ask: A hire turns out fasid. The named rent was £100; the usual rent for such a place is £120. What is owed?
cards.source: والواجب في الأجارة الفاسدة أجر المثل لا يتجاوز به المسمى
cards.why: The usual wage is owed, but capped at what was named, so £100.

cards.title: Received but not used
cards.ar: وإذا قبض المستأجر الدار فعليه الأجرة وإن لم يسكنها فإن غصبها غاصب من يده سقطت الأجرة
cards.en: Once the tenant has received the house, he owes the rent even if he doesn't live in it. If someone seizes it from him by force, the rent drops. If he finds a defect that harms living there, he may cancel.

cards.ask: Daud gets the keys to a rented house but never moves in. Does he owe the rent?
cards.source: فعليه الأجرة وإن لم يسكنها
cards.why: Receiving the house is enough; whether he uses it is up to him.

cards.title: When the benefit is lost
cards.ar: وإذا خربت الدار أو انقطع شرب الضيعة أو انقطع الماء عن الرحى انفسخت الإجارة
cards.en: If the house falls into ruin, or a farm's water supply is cut off, or the water stops reaching a water mill, the hire ends by itself.

cards.title: When one of them dies
cards.ar: وإذا مات أحد المتعاقدين وقد عقد الإجارة لنفسه انفسخت الإجارة وإن عقدها لغيره لم تنفسخ ويصح شرط الخيار في الإجارة
cards.en: If either party dies, having made the hire for himself, it ends. If he made it on behalf of someone else (as an agent), it does not end. A khiyar (an option to cancel) may be set as a condition in a hire.

cards.ask: Yaqub rents his own shop to Nabil for two years. After six months Yaqub dies. What happens to the hire?
options: It continues until the two years are up
cards.source: وإذا مات أحد المتعاقدين وقد عقد الإجارة لنفسه انفسخت الإجارة
cards.why: He made the hire for himself, so his death ends it.

cards.title: Ended by an excuse
cards.ar: وتنفسخ الإجارة بالأعذار كمن استأجر دكانا في السوق ليتجر فيه فذهب ماله وكمن آجر دارا أو دكانا ثم أفلس ولزمته ديون لا يقدر على قضائها إلا من ثمن ما آجر فسخ القاضي العقد وباعها في الدين
cards.en: Hire ends because of real excuses ('udhr): someone rents a shop to trade in and loses his money; or someone rents out his house or shop, then goes bankrupt with debts he can only pay from its price, so the judge cancels the hire and sells it for the debt.

cards.title: Changing your mind about a journey
cards.ar: وكمن استأجر دابة ليسافر عليها ثم بدا له من السفر فهو عذر وإن بدا للمكاري من السفر فليس ذلك بعذر
cards.en: If someone hires an animal to travel and then decides not to go, that is an excuse. But if the mukari (the man who rents out the animal) decides not to travel, that is not an excuse.

cards.ask: Rahim rents a water mill for a year. After two months, the river that drives it dries up. What happens?
options: He must pay the full year
He must wait for the water to return
cards.source: أو انقطع الماء عن الرحى انفسخت الإجارة
cards.why: With the water gone, the mill's benefit is gone, and the hire ends.

cards.ask: Does the hire end (or may it be ended)?
items: The renter decides not to make the trip
The animal's owner decides he won't travel
The shop's renter loses all his money
The tenant has the keys but never moves in
source: ثم بدا له من السفر فهو عذر
وإن بدا للمكاري من السفر فليس ذلك بعذر
ليتجر فيه فذهب ماله
وإذا خربت الدار
فعليه الأجرة وإن لم يسكنها
cards.why: The renter's change of plan, losing his money and a ruined house end it. The animal owner's change of mind is no excuse, and an unused house still costs rent.

lessons.title: Who has the right of pre-emption

cards.title: Three people, in order
cards.ar: ثم للخليط في حق المبيع كالشرب والطريق ثم للجار وليس للشريك في الطريق والشرب والجار شفعة مع الخليط
cards.en: Shuf'a (pre-emption) is the right to take a sold property from the buyer for the same price. First comes the co-owner of the property itself. Next, a partner in its rights, like a shared water channel (shirb) or a private lane. Last, the neighbour (jar). While a co-owner wants it, the others get nothing.

cards.ask: Put the people with a right of pre-emption in order, first to last.
steps: A co-owner of the property itself
A partner in its rights, like a shared water channel or lane
cards.source: ثم للخليط في حق المبيع كالشرب والطريق ثم للجار
cards.why: The co-owner comes first, then the partner in the property's rights, then the neighbour.

cards.ask: Hasan and Ali own a house together. Ali sells his half to a stranger. Zaid, who shares their private lane, and Umar, the next-door neighbour, also want it. Who has the right to take it?
cards.source: وليس للشريك في الطريق والشرب والجار شفعة مع الخليط
cards.why: While there is a co-owner, the lane partner and the neighbour have no pre-emption. Hasan comes first.

cards.title: If the first gives it up
cards.ar: فإن سلم فالشفعة للشريك في الطريق فإن سلم أخذها الجار
cards.en: If the co-owner gives up his right, it passes to the partner in the lane. If he gives it up too, the neighbour may take it.

cards.ask: In the same street, Hasan the co-owner says, "I don't want it." Who may now take the house?
cards.source: فإن سلم فالشفعة للشريك في الطريق
cards.why: When the co-owner gives it up, the right passes to the partner in the lane. Only if he also gives it up does the neighbour get it.

cards.title: Claim it at once, with witnesses
cards.ar: وإذا علم الشفيع بالبيع أشهد في مجلسه ذلك على المطالبة ثم ينهض منه فيشهد على البائع إن كان المبيع في يده أو على المبتاع أو عند العقار
cards.en: The shafi' is the person with the right. As soon as he hears of the sale, he must say in front of witnesses, in that same sitting, that he claims it. Then he gets up and calls witnesses again, in front of the seller (if he still has the property), the buyer, or at the property itself.

cards.ask: Put the steps of a pre-emption claim in order.
steps: He hears of it and claims it before witnesses in that sitting
He calls witnesses again before the seller, the buyer or at the property
He takes it when the buyer hands it over or a judge rules
source: والشفعة تجب بعقد البيع وتستقر بالإشهاد وتملك بالأخذ إذا سلمها المشتري أو حكم بها حاكم
أشهد في مجلسه ذلك على المطالبة ثم ينهض منه فيشهد على البائع
cards.why: The right comes with the sale, is made firm by the witnessing, and becomes ownership when he takes the property, by the buyer's handing it over or a judge's ruling.

cards.title: After that, waiting does not spoil it
cards.ar: فإذا فعل ذلك استقرت شفعته ولم تسقط بالتأخير عند أبي حنيفة وقال محمد: إن تركها شهرا بعد الإشهاد بطلت شفعته
cards.en: Once he has done this, his right is firm, and for Abu Hanifa delay does not end it. Note: Muhammad said that if he leaves it for a month after the witnessing, it ends.

cards.title: Only land and buildings
cards.ar: والشفعة واجبة في العقار وإن كان مما لا يقسم ولا شفعة في العروض والسفن والمسلم والذمي في الشفعة سواء
cards.en: Pre-emption is only in real property ('aqar): land and buildings, even ones too small to divide. There is none in goods or ships. A Muslim and a dhimmi (a non-Muslim citizen of the Muslim state) have the same right.

cards.ask: Is there pre-emption?
items: A small shop too small to divide
A ship sold at the harbour
source: وإذا ملك العقار بعوض هو مال وجبت فيه الشفعة
وإن كان مما لا يقسم
ولا شفعة في العروض والسفن
cards.why: Pre-emption comes when real property is sold for money, even if it cannot be divided. A ship is not real property.

cards.ask: Yusuf, a Christian citizen of the Muslim state, is the only neighbour of a house that is sold to a Muslim. Does Yusuf have the right of pre-emption?
options: Yes, he has it like a Muslim
No: only Muslims have this right
Only if the buyer agrees to it
cards.source: والمسلم والذمي في الشفعة سواء
cards.why: A Muslim and a dhimmi are the same in pre-emption, so Yusuf has the neighbour's right.

cards.ask: A house changes hands this way. Is there pre-emption?
items: A house given as a bride's mahr
A house handed over as the rent for another house
A house handed over in a settlement where the claim was admitted
source: ولا شفعة في الدار التي يتزوج
أو يستأجر بها دارا
فإن صالح عنها بإقرار وجبت فيها الشفعة
cards.why: A house used as mahr (the gift a husband must give his bride) or as rent is not sold for money, so there is no pre-emption. A settlement on an admitted claim counts as a sale.

cards.ask: Which are true of who has pre-emption?

options.text: The co-owner comes before the neighbour
The right is made firm by calling witnesses
There is pre-emption in a ship
A house given as mahr can be taken by pre-emption
Pre-emption can be in land that cannot be divided

source: ثم للجار وليس للشريك في الطريق والشرب والجار شفعة مع الخليط
وتستقر بالإشهاد
ولا شفعة في العروض والسفن
وإن كان مما لا يقسم
cards.why: The co-owner comes first, witnessing makes the right firm, and it applies to land even when it cannot be divided. Ships and a house given as mahr are not included.

lessons.title: Claiming before the judge, and losing the right

cards.title: The judge checks his ownership first
cards.ar: وإذا تقدم الشفيع إلى القاضي فادعى الشراء وطلب الشفعة سأل القاضي المدعى عليه فإن اعترف بملكه الذي يشفع به وإلا كلفه إقامة البينة
cards.en: When the shafi' (the one with the right) brings his claim, the judge first asks the buyer whether he accepts that the claimant owns the property that gives him the right, like the house next door. If not, the claimant must bring bayyina: proof by witnesses. If he cannot, the buyer swears he does not know it.

cards.ask: Put the steps in court in order.
steps: The judge asks whether the claimant owns the property that gives him the right
The judge asks the buyer whether he really bought it
The judge rules for the claimant
The claimant must bring the price
source: سأل القاضي المدعى عليه فإن اعترف بملكه الذي يشفع به
فإن نكل أو قامت بينه سأله القاضي: هل ابتاع أم لا؟
فإذا قضى القاضي له بالشفعة لزمه إحضار الثمن
cards.why: First his ownership is settled, then the purchase. Only after the judge rules must he bring the price.

cards.title: The money comes after the ruling
cards.ar: وتجوز المنازعة في الشفعة وإن لم يحضر الشفيع الثمن إلى مجلس القاضي فإذا قضى القاضي له بالشفعة لزمه إحضار الثمن وللشفيع أن يرد الدار بخيار العيب والرؤية
cards.en: He may argue his claim even if he has not brought the price to court. Once the judge rules for him, he must bring it. Like a buyer, he may return the house for a defect, or because he had not seen it.

cards.ask: Khalid goes to court to claim a house by pre-emption, but he has not brought the 3000 dirhams with him. Will the judge hear his claim?
options: Yes: he pays after the ruling
No: he must bring the money first
Only if he brings half of it
cards.source: وتجوز المنازعة في الشفعة وإن لم يحضر الشفيع الثمن إلى مجلس القاضي
cards.why: The claim may be argued without the price in court. Once the judge rules for him, he must pay.

cards.title: When the seller still holds it
cards.ar: فإن أحضر الشفيع البائع والمبيع في يده فله أن يخاصمه في الشفعة ولا يسمع القاضي البينة حتى يحضر المشتري فيفسخ البيع بمشهد منه ويقضي بالشفعة على البائع ويجعل العهدة عليه
cards.en: If the seller still has the property, the shafi' may bring his case against him. But the judge will not hear the witnesses until the buyer is there too. Then he cancels the sale in front of him and gives the property to the shafi' from the seller, who becomes responsible to him for it.

cards.ask: The seller still lives in the house he sold. The shafi' brings him to court, but the buyer is abroad. Will the judge hear the witnesses now?
options: No: not until the buyer is present
Yes: the seller holds the house
Yes, and the buyer loses his money
cards.source: ولا يسمع القاضي البينة حتى يحضر المشتري
cards.why: The judge waits for the buyer, because the sale to him must be cancelled in front of him.

cards.title: How the right is lost
cards.ar: وإذا ترك الشفيع الإشهاد حين علم وهو يقدر على ذلك بطلت شفعته وكذلك إن أشهد في المجلس ولم يشهد على أحد المتبايعين ولا عند العقار
cards.en: If he hears of the sale and does not call witnesses, though he could, his right is lost. It is also lost if he calls witnesses in the sitting but never does the second witnessing before the seller, the buyer or at the property.

cards.ask: Salim hears at dinner that his neighbour's house was sold. People are around who could act as witnesses, but he says nothing and goes home. A week later he claims it. Has he still got the right?
options: No: he did not call witnesses when he could
Yes, if he pays more than the buyer
cards.source: وإذا ترك الشفيع الإشهاد حين علم وهو يقدر على ذلك بطلت شفعته
cards.why: He knew and could call witnesses but did not, so his right was lost.

cards.ask: The buyer pays Salim 1000 dirhams to drop his claim, and Salim agrees. What happens?
options: His right ends and he must give the 1000 back
His right ends and he keeps the 1000
The deal is binding and his right stays
cards.source: وإن صالح من شفعته على عوض أخذه بطلت شفعته ويرد العوض
cards.why: Selling the right for money ends the right, and the money must be returned.

cards.title: Death, and selling his own house
cards.ar: وإذا مات الشفيع بطلت شفعته وإن مات المشتري لم تسقط وإن باع الشفيع ما يشفع به قبل أن يقضى له بالشفعة بطلت شفعته
cards.en: If the shafi' dies, the right ends. If the buyer dies, it does not. If the shafi' sells the property that gave him the right before the judge rules, the right ends.

cards.ask: Does he still have the right?
items: He sells his own house before the ruling
source: وإذا مات الشفيع بطلت شفعته
وإن مات المشتري لم تسقط
وإن باع الشفيع ما يشفع به قبل أن يقضى له بالشفعة بطلت شفعته
cards.why: The buyer's death does not end it. The shafi's death ends it, and so does selling the house that gave him the right.

cards.title: When the shafi' was an agent
cards.ar: ووكيل البائع إذا باع وكان هو الشفيع فلا شفعة له وكذلك إن ضمن الدرك عن البائع الشفيع ووكيل المشتري إذا ابتاع فله الشفعة
cards.en: A wakil is an agent who buys or sells for someone else. If the shafi' was the seller's agent who made the sale, he has no right. The same if he guaranteed the sale for the seller. If he was the buyer's agent who made the purchase, he keeps his right.

cards.ask: Does the shafi' have the right?
items: He was the seller's agent who made the sale
He guaranteed the sale for the seller
He was the buyer's agent who made the purchase
source: ووكيل البائع إذا باع وكان هو الشفيع فلا شفعة له وكذلك إن ضمن الدرك عن البائع
ووكيل المشتري إذا ابتاع فله الشفعة
cards.why: Selling for the seller, or guaranteeing the sale for him, means he cannot then take it back. The buyer's agent keeps his right.

cards.ask: Fahd sells his house with an option for himself to cancel within three days. The neighbour claims pre-emption on day one. Does he get it?
options: Not yet: only if Fahd drops his option
Never, even after the option ends
source: ومن باع بشرط الخيار فلا شفعة للشفيع فإن أسقط الخيار وجبت الشفعة
ومن اشترى بشرط الخيار وجبت الشفعة
cards.why: While the seller keeps an option, there is no pre-emption. Once he drops it, the right comes. Note: if only the buyer has the option, the right comes at once.

lessons.title: Which price the shafi' pays
lessons.arabic: وإذا اختلف الشفيع والمشتري في الثمن

cards.title: A broken sale
cards.ar: ومن ابتاع دارا شراء فاسدا فلا شفعة لها ولكل واحد من المتعاقدين الفسخ فإن سقط الفسخ وجبت الشفعة
cards.en: A fasid sale is a defective one that should be undone. While either side can still cancel it, there is no pre-emption. Once that right to cancel is gone, pre-emption comes.

cards.title: A sale between dhimmis for wine
cards.ar: وإذا اشترى ذمي دارا بخمر أو خنزير وشفيعها ذمي أخذها بمثل الخمر وقيمة الخنزير
cards.en: Dhimmis may trade in wine and pigs among themselves. If a dhimmi buys a house with wine and the shafi' is a dhimmi, he pays the same amount of wine (or the value of the pig). If the shafi' is a Muslim, he pays the value of the wine and the pig in money.

cards.ask: A dhimmi buys a house for ten jars of wine. Its shafi' is a Muslim neighbour. What does he pay?
options: The value of the ten jars of wine
cards.source: وإن كان شفيعها مسلما أخذها
cards.why: A Muslim cannot pay with wine, so he pays its value.

cards.title: Gifts, and arguing over the price
cards.ar: ولا شفعة في الهبة إلا أن تكون بعوض مشروط وإذا اختلف الشفيع والمشتري في الثمن فالقول قول المشتري فإن أقاما البينة فالبينة بينة الشفيع عند أبي حنيفة ومحمد
cards.en: A gift (hiba) brings no pre-emption, unless something was agreed in return. If the shafi' and the buyer disagree about the price, the buyer's word is taken. If both bring witnesses, the shafi's witnesses win, for Abu Hanifa and Muhammad.

cards.ask: The buyer says he paid 1200. The shafi' says it was 1000. Neither has witnesses. Whose word is taken?
cards.source: وإذا اختلف الشفيع والمشتري في الثمن فالقول قول المشتري
cards.why: When they disagree about the price without proof, the buyer's word is accepted.

cards.ask: The seller says the price was 900, and the buyer says 1000. The seller has not been paid yet. What does the shafi' pay?
source: وإذا ادعى المشتري ثمنا أكثر وادعى البائع أقل منه ولم يقبض الثمن أخذها الشفيع بما قال البائع وكان ذلك حطا عن المشتري
وإن كان قبض الثمن بما قال المشتري ولم يلتفت إلى قول البائع
cards.why: Before he is paid, the seller's lower figure counts, as if he had lowered the price. Had he already been paid, the buyer's figure would count.

cards.title: When the price changes
cards.ar: وإذا حط البائع عن المشتري بعض الثمن سقط ذلك عن الشفيع وإن حط جميع الثمن لم يسقط عن الشفيع وإذا زاد المشتري البائع في الثمن لم تلزم الزيادة الشفيع
cards.en: If the seller lets the buyer off part of the price, the shafi' is let off it too. If he lets him off all of it, the shafi' still pays the full price. If the buyer adds to the price, the shafi' does not pay the extra.

cards.ask: A house sells for 1000. Later the seller, out of kindness, lets the buyer off the whole price. What does the shafi' pay?
cards.source: وإن حط جميع الثمن لم يسقط عن الشفيع
cards.why: Letting off the whole price does not reach the shafi'. He pays the 1000.

cards.title: Several claimants, and paying in goods
cards.ar: وإذا جمع الشفعاء فالشفعة بينهم على عدد رؤوسهم ولا يعتبر اختلاف الأملاك ومن اشترى دارا بعرض أخذها الشفيع بقيمته وإن اشتراها بمكيل أو موزون أخذها بمثله
cards.en: When several people have the same right, they share it by heads, however different their shares are. If the house was bought with goods, the shafi' pays their value. If with something measured or weighed, like wheat, he pays the same amount of it.

cards.ask: A house has three owners. Amir owns half, Nadia a sixth, and the third owner sells his third. Amir and Nadia both claim it. How is it shared?
options: Three to one, by their shares
cards.source: وإذا جمع الشفعاء فالشفعة بينهم على عدد رؤوسهم ولا يعتبر اختلاف الأملاك
cards.why: Pre-emption is shared by heads. The size of each owner's share does not count.

cards.ask: Rami buys a house for 100 sacks of wheat. What does the shafi' pay?
options: The value of the wheat in silver
cards.source: وإن اشتراها بمكيل أو موزون أخذها بمثله
cards.why: Wheat is measured, so the shafi' pays the same amount of it.

cards.ask: Which are true of the price in pre-emption?

options.text: A gift with nothing in return brings no pre-emption
A raise in the price after the sale binds the shafi'
Several shafi's share by heads
A house bought with a horse is taken for the horse's value
A fasid sale brings pre-emption while it can still be cancelled

source: ولا شفعة في الهبة
لم تلزم الزيادة الشفيع
فالشفعة بينهم على عدد رؤوسهم
أخذها الشفيع بقيمته
فإن سقط الفسخ وجبت الشفعة
cards.why: A plain gift brings no pre-emption, claimants share by heads, and goods are paid by value. A later raise does not bind the shafi', and a fasid sale brings the right only once it can no longer be cancelled.

lessons.title: Tricky cases of pre-emption
lessons.arabic: وإذا بلغ الشفيع أنها بيعت بألف

cards.title: Giving it up on wrong news
cards.ar: وإذا بلغ الشفيع أنها بيعت بألف فسلم ثم علم أنها بيعت بأقل أو بحنطة أو شعير قيمتها ألف أو أكثر فتسليمه باطل وله الشفعة وإن بان أنها بيعت بدنانير قيمتها ألف فلا شفعة له
cards.en: If he is told it sold for 1000 and gives up his right, then learns it was cheaper, or sold for wheat or barley worth 1000 or more, his giving up does not count and he keeps the right. If it turns out it sold for gold dinars worth 1000, he has no right.

cards.ask: He gave up his right after hearing "It sold for 1000 dirhams". Then he learns the truth. Does he still have the right?
items: It sold for gold dinars worth 1000
The buyer was not the man he was told
source: فتسليمه باطل وله الشفعة
وإن بان أنها بيعت بدنانير قيمتها ألف فلا شفعة له
ثم علم أنه غيره فله الشفعة
cards.why: A lower price, wheat or barley, or a different buyer makes his giving up void. Dinars worth the same 1000 do not.

cards.title: Agents, and keeping a strip
cards.ar: ومن اشترى دارا لغيره فهو الخصم في الشفعة إلا أن يسلمها إلى الموكل وإذا باع دارا إلا مقدار ذراع في طول الحد يلي الشفيع فلا شفعة له
cards.en: If an agent bought the house for someone else, the shafi' brings his case against the agent until he hands it to the person he bought it for. If the seller keeps back a strip one cubit wide along the side next to the neighbour, the neighbour is no longer next to what was sold, so he has no right.

cards.ask: Tariq buys a small share of a house for a price, and a month later buys the rest. The neighbour claims pre-emption. Which part may he take?
cards.source: منها سهما بثمن ثم ابتاع بقيتها فالشفعة للجار في السهم الأول دون الثاني
cards.why: The neighbour has the right in the first share only. For the second sale, Tariq was already a co-owner, so he comes before the neighbour.

cards.ask: Nabil buys a house for 1000 dirhams, then gives the seller a cloth instead of the money. What does the shafi' pay?
cards.source: وإذا ابتاعها بثمن ثم دفع إليه ثوبا عنه فالشفعة بالثمن دون الثوب
cards.why: The shafi' pays the price of the sale, not what was later given in its place.

cards.title: Tricks to avoid pre-emption
cards.ar: ولا تكره الحيلة في إسقاط الشفعة عند أبي يوسف وقال محمد رحمه الله تكره
cards.en: A hila is a legal trick, such as keeping back that one-cubit strip. Note: Abu Yusuf said a trick to avoid pre-emption is not disliked, and Muhammad said it is disliked.

cards.title: If the buyer has built on it
cards.ar: وإذا بنى المشتري أو غرس ثم قضي للشفيع بالشفعة فهو بالخيار: إن شاء أخذها بالثمن
cards.en: If the buyer has built or planted on it before the judge rules for the shafi', the shafi' chooses. He may take it for the price plus the value of the building or trees as if pulled down. Or he may make the buyer pull them down.

cards.ask: The buyer builds a garage on the land. Then the judge gives the land to the shafi'. What may the shafi' do?
options: Pay for it as rubble, or have it removed
He must take the garage at its full value
His right is lost because the land changed
source: مقلوعا وإن شاء كلف المشتري قلعه
وإذا أخذها الشفيع فبنى أو غرس ثم استحقت رجع بالثمن
cards.why: He chooses between paying for the building at its pulled-down value and having the buyer pull it down. Note: if the shafi' builds and the land then proves to be someone else's, he gets the price back but not the building's cost.

cards.title: Damage before he takes it
cards.ar: وإذا انهدمت الدار أو احترق بناؤها أو جف شجر البستان بغير فعل أحد فالشفيع بالخيار: إن شاء أخذها بجميع الثمن وإن شاء ترك
cards.en: If the house falls down, burns, or the orchard dries up, with no one to blame, the shafi' may take it for the full price or leave it. If the buyer pulls the building down himself, the shafi' may take the bare land ('arsa) for its share of the price, but not the rubble.

cards.ask: Before the shafi' takes the house, lightning burns its building down. What can he do?
options: Take it for the full price, or leave it
Take the land only, for part of the price
Make the buyer rebuild it at his own cost
source: بغير فعل أحد فالشفيع بالخيار: إن شاء أخذها بجميع الثمن وإن شاء ترك
وإن نقض المشتري البناء قيل للشفيع: إن شئت فخذ العرصة بحصتها وإن شئت فدع وليس له أن يأخذ النقض
cards.why: When no one caused the damage, he takes it for the whole price or leaves it.

cards.title: Price paid later
cards.ar: وإذا ابتاع بثمن مؤجل فالشفيع بالخيار: إن شاء أخذها بثمن حال وإن شاء صبر حتى ينقضي الأجل ثم يأخذها
cards.en: If the buyer bought with the price due later, the shafi' chooses: take it now and pay now, or wait until the due date and take it then.

cards.ask: Which are true of cases of pre-emption?

options.text: Land sold with dates on its palms is taken with the dates
The shafi' who never saw the house may return it after seeing it
When partners divide land, their neighbour gets pre-emption
If buyer and seller simply agree to undo the sale, the shafi' still has his right
If the buyer bought on credit, the shafi' must pay at once

source: ومن ابتاع أرضا وعلى نخلها ثمر أخذها الشفيع بثمرها
وإذا قضي للشفيع بالدار ولم يكن رآها فله خيار الرؤية
وإذا قسم الشركاء العقار فلا شفعة لجارهم بالقسمة
وإن ردها بغير قضاء أو تقاتلا فللشفيع الشفعة
وإن شاء صبر حتى ينقضي الأجل ثم يأخذها
cards.why: The dates go with the land, he has the option of seeing, and undoing the sale by agreement keeps his right. Dividing land between partners brings no pre-emption, and with a later price he may wait.

lessons.title: Kinds of partnership, and full partnership

cards.title: Two kinds of partnership
cards.ar: الشركة على ضربين: شركة أملاك وشركة عقود
cards.en: Shirka means partnership. There are two kinds: a partnership of ownership, where people simply own something together, and a partnership of contract, where they agree to work together.

cards.title: Owning something together
cards.ar: فشركة الأملاك: العين يرثها رجلان أو يشتريانها
cards.en: A partnership of ownership is a thing that two people inherit or buy together. Neither may deal with the other's share without his permission: in his partner's share, each is like a stranger.

cards.ask: Two brothers inherit their father's car. One sells the whole car without asking the other. Was he allowed to sell his brother's half?
options: No, he needed his brother's permission
Yes: brothers act for each other
Yes, if he gives his brother half the money
cards.source: إلا بإذنه وكل واحد منهما في نصيب صاحبه كالأجنبي
cards.why: Without his brother's permission he may not deal with his brother's half. In that share he is like a stranger.

cards.title: Four contract partnerships
cards.ar: والضرب الثاني: شركة العقود وهي على أربعة أوجه: مفاوضة وعنان وشركة الصنائع وشركة الوجوه
cards.en: Contract partnerships come in four kinds: mufawada (full, equal partnership), 'inan (limited partnership), partnership in crafts (sana'i), and partnership on reputation (wujuh), where partners buy on credit using their good name.

cards.ask: How many kinds of contract partnership are there?
cards.source: شركة العقود وهي على أربعة أوجه
cards.why: Four: mufawada, inan, partnership in crafts, and partnership on reputation.

cards.ask: Which are among the four contract partnerships?

options.text: Mufawada, the full partnership
'Inan, the limited partnership
Partnership in crafts
Partnership on reputation
Two brothers inheriting a house
Partnership in hunting

source: وهي على أربعة أوجه: مفاوضة وعنان وشركة الصنائع وشركة الوجوه
ولا تجوز الشركة في الاحتطاب والاحتشاش والاصطياد
cards.why: The four are mufawada, 'inan, crafts and reputation. Inheriting is a partnership of ownership, and hunting together is not a valid partnership at all.

cards.title: The full partnership
cards.ar: فيستويان في مالهما وتصرفهما ودينهما فتجوز بين الحرين المسلمين العاقلين البالغين
cards.en: In a mufawada, the two partners are equal in their wealth, in what they may do, and in their religion. So it is allowed between two free, sane, adult Muslims. It is made up of agency (wakala: each acts for the other) and surety (kafala: each stands behind the other's debts).

cards.ask: Can these two make a mufawada?
items: A free man and a slave, in al-Quduri's time
source: فتجوز بين الحرين المسلمين العاقلين البالغين ولا تجوز بين الحر والمملوك ولا بين الصبي والبالغ ولا بين المسلم والكافر وتنعقد على الوكالة والكفالة
cards.why: A mufawada needs the partners to be equal, so it is only between free, sane, adult Muslims.

cards.title: What is shared, and what ends it
cards.ar: وما يشتريه كل واحد منهما يكون على الشركة إلا طعام أهله وكسوتهم
cards.en: Whatever either partner buys belongs to the partnership, except food and clothes for his family. Each also stands behind the other's business debts. If one of them inherits or is given money of a kind partnerships are made with, and it reaches his hand, the mufawada ends and becomes an 'inan.

cards.ask: Umar and Saad are in a mufawada. Umar inherits 5000 dirhams from his uncle and receives them. What happens to the partnership?
options: Nothing: the money joins the partnership
source: فإن ورث أحدهما مالا تصح فيه الشركة أو وهب له ووصل إلى يده بطلت المفاوضة وصارت الشركة عنانا
وما يلزم كل واحد منهما من الديون بدلا عما يصح فيه الاشتراك فالآخر ضامن له
cards.why: Now they are no longer equal in wealth, so the mufawada ends and the partnership becomes an 'inan.

cards.title: What the capital must be
cards.ar: ولا تنعقد الشركة إلا بالدراهم والدنانير والفلوس النافقة
cards.en: A partnership can only be made with dirhams (silver coins), dinars (gold coins) and fulus (copper coins) that are in use. Nothing else, unless people trade with it like money, such as unminted gold or silver.

cards.ask: Rashid has a shop full of cloth and Majid a store of rice. They want to start a partnership with these goods. What does al-Quduri say they do?
options: Each sells half his goods for half of the other's
They just add up what the cloth and rice are worth
They cannot: goods can never be shared at all
source: وإذا أرادا الشركة بالعروض باع كل واحد منهما نصف ماله بنصف مال الآخر ثم عقدا الشركة
ولا يجوز بما سوى ذلك إلا أن يتعامل الناس بها كالتبر والنقرة فتصح الشركة بهما
cards.why: Goods cannot be the capital, so each first sells half of his goods for half of the other's. Then they own everything together and make the partnership.

cards.ask: Which are true of the kinds of partnership?

options.text: A full partner's purchases belong to the partnership, except his family's food and clothes
Fulus in use can be partnership capital
A mufawada is allowed between a boy and an adult
In an inherited house, each brother may sell the other's share
There are four kinds of contract partnership

source: إلا طعام أهله وكسوتهم
والفلوس النافقة
ولا بين الصبي والبالغ
كالأجنبي
وهي على أربعة أوجه
cards.why: Purchases go to the partnership except the family's needs, fulus in use are valid capital, and there are four contract kinds. A boy and an adult are not equal, and a co-heir is a stranger in the other's share.

cards.title: Agency, but not surety
cards.ar: وأما الشركة العنان: فتنعقد على الوكالة دون الكفالة ويصح التفاضل في المال ويصح أن يتساويا في المال ويتفاضلا في الربح
cards.en: An 'inan partnership is made up of agency only: each partner acts for the other, but does not stand behind his debts. The partners may put in different amounts, and may put in the same amount but agree on different shares of the profit.

cards.ask: Adam puts 6000 dirhams into an 'inan, and Bilal 4000. They agree to split the profit half and half. Is that allowed?
options: Yes: the profit may be set apart from the money
No: profit must follow the money
cards.source: ويصح التفاضل في المال ويصح أن يتساويا في المال ويتفاضلا في الربح
cards.why: In an 'inan the money may differ, and the profit shares may be set apart from the money.

cards.title: Part of their money, any currency
cards.ar: ويجوز أن يعقدها كل واحد منهما ببعض ماله دون بعض ولا تصح إلا بما بينا أن المفاوضة تصح به ويجوز أن يشتركا ومن جهة أحدهما دراهم ومن جهة الآخر دنانير
cards.en: Each partner may put in only part of his money. The capital must be what a mufawada is made with: dirhams, dinars or fulus in use. One may bring dirhams and the other dinars.

cards.title: Who pays the seller
cards.ar: وما اشتراه كل واحد منهما للشركة طولب بثمنه دون الآخر ثم يرجع على شريكه بحصته منه
cards.en: When one partner buys something for the partnership, the seller asks only him for the price. Then he claims his partner's share of it from his partner.

cards.ask: In an 'inan, Zaid buys stock for the partnership for 2000. The seller goes to Zaid's partner Hamid for the money. Must Hamid pay the seller?
options: No, only Zaid; he then claims Hamid's share
Yes: both partners owe the seller together
cards.source: وما اشتراه كل واحد منهما للشركة طولب بثمنه دون الآخر
cards.why: An 'inan has agency but no surety. Only the partner who bought is asked for the price. He then claims his partner's share.

cards.title: If the money is lost
cards.ar: وإذا هلك مال الشركة أو أحد المالين قبل أن يشتريا شيئا بطلت الشركة وإن اشترى أحدهما بماله وهلك مال الآخر قبل الشراء فالمشترى بينهما على ما شرطا ويرجع على شريكه بحصته من ثمنه
cards.en: If the partnership money, or one partner's money, is lost before they buy anything, the partnership ends. But if one has already bought with his money and then the other's money is lost, what he bought is shared as agreed, and he claims his partner's share of the price.

cards.ask: Adam and Bilal agree an 'inan. Before they buy anything, Bilal's money is stolen. What happens?
options: Adam must share his money with Bilal
cards.source: وإذا هلك مال الشركة أو أحد المالين قبل أن يشتريا شيئا بطلت الشركة
cards.why: One partner's money was lost before any purchase, so the partnership ends.

cards.ask: This time Adam has already bought goods with his 6000. Then Bilal's money is stolen. Who owns the goods?
options: Both, as agreed; Adam claims Bilal's share
Adam alone, since he paid with his own money
cards.source: فالمشترى بينهما على ما شرطا ويرجع على شريكه بحصته من ثمنه
cards.why: The purchase was made for the partnership before the loss, so it is shared as agreed. Adam claims Bilal's share of what he paid.

cards.title: No need to mix, no fixed sums
cards.ar: وتجوز الشركة وإن لم يخلطا المالين ولا تصح الشركة إذا شرطا لأحدهما
cards.en: The partners do not need to mix their money together. But the partnership is not valid if one of them is promised a fixed number of dirhams from the profit (for example, "the first 100 dirhams are mine").

cards.ask: Complete al-Quduri's words.
cards.ar: وتجوز الشركة وإن لم ____ المالين
cards.source: وتجوز الشركة وإن لم يخلطا المالين
cards.why: يخلطا: the partnership is valid even if they have not mixed their money.

cards.title: What a partner may do
cards.ar: ولكل واحد من المتفاوضين وشريكي العنان أن يبضع المال ويدفعه مضاربة ويوكل من يتصرف فيه ويده في المال يد أمانة
cards.en: A partner in either kind may hand money to someone to trade for free (ibda'), give it out in mudaraba (profit-sharing), or appoint an agent to deal with it. The money is a trust (amana) in his hand: he does not pay for it if it is lost without his fault.

cards.ask: Which of these are true of an 'inan?

options.text: Each partner stands behind the other's debts
One partner may bring dirhams and the other dinars
They may agree "the first 100 dirhams of profit are mine"
A partner may appoint an agent to deal with the money
The money is a trust in each partner's hand

source: فتنعقد على الوكالة دون الكفالة
ومن جهة أحدهما دراهم ومن جهة الآخر دنانير
ولا تصح الشركة إذا شرطا لأحدهما
ويوكل من يتصرف فيه ويده في المال يد أمانة
cards.why: An 'inan has agency but no surety, and a fixed sum from the profit makes it invalid. Mixed currencies, appointing agents and holding the money as a trust are all fine.

lessons.title: Partnerships in work, and when they fail

cards.title: Partners in a craft
cards.ar: وأما شركة الصنائع فالخياطان والصباغان يشتركان على أن يتقبلا الأعمال
cards.en: In a crafts partnership, two tailors or two dyers agree to take on jobs and share what they earn. This is allowed. A job either of them takes on binds him and his partner.

cards.ask: Two tailors are partners. This month only Musa did any sewing, while Isa was ill. They earned 400. How is it split?
source: فإن عمل أحدهما دون الآخر فالكسب بينهما نصفان
وما يتقبله كل واحد منهما من العمل يلزمه ويلزم شريكه
cards.why: If one works and the other does not, the earnings are still half and half.

cards.title: Partners on reputation
cards.ar: وأما شركة الوجوه: فالرجلان يشتركان ولا مال لهما على أن يشتريا بوجوههما ويبيعا فتصح الشركة على هذا وكل واحد منهما وكيل الآخر فيما يشتريه
cards.en: In a wujuh partnership, two people with no money agree to buy on credit, trusting in their good name, and then sell. This is valid, and each is the other's agent in what he buys.

cards.ask: Two traders with no money buy on credit together. They agree the goods are theirs half and half, but the profit 70 to 30. Is the profit split allowed?
options: No: the profit must be half and half too
Yes, if the one with 70 does the selling
cards.source: فإن شرطا أن يكون المشتري بينهما نصفين فالربح كذلك ولا يجوز أن يتفاضلا فيه
cards.why: In a wujuh partnership, the profit follows their shares in the goods. Half the goods means half the profit.

cards.title: Gathering and hunting
cards.ar: ولا تجوز الشركة في الاحتطاب والاحتشاش والاصطياد وما اصطاده كل واحد منهما أو احتطبه فهو له دون صاحبه
cards.en: There is no partnership in gathering firewood, cutting grass, or hunting. Whatever each one hunts or gathers is his alone.

cards.ask: Sami and Tariq agree to gather firewood and split it. Sami gathers 30 bundles and Tariq 10. Who owns what?
cards.source: وما اصطاده كل واحد منهما أو احتطبه فهو له دون صاحبه
cards.why: A partnership in gathering is not valid, so each keeps what he gathered.

cards.title: The mule and the waterskin
cards.ar: وإذا اشتركا ولأحدهما بغل وللآخر رواية يستقي عليها الماء والكسب بينهما لم تصح الشركة والكسب كله للذي استقى
cards.en: One man has a mule and the other a big waterskin. They agree to carry water for sale and share the earnings. This is not valid. All the earnings go to whoever carried the water, and he pays a fair rent for the other's mule or skin. In any fasid (invalid) partnership, profit follows the money put in.

cards.ask: The mule owner did all the carrying and earned 90 dirhams. What happens?
options: He keeps it all, and pays rent for the skin
They split the 90 dirhams half and half
The skin owner gets all 90, as his skin carried it
source: والكسب كله للذي استقى وعليه أجر مثل الراوية إن كان صاحب البغل
وكل شركة فاسدة فالربح فيها على قدر المال ويبطل شرط التفاضل
cards.why: The partnership is invalid, so the earnings go to the one who carried the water, and he owes a fair rent for the skin.

cards.title: When a partnership ends, and zakat
cards.ar: وإذا مات أحد الشريكين أو ارتد ولحق بدار الحرب بطلت الشركة وليس لواحد من الشركين أن يؤدي زكاة مال الأخر إلا بإذنه
cards.en: A partnership ends if a partner dies, or leaves Islam and joins the enemy's land (dar al-harb). Zakat is the yearly charity due on wealth. One partner may not pay the other's zakat without his permission.

cards.ask: Partners Ali and Yasir each allow the other to pay his zakat. Ali pays Yasir's zakat, and then Yasir, not knowing, pays Ali's. Who has to make good what he paid?
options: Both of them, each for half
cards.source: فإن أذن كل واحد منهما لصاحبه أن يؤدي زكاته فأدى كل واحد منهما فالثاني ضامن علم بأداء الأول أو لم يعلم
cards.why: When both pay, the second is liable, whether or not he knew the first had paid.

cards.ask: Is the partnership valid?
items: Two people buying on credit on their good name
A mule owner and a waterskin owner carrying water
Two people cutting grass to sell together
source: فالخياطان والصباغان يشتركان على أن يتقبلا الأعمال
فتصح الشركة على هذا
ولا تجوز الشركة في الاحتطاب والاحتشاش والاصطياد
لم تصح الشركة
cards.why: Crafts and reputation partnerships are valid. Hunting, gathering and the mule-and-waterskin deal are not.

cards.ask: Which are true of partnerships in work?

options.text: A job one craftsman takes on binds his partner too
In an invalid partnership, profit follows the money put in
A partnership carries on after one partner dies
A partner may pay the other's zakat without asking
Each wujuh partner is the other's agent

source: يلزمه ويلزم شريكه
فالربح فيها على قدر المال
وإذا مات أحد الشريكين
إلا بإذنه
وكل واحد منهما وكيل الآخر فيما يشتريه
cards.why: A job binds both craftsmen, invalid partnerships split profit by money, and wujuh partners are each other's agents. Death ends a partnership, and zakat needs permission.

cards.title: Money from one, work from the other
cards.ar: المضاربة: عقد على الشركة بمال من أحد الشريكين وعمل من الآخر
cards.en: Mudaraba is a partnership where one side gives the money and the other does the work. The one with the money is the rabb al-mal (owner of the capital). The one who trades with it is the mudarib (the worker).

cards.ask: What is a mudaraba?
options: One side gives the money, the other the work
Both partners put in money and both of them work
The owner lends money and takes a fixed return
cards.source: المضاربة: عقد على الشركة بمال من أحد الشريكين وعمل من الآخر
cards.why: Mudaraba is a partnership with money from one partner and work from the other.

cards.title: A share of the profit, and the money handed over
cards.ar: ومن شرطها: أن يكون الربح بينهما مشاعا لا يستحق أحدهما منه دراهم مسماة ولا بد أن يكون المال مسلما إلى المضارب
cards.en: The capital must be what a partnership is made with: dirhams, dinars or fulus (copper coins) in use. The profit must be shared as a portion (a half, a third...), never a fixed number of dirhams for one side. And the money must be handed over to the worker, with the owner keeping no hold on it.

cards.ask: Hashim gives Nasir 10,000 dirhams to trade with and says, "You get 500 dirhams of whatever profit there is." Is this a valid mudaraba?
options: No: profit must be a portion
Yes, if the profit is more than 500
cards.source: لا يستحق أحدهما منه دراهم مسماة
cards.why: Neither side may be owed a fixed number of dirhams from the profit. It must be a share like a half or a third.

cards.ask: Complete al-Quduri's condition for the profit.
cards.ar: أن يكون الربح بينهما ____
cards.source: أن يكون الربح بينهما مشاعا
cards.why: مشاعا: the profit is shared between them as a portion of the whole.

cards.title: What the worker may do
cards.ar: فإذا صحت المضاربة مطلقة جاز للمضارب أن يشتري ويبيع ويسافر ويبضع ويوكل وليس له أن يدفع المال مضاربة إلا أن يأذن له رب المال في ذلك
cards.en: In an open (mutlaqa) mudaraba, with no limits set, the worker may buy, sell, travel, hand money to someone to trade for free, and appoint agents. But he may not give the money to another worker in mudaraba unless the owner allows it. The capital must be money a partnership can be made with.

cards.ask: In an open mudaraba, which may the worker do without asking?

options.text: Buy and sell
Travel with the money
Appoint an agent
Give the money to another worker in mudaraba
Marry off a slave from the mudaraba money, in al-Quduri's time

source: جاز للمضارب أن يشتري ويبيع ويسافر ويبضع ويوكل
ولا تصح المضاربة إلا بالمال الذي بيننا أن الشركة تصح به
ولا يزوج عبدا ولا أمة من مال المضاربة
cards.why: He may buy, sell, travel and appoint agents. A second mudaraba needs the owner's permission, and he may not marry off a slave from the money.

cards.title: When the owner sets limits
cards.ar: وإن خص له رب المال التصرف في بلد بعينه أو في سلعة بعينها لم يجز له أن يتجاوز ذلك
cards.en: If the owner limits him to one town or one kind of goods, he may not go beyond it. The owner may also set a time limit, and the contract ends when it runs out.

cards.ask: Hashim tells Nasir, "Trade with this money in Kufa only." Nasir finds a better deal in Basra. May he trade there?
options: No: he may not go beyond the town named
Yes, if it makes more profit
source: لم يجز له أن يتجاوز ذلك
وكذلك إن وقت للمضاربة مدة بعينها جاز وبطل العقد بمضيها
cards.why: When the owner names a town, the worker must stay within it.

cards.title: Buying the owner's relatives
cards.ar: وليس للمضارب أن يشتري أبا رب المال ولا ابنه ولا من يعتق عليه فإن اشتراهم كان مشتريا لنفسه دون المضاربة
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time there were slaves, and a person who came to own his own father or son set them free at once. So the worker may not buy, with mudaraba money, the owner's father, son, or anyone who would be freed on him. If he does, it counts as his own purchase, not the mudaraba's.

cards.ask: In al-Quduri's time, a worker uses mudaraba money to buy the owner's father, who is a slave. Whose purchase is it?
options: The worker's own, not the mudaraba's
The mudaraba's, shared like the rest
The owner's, since it is his father
cards.source: فإن اشتراهم كان مشتريا لنفسه دون المضاربة
cards.why: He may not buy the owner's father with mudaraba money. If he does, it counts as bought for himself.

cards.title: Buying his own relative
cards.ar: وإن لم يكن في المال ربح جاز أن يشتريهم فإن زادت قيمتهم عتق نصيبه منهم ولم يضمن لرب المال شيئا ويسعى المعتق لرب المال في قيمة نصيبه منه
cards.en: His own relatives (those who would be freed on the worker himself) are different. With profit in the money, he may not buy them. With no profit, he may. If their value then rises, his share of them is freed, he owes the owner nothing, and the freed person works off the owner's share.

cards.ask: The mudaraba has already made a profit. The worker uses its money to buy his own father. What follows?
options: He must pay back the mudaraba money
Nothing: it is a normal purchase
The owner's share of the father is freed
cards.source: وإن كان في المال ربح فليس له أن يشتري من يعتق عله فإن اشتراهم ضمن مال المضاربة
cards.why: With profit in the money he may not buy someone who would be freed on him. If he does, he is liable for the mudaraba money.

cards.ask: Which are true of the terms of a mudaraba?

options.text: One side gives the money and the other the work
The owner may set a time limit for the mudaraba
The worker may be promised a fixed 300 dirhams of profit
A worker limited to selling cloth may sell horses too
The money must be handed to the worker

source: بمال من أحد الشريكين وعمل من الآخر
وكذلك إن وقت للمضاربة مدة بعينها جاز
لا يستحق أحدهما منه دراهم مسماة
أو في سلعة بعينها لم يجز له أن يتجاوز ذلك
ولا بد أن يكون المال مسلما إلى المضارب
cards.why: Money from one, work from the other, a possible time limit, and the money handed over. Fixed sums are not allowed, and limits on goods must be kept.

lessons.title: Passing it on, ending it, and losses

cards.title: Passing the money on without permission
cards.ar: وإذا دفع المضارب المال مضاربة ولم يأذن له رب المال في ذلك لم يضمن بالدفع ولا بتصرف المضارب الثاني حتى يربح فإذا ربح ضمن المضارب الأول المال
cards.en: If the worker gives the money to a second worker without the owner's permission, he is not liable just for handing it over, nor for the second worker's trading, until the second worker makes a profit. Once there is profit, the first worker is liable for the money.

cards.ask: Nasir passes Hashim's money to Jamal without permission. Jamal trades and makes a profit. Who is now liable to Hashim for the money?
cards.source: فإذا ربح ضمن المضارب الأول المال
cards.why: Once the second worker makes a profit, the first worker becomes liable for the money.

cards.title: Shares when the owner allows it
cards.ar: وإذا دفع إليه المال مضاربة بالنصف فأذن له أن يدفعها مضاربة فدفعها بالثلث فإن كان رب المال قال له على أن رزق الله بيننا نصفان فلرب المال نصف الربح وللمضارب الثاني ثلث الربح وللأول السدس
cards.en: The owner gives money for half the profit and allows a second mudaraba, and the first worker gives it on for a third. If the owner had said, "Whatever God provides is half and half between us," the owner takes a half, the second worker a third, and the first worker the rest: a sixth.

cards.ask: In that case the profit is 600 dirhams. How much does the first worker get?
cards.source: فلرب المال نصف الربح وللمضارب الثاني ثلث الربح وللأول السدس
cards.why: The owner takes half (300), the second worker a third (200), and the first worker a sixth: 100.

cards.ask: Now the owner had said, "Whatever God provides YOU is half and half between us." The profit is 600. How much does the owner get?
cards.source: وإن قال على أن ما رزقك الله بيننا نصفان فللمضارب الثاني الثلث وما بقي بين رب المال والمضارب الأول نصفان
cards.why: The second worker takes his third (200). The 400 left is what the first worker got, and it is split half and half: 200 to the owner.

cards.title: When the owner said "half is mine"
cards.ar: فإن قال له على أن ما رزق الله فلي نصفه فدفع المال إلى آخر مضاربة بالنصف فللمضارب الثاني نصف الربح ولرب المال النصف ولا شيء للمضارب الأول
cards.en: If the owner said, "Half of what God provides is mine," and the first worker gives it on for half, the second worker takes half, the owner half, and the first worker nothing. Note: if he promised the second worker two-thirds, the first worker pays the missing sixth from his own money.

cards.title: What ends a mudaraba
cards.ar: وإذا مات رب المال أو المضارب بطلت المضاربة وإن ارتد رب المال عن الإسلام ولحق بدار الحرب بطلت المضاربة
cards.en: A mudaraba ends if the owner or the worker dies, or if the owner leaves Islam and joins the enemy's land.

cards.ask: The owner has dismissed the worker. May the worker still do this?
items: Trade before he hears he was dismissed
Sell goods he already holds, after hearing
Buy new goods with the price of those goods
Trade with capital that is already cash, after hearing
source: وإذا عزل رب المال المضارب ولم يعلم بعزله حتى اشترى وباع فتصرفه جائز وإن علم بعزله والمال عروض فله أن يبيعها ولا يمنعه العزل من ذلك ثم لا يجوز أن يشتري بثمنها شيئا آخر
وإن عزله ورأس المال دراهم أو دنانير قد نصت فليس له أن يتصرف فيه
cards.why: Until he knows, his dealings are valid. After he knows, he may turn goods into cash but buy nothing new, and cash he may not touch.

cards.title: Collecting debts at the end
cards.ar: وإذا افترقا وفي المال ديون وقد ربح المضارب فيه أجبره الحاكم على اقتضاء الديون وإن لم يكن له ربح لم يلزمه الاقتضاء ويقال له: وكل رب المال في الاقتضاء
cards.en: If they part while money is still owed to the business, and the worker has made a profit, the judge makes him collect the debts. If there is no profit, he does not have to, but he is told to make the owner his agent to collect them.

cards.title: Losses come out of profit first
cards.ar: وما هلك من مال المضاربة فهو من الربح دون رأس المال فإن زاد الهالك على الربح فلا ضمان على المضارب فيه
cards.en: Whatever is lost comes out of the profit first, not the capital. If the loss is more than the profit, the worker does not pay for it. If they shared out the profit while the mudaraba was still running and then money was lost, they give the profit back until the owner has his capital again.

cards.ask: The capital is 1000. Nasir makes 200 profit, and then 300 is lost. What is the result?
options: The 200 profit is gone, the capital is down to 900, and Nasir owes nothing
The owner loses 300 of his capital and Nasir keeps 100
source: وما هلك من مال المضاربة فهو من الربح دون رأس المال فإن زاد الهالك على الربح فلا ضمان على المضارب فيه
وإن عجز عن رأس المال لم يضمن المضارب
cards.why: The loss first eats the 200 profit. The other 100 comes off the capital, and the worker owes nothing for it.

cards.ask: Which are true of running and ending a mudaraba?

options.text: The worker may sell for cash or on credit
A mudaraba ends when the worker dies
Profit shared out mid-way is given back if the capital is later lost
The worker is liable for any loss bigger than the profit
Profit split after the mudaraba was ended and made again is given back

source: ويجوز للمضارب أن يبيع بالنقد والسيئة
وإذا مات رب المال أو المضارب بطلت المضاربة
وإن كانا قد اقتسما الربح والمضاربة بحالها ثم هلك المال أو بعضه ترادا الربح حتى يستوفي رب المال رأس المال
وإن كانا قد اقتسما الربح وفسخا المضاربة ثم عقداها فهلك المال لم يترادا الربح الأول
cards.why: He may sell for cash or credit, death ends it, and profit shared mid-way goes back to cover lost capital. He is not liable beyond the profit, and profit from an earlier, ended mudaraba stays shared.

cards.title: What you can do, an agent can do
cards.ar: كل عقد جاز أن يعقده الإنسان بنفسه جاز أن يوكل به غيره ويجوز التوكيل بالخصومة في سائر الحقوق وبإثباتها
cards.en: Wakala is agency: appointing someone to act for you. The one who appoints is the muwakkil (principal). The one appointed is the wakil (agent). Any contract you may make yourself, you may appoint someone else to make. You may also appoint an agent to argue a case for you in court (khusuma) and to prove your rights.

cards.ask: Complete al-Quduri's rule.
cards.ar: كل عقد جاز أن يعقده الإنسان ____ جاز أن يوكل به غيره
cards.source: كل عقد جاز أن يعقده الإنسان بنفسه جاز أن يوكل به غيره
cards.why: بنفسه: whatever contract a person may make himself, he may appoint another to make.

cards.title: Collecting rights, except punishments
cards.ar: ويجوز التوكيل بالاستيفاء إلا في الحدود والقصاص فإن الوكالة لا تصح باستيفائهما مع غيبة الموكل عن المجلس
cards.en: You may appoint an agent to collect what you are owed. But for hadd punishments (fixed punishments set by the Sharia) and qisas (retaliation for an injury or killing), an agent cannot carry them out while the principal is away from the place.

cards.ask: A man has a right of qisas against someone. He asks an agent to see it carried out while he himself stays in another city. Is the agency valid?
options: No: not while the principal is away
Yes: any right can be collected by an agent
Yes, if a judge is there
cards.source: فإن الوكالة لا تصح باستيفائهما مع غيبة الموكل عن المجلس
cards.why: An agent may not carry out hadd or qisas while the principal is absent.

cards.title: An agent in court: the opponent's consent
cards.ar: وقال أبو حنيفة: لا يجوز التوكيل بالخصومة إلا برضا الخصم إلا أن يكون الموكل مريضا أو غائبا مسيرة ثلاثة أيام فصاعدا
cards.en: Abu Hanifa said an agent may argue your case only if the other side agrees, unless you are ill or three days' journey away or more. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad said it is allowed without the opponent's consent.

cards.ask: Hamid is in bed with a serious illness and appoints his cousin to argue his case in court. The other side objects. May the cousin act?
options: No: the other side must agree
source: إلا أن يكون الموكل مريضا
وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد: يجوز التوكيل بغير رضا الخصم
cards.why: Even for Abu Hanifa, an ill principal does not need the opponent's consent, and Abu Yusuf and Muhammad never require it.

cards.title: Who can appoint, and who can be appointed
cards.ar: ومن شرط الوكالة: أن يكون الموكل ممن يملك التصرف وتلزمه الأحكام والوكيل ممن يعقل العقد ويقصده
cards.en: The principal must be someone who may deal with his own things and is bound by the rulings. The agent must understand the contract and mean to make it.

cards.title: A boy or a restricted person as agent
cards.ar: وإذا وكل الحر البالغ أو المأذون مثلهما جاز وإن وكلا صبيا محجورا يعقل البيع والشراء أو عبدا محجورا جاز ولا تتعلق بهما الحقوق وتتعلق بموكليهما
cards.en: A free adult may appoint someone like himself. He may also appoint a boy who understands buying and selling, or (in al-Quduri's time) a slave without permission to trade. The deal is valid, but its duties fall on the principal, not on them.

cards.ask: Yusuf sends his 11-year-old nephew, who understands buying and selling, to buy bread with his money. The baker later has a complaint about the payment. Whom does he deal with?
cards.source: جاز ولا تتعلق بهما الحقوق وتتعلق بموكليهما
cards.why: The boy's purchase is valid, but the rights and duties of the deal fall on Yusuf.

cards.ask: Which are true of appointing an agent?

options.text: You may appoint an agent for any contract you may make yourself
An agent must understand the contract
A boy who understands trade may be an agent
An agent may carry out qisas while the principal is far away
Only adults may ever act as agents

source: جاز أن يوكل به غيره
والوكيل ممن يعقل العقد ويقصده
وإن وكلا صبيا محجورا يعقل البيع والشراء
مع غيبة الموكل عن المجلس
cards.why: Any contract can be delegated, the agent must understand it, and a boy who understands trade can be an agent. Qisas cannot be carried out by an agent in the principal's absence.

lessons.title: Whose job is it after the deal?
lessons.arabic: والعقود التي يعقدها الوكلاء على ضربين

cards.title: Deals the agent makes in his own name
cards.ar: فكل عقد يضيفه الوكيل إلى نفسه - مثل البيع والإجارة - فحقوق ذلك العقد تتعلق بالوكيل دون الموكل فيسلم المبيع ويقبض الثمن ويطالب بالثمن إذا اشترى ويقبض المبيع ويخاصم بالعيب
cards.en: Some deals the agent makes in his own name, like a sale or a hire. The rights of those deals sit with the agent, not the principal. He hands over the goods and takes the price; when buying, he is asked for the price, receives the goods, and complains about defects.

cards.title: Deals made in the principal's name
cards.ar: وكل عقد يضيفه إلى موكله - كالنكاح والخلع والصلح من دم العمد - فإن حقوقه تتعلق بالموكل دون الوكيل فلا يطالب وكيل الزوج بالمهر ولا يلزم وكيل المرأة تسليمها
cards.en: Other deals are made in the principal's name, like marriage (nikah), khul' (a wife ending the marriage for payment), and settling a claim for deliberate killing. Their rights sit with the principal. The groom's agent is not asked for the mahr (the bride's due gift), and the bride's agent need not hand her over.

cards.ask: Whose are the rights of this deal?
source: مثل البيع والإجارة
كالنكاح والخلع والصلح من دم العمد
cards.why: Sales and hires are made in the agent's own name, so their rights are his. Marriage, khul' and settling a killing are in the principal's name.

cards.ask: Ibrahim's friend acts as his agent to marry Sumayya for him. Later Sumayya asks the friend for her mahr. Must he pay it?
options: They share it half and half
cards.source: فلا يطالب وكيل الزوج بالمهر
cards.why: Marriage is made in the principal's name, so the husband owes the mahr, not his agent.

cards.ask: An agent sells Rami's horse. Rami himself goes to the buyer for the price, and the buyer pays him. Can the agent now ask the buyer to pay again?
options: No: the buyer validly paid the principal
Yes: the price was the agent's to collect
cards.source: وإذا طالب الموكل المشتري فله أن يمنعه إياه فإن دفعه إليه جاز ولم يكن للوكيل أن يطالبه به ثانيا
cards.why: The buyer could have refused the principal, but once he has paid him, that is valid and the agent cannot ask again.

cards.title: Say what to buy
cards.ar: ومن وكل رجلا بشراء شيء فلا بد من تسمية جنسه وصفته أو جنسه ومبلغ ثمنه إلا أن يوكله وكالة عامة فيقول: ابتع لي ما رأيت
cards.en: When you send an agent to buy something, you must name its kind and description, or its kind and how much to pay, unless you give him general agency: "Buy me whatever you think best."

cards.ask: Which instruction is enough for an agent to buy with?
options: "Buy me something nice for the house"
"Buy me an animal for the farm"
cards.source: فلا بد من تسمية جنسه وصفته أو جنسه ومبلغ ثمنه
cards.why: A kind (horse) with a description (grey, Arab) is enough. "Something" or "an animal" does not name a kind with a description or price.

cards.title: Returning for a defect
cards.ar: وإذا اشترى الوكيل وقبض المبيع ثم اطلع على عيب فله أن يرد بالعيب ما دام المبيع في
cards.en: If the agent buys something, receives it, and then finds a defect, he may return it as long as it is still with him. Once he has handed it to the principal, he may only return it with the principal's permission.

cards.title: Exchange, salam, and paying from his own money
cards.ar: ويجوز التوكيل بعقد الصرف والسلم فإن فارق الوكيل صاحبه قبل القبض بطل العقد ولا تعتبر مفارقة الموكل
cards.en: Sarf is exchanging money for money. Salam is paying now for goods delivered later. You may use an agent for both. If the agent parts from the other side before the handing over, the deal fails; the principal walking away does not matter. A buying agent who pays from his own money may claim it back.

cards.ask: An agent pays 300 dirhams of his own money for a camel for Faris. Before the agent holds it back for payment, the camel dies in his care. Who bears the loss?
options: Faris, and he still owes the agent the 300
The agent, and Faris owes nothing
source: وإذا دفع الوكيل بالشراء الثمن من ماله وقبض المبيع فله أن يرجع به على الموكل فإن هلك المبيع في يده قبل حبسه هلك من مال الموكل ولم يسقط الثمن
وإن سلمه إلى الموكل
cards.why: The agent may claim what he paid. If the item dies in his care before he holds it back, it is lost from the principal's wealth and the price is still owed.

cards.title: Holding it back until paid
cards.ar: وله أن يحبسه حتى يستوفي الثمن فإن حبسه فهلك كان مضمونا ضمان الرهن عند أبي يوسف وضمان المبيع عند محمد
cards.en: The agent may hold the item back until he is paid. Note: if he holds it and it is lost, Abu Yusuf said he is liable as for a pledge (rahn), and Muhammad said as for a sold item.

cards.ask: Which are true of an agent's duties after the deal?

options.text: In a sale, the agent hands over the goods and takes the price
The bride's agent must hand her over
An agent may be appointed for a salam
If the agent walks away before the exchange is handed over, the sarf fails
"Buy me whatever you think best" is never allowed

source: فيسلم المبيع ويقبض الثمن
ولا يلزم وكيل المرأة تسليمها
ويجوز التوكيل بعقد الصرف والسلم
فإن فارق الوكيل صاحبه قبل القبض بطل العقد
ابتع لي ما رأيت
cards.why: The selling agent deals with goods and price, agents may do salam, and his leaving early breaks a sarf. The bride's agent has no such duty, and general agency is allowed.

lessons.title: Two agents, sub-agents, and when agency ends

cards.title: Two agents act together
cards.ar: وإذا وكل رجلين فليس لأحدهما أن يتصرف فيما وكلا فيه دون الآخر إلا أن يوكلهما بالخصومة أو بطلاق زوجته بغير عوض أو برد وديعة عنده أو بقضاء دين عليه
cards.en: If you appoint two agents for one job, neither may act without the other. Except when they are appointed to argue a case, to pronounce a divorce with nothing paid, to return a deposit (wadi'a, something left with you for safekeeping), or to pay off a debt.

cards.ask: Two agents were appointed. May one act alone?
source: إلا أن يوكلهما بالخصومة
أو برد وديعة عنده أو بقضاء دين عليه
فليس لأحدهما أن يتصرف فيما وكلا فيه دون الآخر
cards.why: Arguing, returning a deposit and paying a debt can be done by one. Other jobs, like buying and selling, need both.

cards.title: An agent appointing an agent
cards.ar: وليس للوكيل أن يوكل فيما وكل به إلا أن يأذن له الموكل أو يقول له: اعمل برأيك فإن وكل بغير إذن موكله فعقد وكيله بحضرته جاز وإن عقد بغير حضرته فأجازه الوكيل الأول جاز
cards.en: An agent may not appoint another agent for the job unless the principal allows it or says, "Do as you see fit." If he does so without permission, the second agent's deal is still valid if made in the first agent's presence, or if the first agent approves it afterwards.

cards.ask: Without asking, Karim's agent asks a friend to do the buying. The friend buys the goods while the agent stands beside him. Is the purchase valid?
options: Yes, as the agent was present
No: he had no permission to do it
cards.source: فإن وكل بغير إذن موكله فعقد وكيله بحضرته جاز
cards.why: A sub-agent's deal made in the first agent's presence is valid.

cards.title: Dismissing an agent
cards.ar: الوكيل عن الوكالة فإن لم يبلغه العزل فهو على وكالته وتصرفه جائز حتى يعلم
cards.en: The principal may dismiss the agent. But until news of it reaches the agent, he is still an agent and what he does is valid.

cards.ask: Maha sends a letter dismissing her agent. Before it arrives, the agent sells her land. Is the sale valid?
options: Yes: he had not yet heard
No: she had already dismissed him
Only if the price was good
cards.source: فإن لم يبلغه العزل فهو على وكالته وتصرفه جائز حتى يعلم
cards.why: Dismissal counts only once it reaches the agent, so the sale is valid.

cards.title: When agency ends
cards.ar: وإذا وكل المكاتب ثم عجز أو المأذون فحجر عليه أو الشريكان فافترقا فهذه الوجوه تبطل الوكالة علم الوكيل أو لم يعلم
cards.en: Agency ends when the principal dies, becomes permanently insane, or leaves Islam and joins the enemy's land. It also ends if partners who appointed an agent split up, and in other such cases, whether or not the agent knows.

cards.title: The agent dies, or the principal acts himself
cards.ar: وإذا مات الوكيل أو جن جنونا مطبقا بطلت وكالته وإن لحق بدار الحرب مرتدا لم يجز له التصرف إلا أن يعود مسلما ومن وكل آخر بشيء ثم تصرف فيما وكل به بطلت الوكالة
cards.en: If the agent dies or becomes permanently insane, his agency ends. If he leaves Islam and joins the enemy's land, he may not act unless he returns as a Muslim. And if the principal does the job himself, the agency ends.

cards.ask: Maryam appoints an agent to sell her ring. The next day she sells it herself. What about the agency?
options: It goes on, for another ring
The agent may still sell it
cards.source: ومن وكل آخر بشيء ثم تصرف فيما وكل به بطلت الوكالة
cards.why: When the principal does the job himself, the agency ends.

cards.ask: Does the agency end?
items: The partners who appointed him split up
He was dismissed, but has not heard
source: وتبطل الوكالة بموت الموكل
أو جن جنونا مطبقا بطلت وكالته
أو الشريكان فافترقا
فهو على وكالته
cards.why: Death, permanent insanity and partners splitting end it. A dismissal he has not heard of does not, yet.

cards.ask: Which are true of two agents and sub-agents?

options.text: An agent told "do as you see fit" may appoint another agent
Two agents to sell a house may each sell alone
The partners splitting up ends their agent's agency even if he does not know
An agent's dealings are void from the moment the letter is sent
One of two agents may pay off the debt alone

source: أو يقول له: اعمل برأيك
دون الآخر
علم الوكيل أو لم يعلم
حتى يعلم
أو بقضاء دين عليه
cards.why: "Do as you see fit" allows a sub-agent, cases like partners splitting end it regardless, and one agent may pay a debt. Selling needs both, and dismissal counts only once he knows.

lessons.title: Buying and selling for someone else

cards.title: Selling to his own family
cards.ar: والوكيل بالبيع والشراء لا يجوز أن يعقد عند أبي حنيفة مع أبيه وجده وولده ولده وزوجته وعبده ومكاتبه
cards.en: For Abu Hanifa, an agent to buy or sell may not deal with his own father, grandfather, child, grandchild, wife, slave or mukatab (a slave buying his freedom, in al-Quduri's time). Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad said he may sell to them at the fair value, except to his own slave or mukatab.

cards.ask: In al-Quduri's time, an agent sells his principal's goods to the agent's own slave at the fair price. Is it allowed?
options: No: not to his own slave
Yes, if the principal never finds out
source: وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد: يجوز بيعه منهم بمثل القيمة إلا في عبده ومكاتبه
cards.why: Abu Hanifa forbids it, and even Abu Yusuf and Muhammad, who allow a fair sale to family, make an exception of his own slave and mukatab.

cards.title: At what price may a selling agent sell?
cards.ar: والوكيل بالبيع يجوز بيعه بالقليل والكثير عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: For Abu Hanifa, a selling agent may sell for a low or a high price. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad said he may not sell at a loss that people would not overlook.

cards.title: A buying agent must not overpay much
cards.ar: والوكيل بالشراء يجوز عقده بمثل القيمة وزيادة يتغابن الناس في مثلها ولا يجوز بما لا يتغابن الناس في مثله والذي لا يتغابن الناس فيه: ما لا يدخل تحت تقويم المقومين
cards.en: A buying agent may buy at the fair value, or a little more, the kind of small overpayment people overlook. He may not pay more than that. A loss people do not overlook is a price outside what any of the experts who value goods would say.

cards.ask: Experts value a horse at between 980 and 1020 dirhams. The agent buys it for 1010. Is the purchase binding on the principal?
options: Yes: that is within the experts' values
Only if the principal likes the horse
cards.source: والوكيل بالشراء يجوز عقده بمثل القيمة وزيادة يتغابن الناس في مثلها
cards.why: A small overpayment that the valuers' estimates cover is overlooked, so the purchase stands.

cards.ask: No expert values the horse above 1000, but the agent pays 1500. Is it allowed for the principal?
options: No: it is beyond what people overlook
Yes, if the agent pays the extra
cards.source: ولا يجوز بما لا يتغابن الناس في مثله والذي لا يتغابن الناس فيه: ما لا يدخل تحت تقويم المقومين
cards.why: A price no valuer would give is a loss people do not overlook, so a buying agent may not pay it.

cards.title: Guaranteeing the price, and buying half
cards.ar: وإذا ضمن الوكيل بالبيع الثمن عن المبتاع فضمانه باطل وإذا وكله ببيع عبده فباع نصفه جاز عند أبي حنيفة وإن وكله بشراء عبد فاشترى نصفه فالشراء موقوف
cards.en: A selling agent cannot stand surety for the buyer's price: such a guarantee is void. In al-Quduri's time, if told to sell a slave and he sold half, that was allowed for Abu Hanifa. If told to buy one and he bought half, the purchase waits: if he buys the rest, it binds the principal.

cards.ask: Hadi's agent sells his land and tells Hadi, "I guarantee the buyer will pay." The buyer never pays. Must the agent pay Hadi?
options: Yes: he gave his word to pay it
cards.source: وإذا ضمن الوكيل بالبيع الثمن عن المبتاع فضمانه باطل
cards.why: A selling agent's guarantee of the buyer's price is void, so it binds him to nothing.

cards.title: Ten pounds of meat
cards.ar: وإذا وكله بشراء عشرة أرطال لحم بدرهم فاشترى عشرين رطلا بدرهم من لحم يباع مثله عشرة بدرهم لزم الموكل منه عشرة أرطال بنصف درهم عند أبي حنيفة وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد: يلزمه العشرون
cards.en: He is told to buy ten ratls (pounds) of meat for a dirham, and buys twenty for a dirham, of meat that normally sells ten for a dirham. Abu Hanifa said the principal takes ten pounds for half a dirham. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad said he takes all twenty.

cards.title: A named thing, or any one
cards.ar: وإذا وكله بشراء شيء بعينه فليس له أن يشتريه لنفسه
cards.en: If he is told to buy one particular thing, he may not buy it for himself. If he is told to buy a thing of a kind, not a particular one, what he buys is his own, unless he says he meant it for the principal or pays with the principal's money.

cards.ask: Omar tells his agent, "Buy me that blue car in the showroom window." The agent likes it and buys it for himself. Is that allowed?
options: No: he was sent for that very car
Yes, if he pays with his own money
Yes, if he tells Omar afterwards
cards.source: وإذا وكله بشراء شيء بعينه فليس له أن يشتريه لنفسه
