cards.why: When he is sent to buy a particular thing, he may not buy it for himself.

cards.ask: In al-Quduri's time, an agent is told to buy "a slave", none in particular. He buys one using the principal's money. Whose is the purchase?
cards.source: فاشترى عبدا فهو للوكيل إلا أن يقول: نويت الشراء للموكل أو يشتريه بمال الموكل
cards.why: A thing not named in particular is the agent's, unless he meant it for the principal or paid with the principal's money, as here.

cards.ask: Which are true of agents buying and selling?

options.text: A selling agent's guarantee of the buyer's price is void
A buying agent may pay a little over value that people overlook
A buying agent may pay whatever the seller asks
An agent sent for a particular thing may buy it for himself
Half a slave bought by an agent binds the principal once he buys the rest

source: فضمانه باطل
وزيادة يتغابن الناس في مثلها
ولا يجوز بما لا يتغابن الناس في مثله
فليس له أن يشتريه لنفسه
فالشراء موقوف
cards.why: The guarantee is void, small overpayments are overlooked, and a half purchase waits until he buys the rest. He may not overpay much or take the named thing for himself.

lessons.title: Agents in court and for debts

cards.title: An agent to argue may collect
cards.ar: والوكيل بالخصومة وكيل بالقبض عند أبي حنيفة وأبي يوسف ومحمد والوكيل بقبض الدين وكيل بالخصومة فيه عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: An agent appointed to argue a case may also collect what is won: Abu Hanifa, Abu Yusuf and Muhammad all say so. And for Abu Hanifa, an agent appointed to collect a debt may also argue about it in court.

cards.ask: Layla appoints an agent to argue her claim for 2000 dirhams. He wins. May he collect the money for her?
options: Yes: an agent for the case may also collect
No: he was only appointed to argue
Only with a new letter from Layla
cards.source: والوكيل بالخصومة وكيل بالقبض عند أبي حنيفة وأبي يوسف ومحمد
cards.why: An agent for the case is also an agent to collect.

cards.title: When the agent admits against his principal
cards.ar: وإذا أقر الوكيل بالخصومة على موكله عند القاضي جاز إقراره ولا يجوز إقراره عليه عند غير القاضي عند أبي حنيفة ومحمد إلا أنه يخرج من الخصومة
cards.en: If the agent admits, in front of the judge, something against his principal, the admission counts. Away from the judge, for Abu Hanifa and Muhammad, it does not count against the principal, but the agent is taken off the case. Note: Abu Yusuf said it counts even away from the judge.

cards.ask: In court, before the judge, Badr's agent says, "Yes, my client does owe this money." Does the admission count against Badr?
options: Yes: it was made before the judge
source: وإذا أقر الوكيل بالخصومة على موكله عند القاضي جاز إقراره
وقال أبو يوسف: يجوز إقراره عليه عند غير القاضي
cards.why: An admission made before the judge by the agent for the case counts against the principal.

cards.ask: Complete al-Quduri's words.
cards.ar: وإذا أقر الوكيل بالخصومة على موكله ____ جاز إقراره
cards.source: وإذا أقر الوكيل بالخصومة على موكله عند القاضي جاز إقراره
cards.why: عند القاضي: the agent's admission counts when it is made before the judge.

cards.title: Someone says, "I am his agent"
cards.ar: ومن ادعى أنه وكيل الغائب في قبض دينه فصدقه الغريم أمر بتسليم الدين إليه فإن حضر الغائب فصدقه وإلا دفع إليه الغريم الدين ثانيا ورجع به على الوكيل إن كان باقيا في يده
cards.en: A man says he is the agent of an absent creditor to collect a debt, and the debtor believes him. The debtor is told to pay him. When the creditor comes back, if he agrees, fine. If not, the debtor must pay the creditor again, and may take it back from the "agent" if he still has it.

cards.ask: Hani owes Walid 500. A man says, "Walid sent me to collect it." Hani believes him and pays. Walid returns and says he sent nobody. What now?
options: Hani pays again, and claims it back from the man
Walid loses the 500 and Hani owes nothing
Walid must chase the man himself for the 500 dirhams
cards.source: وإلا دفع إليه الغريم الدين ثانيا ورجع به على الوكيل إن كان باقيا في يده
cards.why: If the creditor denies sending him, the debtor pays again and may reclaim it from the man if it is still with him.

cards.title: A deposit is different
cards.ar: وإن قال إني وكيل بقبض الوديعة فصدقه المودع لم يؤمر بالتسليم إليه
cards.en: If a man says he is the agent to collect a deposit, and the one keeping it believes him, he is not ordered to hand it over.

cards.ask: A man claims to be the owner's agent, and is believed. Is the holder ordered to hand over?
items: A loan of 200 to be repaid
A bag of gold left for safekeeping
A watch left as a deposit
source: أمر بتسليم الدين إليه
لم يؤمر بالتسليم إليه
cards.why: A believed agent for a debt must be paid. For a deposit, the keeper is not ordered to hand it over.

cards.ask: Which are true of agents in court and for debts?

options.text: An agent to collect a debt may argue about it, for Abu Hanifa
The agent's admission before the judge counts
A debtor who paid a false agent owes nothing more
A deposit-keeper who believes the "agent" must hand it over
An agent to argue may also collect

source: والوكيل بقبض الدين وكيل بالخصومة فيه عند أبي حنيفة
عند القاضي جاز إقراره
دفع إليه الغريم الدين ثانيا
لم يؤمر بالتسليم إليه
وكيل بالقبض
cards.why: Collecting and arguing go together, and an admission before the judge counts. A debtor fooled by a false agent pays again, and a deposit need not be handed over.

cards.title: Two kinds of surety
cards.ar: الكفالة ضربان: كفالة بالنفس وكفالة بالمال
cards.en: Kafala is suretyship: taking on someone else's duty as a guarantee. The kafil is the surety. There are two kinds: surety for a person (promising to bring him) and surety for money (promising to pay his debt).

cards.ask: How many kinds of kafala (surety) are there?
cards.source: الكفالة ضربان
cards.why: Two: surety for a person and surety for money.

cards.ask: Which of these are the kinds of kafala?

options.text: Surety for a person
A pledge (rahn)
Surety for money
A transfer of debt (hawala)

cards.source: الكفالة ضربان: كفالة بالنفس وكفالة بالمال
cards.why: Kafala is surety for a person or surety for money. A pledge and a hawala have chapters of their own.

cards.title: Promising to bring someone
cards.ar: فالكفالة بالنفس جائزة والمضمون بها إحضار المكفول به
cards.en: Surety for a person is allowed. What the surety promises is to bring that person when he is wanted. It is made by saying, "I stand surety for so-and-so himself," or for his neck, soul, body, head, half or third of him, or "I guarantee him," "He is on me," or "I am answerable for him."

cards.ask: Which of these words make surety for a person?

options.text: "I stand surety for his body"
"I stand surety for half of him"
"I guarantee him"
"I am answerable for him"
"I know him well"
"I hope he comes"

cards.source: أو بروحه أو بجسده أو برأسه أو بنصفه أو بثلثه وكذلك إن قال ضمنته أو هو علي أو إلي أو أنا زعيم به أو قبيل
cards.why: Naming his body, a part of him, or saying "I guarantee him" or "I am answerable" makes the surety. Knowing him or hoping is not a promise.

cards.title: Bringing him at the agreed time
cards.ar: فإن شرط في الكفالة تسليم المكفول به في وقت بعينه لزمه إحضاره إذا طالبه به في ذلك الوقت فإن أحضره وإلا حبسه الحاكم حتى يحضره
cards.en: If a time was set to hand the person over, the surety must bring him when asked at that time. If he does not, the judge locks the surety up until he brings him.

cards.ask: Jabir stood surety to bring Hakim to court on the first of the month. The day comes and Jabir does not bring him. What does the judge do?
options: Holds Jabir in prison until he brings Hakim
Lets Jabir go, since he tried
Makes Jabir pay a fine and ends the surety
cards.source: فإن أحضره وإلا حبسه الحاكم حتى يحضره
cards.why: If the surety does not bring the person at the agreed time, the judge holds him until he does.

cards.title: Where he must be handed over
cards.ar: وإذا أحضره وسلمه في مكان يقدر المكفول له على محاكمته برئ الكفيل من الكفالة وإذا تكفل به على أن يسلمه في مجلس القاضي فسلمه في السوق برئ وإن سلمه في برية لم يبرأ
cards.en: If he hands the person over in a place where the creditor can take him to court, the surety is free. If he promised to hand him over at the judge's court, handing him over in the market frees him, but in the open desert it does not.

cards.ask: Is the surety now free of his promise?
items: He hands the man over in the market
He hands him over far out in the desert
He hands him over where he can be taken to court
The man he stood surety for dies
source: فسلمه في السوق برئ وإن سلمه في برية لم يبرأ
برئ الكفيل من الكفالة
وإن مات المكفول به برئ الكفيل بالنفس من الكفالة
cards.why: The market, or any place where he can be taken to court, frees the surety, and so does the man's death. The desert does not.

cards.title: Surety for a person, with money if he fails
cards.ar: فإن تكفل بنفسه على أنه إن لم يواف به في وقت كذا فهو ضامن لما عليه وهو ألف ولم يحضره في ذلك الوقت لزمه ضمان المال ولم يبرأ من الكفالة بالنفس
cards.en: If he stood surety for the person on the terms, "If I don't bring him by this time, I will pay what he owes, which is 1000," and he does not bring him, he must pay the money, and he is still surety for bringing the person too.

cards.ask: Dawud says, "If I don't bring Sami by Friday, I'll pay his 1000 debt." Friday passes without Sami. What is Dawud bound to do?
options: Pay the 1000, and still bring Sami
Only pay the 1000; the surety then ends
cards.source: لزمه ضمان المال ولم يبرأ من الكفالة بالنفس
cards.why: He must pay the money, and he is not freed from the surety for the person.

cards.title: Surety in punishment cases
cards.ar: ولا يجوز الكفالة بالنفس في الحدود والقصاص عند أبي حنيفة وقالا: يجوز
cards.en: For Abu Hanifa, surety for a person is not allowed in cases of hadd (a fixed punishment set by the Sharia) or qisas (retaliation for an injury or killing). Note: his two students, Abu Yusuf and Muhammad ("the two"), said it is allowed.

cards.ask: Which are true of surety for a person?

options.text: The surety for a person promises to bring him
Handing him over in the desert frees the surety
If the surety misses the agreed time, the judge may hold him
The surety is freed if the person dies
Paying the money ends the surety for the person too

source: والمضمون بها إحضار المكفول به
وإن سلمه في برية لم يبرأ
وإلا حبسه الحاكم حتى يحضره
وإن مات المكفول به برئ الكفيل
ولم يبرأ من الكفالة بالنفس
cards.why: He promises to bring the person, may be held if he does not, and is freed by the person's death. The desert does not free him, and paying does not end the surety for the person.

cards.title: Known or unknown amounts
cards.ar: وأما الكفالة بالمال فجائزة معلوما كان المال المكفول به أو مجهولا إذا كان دينا صحيحا
cards.en: Surety for money is allowed whether the amount is known or not, as long as it is a sound debt. For example: "I stand surety for him for 1000," or "for what he owes you," or "for whatever comes back on you in this sale."

cards.ask: Complete al-Quduri's words.
cards.ar: فجائزة معلوما كان المال المكفول به أو ____
cards.source: فجائزة معلوما كان المال المكفول به أو مجهولا
cards.why: مجهولا: surety for money is allowed whether the amount is known or unknown.

cards.title: The creditor may ask either one
cards.ar: مثل أن يقول: تكلفت عنه بألف أو بما لك عليه أو بما يدركك في هذا البيع والمكفول به بالخيار: إن شاء طالب الذي عليه الأصل وإن شاء طالب كفيله
cards.en: The creditor may choose: he can ask the original debtor, or he can ask the surety.

cards.ask: Imran owes Fawzi 800, and Bashir stands surety for it. Fawzi goes straight to Bashir for the money. May he?
options: Yes: he may ask either one
No: he must ask Imran first
cards.source: إن شاء طالب الذي عليه الأصل وإن شاء طالب كفيله
cards.why: The creditor may ask the debtor or the surety, as he wishes.

cards.title: Surety on a condition, and unknown amounts
cards.ar: ويجوز تعليق الكفالة بالشرط مثل أن يقول: ما بايعت فلانا فعلي أو ما ذاب لك عليه فعلي
cards.en: Surety may hang on a condition: "Whatever you sell to so-and-so, I'll pay," or "Whatever he comes to owe you, I'll pay," or "Whatever he takes from you by force, I'll pay."

cards.title: How much, if no one is sure
cards.ar: وإذا قال: تكفلت بما لك عليه فقامت البينة بألف عليه ضمنه الكفيل فإن لم تقم البينة فالقول قول الكفيل مع يمينه في مقدار ما يعترف به فإن اعترف المكفول عنه بأكثر من ذلك لم يصدق على كفيله
cards.en: If he stood surety "for what he owes you" and witnesses prove 1000, the surety owes 1000. Without witnesses, the surety's word is taken, under oath, for the amount he admits. If the debtor admits more, that does not bind the surety.

cards.ask: Bashir stood surety "for whatever Imran owes you." There are no witnesses. Bashir swears it is 300. Imran says it is 800. What does Bashir owe?
source: فالقول قول الكفيل مع يمينه في مقدار ما يعترف به
فإن اعترف المكفول عنه بأكثر من ذلك لم يصدق على كفيله
فعلي أو ما غصبك فلانا فعلي
cards.why: Without proof, the surety's sworn word counts for what he owes. The debtor's bigger admission binds only the debtor.

cards.title: Asked to be surety, or not asked
cards.ar: وتجوز الكفالة بأمر المكفول عنه وبغير أمره فإن كفل بأمره رجع بما يؤدي عليه وإن كفل بغير أمره لم يرجع بما يؤديه
cards.en: You may stand surety whether the debtor asked you or not. If he asked you, you can claim back from him what you pay. If he did not ask you, you cannot. And the surety may not ask the debtor for the money before he has paid it.

cards.ask: Without being asked, Uncle Tahir stands surety for his nephew's 500 debt, and later pays it. Can he claim the 500 back from his nephew?
cards.source: وإن كفل بغير أمره لم يرجع بما يؤديه
cards.why: A surety who was not asked by the debtor cannot claim back what he pays.

cards.ask: Who is now free of the debt?
items: The debtor pays the creditor in full
The creditor lets the surety off
source: وإذا أبرأ الطالب المكفول عنه أو استوفى منه برئ الكفيل وإن أبرأ الكفيل لم يبرإ المكفول عنه
cards.why: If the debtor is forgiven or pays, the surety is free too. Letting the surety off does not free the debtor.

cards.title: If the surety is pressed
cards.ar: وليس للكفيل أن يطالب المكفول عنه بالمال قبل أن يؤدي عنه فإن لوزم بالمال كان له أن يلازم المكفول عنه حتى يخلصه
cards.en: The surety may not ask the debtor for the money before paying it himself. But if the creditor keeps after him for the money, he may keep after the debtor in turn until the debtor frees him.

cards.ask: Which are true of surety for money?

options.text: Surety for an unknown amount is allowed
Surety may hang on a condition
The surety may ask the debtor for the money before paying anything
Forgiving the surety also frees the debtor
The creditor may go to the surety first

source: أو مجهولا
ويجوز تعليق الكفالة بالشرط
قبل أن يؤدي عنه
لم يبرإ المكفول عنه
وإن شاء طالب كفيله
cards.why: Unknown amounts and conditions are allowed, and the creditor may go to the surety. The surety pays before he claims, and freeing him does not free the debtor.

lessons.title: What surety can cover, and shared sureties
lessons.arabic: وكل حق لا يمكن استيفاؤه من الكفيل

cards.title: Only what the surety could hand over
cards.ar: ولا يجوز تعليق البراءة من الكفالة بشرط وكل حق لا يمكن استيفاؤه من الكفيل لا تصح الكفالة به كالحدود والقصاص
cards.en: Release from surety cannot be made to depend on a condition. And surety is not valid for any right that cannot be taken from the surety, like hadd punishments and qisas.

cards.title: Price yes, the goods no
cards.ar: وإذا تكفل عن المشتري بالثمن جاز وإن تكفل عن البائع بالمبيع لم يصح ومن استأجر دابة للحمل فإن كانت بعينها لم تصح الكفالة بالحمل وإن كانت بغير عينها جازت الكفالة
cards.en: Surety for a buyer's price is valid. Surety for the seller's goods is not. For hiring an animal to carry a load: if it is a particular animal, surety for the carrying is not valid; if it is any animal, it is.

cards.ask: Is the surety valid?
items: For the price a buyer owes
For the goods a seller must hand over
For carrying a load on any camel
For carrying a load on one particular camel
source: وإذا تكفل عن المشتري بالثمن جاز وإن تكفل عن البائع بالمبيع لم يصح
فإن كانت بعينها لم تصح الكفالة بالحمل وإن كانت بغير عينها جازت الكفالة
كالحدود والقصاص
cards.why: A price and a carrying job on any animal can come from the surety. Specific goods, a specific animal, and punishments cannot.

cards.title: The creditor must accept at the time
cards.ar: ولا تصح الكفالة إلا بقبول المكفول له في مجلس العقد إلا في مسألة واحدة وهي أن يقول المريض لوارثه: تكفل عني بما علي من الدين فتكفل به مع غيبة الغرماء
cards.en: Surety is valid only if the creditor accepts it in the same sitting. There is one exception: a sick man says to his heir, "Stand surety for my debts," and the heir does so while the creditors are absent.

cards.ask: Zaid tells a friend, "I'll stand surety for Ahmad's debt to Bakr." Bakr is not there, and hears of it next week. Was the surety made?
options: No: Bakr did not accept in the sitting
Yes, as soon as Zaid said it to a friend
cards.source: ولا تصح الكفالة إلا بقبول المكفول له في مجلس العقد
cards.why: The creditor must accept in the same sitting, and Bakr was not there.

cards.ask: A sick man says to his son, "Stand surety for my debts," and the son agrees. The creditors are not there. Is the surety valid?
options: Yes: this is the one exception
cards.source: إلا في مسألة واحدة وهي أن يقول المريض لوارثه: تكفل عني بما علي من الدين فتكفل به مع غيبة الغرماء
cards.why: A sick man asking his heir is the one case where surety is valid without the creditors present.

cards.title: Two debtors, each surety for the other
cards.ar: وإذا كان الدين على اثنين وكل واحد منهما كفيل ضامن عن الآخر
cards.en: If two people share a debt and each is surety for the other, whatever one pays is first counted as his own half. He cannot claim from his partner until he has paid more than half, and then he claims the extra.

cards.ask: Ali and Hadi owe 1000 together, 500 each, and each is surety for the other. Ali pays 700. How much can he claim from Hadi?
cards.source: لم يرجع به على شريكه حتى يزيد ما يؤديه على النصف فيرجع بالزيادة
cards.why: His own half is 500. He claims only what he paid above that: 200.

cards.title: Two sureties for one man
cards.ar: يرجع بنصفه على شريكه قليلا كان أو كثيرا ولا تجوز الكفالة بمال الكتابة حر تكفل به أو عبد
cards.en: If two people stand surety for one man's 1000, each surety for the other too, whatever one of them pays, he claims half from the other, little or much. In al-Quduri's time, no one could stand surety for the money a mukatab (a slave buying his freedom) owed for his freedom.

cards.ask: Two friends stand surety for Kamal's 1000, each also surety for the other. One friend pays 200. How much can he claim from the other friend?
cards.source: يرجع بنصفه على شريكه قليلا كان أو كثيرا
cards.why: Here each claims half of whatever he pays, little or much: half of 200 is 100.

cards.title: Surety for a man who died penniless
cards.ar: وإذا مات الرجل وعليه ديون ولم يترك شيئا فتكفل رجل عنه للغرماء لم تصح الكفالة عند أبي حنيفة وقالا: تصح
cards.en: If a man dies owing debts and leaves nothing, and someone stands surety for him to his creditors, Abu Hanifa said the surety is not valid. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad said it is.

cards.ask: Which are true of the limits of surety?

options.text: Surety for a buyer's price is valid
Release from surety can be tied to a condition
Surety needs the creditor to accept in the sitting, with one exception
Surety for hadd punishments is valid
A debtor-surety claims from his partner only beyond his half

source: وإذا تكفل عن المشتري بالثمن جاز
ولا يجوز تعليق البراءة من الكفالة بشرط
إلا في مسألة واحدة
كالحدود والقصاص
فيرجع بالزيادة
cards.why: Surety for a price is valid, it needs acceptance in the sitting (bar one case), and a debtor-surety claims only beyond his half. Release cannot hang on a condition, and punishments cannot be guaranteed.

cards.title: Moving a debt to someone else
cards.ar: الحوالة: جائزة بالديون وتصح برضا المحيل والمحتال له والمحال عليه
cards.en: Hawala is transferring a debt. The muhil is the debtor who transfers it. The muhtal is the creditor. The muhal 'alayh is the person who takes the debt on. It is allowed for debts, and needs all three to agree.

cards.ask: What is a hawala?
options: Moving a debt from one debtor to another
Standing surety to bring a person to court
Leaving goods with someone to keep them safe
cards.source: الحوالة: جائزة بالديون
cards.why: A hawala transfers a debt: the debtor moves it onto someone else.

cards.ask: Complete al-Quduri's words: whose agreement does a hawala need?
cards.ar: وتصح برضا المحيل والمحتال له و____
cards.source: وتصح برضا المحيل والمحتال له والمحال عليه
cards.why: المحال عليه: the debtor, the creditor and the one who takes on the debt must all agree.

cards.title: The first debtor is free
cards.ar: وإذا تمت الحوالة برىء المحيل من الدين ولم يرجع المحتال على المحيل
cards.en: Once the hawala is complete, the original debtor is free of the debt. The creditor cannot come back to him, unless his right is lost (tawa).

cards.ask: Ahmad owes Bilal 100. With everyone's agreement, he transfers the debt to Karim. Later Bilal asks Ahmad for the 100. Must Ahmad pay?
options: Yes: he was the first debtor
cards.source: وإذا تمت الحوالة برىء المحيل من الدين ولم يرجع المحتال على المحيل
cards.why: After a complete hawala the original debtor is free, and the creditor cannot come back to him while his right is safe.

cards.title: When the right is lost
cards.ar: والتوى عند أبي حنيفة أحد أمرين: إما أن يجحد الحوالة ويحلف ولا بينة عليه أو يموت مفلسا
cards.en: For Abu Hanifa, the right is lost (tawa) in one of two ways: the taker denies the hawala on oath and there are no witnesses, or he dies bankrupt. Then the creditor may go back to the first debtor. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad add a third: a judge declares him bankrupt in his lifetime.

cards.ask: For Abu Hanifa, in how many ways is the creditor's right lost (tawa)?
cards.source: والتوى عند أبي حنيفة أحد أمرين
cards.why: Two: the taker denies the hawala on oath with no proof against him, or he dies bankrupt.

cards.ask: For Abu Hanifa, which of these make the creditor's right lost (tawa)?

options.text: The taker denies the hawala on oath, with no proof against him
The taker dies bankrupt
A judge declares the taker bankrupt in his lifetime
The taker is slow to pay

source: والتوى عند أبي حنيفة أحد أمرين: إما أن يجحد الحوالة ويحلف ولا بينة عليه أو يموت مفلسا
وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد هاذان ووجه ثالث وهو أن يحكم الحاكم بإفلاسه في حال حياته
cards.why: Abu Hanifa names two: denial on oath with no proof, and dying bankrupt. A judge's ruling of bankruptcy is the third way that Abu Yusuf and Muhammad add.

cards.ask: Karim, who took on Ahmad's debt, dies with nothing at all. Can Bilal now go back to Ahmad for the 100?
options: Yes, as his right is lost
No: Ahmad was freed for ever
source: إلاأن يتوى حقه
أو يموت مفلسا
وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد هاذان ووجه ثالث وهو أن يحكم الحاكم بإفلاسه في حال حياته
cards.why: Dying bankrupt is one of the ways the right is lost, and then the creditor may return to the first debtor.

cards.title: When the taker claims it back
cards.ar: وإذا طالب المحال عليه المحيل بمثل مال الحواله فقال المحيل: أحلت بدين لي عليك لم يقبل قوله وكان عليه مثل الدين
cards.en: If the taker later asks the first debtor for the same amount, and the first debtor says, "I only transferred it because you owed me," his word is not accepted. He must pay back the same amount. Note: the book then begins another case, but our copy breaks off before its ruling.

cards.ask: Karim paid Bilal the 100 and now asks Ahmad for it. Ahmad says, "You owed me 100 anyway, that's why I sent the debt to you." He has no proof. What happens?
source: لم يقبل قوله وكان عليه مثل الدين
وإن طالب المحيل المحتال بما أحاله به فقال: إنما أحلتك لتقبضه لي وقال المحتال: بل أحلتني بدين
cards.why: The first debtor's claim that the taker owed him is not accepted, so he owes the same amount.

cards.ask: Which are true of hawala?

options.text: Hawala is allowed for debts
The creditor need not agree to a hawala
After a complete hawala the first debtor is free
For Abu Hanifa, dying bankrupt is one way the right is lost
The creditor may always go back to the first debtor

source: الحوالة: جائزة بالديون
والمحتال له
برىء المحيل من الدين
أو يموت مفلسا
ولم يرجع المحتال على المحيل
cards.why: Hawala is for debts, needs all three, and frees the first debtor. The creditor returns to him only if his right is lost, such as by the taker dying bankrupt.

cards.title: Admitting, staying silent, denying
cards.ar: الصلح: على ثلاثة أضرب: صلح مع إقرار وصلح مع سكوت وهو أن لا يقر المدعى عليه ولا ينكره وصلح مع إنكار وكل ذلك جائز
cards.en: Sulh is a settlement: ending a dispute by agreement. There are three kinds: with admission (the one claimed against says the claim is true), with silence (he neither admits nor denies), and with denial. All three are allowed.

cards.ask: How many kinds of settlement does al-Quduri give?
cards.source: الصلح: على ثلاثة أضرب
cards.why: Three: with admission, with silence, and with denial.

cards.ask: Which of these are al-Quduri's kinds of settlement?

options.text: With admission
With an oath
With silence
With denial
By a judge's order

cards.source: الصلح: على ثلاثة أضرب: صلح مع إقرار وصلح مع سكوت وهو أن لا يقر المدعى عليه ولا ينكره وصلح مع إنكار
cards.why: The three are settlement with admission, with silence and with denial. An oath and a judge's order are not on the list.

cards.ask: Which kind of settlement is it?
items: "Yes, I owe you. Take this car and we're done."
He says nothing either way, but pays 100 to end it
"I owe you nothing, but here is 100 to end the matter."
"You're right that the land is yours. Take 500 for it."
cards.source: صلح مع إقرار وصلح مع سكوت وهو أن لا يقر المدعى عليه ولا ينكره وصلح مع إنكار
cards.why: Admitting the claim, saying nothing either way, and denying it are the three kinds.

cards.title: A settlement with admission is a trade
cards.ar: فإن وقع الصلح عن إقرار اعتبر فيه ما يعتبر في البياعات إن وقع عن مال بمال وإن وقع عن مال بمنافع فيعتبر بالإجارات
cards.en: When the claim is admitted, the settlement follows the rules of sales if property is given for property. If property is given for a use of something (manfa'a, like living in a house or riding an animal), it follows the rules of hire (ijara).

cards.ask: Zaid admits he owes Umar 1000 dirhams. They settle: Umar may ride Zaid's camel for a month instead. Which rules does the settlement follow?
options: No rules: it is a gift
cards.source: وإن وقع عن مال بمنافع فيعتبر بالإجارات
cards.why: It was admitted, and property was settled for the use of a camel, so it follows the rules of hire.

cards.title: Silence or denial: two sides, two meanings
cards.ar: والصلح عن السكوت والإنكار في حق المدعى عليه لافتداء اليمين وقطع الخصومة وفي حق المدعي بمعنى المعاوضة
cards.en: In a settlement with silence or denial, the one claimed against is paying to avoid an oath and end the quarrel. For the claimant, it is an exchange. So a claimed house brings no shuf'a (a neighbour's or partner's right to buy it first), but a house given as the payment does.

cards.ask: Musa claims a house from Harun, who denies it. Harun settles by giving Musa a different house. Does a neighbour have pre-emption in the house Musa receives?
options: Yes: a house given as the payment brings pre-emption
cards.source: وإذا صالح عن دار لم تجب فيه شفعة وإذا صالح على دار وجبت فيها الشفعة
cards.why: For the claimant, the settlement is an exchange, so a house received as payment brings pre-emption. The claimed house, which Harun keeps, does not.

cards.title: If someone else owns part of it
cards.ar: وإذا كان الصلح عن إقرار فاستحق بعض المصالح عنه رجع المدعى عليه بحصة ذلك من العوض
cards.en: In a settlement with admission, if part of the thing settled over turns out to belong to a third person, the one who paid takes back that part's share of the payment.

cards.ask: Hamza admits Nuh's claim to 10 goats and pays 500 dirhams to settle. Later, 2 of the goats are proved to belong to someone else. What does Hamza get back?
cards.source: رجع المدعى عليه بحصة ذلك من العوض
cards.why: He gets back the share of the payment for the 2 goats: 2 out of 10 of 500 is 100.

cards.title: After a denial
cards.ar: وإن وقع الصلح عن سكوت أو إنكار فاستحق المتنازع فيه رجع المدعي بالخصومة ورد العوض
cards.en: In a settlement with silence or denial, if the thing argued over turns out to belong to a third person, the claimant returns the payment and takes his quarrel to that person instead. If only part of it does, he returns that part's share.

cards.ask: Salih claims "a right" in a house without saying what. Settling, Fadl pays him 100. Later part of the house is proved to be someone else's. Must Salih give anything back?
options: No: his right may be in what remains
Yes, a share for the lost part
cards.source: وإن ادعى حقا في دار لم يبينه فصولح من ذلك على شيء ثم استحق بعض الدار لم يرد شيئا من العوض لأن دعواه يجوز أن تكون فيما بقي
cards.why: He never said which part his right was in, so it may be in what remains. He gives nothing back.

cards.ask: Which can be settled?

options.text: A claim to money
A claim to the use of a house
A claim over a deliberate injury
A claim over an accidental injury
A claim of a hadd (a fixed Sharia punishment)

source: والصلح جائز من دعوى الأموال والمنافع
العمد والخطإ ولا يجوز من دعوى حد
cards.why: Claims to money, uses, and deliberate or accidental harm may be settled. A hadd punishment may not.

cards.title: Claims of marriage
cards.ar: وإذا ادعى رجل على امرأة نكاحا وهي تجحد فصالحته على مال بذلته حتى يترك الدعوى جاز وكان في معنى الخلع وإن ادعت امرأة نكاحا على رجل فصالحها على مال بذله لها لم تجز
cards.en: If a man claims a woman is his wife and she denies it, she may pay him to drop the claim. It is like khul' (a wife paying to end a marriage). But if a woman claims a man is her husband, he may not pay her to drop it.

cards.ask: Is this settlement allowed?
items: A man claims she is his wife; she pays him to drop it
A woman claims he is her husband; he pays her to drop it
In al-Quduri's time, a man claims another is his slave; the other pays him to drop it
source: حتى يترك الدعوى جاز وكان في معنى الخلع
فصالحها على مال بذله لها لم تجز
وإن ادعى على رجل أنه عبده فصالحته على مال أعطاه جاز وكان في حق المدعي في معنى العتق على مال
cards.why: The woman paying is like khul', and the man paying to end a claim that he is a slave is like freeing for money. The man paying off a woman's marriage claim is not allowed.

cards.title: Taking less of a debt is not a swap
cards.ar: وكل شيء وقع عليه الصلح وهو مستحق بعقد المداينة
cards.en: When a settlement is over a debt, and what he takes is something the debt already owed him, it is not treated as a swap. It is as if he took part of his right and let go of the rest.

cards.title: Less, poorer, or later
cards.ar: جياد فصالحه على خمسمائة زيوف جاز وصار كأنه أبرأه عن بعض حقه وأخذ باقيه ولو صالحه على ألف مؤجل جاز وصار كأنه أجل نفس الحق
cards.en: Someone is owed 1000 good dirhams and settles for 500 poor-quality ones (zuyuf). That is allowed: it is as if he let go of part and took the rest. If he settles for the 1000 paid later, that is allowed too: he has simply given more time.

cards.ask: Ilyas is owed 1000 good dirhams. He agrees to take 500 poor-quality dirhams to settle it. Is it allowed?
options: Yes: he takes part and forgives the rest
No: the coins must be the same quality
source: وإنما يحمل على أنه استوفى بعض حقه
وصار كأنه أبرأه عن بعض حقه وأخذ باقيه
cards.why: Less and poorer is still within what he was owed, so it counts as taking part and forgiving the rest.

cards.ask: Someone is owed money and settles like this. Is it allowed?
items: 1000 good dirhams settled for 500 poor ones
1000 due now settled for 1000 due in a month
1000 dirhams settled for dinars due in a month
1000 due later settled for 500 paid now
1000 black dirhams settled for 500 white ones
source: جاز وصار كأنه أبرأه عن بعض حقه
ولو صالحه على ألف مؤجل جاز
ولو صالحه على دنانير إلى شهر لم يجز ولو كان له ألف مؤجلة فصالحه على خمسمائة حالة لم يجز ولو كان له ألف سود فصالحه على خمسمائة بيض لم يجز
cards.why: Taking less, poorer, or later is allowed. Dinars later, paying early for less, or better coins all bring in something he was not owed, and are not allowed.

cards.title: An agent who settles
cards.ar: ومن وكل رجلا بالصلح عنه فصالحه لم يلزم الوكيل ما صالح عليه إلا أن يضمنه والمال لازم للموكل
cards.en: If you appoint an agent to settle for you, he does not owe the settlement money unless he guaranteed it. The money is owed by you, the principal.

cards.ask: Qasim's agent settles a claim against him for 2000. The claimant asks the agent for the money. Must the agent pay it?
cards.source: لم يلزم الوكيل ما صالح عليه إلا أن يضمنه والمال لازم للموكل
cards.why: The settlement money is owed by the principal. The agent owes it only if he guaranteed it.

cards.title: Someone settles without being asked
cards.ar: فإن صالح عنه على شيء بغير أمره فهو على أربعة أوجه: إن صالح بمال وضمنه تم الصلح
cards.en: If an outsider settles for someone without being asked, there are four cases. The settlement is complete if he guarantees the money, or says "I settle with you for this 1000 of mine," or names 1000 and hands it over. If he names 1000 but does not hand it over, the settlement waits for the person claimed against.

cards.ask: An outsider settles for someone without being asked. In how many ways does al-Quduri set out the case?
cards.source: فإن صالح عنه على شيء بغير أمره فهو على أربعة أوجه
cards.why: Al-Quduri says such a settlement falls into four cases.

cards.ask: An outsider settles for someone without being asked. In which of these cases is the settlement complete?

options.text: He guarantees the money
He says, "I settle with you for this 1000 of mine"
He names 1000 and hands it over
He names 1000 but does not hand it over

source: إن صالح بمال وضمنه تم الصلح
وكذلك لو قال: صالحتك على ألفي هذه تم الصلح ولزمه تسليمها وكذلك لو قال: صالحتك على ألف وسلمها
وإن قال: صالحتك على ألف ولم يسلمها فالعقد موقوف
cards.why: Guaranteeing, naming his own 1000, or naming 1000 and handing it over completes it. Naming 1000 without handing it over leaves it waiting on the one claimed against.

cards.ask: Without being asked, Nadir says to a claimant, "I settle with you for 1000 on Rafi's behalf," but pays nothing. Rafi hears of it and refuses. What happens?
source: وكذلك لو قال: صالحتك على ألفي هذه تم الصلح ولزمه تسليمها وكذلك لو قال: صالحتك على ألف وسلمها
وإن قال: صالحتك على ألف ولم يسلمها فالعقد موقوف: فإن أجازه المدعى عليه جاز ولزمه الألف وإن لم يجزه بطل
cards.why: Naming 1000 without handing it over leaves the settlement waiting. If Rafi approves, he owes the 1000; since he refused, it is void.

cards.ask: Which are true of settling claims and debts?

options.text: A woman may pay a man to drop his claim that she is his wife
Settling 1000 for 1000 paid later is allowed
An agent who settles always owes the money himself
Settling a debt due later for less paid now is allowed
An outsider who guarantees the money completes the settlement

source: وكان في معنى الخلع
ولو صالحه على ألف مؤجل جاز
إلا أن يضمنه
فصالحه على خمسمائة حالة لم يجز
إن صالح بمال وضمنه تم الصلح
cards.why: The woman's payment is like khul', giving more time is allowed, and an outsider's guarantee completes it. An agent owes only if he guaranteed, and paying early for less is not allowed.

cards.title: One partner settles his share
cards.ar: وإذا كان الدين بين شريكين فصالح أحدهما من نصيبه على ثوب فشريكه بالخيار: إن شاء اتبع عليه الدين بنصفه وإن شاء أخذ نصف الثوب إلا أن يضمن له شريكه ربع الدين
cards.en: Two partners are owed a debt together. One settles his share for a cloth. His partner may choose: go after the debtor for his own half, or take half the cloth. Unless the first partner pays him a quarter of the debt instead.

cards.ask: Ali and Umar are owed 1000 by Zaid, half each. Ali settles his 500 share for a fine cloth. Ali wants to keep the whole cloth. What must he pay Umar?
cards.source: إلا أن يضمن له شريكه ربع الدين
cards.why: Umar could take half the cloth, unless Ali pays him a quarter of the debt: a quarter of 1000 is 250.

cards.title: If one partner collects some
cards.ar: ولو استوفى نصف نصيبه من الدين كان لشريكه أن يشركه فيما قبض ثم يرجعان على الغريم بالباقي
cards.en: If one partner collects half his share, the other partner may share in what he collected. Then both go after the debtor for the rest. If one partner buys goods from the debtor with his share, his partner may make him pay a quarter of the debt.

cards.ask: Ali collects 250 of his 500 share from Zaid. What may Umar do?
options: Nothing: Ali collected his own share
source: كان لشريكه أن يشركه فيما قبض ثم يرجعان على الغريم بالباقي
ولو اشترى أحدهما نصيبه من الدين سلعة كان لشريكه أن يضمنه ربع الدين
cards.why: What one partner collects of a shared debt may be shared by the other, and then they both claim the rest.

cards.title: A shared salam
cards.ar: وإذا كان السلم بين شريكين فصالح أحدهما من نصيبه على رأس المال لم يجز عند أبي حنيفة ومحمد رحمهما الله وقال أبو يوسف رحمه الله: يجوز الصلح
cards.en: In a salam, the buyer pays now for goods delivered later. If two partners made a salam together and one settles his share by taking back his money, Abu Hanifa and Muhammad said it is not allowed. Note: Abu Yusuf said the settlement is allowed.

cards.title: Buying out an heir
cards.ar: وإذا كانت التركة بين ورثة فأخرجوا أحدهم منها بمال أعطوه إياه والتركة عقار أو عروض جاز قليلا كان ما أعطوه أو كثيرا
cards.en: The tarika is what a dead person leaves behind. If the heirs pay one heir to leave the inheritance to them, and it is land or goods, that is allowed, whether they pay him a little or a lot. The same if it is all silver and they pay him gold, or all gold and they pay him silver.

cards.ask: An estate is a house and its furniture. The other heirs pay Fatima 2000 dirhams to step out of the inheritance. Is it allowed?
options: Yes, whether 2000 is little or a lot
Only if 2000 equals her share exactly
No: heirs cannot be bought out
source: والتركة عقار أو عروض جاز قليلا كان ما أعطوه أو كثيرا
وإن كانت التركة فضة فأعطوه ذهبا أو كانت ذهبا فأعطوه فضة فهو كذلك
cards.why: For land or goods, buying an heir out is allowed for any amount.

cards.title: An estate of gold, silver and more
cards.ar: وإن كانت التركة ذهبا وفضة وغير ذلك فصالحوه على فضة أو ذهب فلا بد أن يكون ما أعطوه أكثر من نصيبه من ذلك الجنس حتى يكون نصيبه بمثله والزيادة بحقه من بقية الميراث
cards.en: If the estate has gold, silver and other things, and they pay him in silver (or gold), they must give him more than his share of that metal. Then his share of the metal is matched by the same amount, and the extra is for his share of everything else.

cards.ask: An estate has silver and land. Hasan's share of the silver is 300 dirhams. The others pay him in silver to leave. Which payment works?
cards.source: فلا بد أن يكون ما أعطوه أكثر من نصيبه من ذلك الجنس
cards.why: He must get more than his 300 of silver: 300 matches his silver, and the extra is for his share of the land.

cards.title: Debts owed to the estate
cards.ar: وإن كان في التركة دين على الناس فأدخلوه في الصلح على أن يخرجوا المصالح عنه ويكون الدين لهم فالصلح باطل
cards.en: If people owe debts to the estate and the heirs include those debts in the buy-out, so that the debts become theirs, the settlement is void. But if they agree that he lets the debtors off his part, without claiming his share from them, it is allowed.

cards.ask: Is the settlement valid?
items: Heirs pay one heir any sum for his share of land
An estate of only gold, the heir is paid in silver
The heirs take over his share of debts owed to the estate
He lets the debtors off his part of their debts
Estate of silver and land, he gets less silver than his silver share
source: جاز قليلا كان ما أعطوه أو كثيرا
أو كانت ذهبا فأعطوه فضة فهو كذلك
ويكون الدين لهم فالصلح باطل
فإن شرطوا أن يبرئ الغرماء منه ولا يرجع عليهم بنصيب المصالح فالصلح جائز
أكثر من نصيبه من ذلك الجنس
cards.why: Any sum for land, gold for silver, and letting the debtors off are fine. Taking over his share of the debts is void, and silver must be more than his silver share.

lessons.title: Making a gift: the words and taking it

cards.title: Offer and acceptance
cards.ar: الهبة: تصح بالإيجاب والقبول
cards.en: A hiba is a gift: giving something you own to someone for free. It is made by an offer (ijab) from the giver, such as "I give you this", and an acceptance (qabul) from the one who receives it. It is completed when he takes possession of it (qabd).

cards.title: Taking it in the same sitting
cards.ar: فإذا قبض الموهوب له في المجلس بغير أمر الواهب جاز وإن قبض بعد الافتراق لم تصح إلا أن يأذن له الواهب في القبض
cards.en: If the receiver takes the gift in the same sitting (majlis), it is valid, even if the giver did not tell him to take it. If he takes it after they have parted, it does not count unless the giver gave him permission to take it.

cards.ask: Yusuf says to Hamza, "I give you my watch," and Hamza accepts. They part. Next day Hamza picks the watch up from Yusuf's desk without asking. Is the gift complete?
options: No, not without the giver's permission
Yes: he had already accepted it the day before
cards.source: وإن قبض بعد الافتراق لم تصح إلا أن يأذن له الواهب في القبض
cards.why: After the two have parted, taking the gift only counts if the giver allows it. Yusuf did not.

cards.title: The words of a gift
cards.ar: وتنعقد الهبة بقوله: وهبت ونحلت وأعطيت وأطعمتك هذا الطعام وجعلت هذا الثوب لك وأعمرتك هذا الشيء وحملتك على هذه الدابة إذا نوى بالحملان الهبة
cards.en: A gift is made with words like "I have given you" (wahabtu, nahaltu, a'taytu), "I have fed you this food", "I have made this garment yours", "This thing is yours for life". "I have mounted you on this animal" is a gift only if he means a gift by it, not just a ride.

cards.ask: Which of these make a gift?

options.text: "I have given you this" (wahabtu)
"I have made this garment yours"
"This thing is yours for life"
"I have mounted you on this animal", meaning only a ride
"I have fed you this food"

cards.source: وتنعقد الهبة بقوله: وهبت ونحلت وأعطيت وأطعمتك هذا الطعام وجعلت هذا الثوب لك وأعمرتك هذا الشيء وحملتك على هذه الدابة إذا نوى بالحملان الهبة
cards.why: All these words make a gift, but mounting someone on an animal is a gift only when the giver means it as one.

cards.title: Things that can be divided
cards.ar: ولا تجوز الهبة فيما يقسم إلا محوزة مقسومة وهبة المشاع فيما لا يقسم جائزة
cards.en: Something that can be divided, like a big field or a sack of rice, may only be given once the gifted part is split off and held on its own. A share (musha', shared and not split) of something that cannot be divided, like one small room or one animal, may be given.

cards.title: A share, then divided
cards.ar: ومن وهب شقصا مشاعا فالهبة فاسدة فإن قسمه وسلمه جاز
cards.en: If someone gives an undivided share of something that can be divided, the gift is fasid (faulty, not valid as it stands). If he then divides it and hands it over, it becomes valid.

cards.ask: Omar owns a large field. He gives his brother "half of my field" without marking which half. Later he divides the field and hands his brother one half. What is the gift now?
options: Valid, now that it is split off
Still fasid, as it began shared
source: ومن وهب شقصا مشاعا فالهبة فاسدة
فإن قسمه وسلمه جاز
cards.why: A share of a field that can be divided is fasid, but once he divides it and hands it over, the gift is valid.

cards.title: Flour still in the wheat
cards.ar: ولو وهب دقيقا في حنطة أو دهنا في سمسم فالهبة فاسدة
cards.en: Giving flour that is still in the wheat (not yet ground), or oil still in the sesame seeds, is fasid. Even if he later grinds it and hands it over, it does not become valid, because the thing he named did not exist yet when he gave it.

cards.ask: Valid gift or not?
items: A share in one small room that cannot be divided
Half of a big field, not split off
Half of a big field, later divided and handed over
"The flour in this wheat", later ground and handed over
A book taken in the same sitting, without being told to
source: وهبة المشاع فيما لا يقسم جائزة
ولا تجوز الهبة فيما يقسم إلا محوزة مقسومة
فإن قسمه وسلمه جاز
طحن وسلم لم يجز
فإذا قبض الموهوب له في المجلس بغير أمر الواهب جاز
cards.why: A share is fine in what cannot be divided, and in what can once it is divided and handed over. Flour in wheat stays invalid even after grinding. Taking it in the sitting is enough.

lessons.title: Who takes the gift
lessons.arabic: وإذا وهب الأب لابنه الصغير هبة ملكها الابن بالعقد

cards.title: Already in his hand
cards.ar: وإذا كانت العين في يد الموهوب ملكها بالهبة
cards.en: If the thing is already in the receiver's hand, for example he borrowed it, he owns it by the gift alone. He does not need to hand it back and take it again.

cards.ask: Bilal has borrowed Adam's book. Adam says, "Keep it, it is a gift," and Bilal accepts. Must Bilal give it back and take it again for the gift to be complete?
options: Yes, he must hand it back and take it again
No, but the gift is fasid
cards.source: وإذا كانت العين في يد الموهوب ملكها بالهبة
cards.why: The book is already in Bilal's hand, so the gift makes it his without taking it again.

cards.title: A father's gift to his small son
cards.ar: وإذا وهب الأب لابنه الصغير هبة ملكها الابن بالعقد فإن وهب له أجنبي هبة تمت بقبض الأب
cards.en: When a father gives his small son a gift, the son owns it by the words of the contract alone. If an outsider (ajnabi, someone other than the father) gives the child a gift, it is complete when the father takes it for him.

cards.ask: Ibrahim says to his six-year-old son, "I give you this tablet." The tablet stays on Ibrahim's desk. Whose is it?
options: The son's, by the words alone
Still Ibrahim's until the son picks it up
cards.source: وإذا وهب الأب لابنه الصغير هبة ملكها الابن بالعقد
cards.why: A father's gift to his small son is owned by the contract itself; no taking is needed.

cards.title: An orphan's gift
cards.ar: وإذا وهب لليتيم هبة فقبضها له وليه جاز
cards.en: An orphan (yatim) is a child whose father has died. His wali (guardian) may take a gift for him. If he lives in his mother's care, she may take it for him, and so may an outsider who is raising him. And a child who understands may take the gift himself.

cards.ask: Musa is an orphan who lives with his mother. A neighbour gives him a bicycle. Who may take it for him?

options.text: His wali (guardian)
His mother, who looks after him
Musa himself
A passer-by who does not look after him
No one: an orphan cannot be given gifts

source: وإذا وهب لليتيم هبة فقبضها له وليه جاز
كان في حجر أمه فقبضها له جائز وكذلك إن كان في حجر أجنبي يربيه فقبضه له جائز
وإن قبض الصبي الهبة بنفسه له جاز
cards.why: His guardian, the one raising him (here his mother), or the child himself may take it. A stranger who does not raise him may not.

cards.title: Two givers, two receivers
cards.ar: وإن وهب اثنان من واحد دارا جاز وإن وهب واحد من اثنين دارا لم يصح عند أبي حنيفة وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد: يصح
cards.en: Two people may give one house together to one person. But one person giving one house to two people is not valid according to Abu Hanifa, because each would receive an undivided share. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say it is valid.

cards.ask: Two brothers own a house together. They give it together to their cousin Tariq. Is the gift valid?
options: Not valid, because it is shared
Valid for one brother's half only
cards.source: وإن وهب اثنان من واحد دارا جاز
cards.why: Two givers to one receiver is valid: Tariq receives the whole house.

cards.ask: One man gives his house to two people. What does Abu Hanifa say? Complete it.
cards.ar: وإن وهب واحد من اثنين دارا ____ عند أبي حنيفة
cards.source: وإن وهب واحد من اثنين دارا لم يصح عند أبي حنيفة
cards.why: لم يصح: according to Abu Hanifa, one giver to two receivers is not valid.

cards.ask: Is the gift valid and complete?
items: A father gives his small son a toy that stays on the shelf
An uncle gives a child money, and the child's father takes it for him
A friend gives Ali the coat he is already borrowing
One man gives his one house to two friends (Abu Hanifa)
source: ملكها الابن بالعقد فإن وهب له أجنبي هبة تمت بقبض الأب
وإذا كانت العين في يد الموهوب ملكها بالهبة
وإن وهب واحد من اثنين دارا لم يصح عند أبي حنيفة
cards.why: The father's own gift is complete by the words, an outsider's by the father taking it, and a thing already in hand needs no new taking. One house to two people is not valid for Abu Hanifa.

lessons.title: Taking a gift back
lessons.arabic: وإذا وهب هبة لأجنبي فله الرجوع فيها

cards.title: When a gift can be taken back
cards.ar: وإذا وهب هبة لأجنبي فله الرجوع فيها إلا أن يعوضه عنها أو تزيد زيادة متصلة أو يموت أحد المتعاقدين أو تخرج الهبة من ملك الموهوب له
cards.en: If someone gives a gift to an outsider (not a close relative), he may take it back (ruju'), unless: the receiver gave something in return ('iwad); the gift grew with an increase joined to it, like a building on land; one of the two died; or the gift left the receiver's ownership, say by a sale.

cards.ask: Which of these stop the giver from taking his gift back?

options.text: The receiver gave him something in return
The receiver built a room onto the gifted land
The receiver has died
The receiver has sold it
The giver has changed his mind
The receiver is rich

cards.source: إلا أن يعوضه عنها أو تزيد زيادة متصلة أو يموت أحد المتعاقدين أو تخرج الهبة من ملك الموهوب له
cards.why: A return gift, a joined increase, the death of either one, or the gift leaving the receiver's ownership all block taking it back. Changing one's mind does not.

cards.title: Close relatives and spouses
cards.ar: وإن وهب هبة لذي رحم محرم منه فلا رجوع فيها وكذلك ما وهب أحد الزوجين لآخر
cards.en: There is no taking back a gift given to a close relative whom one may never marry (dhu rahim mahram), like a brother, sister, aunt or nephew. The same goes for a gift between husband and wife.

cards.ask: Can the giver take it back?
items: A gift to a friend, unchanged, with nothing given in return
A gift to a neighbour who has since sold it
A gift to a work colleague, still unchanged
source: وإذا وهب هبة لأجنبي فله الرجوع فيها
وإن وهب هبة لذي رحم محرم منه فلا رجوع فيها وكذلك ما وهب أحد الزوجين لآخر
تخرج الهبة من ملك الموهوب له
cards.why: Gifts to outsiders can be taken back unless something blocks it, like a sale. Gifts to close mahram relatives and between spouses cannot.

cards.title: A gift in return
cards.ar: وإذا قال الموهوب له للواهب: خذ هذا عوضا عن هبتك أو بدلا عنها أو في مقابلتها فقبضه الواهب سقط الرجوع وإن عوضه أجنبي عن الموهوب له متبرعا فقبض الواهب العوض سقط الرجوع
cards.en: If the receiver says, "Take this in return for your gift" (or "in exchange for it"), and the giver takes it, the right to take back is gone. It is the same if an outsider gives the return on the receiver's behalf, freely, and the giver takes it.

cards.ask: Sara gave her friend a bracelet. The friend's father kindly gives Sara a scarf "in return for the bracelet", and Sara takes it. Can Sara take the bracelet back?
options: No, the return was given and taken
Yes, because the father was not the receiver
Yes, as long as she gives the scarf back
cards.source: وإن عوضه أجنبي عن الموهوب له متبرعا فقبض الواهب العوض سقط الرجوع
cards.why: A return given freely by someone else on the receiver's behalf still ends the right to take back, once the giver takes it.

cards.title: Only by agreement or a judge
cards.ar: ولا يصح الرجوع إلا بتراضيهما أو بحكم الحاكم
cards.en: Even where taking back is allowed, it only happens when both agree, or by a judge's ruling.

cards.ask: Khalid gave his friend a bike and now wants it back. Nothing blocks it, but the friend refuses and no judge has ruled. Can Khalid just take it?
options: No, only by agreement or a judge's ruling
Yes, a giver may always take his gift
Yes, if he leaves some money
cards.source: ولا يصح الرجوع إلا بتراضيهما أو بحكم الحاكم
cards.why: Taking back is only valid with both agreeing or by a judge's ruling.

cards.title: When someone else proves it is his
cards.ar: وإذا استحق نصف الهبة رجع بنصف العوض وإن استحق نصف العوض لم يرجع في الهبة إلا أن يرد ما بقي من العوض ثم يرجع
cards.en: Sometimes a third person proves a thing was really his (istihqaq). If half the gift is proven someone else's, the receiver takes back half of what he gave in return. If half the return is proven someone else's, the giver can only take back the gift after giving back the rest of the return.

cards.ask: Rami gave Hadi a field, and Hadi gave him a horse in return. Then half the field is proven to be someone else's. What may Hadi do?
options: Take back half the value of the horse
Take back the whole horse he gave
cards.source: وإذا استحق نصف الهبة رجع بنصف العوض
cards.why: When half the gift is proven to belong to someone else, the receiver takes back half of what he gave in return.

cards.title: A gift on condition of a return
cards.ar: وإذا وهب بشرط العوض اعتبر التقابض في العوضين وإذا تقابضا صح العقد وصار في حكم البيع: يرد بالعيب وخيار الرؤية
cards.en: If he gives on condition of getting something back, both things must be handed over. Once they are, it counts like a sale: it can be returned for a defect, there is the option of seeing (khiyar al-ru'ya: cancelling when you first see it), and shuf'a applies (a neighbour or partner's right to take it first).

cards.ask: Hadi gives Rami his house "on condition you give me your car", and both are handed over. Later Rami finds a hidden crack in the walls. What can he do?
options: Return it for the defect, as in a sale
Nothing: a gift cannot be returned
Only take it back with the judge's ruling
source: وإذا تقابضا صح العقد وصار في حكم البيع: يرد بالعيب
وإذا تلفت العين الموهوبة فاستحقها مستحق فضمن الموهوب له لم يرجع على الواهب
cards.why: A gift for a return, once both sides are handed over, is treated as a sale, so a defect lets him return it.

cards.title: A gift for life ('umra)
cards.ar: والعمرى جائزة للمعمر في حال حياته ولورثته من بعده
cards.en: An 'umra is saying "This is yours for your lifetime." It is valid: the thing is his while he lives, and goes to his heirs after him.

cards.title: Ruqba
cards.ar: والرقبى باطلة عند أبي حنيفة ومحمد وقال أبو يوسف: جائزة
cards.en: A ruqba is saying "If I die first it is yours, and if you die first it comes back to me." It is invalid according to Abu Hanifa and Muhammad. Note: Abu Yusuf says it is valid.

cards.ask: Grandmother says to Ali, "This house is yours for your lifetime." Ali later dies. Who gets the house?
options: Grandmother, because it was only for his life
cards.source: والعمرى جائزة للمعمر في حال حياته ولورثته من بعده
cards.why: An 'umra belongs to the receiver for life and to his heirs after him.

cards.ask: What is a ruqba, according to Abu Hanifa and Muhammad? Complete it.
cards.ar: والرقبى ____ عند أبي حنيفة ومحمد
cards.source: والرقبى باطلة عند أبي حنيفة ومحمد
cards.why: باطلة: a ruqba is invalid for Abu Hanifa and Muhammad.

cards.title: Excluding the unborn
cards.ar: ومن وهب جارية إلا حملها صحت الهبة وبطل الاستثناء
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time, if someone gave a slave woman but said "except the child she is carrying", the gift was valid and the exception was cancelled, so the unborn child went with the gift.

cards.title: Charity is like a gift
cards.ar: والصدقة كالهبة: لا تصح إلا بالقبض ولا تجوز في مشاع يحتمل القسمة
cards.en: Sadaqa is charity given for Allah. It is like a gift: it is only complete when taken, and it cannot be an undivided share of something that can be divided. It may be given to two poor people together. And once it is taken, it can never be taken back.

cards.ask: Amina gives 50 dirhams as sadaqa to a poor man, who takes it. Next day she regrets it. Can she take it back?
options: No, charity cannot be taken back once it is taken
Yes, just like a gift to an outsider
Yes, if he has not spent it yet
source: ولا يجوز الرجوع في الصدقة بعد القبض
وإذا تصدق على فقيرين
cards.why: Unlike a gift to an outsider, charity can never be taken back after the poor man takes it.

cards.title: A vow to give your wealth
cards.ar: ومن نذر أن يتصدق بماله لزمه أن يتصدق بجنس ما تجب فيه الزكاة
cards.en: A nadhr is a vow: promising Allah to do a good deed. If someone vows to give "his wealth" (mal) in charity, he must give the kinds of wealth that zakat (the yearly charity due on wealth) is due on.

cards.title: A vow to give everything he owns
cards.ar: ومن نذر أن يتصدق بملكه لزمه أن يتصدق بالجميع ويقال له: أمسك منه مقدار ما تنفقه على نفسك وعيالك إلى أن تكسب مالا فإذا اكتسبت مالا تصدق بمثل ما أمسكت لنفسك
cards.en: If he vows to give "everything I own" (milk), he must give all of it. But he is told: keep back enough to spend on yourself and your family until you earn money; when you earn, give the same amount you kept.

cards.ask: Faisal vows, "I will give everything I own in charity." He has a wife and children. What is he told?
options: Give all, but keep enough to live on
Give only the kinds that zakat is due on
Nothing: such a vow does not count
cards.source: ومن نذر أن يتصدق بملكه لزمه أن يتصدق بالجميع ويقال له: أمسك منه مقدار ما تنفقه على نفسك وعيالك
cards.why: A vow of everything he owns covers all of it, but he keeps enough to live on and gives its like once he earns.

cards.ask: Which are true of 'umra and charity?

options.text: An 'umra goes to the receiver's heirs after him
Charity can be given to two poor people together
Charity is complete only when it is taken
Charity can be taken back after it is taken
In a gift that excludes the unborn child, the exception stands

source: والعمرى جائزة للمعمر في حال حياته ولورثته من بعده
وإذا تصدق على فقيرين
والصدقة كالهبة: لا تصح إلا بالقبض
ولا يجوز الرجوع في الصدقة بعد القبض
صحت الهبة وبطل الاستثناء
cards.why: The first three are in the text. Charity cannot be taken back once taken, and the exception of the unborn child is cancelled.

lessons.title: When an endowment leaves its owner
lessons.arabic: لا يزول ملك الواقف عن الوقف

cards.title: When a waqf is binding
cards.ar: لا يزول ملك الواقف عن الوقف عند أبي حنيفة إلا أن يحكم به الحاكم أو يعلقه بموته فيقول: إذا مت فقد وقفت داري على كذا
cards.en: A waqf (endowment) is setting property aside so that its use or income goes to a good cause for ever. According to Abu Hanifa, the founder (waqif) still owns it unless a judge rules it a waqf, or he ties it to his death by saying: "When I die, my house is a waqf for such-and-such."

cards.title: The two companions
cards.ar: وقال أبو يوسف: يزول الملك بمجرد القول وقال محمد: لا يزول الملك حتى يجعل للوقف وليا ويسلمه إليه
cards.en: Note: Abu Yusuf says the ownership ends by the words alone. Muhammad says it does not end until the founder appoints a manager (wali) for the waqf and hands it over to him.

cards.ask: Hasan says, "My shop is a waqf for the poor." No judge has ruled on it, and he did not tie it to his death. According to Abu Hanifa, whose is the shop?
cards.source: لا يزول ملك الواقف عن الوقف عند أبي حنيفة إلا أن يحكم به الحاكم أو يعلقه بموته
cards.why: For Abu Hanifa the words alone do not take it out of his ownership; a judge's ruling or tying it to his death does.

cards.ask: According to Abu Hanifa, which of these make the waqf binding?

options.text: A judge rules that it is a waqf
He says, "When I die, my house is a waqf for the poor"
He tells his friends that it is a waqf
He puts up a sign saying "Waqf"

cards.source: إلا أن يحكم به الحاكم أو يعلقه بموته فيقول: إذا مت فقد وقفت داري على كذا
cards.why: Only a judge's ruling or tying it to his death; telling people or putting up a sign is still just words.

cards.title: Out of everyone's ownership
cards.ar: وإذا صح الوقف - على اختلافهم - خرج عن ملك الواقف ولم يدخل في ملك الموقوف عليه ووقف المشاع جائز عند أبي يوسف وقال محمد: لا يجوز
cards.en: Once the waqf is valid (by whichever of their views), it leaves the founder's ownership, and it does not become the property of those it is for (the beneficiaries). Note: Abu Yusuf allows a waqf of an undivided share; Muhammad does not.

cards.title: It cannot be sold
cards.ar: لم يجز بيعه ولا تمليكه إلا أن يكون مشاعا عند أبي يوسف فيطلب الشريك القسمة فتصح مقاسمته
cards.en: Once a waqf is valid, it cannot be sold or handed over as anyone's property. The one exception (on Abu Yusuf's view) is an undivided share whose partner asks for it to be divided: then it may be divided.

cards.ask: A valid waqf of an orchard is made for students. The students want to sell it and share the money. Can they?
options: No, a waqf cannot be sold
Yes, if all the students agree to it
source: ولم يدخل في ملك الموقوف عليه
لم يجز بيعه ولا تمليكه
cards.why: The orchard did not become the students' property, and a valid waqf cannot be sold.

cards.title: It must end in a cause that never ends
cards.ar: ولا يتم الوقف عند أبي حنيفة ومحمد حتى يجعل آخره لجهة لا تنقطع أبدا
cards.en: According to Abu Hanifa and Muhammad, a waqf is not complete until its last beneficiary is a cause that never ends, like the poor. Note: Abu Yusuf says if he names a cause that can end, it is valid, and after it the waqf goes to the poor even if he did not name them.

cards.ask: Layla makes a waqf "for my three nephews" and says nothing about after them. According to Abu Hanifa, what is it?
options: Not complete: it needs an unending cause
Complete, and it goes back to her after them
Complete, and it belongs to the nephews
cards.source: ولا يتم الوقف عند أبي حنيفة ومحمد حتى يجعل آخره لجهة لا تنقطع أبدا
cards.why: Three nephews will one day be gone, so without an unending cause at the end, the waqf is not complete.

cards.title: What can be a waqf
cards.ar: ويصح وقف العقار ولا يجوز وقف ما ينقل ويحول وقال أبو يوسف: إذا وقف ضيعة ببقرها وهم عبيده جاز وقال محمد: يجوز حبس الكراع والسلاح
cards.en: A waqf of 'aqar (land and buildings) is valid; a waqf of things that can be moved is not. Note: Abu Yusuf allows a farm to be made a waqf along with its oxen and, in al-Quduri's time, the slaves who worked it. Muhammad allows horses and weapons to be set aside.

cards.ask: Can it be made a waqf, by the basic rule?
source: ويصح وقف العقار ولا يجوز وقف ما ينقل ويحول
لا يزول ملك الواقف عن الوقف عند أبي حنيفة
cards.why: Land and buildings can be a waqf; things you can pick up and move cannot.

lessons.title: Repairs, mosques and wells
lessons.arabic: أن يبدأ من ريع الوقف بعمارته

cards.title: Repairs come first
cards.ar: والواجب: أن يبدأ من ريع الوقف بعمارته شرط الواقف ذلك أو لم يشرط
cards.en: The income (ri') of a waqf is spent first on keeping it in repair ('imara), whether the founder made that a condition or not.

cards.ask: A waqf shop earns 1,000 dirhams of rent this year. Its roof needs 300 dirhams of repairs. The founder never mentioned repairs. What comes first?
options: Fixing the roof from the rent
Waiting for the founder to pay
cards.source: والواجب: أن يبدأ من ريع الوقف بعمارته شرط الواقف ذلك أو لم يشرط
cards.why: Repairs come first from the income, whether or not the founder said so.

cards.title: A house to live in
cards.ar: وإن وقف دارا على سكنى ولده فالعمارة على من له السكنى فإن امتنع من ذلك أو كان فقيرا أجرها الحاكم وعمرها بأجرتها فإذا عمرت
cards.en: If he makes a house a waqf for his child to live in, the repairs are on the one who lives there. If he refuses, or is too poor, the judge rents it out and repairs it from the rent. Once it is repaired, it goes back to the one who has the right to live there.

cards.ask: The son living in a waqf house refuses to repair it. Put what happens in order.
steps: The judge rents the house out
The repairs are paid from the rent
The house goes back to the son to live in
source: فإن امتنع من ذلك أو كان فقيرا أجرها الحاكم وعمرها بأجرتها فإذا عمرت
إلى من له السكنى
cards.why: The judge rents it, repairs it from the rent, and then returns it to the one who has the right to live in it.

cards.title: Fallen bricks and timber
cards.ar: وما انهدم من بناء الوقف وآلته صرفه الحاكم في عمارة الوقف إن احتاج إليه وإن استغنى عنه أمسكه حتى يحتاج إلى عمارته فيصرفه فيها ولا يجوز أن يقسمه بين مستحقي الوقف
cards.en: What falls down from a waqf building, and its materials, the judge uses for repairing the waqf if it needs them. If not, he keeps them until they are needed. He may not share them out among the beneficiaries.

cards.ask: Part of a waqf wall falls down, leaving good bricks and wood. The building does not need them now. The beneficiaries ask to share them out. What does the judge do?
options: Shares them out among the beneficiaries
cards.source: وإن استغنى عنه أمسكه حتى يحتاج إلى عمارته فيصرفه فيها ولا يجوز أن يقسمه بين مستحقي الوقف
cards.why: Materials not needed now are kept for repairs later; sharing them out among the beneficiaries is not allowed.

cards.title: Income for himself
cards.ar: وإذا جعل الوقف غلة الوقف لنفسه أو جعل الولاية إليه جاز عند أبي يوسف
cards.en: Note: if the founder makes the waqf's income his own, or makes himself its manager (wilaya), that is allowed according to Abu Yusuf.

cards.title: A mosque
cards.ar: وإذا بنى مسجدا لم يزل ملكه عنه حتى يفرزه عن ملكه بطريقه ويأذن للناس بالصلاة فيه فإذا صلى فيه واحد زال ملكه عنه عند أبي حنيفة ومحمد
cards.en: If someone builds a mosque, it stays his until he separates it from his property, with its own way in, and lets people pray in it. Once one person prays there, it is no longer his, for Abu Hanifa and Muhammad. Note: Abu Yusuf says it leaves him once he says, "I have made it a mosque."

cards.ask: Yaqub builds a prayer hall on his land, separates it with its own path, and invites people to pray. One man comes and prays in it. According to Abu Hanifa, is it still Yaqub's?
options: No, it has left his ownership
Yes, until a Friday prayer is held in it
cards.source: فإذا صلى فيه واحد زال ملكه عنه عند أبي حنيفة ومحمد
cards.why: Once it is separated, opened to people, and one person prays in it, it is a mosque and no longer his.

cards.title: Fountains, inns and graveyards
cards.ar: ومن بنى سقاية للمسلمين أو خانا يسكنه بنو السبيل أو رباطا أو جعل أرضه مقبرة لم يزل ملكه عن ذلك عند أبي حنيفة حتى يحكم به حاكم وقال أبو يوسف: يزول ملكه بالقول
cards.en: If someone builds a drinking fountain (siqaya) for Muslims, an inn (khan) for travellers or a ribat (a hostel), or makes his land a graveyard, it stays his, for Abu Hanifa, until a judge rules on it. Note: Abu Yusuf says his words end his ownership; Muhammad says people using it does.

cards.ask: According to Abu Hanifa, when does it stop being the builder's?
into: When one person prays in it
items: A mosque with its own way in
When one person prays in it
source: فإذا صلى فيه واحد زال ملكه عنه عند أبي حنيفة ومحمد
لم يزل ملكه عن ذلك عند أبي حنيفة حتى يحكم به حاكم
cards.why: A mosque leaves his ownership when one person prays in it; a fountain, inn or graveyard only by a judge's ruling.

lessons.title: What the one who takes by force must pay
lessons.arabic: ومن غصب شيئا مما له مثل

cards.title: The same thing, or its value
cards.ar: ومن غصب شيئا مما له مثل فهلك في يده فعليه ضمان مثله وإن كان مما لا مثل له فعليه قيمته يوم الغصب
cards.en: Ghasb is taking someone's property by force or without right; the taker is the ghasib. If the thing has exact equals (like wheat or oil) and is destroyed while he has it, he replaces it with the same. If it has no exact equal (like a horse), he pays its value on the day he took it.

cards.ask: Jamal takes ten sa' of his neighbour's wheat by force, and mice eat it. What must he pay?
options: Ten sa' of the same kind of wheat
Its price on the day he pays
cards.source: ومن غصب شيئا مما له مثل فهلك في يده فعليه ضمان مثله
cards.why: Wheat has exact equals, so he replaces it with the same amount of the same wheat.

cards.ask: Rashid takes a neighbour's horse by force, and it dies with him. It was worth 500 dirhams when he took it, and horses like it are now worth 400. What does he pay?
options: 500, its value on the day he took it
cards.source: وإن كان مما لا مثل له فعليه قيمته يوم الغصب
cards.why: A horse has no exact equal, so he pays its value on the day of the taking: 500.

cards.title: He must give it back
cards.ar: وعلى الغاصب رد العين المغصوبة فإن ادعى هلاكها حبسه الحاكم حتى يعلم أنها لو كانت باقية لأظهرها ثم قضى عليه ببدلها
cards.en: The ghasib must return the thing he took. If he claims it was destroyed, the judge keeps him in prison until it is clear that, if it still existed, he would have shown it. Then the judge orders him to pay its replacement.

cards.title: Land and buildings
cards.ar: والغصب فيما ينقل ويحول وإذا غصب عقارا فهلك في يده لم يضمنه عند أبي حنيفة وأبي يوسف وقال محمد: يضمنه
cards.en: Ghasb is really in things that can be moved. If he takes land or a building and it is destroyed while he has it (by a flood), he is not liable, for Abu Hanifa and Abu Yusuf. But damage he causes himself, like knocking it down, he must pay for. Note: Muhammad says he pays for the flood too.

cards.ask: A man seizes his neighbour's house. A flood, which was not his fault, destroys it. According to Abu Hanifa, must he pay for it?
options: No: land lost without his doing is not paid for
cards.source: وإذا غصب عقارا فهلك في يده لم يضمنه عند أبي حنيفة وأبي يوسف
cards.why: Land and buildings destroyed without his doing are not his to pay for, according to Abu Hanifa.

cards.title: Destroyed or damaged
cards.ar: وإذا هلك المغصوب في يد الغاصب بفعله أو بغير فعله فعليه ضمانه وإن نقص في يده فعليه ضمان النقصان
cards.en: If a taken thing is destroyed while he has it, by his doing or not, he must pay for it. If it loses value while he has it, he pays the loss.

cards.title: A slaughtered sheep, a torn garment
cards.ar: ومن ذبح شاة غيره فمالكها بالخيار: إن شاء ضمنه قيمتها وسلمها إليه وإن شاء ضمنه نقصانها ومن خرق ثوب غيره خرقا يسيرا ضمن نقصانه وإن خرقه خرقا كثيرا يبطل عامة منفعته فلمالكه أن يضمنه جميع قيمته
cards.en: If someone slaughters another's sheep, the owner chooses: take its full value and hand over the carcass, or keep it and take the loss in value. If he tears someone's garment a little, he pays the loss. If he tears it badly, ruining most of its use, the owner may claim its whole value.

cards.ask: Omar slaughters Bakr's sheep without permission. What may Bakr choose?
options: Either its value or its loss in value
Only its full value, and Omar keeps the meat
Only keep the meat, with nothing more
cards.source: فمالكها بالخيار: إن شاء ضمنه قيمتها وسلمها إليه وإن شاء ضمنه نقصانها
cards.why: The owner has the choice between the full value (handing over the sheep) and the loss in value (keeping it).

cards.ask: What must he pay?
items: A small tear in a seized shirt
A big tear that ruins most of a garment's use (if the owner wants)
A seized phone gets scratched while he has it
A seized phone is lost completely
source: ومن خرق ثوب غيره خرقا يسيرا ضمن نقصانه
فلمالكه أن يضمنه جميع قيمته
وإن نقص في يده فعليه ضمان النقصان
وإذا هلك المغصوب في يد الغاصب بفعله أو بغير فعله فعليه ضمانه
cards.why: Small damage and loss of value cost the loss; a thing lost completely, or so badly torn that most of its use is gone, costs its whole value.

lessons.title: When the taken thing is changed
lessons.arabic: وإذا تغيرت العين المغصوبة بفعل الغاصب

cards.title: Changed into something else
cards.ar: وإذا تغيرت العين المغصوبة بفعل الغاصب حتى زال اسمها وأعظم منافعها زال ملك المغصوب منه عنها وملكها الغاصب وضمنها ولم يحل له الانتفاع بها حتى يؤدي بدلها
cards.en: If the ghasib changes the thing so much that it loses its name and its main use, the owner no longer owns it: the ghasib owns it and must pay for it. But he may not use it until he has paid its replacement.

cards.ask: Imran takes his neighbour's wheat and grinds it into flour. Can he use the flour?
options: It is his, but only once he pays
Yes, freely: it became his when he ground it
No, he must give the flour back
source: زال ملك المغصوب منه عنها وملكها الغاصب وضمنها ولم يحل له الانتفاع بها حتى يؤدي بدلها
أو غصب حنطة فطحنها
cards.why: Wheat ground into flour has lost its name and main use, so it becomes his, but using it is not allowed until he pays.

cards.title: Gold and silver
cards.ar: وإن غصب فضة أو ذهبا فضربها دنانير أو دراهم أو دنانير أو آنية لم يزل ملك مالكها عنها عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: If he takes silver or gold and strikes it into coins (dinars or dirhams) or makes it into vessels, it still belongs to its owner according to Abu Hanifa.

cards.ask: Which of these make the thing the ghasib's (and he must pay)?

options.text: Slaughtering a seized sheep and roasting it
Grinding seized wheat into flour
Making seized iron into a sword
Striking seized silver into dirhams (Abu Hanifa)
Keeping a seized sheep in his barn

source: وهذا كمن غصب شاة فذبحها وشواها أو طبخها أو غصب حنطة فطحنها أو حديدا فاتخذه سيفا
وإن غصب فضة أو ذهبا فضربها دنانير أو دراهم
cards.why: Roasting, grinding and forging change the name and main use. Silver made into coins still belongs to its owner for Abu Hanifa, and a sheep kept unchanged is simply returned.

cards.title: A beam built into a house
cards.ar: ومن غصب ساجة فبنى عليها زال ملك مالكها عنها ولزم الغاصب قيمتها
cards.en: If he takes a saja (a large wooden beam) and builds on it, the owner no longer owns it, and the ghasib must pay its value.

cards.title: Planting or building on seized land
cards.ar: ومن غصب أرضا فغرس فيها أو بنى قيل له: اقلع الغرس والبناء وردها فارغة فإن كانت الأرض تنقص بقلع ذلك فللمالك أن يضمن له قيمة البناء والغرس مقلوعا فيكون له
cards.en: If he takes land and plants trees or builds on it, he is told: pull out the trees and the building, and return the land empty. If pulling them out would harm the land, the owner may pay him the value of the building and trees as if already pulled out, and keep them.

cards.ask: Zubair seizes a plot of land and plants olive trees on it. The owner wants his land back. What is Zubair told?
options: Pull out the trees and return the land empty
Keep the land and pay its price
Leave the trees; the owner pays their full value as they stand
cards.source: قيل له: اقلع الغرس والبناء وردها فارغة
cards.why: Seized land must be returned empty. Only if uprooting harms the land may the owner pay for the trees as uprooted ones.

cards.title: Dyed cloth, buttered meal
cards.ar: ومن غصب ثوبا فصبغه أحمر أو سويقا فلته بسمن فصاحبه بالخيار: إن شاء ضمنه قيمة ثوبه أبيض ومثل السويق وسلمها للغاصب وإن شاء أخذهما وضمن ما زاد الصبغ والسمن فيهما
cards.en: If he takes a white cloth and dyes it red, or takes sawiq (barley meal) and mixes it with ghee, the owner chooses: make him pay the value of the white cloth, or the same amount of sawiq, and leave them with him; or take them back and pay what the dye or ghee added.

cards.ask: Musa seizes a white cloth and dyes it red. What may the owner do?
options: Take its white value, or take it and pay for the dye
Only take the red cloth back, and pay nothing for the dye
Only take the value of the red cloth
cards.source: فصاحبه بالخيار: إن شاء ضمنه قيمة ثوبه أبيض ومثل السويق وسلمها للغاصب وإن شاء أخذهما وضمن ما زاد الصبغ والسمن فيهما
cards.why: The owner has the choice: the white cloth's value, or the cloth back while paying for the added dye.

cards.ask: Whose is it now?
items: Seized silver struck into dirhams (Abu Hanifa)
A seized beam built into a house
Seized land with a shed built on it
source: أو غصب حنطة فطحنها
لم يزل ملك مالكها عنها عند أبي حنيفة
ومن غصب ساجة فبنى عليها زال ملك مالكها عنها ولزم الغاصب قيمتها
غصب شاة فذبحها وشواها
اقلع الغرس والبناء وردها فارغة
cards.why: Big changes like grinding, roasting or building a beam in pass ownership to the ghasib, who pays. Minted silver and seized land stay the owner's.

cards.title: He hides it and pays
cards.ar: ومن غصب عينا فغيبها فضمنه المالك قيمتها ملكها الغاصب والقول في القيمة قول الغاصب مع يمينه إلا أن يقيم المالك البينة بأكثر من ذلك
cards.en: If the ghasib hides the thing and the owner makes him pay its value, the ghasib now owns it. If they disagree about the value, the ghasib's word is taken with his oath, unless the owner brings proof (witnesses) of a higher value.

cards.ask: The owner says a hidden ring was worth 300 dirhams. The ghasib swears it was worth 200. The owner has no witnesses. Whose word counts?
cards.source: والقول في القيمة قول الغاصب مع يمينه إلا أن يقيم المالك البينة بأكثر من ذلك
cards.why: Without proof from the owner, the ghasib's sworn word decides the value.

cards.title: It turns up again
cards.ar: فإن ظهرت العين وقيمتها أكثر مما ضمن وقد ضمنها بقول المالك أو ببينة أقامها أو بنكول الغاصب عن اليمين فلا خيار للمالك وإن كان ضمنها بقول الغاصب مع يمينه فالمالك بالخيار: إن شاء أمضى الضمان وإن شاء أخذ العين ورد العوض
cards.en: If the thing then turns up worth more than was paid: if the value was set by the owner's word, his witnesses, or the ghasib refusing to swear (nukul), the owner has no choice. But if it was set by the ghasib's sworn word, the owner chooses: keep the payment, or take the thing back and return the payment.

cards.ask: A ghasib hid a bike and paid 100 dirhams, its value by his own sworn word. Then the bike turns up worth 200. What may the owner do?
options: Keep the 100, or take the bike back and return the 100
He must take the bike and keep the 100 too
cards.source: وإن كان ضمنها بقول الغاصب مع يمينه فالمالك بالخيار: إن شاء أمضى الضمان وإن شاء أخذ العين ورد العوض
cards.why: Because the value came from the ghasib's own oath, the owner gets the choice.

cards.ask: When the hidden thing turns up worth more, does the owner get a choice?
items: The value was set by the owner's own word
The value was set by the owner's witnesses
The value was set by the ghasib's sworn word
source: وقد ضمنها بقول المالك أو ببينة أقامها أو بنكول الغاصب عن اليمين فلا خيار للمالك
وإن كان ضمنها بقول الغاصب مع يمينه فالمالك بالخيار
cards.why: Only when the value rested on the ghasib's oath does the owner get to choose again.

cards.title: Young, growth and fruit
cards.ar: وولد المغصوبة ونماؤها وثمرة البستان المغصوب أمانة في يد الغاصب فإن هلك فلا ضمان عليه إلا أن يتعدى فيها أو يطلبها مالكها فيمنعها إياه
cards.en: The young of a seized animal, its growth, and the fruit of a seized orchard are an amana (a trust) in the ghasib's hand. If they are lost, he does not pay, unless he misuses them, or the owner asks for them and he refuses.

cards.ask: Ahmad seizes an orchard. Fruit grows on the trees, and birds eat some of it without any fault of his. Must he pay for that fruit?
cards.source: وثمرة البستان المغصوب أمانة في يد الغاصب فإن هلك فلا ضمان عليه
cards.why: The new fruit is a trust; lost without his misuse or refusal, he owes nothing for it.

cards.title: Paying for use
cards.ar: وما نقصت الجارية بالولادة في ضمان الغاصب فإن كان في قيمة الولد وفاء به خير النقصان بالولد وسقط ضمانه عن الغاصب ولا يضمن الغاصب منافع ما غصبه
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time, if a seized slave woman lost value by giving birth, the ghasib was liable; but if the child's value covered the loss, it made up for it and he owed nothing. The ghasib does not pay for the use (manafi') of what he took, unless it lost value by his using it: then he pays the loss.

cards.ask: Bashir seizes a car, drives it for a month, and returns it with no damage and no loss in value. Must he pay rent for the month?
options: Yes, a fair rent for the month
cards.source: ولا يضمن الغاصب منافع ما غصبه
cards.why: Use alone is not paid for; only a loss in value from using it would be.

cards.title: Wine and pigs
cards.ar: وإذا استهلك المسلم خمر الذمي أو خنزيره ضمن قيمتهما وإن استهلكهما المسلم على المسلم لم يضمن
cards.en: A dhimmi is a non-Muslim living under Muslim rule with protection. If a Muslim destroys a dhimmi's wine or pig, he pays their value. If he destroys a Muslim's, he pays nothing.

cards.ask: Which must the ghasib pay for?

options.text: A dhimmi's wine that a Muslim pours away
The loss in value of a car worn by his driving it
Orchard fruit he refused to hand over when asked, which then spoiled
Fruit eaten by birds, with no fault of his
