The use of a house he lived in, with no damage
A Muslim's wine that he poured away

source: وإذا استهلك المسلم خمر الذمي أو خنزيره ضمن قيمتهما
باستعماله فيغرم النقصان
أو يطلبها مالكها فيمنعها إياه
وإن استهلكهما المسلم على المسلم لم يضمن
cards.why: He pays for a dhimmi's wine, for loss caused by use, and for fruit he refused to return. Fruit lost without fault, plain use, and a Muslim's wine cost him nothing.

cards.title: A deposit is a trust
cards.ar: الوديعة: أمانة في يد المودع إذا هلكت لم يضمنها وللمودع أن يحفظها بنفسه وبمن في عياله فإن حفظها بغيرهم أو أودعها ضمن
cards.en: A wadi'a (deposit) is something left with a person to keep safe. It is an amana (trust): if it is lost without his fault, he does not pay. He may keep it himself, or by the people of his household ('iyal) who live with him. If he has others keep it, or deposits it with someone else, he is liable.

cards.ask: Hamid is keeping a neighbour's gold. Who may he let look after it without becoming liable?

options.text: Himself
His wife who lives with him
His son who lives with him
A friend from work
Another neighbour down the street

cards.source: وللمودع أن يحفظها بنفسه وبمن في عياله فإن حفظها بغيرهم أو أودعها ضمن
cards.why: He may keep it himself or by his household. Handing it to anyone outside his household makes him liable.

cards.title: Fire and shipwreck
cards.ar: إلا أن يقع في داره حريق فيسلمها إلى جاره أو يكون في سفينة يخاف الغرق
cards.en: But if his house catches fire and he hands it to his neighbour, or he is on a ship that he fears will sink and he throws it onto another ship, he is not liable.

cards.ask: Ali is keeping his friend's laptop. His house catches fire, so he hands the laptop to his neighbour, who then drops and breaks it. Is Ali liable?
options: No, the fire allowed him to hand it over
Yes, he gave it to someone outside his household
cards.source: إلا أن يقع في داره حريق فيسلمها إلى جاره
cards.why: Handing it to a neighbour during a fire is allowed, so Ali does not pay.

cards.title: Mixing and holding back
cards.ar: وإن خلطها المودع بماله حتى لا تتميز ضمنها فإن طلبها صاحبها فحبسها عنه وهو يقدر على تسليمها ضمنها
cards.en: If the keeper mixes the deposit with his own wealth so it cannot be told apart, he is liable. If the owner asks for it and he holds it back when he could hand it over, he is liable too.

cards.ask: Rami keeps his friend's 100 silver coins. He pours them into his own jar of coins, and now nobody can tell which are whose. Then the jar is stolen. Is Rami liable?
options: No: the theft was not his fault
Only for half of the 100 coins
cards.source: وإن خلطها المودع بماله حتى لا تتميز ضمنها
cards.why: Mixing the deposit with his own wealth so it cannot be told apart makes the keeper liable, whatever happens next.

cards.title: Mixed by accident, or spent and replaced
cards.ar: وإن اختلطت بماله من غيره فعله فهو شريك لصاحبها وإن أنفق المودع بعضها ثم رد مثله فخلطه بالباقي ضمن الجميع
cards.en: If it gets mixed with his wealth without his doing, he becomes the owner's partner in it. If he spends some, then puts back the same amount mixed with the rest, he is liable for all of it.

cards.ask: Is the keeper liable?
items: He mixes the coins with his own so they cannot be told apart
The coins get mixed with his by accident, not his doing
He spends some, then puts back the same amount and mixes it in
The owner asks for it, he could hand it over but holds it back, and it is lost
It is stolen from his locked house, with no fault of his
source: وإن خلطها المودع بماله حتى لا تتميز ضمنها
فهو شريك لصاحبها
وإن أنفق المودع بعضها ثم رد مثله فخلطه بالباقي ضمن الجميع
فإن طلبها صاحبها فحبسها عنه وهو يقدر على تسليمها ضمنها
إذا هلكت لم يضمنها
cards.why: Mixing it himself, spending and replacing, or holding it back all make him liable. An accidental mixing makes him a partner, and a loss without fault costs nothing.

cards.title: Misuse, then stopping
cards.ar: وإذا تعدى المودع في الوديعة - بأن كانت دابة فركبها أو ثوبا فلبسه أو عبدا فاستخدمه أو أودعها عند غيره - ثم أزال التعدي وردها إلى يده زال الضمان
cards.en: Ta'addi is overstepping: riding a deposited animal, wearing a deposited garment, putting a deposited servant to work (in al-Quduri's time), or depositing it with someone else. If he then stops and takes it back into his keeping, he is no longer liable.

cards.ask: Yasir rides a horse left with him, then puts it back in his stable and stops riding it. Later it dies, with no fault of his. Is he liable?
options: No, his liability ended when he stopped
Yes, because he once rode it
Yes, but only half its value
cards.source: ثم أزال التعدي وردها إلى يده زال الضمان
cards.why: Once he stopped overstepping and kept it properly again, the liability was gone.

cards.title: Denying he has it
cards.ar: فإن طلبها صاحبها فجحدها إياه فهلكت ضمنها فإن عاد إلى الاعتراف لم يبرأ من الضمان
cards.en: If the owner asks for it and he denies having it, and then it is lost, he is liable. Admitting it again later does not free him.

cards.ask: The owner asks for his gold ring. Kamal says, "You never gave me any ring." That night the ring is stolen. Next day Kamal admits he had it. Is he liable?
options: Yes, admitting later does not clear him
No: he admitted it in the end, so he is clear
cards.source: فإن طلبها صاحبها فجحدها إياه فهلكت ضمنها فإن عاد إلى الاعتراف لم يبرأ من الضمان
cards.why: Denying the deposit when asked makes him liable for its loss, and coming back to admit it does not remove that.

cards.title: Travelling with it
cards.ar: وللمودع أن يسافر بالوديعة وإن كان لها حمل ومؤنة
cards.en: The keeper may travel with the deposit, even if it is heavy and costs money to carry.

cards.ask: Nabil is keeping his cousin's heavy trunk and must move to another city. May he take the trunk with him?
options: Yes, even though it is heavy to carry
No, he must leave it behind
cards.source: وللمودع أن يسافر بالوديعة وإن كان لها حمل ومؤنة
cards.why: Travelling with a deposit is allowed, even with the cost of carrying it.

cards.title: Two owners, one comes alone
cards.ar: وإذا أودع رجلان عند رجل وديعة ثم حضر أحدهما فطلب نصيبه منها لم يدفع إليه شيئا حتى يحضر الآخر عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: If two men leave a deposit with one man, and one of them comes and asks for his share, the keeper gives him nothing until the other comes too, according to Abu Hanifa. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say he gives him his share.

cards.ask: Two brothers leave 1,000 dirhams with Uncle Saad. One comes alone and asks for his 500. According to Abu Hanifa, what does Saad do?
options: Gives him his 500 share at once
cards.source: لم يدفع إليه شيئا حتى يحضر الآخر عند أبي حنيفة
cards.why: For Abu Hanifa the keeper waits until both owners are present.

cards.title: One owner, two keepers
cards.ar: وإن أودع رجل عند رجلين شيئا مما يقسم لم يجز أن يدفعه أحدهما إلى الآخر ولكنهما يقتسمانه فيحفظ كل واحد منهما نصفه وإن كان مما لا يقسم جاز أن يحفظه أحدهما بإذن الآخر
cards.en: If one person leaves something that can be divided with two keepers, one may not hand it all to the other; they divide it, and each keeps half. If it cannot be divided, one may keep it with the other's permission.

cards.ask: Hiba leaves 200 dirhams with two friends, Aisha and Maryam. What should they do?
options: One keeps it all with the other's permission
cards.source: لم يجز أن يدفعه أحدهما إلى الآخر ولكنهما يقتسمانه فيحفظ كل واحد منهما نصفه
cards.why: Money can be divided, so each keeper keeps half; one may not hand it all to the other.

cards.ask: Something that cannot be divided is left with two keepers. Complete the rule.
cards.ar: وإن كان مما لا يقسم ____ أن يحفظه أحدهما بإذن الآخر
cards.source: وإن كان مما لا يقسم جاز أن يحفظه أحدهما بإذن الآخر
cards.why: جاز: if it cannot be divided, one may keep it with the other's permission.

cards.title: The owner's instructions
cards.ar: وإذا قال صاحب الوديعة للمودع: لا تسلمها إلى زوجتك فسلمها إليها لم يضمن وإن قال له: احفظها في هذا البيت فحفظها في بيت آخر من الدار لم يضمن
cards.en: If the owner says, "Don't give it to your wife," and he gives it to her, he is not liable. If he says, "Keep it in this room," and he keeps it in another room of the same house, he is not liable. But if he keeps it in a different house, he is liable.

cards.ask: Rania was told, "Keep my bag in this room." She moves it to her brother's house next door, where it is stolen. Is she liable?
options: Yes, she kept it in a different house
No, the owner only named a room
cards.source: في دار أخرى ضمن
cards.why: Another room of the same house would be fine, but a different house makes her liable.

cards.ask: If it is lost, is the keeper liable?
items: Told "Don't give it to your wife", he gives it to her
Told "Keep it in this room", he keeps it in another room of the same house
He keeps it in another house
He hands it to a stranger outside his household
He takes it with him on a journey
source: لا تسلمها إلى زوجتك فسلمها إليها لم يضمن
فحفظها في بيت آخر من الدار لم يضمن
في دار أخرى ضمن
فإن حفظها بغيرهم أو أودعها ضمن
وللمودع أن يسافر بالوديعة
cards.why: His wife and another room of the same house are fine, as is travelling. Another house, or a stranger outside his household, makes him liable.

cards.title: What a loan is
cards.ar: العارية: جائزة وهي: تمليك المنافع بغير عوض وتصح بقوله: أعرتك وأطعمتك هذه الأرض ومنحتك هذا الثوب وحملتك على هذه الدابة إذا لم يرد به الهبة وأخدمتك هذا العبد وداري لك سكنى وداري لك عمرى سكنى
cards.en: An 'ariya is a loan for use: giving someone the use of a thing for free. It is made with words like "I lend you", "I give you this land to eat from", "I give you this garment", "I mount you on this animal" (not meant as a gift), and "My house is yours to live in".

cards.ask: What is an 'ariya?
options: Giving the use of a thing for free
Giving the use of a thing for a rent
Giving the thing itself for free
cards.source: وهي: تمليك المنافع بغير عوض
cards.why: An 'ariya is giving someone the benefits of a thing without payment.

cards.title: Taking it back, and losing it
cards.ar: وللمعير أن يرجع في العارية متى شاء والعارية أمانة: إن هلكت من غير تعد لم يضمن شيئا
cards.en: The lender may take back what he lent whenever he likes. A loan is an amana (trust): if it is lost without misuse, the borrower pays nothing.

cards.ask: Saleh borrows Idris's bike. It is stolen from a locked shed, with no fault of Saleh's. Must he pay?
options: No: a loan is a trust
cards.source: والعارية أمانة: إن هلكت من غير تعد لم يضمن شيئا
cards.why: A loan is a trust; lost without misuse, the borrower pays nothing.

cards.title: Renting or pawning a loan
cards.ar: وليس للمستعير أن يؤاجر ما استعاره ولا أن يرهنه وله أن يعيره إذا كان مما لا يختلف باختلاف المستعمل
cards.en: The borrower may not rent out what he borrowed, nor pawn it (rahn: leave it as security for a debt). He may lend it on to someone else, if it is something used the same way by anyone.

cards.ask: Bilal has borrowed a house to live in. Which may he do?

options.text: Live in it himself
Lend it to someone else, since anyone uses a house the same way
Rent it out for money
Pawn it as security for his debt
Keep it after the owner asks for it back

source: وليس للمستعير أن يؤاجر ما استعاره ولا أن يرهنه وله أن يعيره إذا كان مما لا يختلف باختلاف المستعمل
وللمعير أن يرجع في العارية متى شاء
cards.why: He may use it and lend it on, but not rent or pawn it, and the owner may take it back whenever he likes.

cards.title: Lending money is a qard
cards.ar: وعارية الدراهم والدنانير والمكيل والموزون قرض
cards.en: "Lending" dirhams, dinars, or things sold by measure or weight is really a qard: a loan that is paid back with the same amount, because they are used up when used.

cards.ask: Nasir "lends" his neighbour 5 kilos of rice to cook. What is this?
options: A qard: the neighbour pays back 5 kilos of rice
An 'ariya: he must return the same grains
cards.source: وعارية الدراهم والدنانير والمكيل والموزون قرض
cards.why: Rice is weighed and used up, so lending it is a qard, repaid with the same amount.

cards.title: Building on borrowed land
cards.ar: وإذا استعار أرضا ليبني فيها أو يغرس نخلا جاز وللمعير أن يرجع فيها ويكلفه قلع البناء والغرس فإن لم يكن وقت العارية فلا ضمان عليه وإن كان وقت العارية فرجع قبل الوقت ضمن المعير
cards.en: Borrowing land to build on or plant palms is allowed. The lender may take it back and make him remove the building and trees. If he set no time for the loan, the lender owes nothing. If he set a time and takes it back early, he must pay for the loss caused by pulling them down.

cards.ask: Hamza lets Ilyas build a shed on his land "for five years". After two years Hamza wants his land back. What is the rule?
options: He may, but pays the loss of pulling it down
He may not take it until the five years are up
cards.source: وإن كان وقت العارية فرجع قبل الوقت ضمن المعير
cards.why: He can always take it back, but taking it back before the set time means he pays for the loss of pulling it down.

cards.title: Bringing it back
cards.ar: وإذا استعار دابة فردها إلى دار مالكها ولم يسلمها إليه ضمن
cards.en: If he borrows an animal and leaves it at the owner's house without handing it over, he is liable; the same goes for a deposit. The cost of bringing things back: a loan, on the borrower; a hired thing, on the one who rented it out; a seized thing, on the ghasib (the one who seized it).

cards.ask: Who pays the cost of bringing it back?
into: The owner who rented it out
items: The owner who rented it out
cards.source: وأجرة رد العارية على المستعمر وأجرة رد العين المستأجرة على المؤجر وأجرة المغصوبة على الغاصب
cards.why: The borrower brings back a loan, the one who rented a thing out pays for bringing it back, and the ghasib pays for returning what he seized.

cards.ask: Which are true of a loan for use?

options.text: The lender may take it back whenever he likes
Returning it means handing it to the owner, not leaving it at his house
"Lending" money is really a qard
The borrower may rent it out
If it is lost without misuse, the borrower pays

source: وللمعير أن يرجع في العارية متى شاء
فردها إلى دار مالكها ولم يسلمها إليه ضمن
وعارية الدراهم والدنانير والمكيل والموزون قرض
وليس للمستعير أن يؤاجر ما استعاره
إن هلكت من غير تعد لم يضمن شيئا
cards.why: The first three are in the text. A borrower may not rent it out, and pays nothing for a loss without misuse.

cards.title: Free and Muslim
cards.ar: اللقيط: حر مسلم ونفقته من بيت المال
cards.en: A laqit is a foundling: a baby who has been left and is found by someone. He is free and Muslim, and his costs are paid from the bayt al-mal (the public treasury).

cards.title: Who keeps him, and who claims him
cards.ar: فإن التقطه رجل لم يكن لغيره أن يأخذه من يده فإن ادعى مدع أنه ابنه فالقول قوله وإن ادعاه اثنان ووصف أحدهما علامة في جسده فهو أولى به
cards.en: Once a man has picked him up, nobody else may take him away from him. If someone claims he is his son, his word is accepted. If two people claim him and one describes a mark on his body, that one has the better right to him.

cards.ask: Karim finds a baby and cares for him. A neighbour says, "Give him to me, I'll raise him instead." What is the rule?
options: The neighbour may not take him from Karim
The neighbour may take him if he wants
The judge must decide who is better
cards.source: فإن التقطه رجل لم يكن لغيره أن يأخذه من يده
cards.why: The one who picked him up keeps him; no one else may take him away.

cards.ask: Two men each claim a foundling as their son. One says, "He has a birthmark on his left shoulder," and he does. Who has the better right?
options: The one who described the mark
Neither; he stays with the finder
cards.source: وإن ادعاه اثنان ووصف أحدهما علامة في جسده فهو أولى به
cards.why: When two claim him, the one who describes a mark on his body has the better right.

cards.title: Where he is found
cards.ar: وإذا وجد في مصر من أمصار المسلمين أو في قرية من قراهم فادعى ذمي أنه ابنه
cards.en: If he is found in a Muslim town or village and a dhimmi (a non-Muslim living under Muslim protection) claims he is his son, the lineage is his, but the child counts as Muslim. If he is found in a village of the dhimmis, or in a synagogue or church, he counts as a dhimmi.

cards.ask: Does the foundling count as Muslim or as a dhimmi?
items: Found in a Muslim village; a dhimmi claims him as his son
Found in a village of dhimmis
source: اللقيط: حر مسلم
نسبه منه وكان مسلما وإن وجد في قرية من قرى أهل الذمة أو في بيعة أو كنيسة كان ذميا
cards.why: Found among Muslims he is Muslim, even if a dhimmi is his father. Found in a dhimmi village, synagogue or church, he counts as a dhimmi.

cards.title: A false claim of ownership
cards.ar: ومن ادعى أن اللقيط عبده لم يقبل منه فإن ادعى عبد أنه ابنه ثبت نسبه منه وكان حرا
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time, if someone claimed a foundling was his slave, it was not accepted. If a slave claimed the foundling was his son, the lineage was his, and the child stayed free.

cards.title: His money, and what the finder may do
cards.ar: وإن وجد مع اللقيط مال مشدود عليه فهو له ولا يجوز تزويج الملتقط ولا تصرفه في مال اللقيط ويجوز أن يقبض له الهبة ويسلمه في صناعة ويؤاجره
cards.en: If money is found tied to the foundling, it is his. The finder (multaqit) may not arrange his marriage or use his money. He may accept gifts for him, send him to learn a trade, and hire him out for work.

cards.ask: What may the finder do for the foundling?

options.text: Accept a gift for him
Send him to learn a trade
Hire him out for work
Spend the money found tied to him
Arrange his marriage

cards.source: ولا يجوز تزويج الملتقط ولا تصرفه في مال اللقيط ويجوز أن يقبض له الهبة ويسلمه في صناعة ويؤاجره
cards.why: He may take gifts for him, teach him a trade and hire him out, but not marry him off or use his money.

cards.ask: A baby is found in a Muslim town with a purse tied to him. Which is right?
options: He is free and Muslim, and the purse is his
He is free, and the purse goes to the finder
He belongs to whoever claims him, and the purse to the treasury
source: اللقيط: حر مسلم
وإن وجد مع اللقيط مال مشدود عليه فهو له
cards.why: A foundling is free and Muslim, and money tied to him is his own.

cards.title: A trust, announced
cards.ar: اللقطة: أمانة إذا أشهد الملتقط أنه يأخذها ليحفظها ويردها على صاحبها فإن كانت أقل من عشرة دراهم عرفها أياما وإن كانت عشرة فصاعدا عرفها حولا
cards.en: A luqata is found property. It is an amana (trust) if the finder has witnesses that he is taking it to keep it safe and return it to its owner. He must announce it (ta'rif): if it is less than ten dirhams, for some days; if it is ten or more, for a hawl (a full year).

cards.ask: Zaid finds a purse with 25 dirhams in it. How long must he announce it?
cards.source: وإن كانت عشرة فصاعدا عرفها حولا
cards.why: 25 dirhams is ten or more, so he announces it for a full year.

cards.title: After the announcing
cards.ar: فإن جاء صاحبها وإلا تصدق بها فإن جاء صاحبها فهو بالخيار: إن شاء أمضى الصدقة وإن شاء ضمن الملتقط
cards.en: If the owner comes, he gets it. If not, the finder gives it in charity. If the owner comes after that, he chooses: let the charity stand (and get its reward), or make the finder pay him.

cards.ask: After a year of announcing, Zaid gives the 25 dirhams in charity. A month later the owner turns up. What may the owner do?
options: Let the charity stand, or make Zaid pay him
Nothing: it is already given away
Take it back from the poor man
cards.source: فإن جاء صاحبها فهو بالخيار: إن شاء أمضى الصدقة وإن شاء ضمن الملتقط
cards.why: The owner has the choice: accept the charity, or have the finder pay him back.

cards.title: Stray animals
cards.ar: ويجوز الالتقاط في الشاة والبقرة والبعير فإن أنفق الملتقط عليها بغير إذن الحاكم فهو متبرع وإن أنفق بأمره كان ذلك دينا على مالكها
cards.en: Stray sheep, cows and camels may be picked up. If the finder spends on feeding one without the judge's permission, he is a volunteer: it is his gift. If he spends by the judge's order, it is a debt the owner must repay.

cards.ask: Ilyas finds a stray cow and spends 50 dirhams feeding it, without asking the judge. The owner comes. Can Ilyas claim the 50?
options: No, he spent it as a volunteer
He may keep the cow instead
cards.source: فإن أنفق الملتقط عليها بغير إذن الحاكم فهو متبرع
cards.why: Without the judge's permission, his spending counts as a free gift.

cards.title: What the judge does
cards.ar: وإذا رفع ذلك إلى الحاكم نظر فيه فإن كان للبهيمة منفعة أجرها وأنفق عليها من أجرتها
cards.en: When the stray is brought to the judge, he looks at what is best for it. If the animal can be used, he rents it out and feeds it from the rent.

cards.ask: A stray horse that can carry loads is brought to the judge. How is it fed?
options: The finder feeds it, as a free gift
The judge sells it at once and keeps the price
cards.source: فإن كان للبهيمة منفعة أجرها وأنفق عليها من أجرتها
cards.why: An animal that can be used is rented out, and its feed comes from the rent.

cards.title: Selling it, or feeding it as a debt
cards.ar: وإن لم يكن لها منفعة وخاف أن تستغرق النفقة قيمتها باعها وأمره بحفظ ثمنها وإن كان الأصلح الإنفاق عليها أذن له في ذلك وجعل النفقة دينا على مالكها
cards.en: If it cannot be used and feeding it might cost more than it is worth, he sells it and tells the finder to keep the price. If feeding it is best, he allows that and makes the cost a debt on the owner.

cards.ask: A stray old donkey is brought to the judge. Nobody can use it, and feeding it will soon cost more than it is worth. What does the judge do?
options: Sells it; the finder keeps the price
Rents it out and feeds it from the rent
cards.source: وإن لم يكن لها منفعة وخاف أن تستغرق النفقة قيمتها باعها وأمره بحفظ ثمنها
cards.why: With no use and costs eating up its value, the judge sells it and the price is kept for the owner.

cards.ask: Who bears the cost of feeding the stray?
items: The judge decided feeding was best and allowed it
source: فإن أنفق الملتقط عليها بغير إذن الحاكم فهو متبرع وإن أنفق بأمره كان ذلك دينا على مالكها
وإن كان الأصلح الإنفاق عليها أذن له في ذلك وجعل النفقة دينا على مالكها
cards.why: Spending without the judge is the finder's gift; with the judge's order or permission it is a debt on the owner.

lessons.title: Claims, and who may use found property

cards.title: Holding it until paid
cards.ar: فإذا حضر مالكها فللملتقط أن يمنعه منها حتى يأخذ النفقة
cards.en: When the owner of the stray animal comes, the finder may keep it from him until he is paid back what he spent (when that spending was a debt on the owner).

cards.ask: Ilyas fed a stray camel by the judge's order, spending 80 dirhams. The owner arrives and demands his camel. What may Ilyas do?
options: Keep it until he is paid the 80
Nothing: he must hand it over at once
Keep the camel as his own
cards.source: فإذا حضر مالكها فللملتقط أن يمنعه منها حتى يأخذ النفقة
cards.why: The finder may hold the animal until he receives what he spent.

cards.title: Inside the Haram too
cards.ar: الحل والحرم سواء
cards.en: Found property inside the Haram (the sacred area around Makka) and outside it follow the same rules.

cards.title: A claim with signs
cards.ar: فإن أعطى علامتها حل للملتقط أن يدفعها إليه ولا يجبر على ذلك في القضاء
cards.en: If a man comes and says the found thing is his, it is not handed to him until he brings proof (witnesses). If he describes its signs correctly, the finder is allowed to give it to him, but a court will not force him to.

cards.ask: A man claims a found purse is his. Complete the rule.
cards.ar: وإذا حضر الرجل فادعى أن اللقطة له ____ إليه
cards.source: وإذا حضر الرجل فادعى أن اللقطة له لم تدفع إليه
cards.why: لم تدفع: it is not handed over until he brings proof.

cards.ask: A woman describes the colour of a found purse and the exact coins in it, but has no witnesses. Must the finder hand it over?
options: He may, but a court will not force him
Yes, a court will force him
No, he is not allowed to
cards.source: فإن أعطى علامتها حل للملتقط أن يدفعها إليه ولا يجبر على ذلك في القضاء
cards.why: Correct signs make handing it over allowed, but not compulsory in court.

cards.title: Who may use it
cards.ar: ولا يتصدق باللقطة على غني وإن كان الملتقط غنيا لم يجز له أن ينتفع بها وإن كان فقيرا فلا بأس أن ينتفع بها ويجوز أن يتصدق بها إذا كان غنيا على أبيه وابنه وزوجته إذا كانوا فقراء
cards.en: Found property is not given in charity to a rich person. A rich finder may not use it himself; a poor finder may. A rich finder may give it in charity to his father, son or wife if they are poor.

cards.ask: Tariq is rich. He announced a found purse for a year and nobody came. May he spend it on himself?
options: No, but he may give it to his poor father
Yes, after a full year it is his to keep
Yes, but only half of it
source: وإن كان الملتقط غنيا لم يجز له أن ينتفع بها
ويجوز أن يتصدق بها إذا كان غنيا على أبيه وابنه وزوجته إذا كانوا فقراء
cards.why: A rich finder may not use it himself, but may give it as charity to a poor father, son or wife.

cards.ask: After the announcing, with no owner, is this allowed?
items: A poor finder uses it himself
A rich finder uses it himself
A rich finder gives it to his poor son
It is given as charity to a rich stranger
source: وإن كان فقيرا فلا بأس أن ينتفع بها
وإن كان الملتقط غنيا لم يجز له أن ينتفع بها
ويجوز أن يتصدق بها إذا كان غنيا على أبيه وابنه
ولا يتصدق باللقطة على غني
cards.why: The poor may use it; the rich may not, but may pass it to poor close family. It is never charity for a rich person.

cards.ask: Which are true?

options.text: Found property in the Haram follows the same rules
Under ten dirhams is announced for some days
The finder may hold a stray he fed by the judge's order until he is paid
A court must force the finder to give it to someone who describes it
Found property may be given as charity to a rich person

source: الحل والحرم سواء
فإن كانت أقل من عشرة دراهم عرفها أياما
فللملتقط أن يمنعه منها حتى يأخذ النفقة
ولا يجبر على ذلك في القضاء
ولا يتصدق باللقطة على غني
cards.why: The first three are in the text. Describing it does not let a court force handing it over, and found property is not charity for the rich.

cards.title: How the child is judged
cards.ar: إذا كان للمولود فرج وذكر فهو خنثى فإن كان يبول من الذكر فهو غلام وإن كان يبول من الفرج فهو أنثى وإن كان يبول منهما والبول يسبق من أحدهما نسب إلى الأسبق فإن كانا في السبق سواء فلا عبرة بالكثرة عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: Sometimes a baby is born with both male and female organs: a khuntha. The child is judged by where urine comes from: the male organ, a boy; the female organ, a girl. If from both, by whichever comes first. Note: if both start together, Abu Hanifa ignores which is more, but his two students go by the greater.

cards.ask: A baby khuntha passes urine from both organs, but it always comes first from the male organ. How is the child counted?
cards.source: وإن كان يبول منهما والبول يسبق من أحدهما نسب إلى الأسبق
cards.why: When urine comes from both, the child is counted by the one it comes from first.

cards.title: Signs when grown up
cards.ar: وإذا بلغ الخنثى وخرجت له لحية أو وصل إلى النساء فهو رجل وإن ظهر له ثدي كثدي المرأة أو نزل له لبن في ثديه أو حاض أو حبل أو أمكن الوصول إليه من الفرج فهو امرأة فإن لم تظهر إحدى هذه العلامات فهو خنثى مشكل
cards.en: When the khuntha reaches adulthood, signs settle it. A beard, or being able to be with women as a husband, means a man. Breasts like a woman's, milk, monthly periods, or pregnancy, mean a woman. If none of these signs appear, the person is a khuntha mushkil (an unclear case).

cards.ask: Counted as a man or a woman?
items: As a child, passed urine only from the male organ
source: وخرجت له لحية أو وصل إلى النساء فهو رجل
وإن ظهر له ثدي كثدي المرأة أو نزل له لبن في ثديه أو حاض
فإن كان يبول من الذكر فهو غلام
cards.why: A beard or the male sign as a child mean a man; breasts or periods mean a woman.

cards.title: In the prayer rows
cards.ar: وإذا وقف خلف الإمام قام بين صف الرجال والنساء
cards.en: An unclear khuntha praying behind the imam stands between the men's row and the women's row.

cards.ask: Where does an unclear khuntha (khuntha mushkil) stand in congregational prayer?
options: Between the men's and women's rows
With the women, at the back of their row
cards.source: وإذا وقف خلف الإمام قام بين صف الرجال والنساء
cards.why: Since it is unclear which they are, they stand between the two.

cards.title: Circumcision
cards.ar: وتبتاع له أمة تختنه إن كان له مال فإن لم يكن له مال ابتاع له الإمام من بيت المال فإذا ختنته باعها ورد ثمنها إلى بيت المال
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time, a slave woman was bought to circumcise the unclear khuntha, from his own money if he had any, or otherwise by the ruler from the bayt al-mal (public treasury). Afterwards she was sold and the price returned to the treasury.

cards.title: Inheritance (Abu Hanifa)
cards.ar: وإذا مات أبوه وخلف ابنا وخنثى فالمال بينهما عند أبي حنيفة على ثلاثة أسهم: للابن سهمان وللخنثى سهم وهو أنثى عنده في الميراث إلا أن يثبت غير ذلك فيتبع
cards.en: If the father dies leaving a son and an unclear khuntha, Abu Hanifa divides the estate into three shares: two for the son and one for the khuntha. For inheritance he counts the khuntha as female, unless something else is proven.

cards.ask: A father dies leaving 900 dirhams, a son, and an unclear khuntha child. According to Abu Hanifa, how much does each get?
cards.source: فالمال بينهما عند أبي حنيفة على ثلاثة أسهم: للابن سهمان وللخنثى سهم
cards.why: Three shares of 300: two (600) for the son, one (300) for the khuntha, who counts as female.

cards.title: A note on the two companions
cards.ar: وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد: للخنثى نصف ميراث الذكر ونصف ميراث الأنثى
cards.en: Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say the khuntha gets half a male's share plus half a female's share. They worked it out differently: Abu Yusuf makes seven shares (four for the son, three for the khuntha), Muhammad twelve (seven for the son, five for the khuntha).

cards.ask: According to Abu Hanifa, which are true of an unclear khuntha?

options.text: Stands between the men's and women's rows
Inherits as a female unless something else is proven
Is counted a man if a beard grows
Is judged by which organ passes more urine
Is counted a woman if a beard grows

source: قام بين صف الرجال والنساء
وهو أنثى عنده في الميراث إلا أن يثبت غير ذلك فيتبع
وخرجت له لحية أو وصل إلى النساء فهو رجل
فلا عبرة بالكثرة عند أبي حنيفة
cards.why: The first three are in the text. For Abu Hanifa the amount of urine does not count, and a beard is a man's sign.

lessons.title: The missing person, and the runaway

cards.title: While he is missing
cards.ar: إذا غاب الرجل ولم يعرف له موضع ولا يعلم أحي هو أم ميت نصب القاضي من يحفظ ماله ويقوم عليه ويستوفي حقوقه وينفق على زوجته وأولاده من ماله
cards.en: A mafqud is a missing person: a man who has gone away, and nobody knows where he is or whether he is alive or dead. The judge appoints someone to look after his property, manage it, collect what is owed to him, and spend on his wife and children from his money.

cards.title: His marriage stays
cards.ar: ولا يفرق بينه وبين امرأته
cards.en: His marriage is not ended: the judge does not separate him from his wife.

cards.ask: Hamid disappears on a journey and no one knows if he is alive. His wife asks the judge to end the marriage after a year. What does the judge do?
options: He ends the marriage at once
He ends it after one year
cards.source: ولا يفرق بينه وبين امرأته
cards.why: The missing man's marriage stays in place; the judge does not separate them.

cards.title: Judged dead at 120
cards.ar: فإذا تم له مائة وعشرون سنة من يوم ولد حكمنا بموته واعتدت امرأته وقسم ماله بين ورثته الموجودين في ذلك الوقت ومن مات منهم قبل ذلك لم يرث منه ولا يرث المفقود من أحد مات في حال فقده
cards.en: When 120 years have passed since the day he was born, he is judged dead. His wife keeps her 'idda (the waiting time before she may remarry), and his wealth goes to his heirs alive at that time. Heirs who died before then get nothing, and he inherits from no one who died while he was missing.

cards.ask: Salim was born in the year 1300 and went missing in 1340. In which year is he judged dead?
cards.source: فإذا تم له مائة وعشرون سنة من يوم ولد حكمنا بموته
cards.why: 120 years from his birth: 1300 + 120 = 1420. The year he went missing does not matter.

cards.ask: When missing Salim is judged dead, which are true?

options.text: His wife begins her 'idda
His wealth goes to the heirs alive at that time
A son who died before that time inherits from him
He inherits from a brother who died while he was missing

source: واعتدت امرأته وقسم ماله بين ورثته الموجودين في ذلك الوقت
ومن مات منهم قبل ذلك لم يرث منه ولا يرث المفقود من أحد مات في حال فقده
cards.why: The wife starts her 'idda and living heirs inherit. Heirs who died earlier get nothing, and he inherits from no one who died while he was missing.

cards.title: The reward for returning a runaway
cards.ar: إذا أبق مملوك فرده رجل على مولاه من مسيرة ثلاثة أيام فصاعدا فله عليه الجعل أربعون درهما وإن رده لأقل من ذلك فبحسابه وإن كانت قيمته أقل من أربعين درهما قضي له بقيمته إلا درهما
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time, if a slave ran away (ibaq) and a man brought him back to his master from three days' journey or more, he was owed a reward (ju'l) of forty dirhams. For less than that, it was in proportion. If the runaway was worth less than forty dirhams, the reward was his value less one dirham.

cards.ask: In al-Quduri's time, a runaway worth 30 dirhams is brought back from four days' journey. What is the reward?
cards.source: وإن كانت قيمته أقل من أربعين درهما قضي له بقيمته إلا درهما
cards.why: Worth less than forty, so the reward is his value less one dirham: 30 - 1 = 29.

cards.title: Escaping again, witnesses, a pledge
cards.ar: وإن أبق من الذي رده فلا شيء عليه وينبغي أن يشهد إذا أخذه أنه يأخذه ليرده فإن كان العبد الآبق رهنا فالجعل على المرتهن
cards.en: If the runaway escapes again from the man bringing him back, that man owes nothing. He should have witnesses when he takes him that he is taking him to return him. If the runaway had been pledged as security for a debt, the reward is on the murtahin (the one holding the pledge).

cards.ask: Which are true?

options.text: A missing man's marriage stays in place
The reward for three days' journey or more is forty dirhams
If the runaway escapes again from the finder, the finder owes nothing
A missing man inherits from relatives who die while he is missing
If the runaway was pledged, his owner pays the reward

source: ولا يفرق بينه وبين امرأته
من مسيرة ثلاثة أيام فصاعدا فله عليه الجعل أربعون درهما
وإن أبق من الذي رده فلا شيء عليه
ولا يرث المفقود من أحد مات في حال فقده
فالجعل على المرتهن
cards.why: The first three are in the text. The missing man does not inherit while missing, and for a pledged runaway the pledge-holder pays.

lessons.title: Reviving dead land
lessons.arabic: الموات: ما لا ينتفع به من الأرض

cards.title: What dead land is
cards.ar: الموات: ما لا ينتفع به من الأرض لانقطاع الماء عنه أو لغلبه الماء عليه أو ما أشبه ذلك مما يمنع الزراعة
cards.en: Mawat (dead land) is land that cannot be used, because water does not reach it, or water floods it, or something like that which stops it being farmed.

cards.ask: What is mawat?
options: Land that cannot be used, such as land cut off from water
Land near a village, kept as grazing for its people
Land owned in Islam whose owner is well known
cards.source: الموات: ما لا ينتفع به من الأرض لانقطاع الماء عنه
cards.why: Mawat is land that cannot be used, for example because water has been cut off from it.

cards.title: Ownerless and far away
cards.ar: فما كان منها عاديا لا مالك له أو كان مملوكا في الإسلام لا يعرف له مالك بعينه وهو بعيد من القرية بحيث إذا وقف إنسان في أقصى العامر فصاح لم يسمع الصوت فيه فهو موات
cards.en: It counts as mawat if it has no owner from ancient times, or was owned in Islamic times but no particular owner is known, and it is far from the village: so far that if a person stood at the edge of the lived-in land and shouted, his voice would not be heard there.

cards.ask: A patch of dry land has no known owner. If you stand by the last house of the village and shout, your voice can be heard there. Is it mawat?
options: No, it is too close to the village
Yes, because it has no owner
Yes, if no water reaches it
cards.source: بحيث إذا وقف إنسان في أقصى العامر فصاح لم يسمع الصوت فيه فهو موات
cards.why: Mawat must be far enough that a shout from the edge of the village is not heard there.

cards.title: With the imam's permission
cards.ar: من أحياه بإذن الإمام ملكه وإن أحياه بغير إذنه لم يملكه عند أبي حنيفة وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد: يملكه ويملك الذمي بالإحياء كما يملك المسلم
cards.en: Reviving (ihya') land is bringing it to life, as by farming it. Whoever revives it with the permission of the imam (the ruler) owns it; without it, he does not, for Abu Hanifa. A dhimmi (a non-Muslim under Muslim rule) owns land by reviving it, as a Muslim does. Note: Abu Hanifa's two students say he owns it anyway.

cards.title: Marking land but leaving it
cards.ar: ومن حجر أرضا ولم يعمرها ثلاث سنين أخذها الإمام ودفعها إلى غيره
cards.en: If someone marks off land (tahjir, for example with a ring of stones) but does not work it for three years, the imam takes it and gives it to someone else.

cards.ask: According to Abu Hanifa, does he own the land?
items: Adil revives it with the imam's permission
Bashir, a dhimmi, revives it with the imam's permission
Hadi revives it without asking the imam
Karim marks it with stones and does nothing for three years
source: من أحياه بإذن الإمام ملكه وإن أحياه بغير إذنه لم يملكه عند أبي حنيفة
ويملك الذمي بالإحياء كما يملك المسلم
ومن حجر أرضا ولم يعمرها ثلاث سنين أخذها الإمام ودفعها إلى غيره
cards.why: Reviving with the imam's permission gives ownership, to a dhimmi as to a Muslim. Without permission, or marking it and leaving it three years, does not.

cards.title: Land near the village
cards.ar: ولا يجوز إحياء ما قرب من العامر ويترك مرعى لأهل القرية ومطرحا لحصائدهم
cards.en: Land close to the lived-in area may not be revived. It is left as grazing for the village people and a place to lay out their harvest.

cards.title: The zone around a well
cards.ar: ومن حفر بئرا في برية فله حريمها فإن كانت البئر للعطن فحريمها أربعون ذراعا وإن كانت للناضح فستون ذراعا وإن كانت عينا فحريمها ثلاثمائة ذراع ومن أراد أن يحفر في حريمها منع منه
cards.en: Whoever digs a well in the open desert has its harim: a protected zone around it. A well where camels rest and drink ('atan) has 40 cubits (a cubit, dhira', is about an arm's length). A well where a camel draws water for crops (nadih) has 60. A spring has 300. No one may dig inside that zone.

cards.ask: Yusuf digs a well in the desert, and a camel draws its water to irrigate his fields. How big is its protected zone?
cards.source: وإن كانت للناضح فستون ذراعا
cards.why: A well where a camel draws water for crops (nadih) has a zone of 60 cubits.

cards.ask: Next to Yusuf's spring, 100 cubits away, Omar starts digging his own well. What happens?
options: He is stopped: a spring's zone is 300 cubits
He may dig: he is outside 60 cubits
He may dig if the imam allows
source: وإن كانت عينا فحريمها ثلاثمائة ذراع
ومن أراد أن يحفر في حريمها منع منه
cards.why: A spring is protected for 300 cubits, so digging at 100 is inside its zone and is stopped.

cards.title: Land a river leaves
cards.ar: وما ترك الفرات أو الدجلة وعدل عنه فإن كان يجوز عوده إليه لم يجز إحياؤه وإن كان لا يجوز أن يعود إليه فهو كالموات
cards.en: Land that the Euphrates or Tigris has left, as the river changed its course: if the river might come back to it, it may not be revived. If it cannot come back, it is like dead land, and whoever revives it with the imam's permission owns it.

cards.ask: Which are true?

options.text: Land a river left, which it may return to, cannot be revived
Land near the village, kept for grazing, cannot be revived
Marked land left unworked for three years is given to someone else
A man with a canal in another's land has a bank zone without proof (Abu Hanifa)
A spring's protected zone is 40 cubits

source: فإن كان يجوز عوده إليه لم يجز إحياؤه
ولا يجوز إحياء ما قرب من العامر ويترك مرعى لأهل القرية
ومن حجر أرضا ولم يعمرها ثلاث سنين أخذها الإمام ودفعها إلى غيره
ومن كان له نهر في أرض غيره فليس له حريمه عند أبي حنيفة إلا أن يقيم بينة على ذلك
وإن كانت عينا فحريمها ثلاثمائة ذراع
cards.why: The first three are in the text. For Abu Hanifa a canal in someone else's land has no zone unless he proves it, and a spring's zone is 300 cubits.

lessons.title: Permission to trade
lessons.arabic: إذا أذن المولى لعبده في التجارة

cards.title: General permission
cards.ar: إذا أذن المولى لعبده في التجارة إذنا عاما جاز تصرفه في سائر التجارات: يشتري ويبيع ويرهن ويسترهن
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time, a master (mawla) could give his slave permission (idhn) to trade. Such a slave is called ma'dhun, "the permitted one". With general permission he may do every kind of trade: buy, sell, give a pledge and take a pledge (rahn: security for a debt).

cards.title: One kind, or one thing
cards.ar: وإن أذن له في نوع منها دون غيره فهو مأذون
cards.en: If the master gives permission for one kind of trade only, he is permitted in all of them. But if he gives permission for one particular thing, like "buy me this sheep", he is not a permitted trader at all; it is just an errand.

cards.ask: In al-Quduri's time, a master told his slave, "Trade only in cloth." The slave also buys and sells grain. Was that allowed?
options: Yes, permission for one kind covers all kinds
Only if the master allows it again
cards.source: وإن أذن له في نوع منها دون غيره فهو مأذون
cards.why: Permission for one kind of trade makes him a permitted trader in every kind.

cards.ask: A master tells his slave, "Go and buy me this one sheep." Is the slave now a permitted trader?
options: No, it was only an errand
Yes, in all kinds of trade
cards.source: وإن أذن له في شيء بعينه فليس بمأذون
cards.why: Permission for one particular thing does not make him a permitted trader.

cards.title: What he may and may not do
cards.ar: وإقرار المأذون بالديون والغصوب جائز وليس له أن يتزوج ولا أن يزوج مماليكه ولا يكاتب ولا يعتق على مال ولا يهب بعوض ولا بغير عوض إلا أن يهدي اليسير من الطعام أو يضيف من يطعمه
cards.en: His iqrar (admission) that he owes debts or took things by force is accepted. But he may not marry, marry off the slaves under him, make a kitaba (a deal to free a slave for payment), free a slave for money, or give gifts. He may give a small present of food or invite someone to a meal.

cards.ask: Can the permitted trader do it?
items: Admit that he owes a debt
source: يشتري ويبيع ويرهن ويسترهن
وإقرار المأذون بالديون والغصوب جائز وليس له أن يتزوج
cards.why: Trading and admitting debts are allowed. Marrying is not.

cards.ask: Can the permitted trader give this away?
items: Invite a customer to a meal
source: ولا يعتق على مال ولا يهب بعوض ولا بغير عوض إلا أن يهدي اليسير من الطعام أو يضيف من يطعمه
cards.why: Small hospitality is allowed. Gifts and freeing a slave for money are not.

cards.title: His debts
cards.ar: وديونه متعلقة برقبته: يباع للغرماء إلا أن يفديه المولى ويقسم ثمنه بينهم بالحصص فإن فضل من ديونه شيء طولب به بعد الحرية
cards.en: His trading debts are tied to his own person: he is sold to pay his creditors (ghurama'), unless the master pays them off instead. The price is shared among the creditors in proportion to what each is owed. Whatever debt is left over, he is asked to pay after he becomes free.

cards.ask: A permitted trader owes Amr 1,000 dirhams and Zaid 500. He is sold for 900. How is the 900 shared?
cards.source: ويقسم ثمنه بينهم بالحصص
cards.why: In proportion: Amr is owed two-thirds of the debt and Zaid one-third, so 600 and 300.

cards.ask: After the sale, 600 dirhams of his debts are still unpaid. What happens to them?
options: He pays them once he is free
The master must pay them off himself
cards.source: فإن فضل من ديونه شيء طولب به بعد الحرية
cards.why: Leftover debt waits until he is free, and then he is asked to pay it.

cards.ask: Which are true?

options.text: Permission for one kind of trade covers every kind
The master can stop the sale by paying the debts himself
His admission that he owes a debt is accepted
General permission lets him marry
Permission for one particular thing makes him a permitted trader

source: وإن أذن له في نوع منها دون غيره فهو مأذون
إلا أن يفديه المولى
وإقرار المأذون بالديون والغصوب جائز
وليس له أن يتزوج
وإن أذن له في شيء بعينه فليس بمأذون
cards.why: The first three are in the text. He may not marry, and permission for one particular thing is not trading permission.

lessons.title: When permission ends, and dealing with the master
lessons.arabic: وإن حجر عليه لم يصر محجورا عليه

cards.title: Stopping him
cards.ar: وإن حجر عليه لم يصر محجورا عليه حتى يظهر الحجر بين أهل سوقه فإن مات المولى أو جن أو لحق بدار الحرب مرتدا صار المأذون محجورا عليه وإن أبق العبد صار محجورا عليه
cards.en: Hajr is stopping someone from trading. If the master stops him, it only counts once it is made known among the people of his market. His permission also ends if the master dies, goes insane, or leaves Islam and joins the enemy's land (dar al-harb), or if the slave runs away.

cards.ask: A master privately tells his permitted trader at home, "Stop trading." Nobody in the market knows. Next day the trader sells a rug to Ahmad. Is the sale valid?
options: Yes, the ban was not public
No: the master had already stopped him
cards.source: لم يصر محجورا عليه حتى يظهر الحجر بين أهل سوقه
cards.why: A ban only takes effect once it is known among the people of his market.

cards.ask: Which of these end his permission to trade?

options.text: The master dies
The master goes insane
The slave runs away
The master's ban is made known in the market
The master tells him privately to stop
The master travels to another city

source: حتى يظهر الحجر بين أهل سوقه فإن مات المولى أو جن
وإن أبق العبد صار محجورا عليه
cards.why: Death, insanity, running away and a ban made known in the market all end it. A private word or a journey does not.

cards.title: His word after the ban
cards.ar: وإذا حجر عليه فإقراره جائز فيما في يده من المال عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: After he is stopped, his admission about the goods still in his hand is accepted, according to Abu Hanifa.

cards.ask: His master has banned him and the market knows. He then admits he owes Zaid 200, to be paid from goods in his hand. For Abu Hanifa, does it count?
options: Yes, for the goods in his hand
No, a banned trader's word is void
cards.source: وإذا حجر عليه فإقراره جائز فيما في يده من المال عند أبي حنيفة
cards.why: For Abu Hanifa, his admission still counts for the goods he holds after the ban.

cards.title: Debts that swallow everything
cards.ar: وإن لزمته ديون تحيط بماله ورقبته لم يملك المولى ما في يده فإن أعتق عبيده لم يعتقوا عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: If his debts are as large as his goods and his own value together, the master does not own what is in his hand. So if the master frees slaves the trader bought, they are not freed, for Abu Hanifa. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say the master does own them.

cards.ask: A permitted trader's debts are greater than all his goods and his own value. His master frees one of the slaves the trader bought. According to Abu Hanifa, is that slave freed?
options: No: the master does not own those slaves
Yes: the trader bought them for the master
Yes, and the master pays the creditors
cards.source: فإن أعتق عبيده لم يعتقوا عند أبي حنيفة
cards.why: With debts that swallow everything, the master does not own those slaves, so his freeing them does not work, for Abu Hanifa.

cards.title: Selling to and from the master
cards.ar: وإذا باع من المولى شيئا بمثل قيمته جاز فإن باعه بنقصان لم يجز فإن باعه المولى شيئا بمثل القيمة جاز البيع فإن سلمه إليه قبل قبض الثمن بطل الثمن وإن أمسكه في يده حتى يستوفي الثمن جاز
cards.en: If the trader sells something to his master at its fair value, it is valid; below its value, it is not. If the master sells him something at fair value, the sale is valid. But if the master hands it over before being paid, the price is cancelled. If he keeps it until he is paid, it is fine.

cards.ask: Is the sale valid?
items: The trader sells his master a camel at its fair value
The trader sells his master a camel below its value
The master sells the trader a horse at fair value
cards.source: وإذا باع من المولى شيئا بمثل قيمته جاز فإن باعه بنقصان لم يجز فإن باعه المولى شيئا بمثل القيمة جاز البيع
cards.why: Fair value both ways is valid; the trader selling to his master below value is not.

cards.title: Freeing a trader in debt
cards.ar: وإن أعتق المولى المأذون وعليه ديون فعتقه جائز والمولى ضامن لقيمته للغرماء وما بقي من الديون يطالب به المعتق وإذا ولدت المأذونة من مولاها فذلك حجر عليها
cards.en: If the master frees the permitted trader while he has debts, the freeing is valid, but the master must pay the creditors the trader's value. The freed man is asked for the rest of the debts. And if a permitted woman trader has a child by her master, that ends her permission.

cards.ask: A master frees his permitted trader, who is worth 1,000 dirhams and owes 1,500. Who pays what?
options: The master pays all 1,500 of it
cards.source: والمولى ضامن لقيمته للغرماء وما بقي من الديون يطالب به المعتق
cards.why: The master pays the trader's value (1,000) to the creditors; the remaining 500 is on the freed man.

cards.title: A child given permission
cards.ar: وإن أذن ولي الصبي في التجارة فهو في الشراء والبيع كالعبد المأذون إذا كان يعقل البيع والشراء
cards.en: If a child's guardian (wali) gives him permission to trade, he is like the permitted trader in buying and selling, as long as he understands buying and selling.

cards.ask: Which are true?

options.text: A guardian can let a child who understands trade, like a permitted trader
Freeing a trader in debt is valid, but the master owes the creditors his value
If the master hands over what he sold before being paid, the price is cancelled
A ban told only in private stops his trading
The trader may sell to his master below value

source: وإن أذن ولي الصبي في التجارة فهو في الشراء والبيع كالعبد المأذون
فعتقه جائز والمولى ضامن لقيمته للغرماء
فإن سلمه إليه قبل قبض الثمن بطل الثمن
حتى يظهر الحجر بين أهل سوقه
فإن باعه بنقصان لم يجز
cards.why: The first three are in the text. A ban must be known in the market, and selling to the master below value is not allowed.

cards.title: Abu Hanifa and the two companions
cards.ar: قال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله: المزارعة بالثلث والربع باطلة وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد: جائزة
cards.en: Muzara'a (sharecropping) is when one person gives land and another farms it, and they share the crop, for example a third or a quarter each way. Abu Hanifa says sharecropping for a third or a quarter is invalid. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say it is allowed, and al-Quduri goes on to set out its details on their view.

cards.ask: What does Abu Hanifa say about sharecropping for a third or a quarter? Complete it.
cards.ar: قال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله: المزارعة بالثلث والربع ____
cards.source: قال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله: المزارعة بالثلث والربع باطلة
cards.why: باطلة: for Abu Hanifa, sharecropping for a share of the crop is invalid.

cards.title: The four ways (on the two companions' view)
cards.ar: وهي عندهما على أربعة أوجه: إذا كانت الأرض والبذر لواحد والعمل والبقر لواحد جازت المزارعة وإن كانت الأرض لواحد والعمل والبقر والبذر لآخر جازت
cards.en: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad allow it, and the rest of these lessons follow their view. For them it comes in four ways. Land and seed from one, work and oxen from the other: allowed. Land from one, and work, oxen and seed from the other: allowed.

cards.ask: On the two companions' view, in how many ways can sharecropping be set up?
cards.source: وهي عندهما على أربعة أوجه
cards.why: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad set out four ways of sharing land, seed, oxen and work.

cards.ask: Sami gives the land and the seed. Bakr brings his oxen and does the work. For Abu Yusuf and Muhammad, is this sharecropping valid?
options: Yes: it is one of the allowed ways
No: the oxen must come with the land
Only if Bakr also brings the seed
cards.source: إذا كانت الأرض والبذر لواحد والعمل والبقر لواحد جازت المزارعة
cards.why: Land and seed from one side, and work and oxen from the other, is one of the allowed ways.

cards.title: The other two ways
cards.ar: وإن كانت الأرض والبقر والبذر لواحد والعمل لآخر جازت وإن كانت الأرض والبقر لواحد والبذر والعمل لآخر فهي باطلة
cards.en: Land, oxen and seed from one, and only the work from the other: allowed. But land and oxen from one, and seed and work from the other: invalid.

cards.ask: For Abu Yusuf and Muhammad, which of the four ways of sharecropping are allowed?

options.text: Land and seed from one; work and oxen from the other
Land from one; work, oxen and seed from the other
Land and oxen from one; seed and work from the other
Land, oxen and seed from one; only the work from the other

source: وهي عندهما على أربعة أوجه: إذا كانت الأرض والبذر لواحد والعمل والبقر لواحد جازت المزارعة وإن كانت الأرض لواحد والعمل والبقر والبذر لآخر جازت
وإن كانت الأرض والبقر والبذر لواحد والعمل لآخر جازت وإن كانت الأرض والبقر لواحد والبذر والعمل لآخر فهي باطلة
cards.why: Three of the four ways are allowed. Only land and oxen from one side, with seed and work from the other, is invalid.

cards.title: A known period
cards.ar: ولا تصح المزارعة إلا على مدة معلومة
cards.en: For Abu Yusuf and Muhammad, who allow it, sharecropping is only valid for a known period, such as one year.

cards.ask: Two neighbours agree to sharecrop a field "for as long as we like", with no period named. For Abu Yusuf and Muhammad, is the contract valid?
options: No, it needs a known period
cards.source: ولا تصح المزارعة إلا على مدة معلومة
cards.why: Sharecropping is only valid for a known period.

cards.title: The crop must be shared
cards.ar: ومن شرائطها: أن يكون الخارج مشاعا بينهما فإن شرطا لأحدهما قفزانا مسماة فهي باطلة وكذلك إن شرطا ما على الماذيانات والسواقي
cards.en: Another condition: the crop must be shared between them as a portion, like a half. If they set a fixed number of qafiz (a measure of grain) for one of them, it is invalid. The same if they give one side whatever grows along the water channels (madhiyanat and sawaqi).

cards.ask: A farmer and a landowner agree, "The first 10 qafiz of wheat go to the landowner, and the rest we split." Is it valid?
options: No: the crop must be shared as a portion
Yes, if the harvest is big
Yes, the split makes it fair
cards.source: فإن شرطا لأحدهما قفزانا مسماة فهي باطلة
cards.why: Naming a fixed number of qafiz for one side spoils it: the crop must be shared as a portion.

cards.ask: Which does a valid sharecropping contract need, for Abu Yusuf and Muhammad?

options.text: A known period
The crop shared as a portion between them, such as a half
A fixed number of qafiz for the landowner
The crop by the water channels kept for one side
Payment in cash before sowing

source: ولا تصح المزارعة إلا على مدة معلومة
ومن شرائطها: أن يكون الخارج مشاعا بينهما
وكذلك إن شرطا ما على الماذيانات والسواقي
cards.why: A known period and a shared portion of the crop. A fixed amount or the channel crop for one side makes it invalid.

cards.title: When the contract is valid
cards.ar: وإذا صحت المزارعة فالخارج بينهما على الشرط فإن لم تخرج الأرض شيئا فلا شيء للعامل
cards.en: When the sharecropping is valid, the crop is shared as they agreed. If the land produces nothing, the worker gets nothing.

cards.ask: Their valid contract gives the farmer half the crop. A drought comes and nothing grows. What does the farmer get?
options: A fair wage for his work
Half the value of an average crop
cards.source: فإن لم تخرج الأرض شيئا فلا شيء للعامل
cards.why: In a valid contract his pay is his share of the crop, so with no crop he gets nothing.

cards.title: When the contract is fasid
cards.ar: وإذا فسدت المزارعة فالخارج لصاحب البذر فإن كان البذر من قبل رب الأرض فللعامل أجر مثله لا يزاد على مقدار ما شرط له من الخارج وإن كان البذر من قبل العامل فلصاحب الأرض أجر مثلها
cards.en: If the sharecropping is fasid (faulty), the crop belongs to whoever gave the seed. If the landowner gave the seed, the worker gets a fair wage (the usual pay for such work), but no more than the share of the crop he was promised. If the worker gave the seed, the landowner gets a fair rent for his land.

cards.ask: Their contract turns out fasid. The landowner gave the seed. Who gets the crop, and what does the farmer get?
options: The landowner; the farmer gets a capped wage
The farmer gets the crop, since he did the work
They split the crop in half anyway
cards.source: فإن كان البذر من قبل رب الأرض فللعامل أجر مثله لا يزاد على مقدار ما شرط له من الخارج
cards.why: In a fasid contract the crop follows the seed, and the worker is paid a capped fair wage.

cards.ask: Another fasid contract: this time the farmer brought the seed. Who gets the crop?
options: The farmer, who pays the landowner a fair rent
The landowner, who pays the farmer a wage
source: وإذا فسدت المزارعة فالخارج لصاحب البذر
وإن كان البذر من قبل العامل فلصاحب الأرض أجر مثلها
cards.why: The crop goes to the seed owner, here the farmer, and the landowner gets a fair rent for the land.

cards.title: Refusing to go on, and death
cards.ar: وإن امتنع الذي ليس من قبله البذر أجبره الحاكم على العمل وإذا مات أحد المتعاقدين بطلت المزارعة
cards.en: Once the contract is made, if the one who gives the seed refuses to go on, he is not forced. But if the other one refuses, the judge forces him to do his part. If either of them dies, the sharecropping ends.

cards.ask: The landowner provides the seed. After the contract, the farmer (who gives no seed) refuses to work. What happens?
options: Nothing: no one can be forced
cards.source: وإن امتنع الذي ليس من قبله البذر أجبره الحاكم على العمل
cards.why: The side that gives no seed can be forced by the judge; only the seed owner is free to refuse.

cards.title: The period ends before harvest
cards.ar: انقضت مدة المزارعة والزرع لم يدرك كان على المزارع أجر مثل نصيبه من الأرض إلى أن يستحصد والنفقة على الزرع عليهما على مقدار حقوقهما وأجره الحصاد والرفاع والدياس والتذرية عليهما بالحصص فإن شرطاه في المزارعة على العامل فسدت
cards.en: If the period ends before the crop is ripe, the farmer pays a fair rent for his share of the land until harvest, and the crop's costs are on both by their shares. So are harvesting, carrying, threshing and winnowing. If the contract puts these on the worker alone, it becomes fasid.

cards.ask: The period has ended before harvest. Who pays?
items: Looking after the crop until it ripens
Rent for his share of the land until harvest
source: كان على المزارع أجر مثل نصيبه من الأرض إلى أن يستحصد والنفقة على الزرع عليهما على مقدار حقوقهما
والدياس والتذرية عليهما بالحصص
cards.why: Crop costs and harvest work are shared by their shares; the farmer alone pays rent for his share of the land until harvest.

cards.ask: Which are true?

options.text: The death of either one ends the sharecropping
In a fasid contract, the crop goes to whoever gave the seed
The side that gives no seed can be forced to work
Making the worker pay all harvest costs in the contract is fine
In a valid contract with no crop, the worker gets a fair wage

source: وإذا مات أحد المتعاقدين بطلت المزارعة
وإذا فسدت المزارعة فالخارج لصاحب البذر
أجبره الحاكم على العمل
فإن شرطاه في المزارعة على العامل فسدت
فإن لم تخرج الأرض شيئا فلا شيء للعامل
cards.why: The first three are in the text. Putting harvest costs on the worker makes it fasid, and in a valid contract with no crop he gets nothing.

cards.title: Musaqat
cards.ar: باب المساقاة قال أبو حنيفة: المسافاة بجزء من الثمرة باطلة
cards.en: Musaqat is when one person gives his trees and another waters and tends them for a share of the fruit. Abu Hanifa says musaqat for a share of the fruit is invalid. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad allow it if they name a known period and a shared portion of the fruit.

cards.ask: What does Abu Hanifa say about musaqat for a share of the fruit? Complete it.
cards.ar: بجزء من الثمرة ____ وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد
cards.source: بجزء من الثمرة باطلة
cards.why: باطلة: for Abu Hanifa, musaqat for a share of the fruit is invalid.

cards.title: What it can be on
cards.ar: وتجوز المساقاة في النخل والشجر والكرم والرطاب وأصول الباذنجان
cards.en: For Abu Yusuf and Muhammad, who allow it, musaqat can be on date palms, other trees, grapevines (karm), green fodder plants (ritab), and aubergine plants.

cards.ask: Which can musaqat be made on?

options.text: Date palms
Grapevines
Aubergine plants
Fruit trees
A flock of sheep
A shop

cards.source: وتجوز المساقاة في النخل والشجر والكرم والرطاب وأصول
cards.why: Palms, trees, vines, green plants and aubergines are listed; animals and shops are not.

cards.title: Fruit already on the palms
cards.ar: فإن دفع نخلا فيه ثمره مساقاة والثمرة تزيد بالعمل جاز وإن كانت قد انتهت لم يجز
cards.en: If he gives palms with fruit already on them, it is allowed if the fruit still grows with the work. If the fruit is already fully grown, it is not allowed.

cards.ask: Idris gives his palms to a worker for musaqat, but the dates are already fully ripe and nothing more will grow from the work. Is it allowed?
options: No: the work must make the fruit grow
Yes: any palms may be given for musaqat
cards.source: وإن كانت قد انتهت لم يجز
cards.why: The work must make the fruit grow; fruit that is already finished cannot be tended for a share.

cards.title: Fasid, death, and excuses
cards.ar: وإذا فسدت المساقاة فللعامل أجر مثله وتبطل المساقاة بالموت وتفسخ بالإعذار كما تفسخ الإجارة
cards.en: If the musaqat is fasid, the worker gets a fair wage. It ends with death, and it can be cancelled for genuine excuses ('udhr), just as an ijara (a hire contract) can be.

cards.ask: A musaqat contract turns out to be fasid after a season of the worker's watering and pruning. What does the worker get?
options: A fair wage for his work
cards.source: وإذا فسدت المساقاة فللعامل أجر مثله
cards.why: In a fasid musaqat the worker is paid the usual wage for such work.

cards.ask: Which are true of musaqat?

options.text: It ends when one of them dies
It can be cancelled for genuine excuses, like a hire contract
It is allowed on palms whose fruit still grows with the work
It is allowed on dates that are already fully ripe
In a fasid musaqat the worker gets nothing

source: وتبطل المساقاة بالموت وتفسخ بالإعذار كما تفسخ الإجارة
والثمرة تزيد بالعمل جاز
وإن كانت قد انتهت لم يجز
فللعامل أجر مثله
cards.why: The first three are in the text. Fully ripe fruit cannot be given for musaqat, and a worker in a fasid one gets a fair wage.

lessons.title: Making a nikah: offer, acceptance, witnesses

cards.title: Offer and acceptance
cards.ar: النكاح ينعقد بالإيجاب والقبول بلفظين يعبر بهما عن الماضي أو يعبر بأحدهما عن الماضي وبالآخر عن المستقبل مثل أن يقول: زوجتي فيقول زوجتك
cards.en: A nikah (the marriage contract) is made by an offer (ijab) and an acceptance (qabul). Both phrases can be in the past tense, like "I have married you", or one can be past and the other about the future. For example, one asks "Marry me", and the other answers "I have married you".

cards.ask: What makes a nikah? Complete it.
cards.ar: النكاح ينعقد بالإيجاب ____
cards.source: النكاح ينعقد بالإيجاب والقبول
cards.why: والقبول: a nikah is made by an offer and an acceptance.

cards.title: Two witnesses
cards.ar: ولا يعقد نكاح المسلمين إلا بحضور شاهدين حرين بالغين عاقلين مسلمين أو رجل وامرأتين
cards.en: A nikah between Muslims is only made in front of two witnesses: two men, or one man and two women. Each must be 1) free, 2) adult, 3) sane and 4) Muslim.

cards.title: Even if not known as upright
cards.ar: عدولا كانوا
cards.en: The witnesses count whether or not they are known as upright ('adl) people, and even if they were once punished for qadhf (falsely accusing someone of zina, unlawful relations).

cards.ask: Yusuf and Maryam make their nikah. The only witness is Maryam's friend Hafsa, an adult Muslim woman. Is the nikah made?
options: No: one woman alone is not enough
Yes: one Muslim witness is enough
Yes, if Hafsa is known as upright
cards.source: إلا بحضور شاهدين حرين بالغين عاقلين مسلمين أو رجل وامرأتين
cards.why: The book needs two witnesses, or one man and two women. One woman alone does not make the nikah.

cards.ask: Which of these can be the witnesses of a Muslim nikah?

options.text: Two free, adult, sane Muslim men
One Muslim man and two Muslim women
Two Muslim men not known as upright
Two 10-year-old Muslim boys
One Muslim man on his own

source: شاهدين حرين بالغين عاقلين مسلمين أو رجل
عدولا كانوا
cards.why: Two adult Muslim men, or one man and two women, even if they are not known as upright. Children and a single man are not enough.

cards.title: A Muslim man marrying a dhimmi woman
cards.ar: فإن تزوج مسلم ذمية بشهادة ذميين جاز عند أبي حنيفة وأبي يوسف وقال محمد: لا يجوز
cards.en: A dhimmi is a Jew or Christian living under Muslim rule. If a Muslim man marries a dhimmi woman with two dhimmi witnesses, it is valid for Abu Hanifa and Abu Yusuf. Note: Muhammad says it is not valid.

cards.title: Which words make a nikah
cards.ar: وينعقد النكاح بلفظ النكاح والتزويج والتمليك والهبة والصدقة ولا ينعقد بلفظ الإجارة والإباحة
cards.en: A nikah is made with five words: 1) nikah, 2) tazwij (marrying), 3) tamlik (giving ownership), 4) hiba (gift), 5) sadaqa (charity). It is not made with ijara (hiring) or ibaha (allowing).

cards.ask: How many words does the book name that make a nikah?
cards.source: وينعقد النكاح بلفظ النكاح والتزويج والتمليك والهبة والصدقة
cards.why: Five: nikah, tazwij, tamlik, hiba and sadaqa.

cards.ask: Which of these words make a nikah?

options.text: Tamlik (giving ownership)
Ijara (hiring)
Sadaqa (charity)
Nikah
Ibaha (allowing)

cards.source: وينعقد النكاح بلفظ النكاح والتزويج والتمليك والهبة والصدقة ولا ينعقد بلفظ الإجارة والإباحة
cards.why: Tamlik, sadaqa and nikah are among the five words. Ijara and ibaha do not make a nikah.

cards.ask: Does this word make a nikah?
cards.source: وينعقد النكاح بلفظ النكاح والتزويج والتمليك والهبة والصدقة ولا ينعقد بلفظ الإجارة والإباحة
cards.why: Nikah, tazwij, tamlik, hiba and sadaqa make a nikah. Ijara and ibaha do not.

cards.ask: Ali says to Zaynab's father, before two adult Muslim men, "Marry your daughter to me", and with her consent he answers "I have married her to you". Is the nikah made?
options: Yes: offer, acceptance and two witnesses
No: both phrases must be in the past tense
source: أو يعبر بأحدهما عن الماضي وبالآخر عن المستقبل
ولا يعقد نكاح المسلمين إلا بحضور شاهدين
cards.why: One phrase may be about the future and the other past, and two witnesses were there, so the nikah is made.

lessons.title: Whom a man may never marry
lessons.arabic: ولا يحل للرجل أن يتزوج بأمه

cards.title: Close family by blood
cards.ar: ولا يحل للرجل أن يتزوج بأمه ولا بجداته من قبل الرجال والنساء ولا ببنته ولا ببنت ولده وإن سفلت ولا بأخته ولا ببنات أخته ولا ببنات أخيه ولا بعمته
cards.en: A man may never marry his mother, his grandmothers on his father's or mother's side, his daughter, his granddaughters however many generations down, his sister, his sister's or brother's daughters, or his father's sister.

cards.ask: Granddaughters however far... Complete it.
cards.ar: ولا ببنت ولده وإن ____
cards.source: ولا ببنت ولده وإن سفلت
cards.why: وإن سفلت: however many generations down she is, she is forbidden.

cards.title: Family through marriage
cards.ar: بخالته ولا بأم دخل بابنتها أو لم يدخل ولا ببنت امرأته التي دخل بها سواء كانت في حجره أو في حجر غيره ولا بامرأة أبيه وأجداده ولا بامرأة ابنه وبني أولاده
cards.en: Nor his mother's sister. Nor his wife's mother, whether or not the marriage was consummated (dukhul: the couple have been together as husband and wife). Nor his wife's daughter, once the marriage with her mother was consummated, whether she grew up in his home or not. Nor the wives of his father or grandfathers, or of his sons or grandsons.

cards.ask: Khalid married Huda, but they divorced before they were ever together as husband and wife. May Khalid now marry Huda's mother?
options: No: a wife's mother is forbidden either way
Yes: without dukhul her mother is not forbidden
Yes, but only after Huda remarries
cards.source: ولا بأم دخل بابنتها أو لم يدخل
cards.why: A wife's mother is forbidden whether or not the marriage was consummated.

cards.ask: Khalid's divorce from Huda came before any dukhul. Huda has a daughter, Sana, from an earlier marriage. May Khalid marry Sana?
options: Yes: there was no dukhul with her mother
No: a wife's daughter is always forbidden
No, because Sana grew up away from him
cards.source: ولا ببنت امرأته التي دخل بها
cards.why: The book forbids the daughter of a wife "he has been with". Here there was no dukhul, so Sana is not forbidden.

cards.title: Milk relations
cards.ar: ولا بأمه من الرضاعة
cards.en: Nor his milk-mother: a woman who breastfed him as a baby (rada'a). The book goes on to name milk-siblings too.

cards.ask: Which of these may a man never marry?

options.text: His mother's sister
His wife's mother
His father's former wife
His son's wife
His father's brother's daughter (his cousin)

source: بخالته ولا بأم دخل بابنتها أو لم يدخل
ولا بامرأة أبيه وأجداده ولا بامرأة ابنه
cards.why: His maternal aunt, his wife's mother, his father's wife and his son's wife are all named. A cousin is not in the list.

cards.ask: Forbidden to him, or not?
source: ولا بأمه من الرضاعة
ولا بأم دخل بابنتها أو لم يدخل ولا ببنت امرأته التي دخل بها
cards.why: The milk-mother and the wife's mother are forbidden. The wife's daughter is forbidden only after dukhul. A cousin is not named.

cards.ask: Umar's son divorced his wife Rania. May Umar marry Rania?
options: No: a son's wife is forbidden to him
Yes: she is no longer his son's wife
Yes, if his son never had dukhul with her
cards.source: ولا بامرأة ابنه وبني أولاده
cards.why: The wife of his son or grandson is forbidden to him, so Umar may not marry Rania.

lessons.title: Who may not be married together

cards.title: Two sisters, or a woman and her aunt
cards.ar: ولا يجمع بين أختين بنكاح ولا بملك يمين وطئا ولا يجمع بين المرأة وبين عمتها وخالتها ولا ابنة أخيها ولا ابنة أختها
cards.en: A man may not be married to two sisters at the same time. Nor may he be married at once to a woman and her aunt (father's or mother's sister), or a woman and her niece.

cards.ask: Omar is married to Amina. May he also marry Amina's sister Safa while Amina is his wife?
options: No: two sisters may not be married together
Yes: a man may have up to four wives at once
cards.source: ولا يجمع بين أختين بنكاح
cards.why: Two sisters may never be his wives at the same time.

cards.title: The general rule
cards.ar: ولا يجمع بين امرأتين لو كانت كل واحدة منهما رجلا لم يجز له أن يتزوج بالأخرى ولا بأس أن يجمع بين امرأة وابنة زوج كان لها من قبل
cards.en: The rule: two women may not be married to one man together if, were either of them a man, he could not marry the other. But there is no harm in marrying a woman and the daughter of her former husband (from another wife) together.

cards.ask: Hassan is married to Layla. Layla's former husband has a daughter, Nour, from a different wife. May Hassan marry Nour as well?
options: No: they are like mother and daughter
No: they are like two sisters
cards.source: ولا بأس أن يجمع بين امرأة وابنة زوج كان لها من قبل
cards.why: The book says there is no harm in marrying a woman and her former husband's daughter together.

cards.ask: Which pairs may NOT be one man's wives at the same time?

options.text: Two sisters
A woman and her father's sister
A woman and her mother's sister
A woman and her brother's daughter
A woman and her former husband's daughter
Two women who are not related

source: ولا يجمع بين أختين
ولا يجمع بين المرأة وبين عمتها وخالتها ولا ابنة أخيها ولا ابنة أختها
ولا بأس أن يجمع بين امرأة وابنة زوج كان لها من قبل
cards.why: Sisters, aunt and niece may not be combined. A woman and her former husband's daughter may, and unrelated women may.

cards.title: After zina
cards.ar: ومن زنى بامرأة حرمت عليه أمها وابنتها
cards.en: If a man commits zina (unlawful relations) with a woman, her mother and her daughter become forbidden for him to marry.

cards.title: Her sister during the iddah
cards.ar: امرأته طلاقا بائنا لم يجز له أن يتزوج بأختها حتى تنقضي عدتها
cards.en: If a man gives his wife a ba'in divorce (a final divorce that ends the marriage at once), he may not marry her sister until her iddah ends. The iddah is the waiting period a woman keeps after a divorce.

cards.ask: Tariq gave his wife a ba'in divorce. Her iddah has one month left. May he marry her sister now?
options: No: not until the iddah ends
Yes: a ba'in divorce ends the marriage at once
Yes, if his former wife agrees
cards.source: لم يجز له أن يتزوج بأختها حتى تنقضي عدتها
cards.why: He must wait until his former wife's iddah is over before marrying her sister.

cards.title: Owner and slave
cards.ar: ولا يجوز أن يتزوج المولى أمته ولا المرأة عبدها
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time some people were enslaved. An owner (mawla) may not marry his own slave woman (ama), and a woman may not marry her own slave ('abd).

cards.ask: Which of these may a man do?
options: Marry a woman and her former husband's daughter together
Marry a woman and her mother's sister at the same time
Marry his ex-wife's sister while her iddah is still running
source: ولا بأس أن يجمع بين امرأة وابنة زوج كان لها من قبل
ولا ابنة أخيها ولا ابنة أختها
حتى تنقضي عدتها
cards.why: Only the woman and her former husband's daughter may be combined. Aunt and niece may not, and the sister must wait for the iddah to end.

lessons.title: People of the Book, ihram, two in one contract

cards.title: Women of the Book
cards.ar: ويجوز تزوج الكتابيات ولا يجوز تزوج المجوسيات ولا الوثنيات
cards.en: A Muslim man may marry a kitabiyya: a Jewish or Christian woman, from the People of the Book. He may not marry a Majusi woman (a fire-worshipper) or an idol-worshipper.

cards.title: The Sabians
cards.ar: ويجوز تزوج الصابئيات إذا كانوا يؤمنون بنبي ويقرون بكتاب وإن كانوا يعبدون الكواكب ولا كتاب لهم لم تجز مناكحتهم
cards.en: He may marry a Sabian woman if her people believe in a prophet and accept a revealed book. If they worship the stars and have no book, marrying them is not allowed.

cards.ask: Adam, a Muslim, wants to marry Sarah, a Christian woman. Is this allowed?
options: No: she must become Muslim first
Only if she is a Sabian
cards.source: ويجوز تزوج الكتابيات
cards.why: A Christian woman is from the People of the Book, so he may marry her.

cards.ask: May a Muslim man marry her?
items: A Sabian who believes in a prophet and a book
source: ويجوز تزوج الكتابيات ولا يجوز تزوج المجوسيات ولا الوثنيات
وإن كانوا يعبدون الكواكب ولا كتاب لهم لم تجز مناكحتهم
cards.why: Women of the Book and Sabians with a prophet and book are allowed. Majusi, idol-worshipping and bookless star-worshipping women are not.

cards.title: Nikah in ihram
cards.ar: ويجوز للمحرم والمحرمة أن يتزوجا في حال الإحرام
cards.en: Ihram is the sacred state a pilgrim enters for Hajj or Umrah. A man or woman in ihram may still marry.

cards.ask: Bilal and Zaynab are both in ihram for Umrah. Their families want to hold the nikah in Makkah before they finish. May they?
options: Yes: a nikah in ihram is allowed
No: they must wait until they leave ihram
Only the woman may be in ihram
cards.source: ويجوز للمحرم والمحرمة أن يتزوجا في حال الإحرام
cards.why: Al-Quduri allows both the man and the woman in ihram to marry.

cards.title: Two women in one contract
cards.ar: ومن تزوج امرأتين في عقد واحد إحداهما لا يحل له نكاحها صح نكاح التي يحل له نكاحها وبطل نكاح الأخرى
cards.en: If a man marries two women in one contract and one of them is not allowed for him, the nikah with the allowed woman stands and the other is void.

cards.ask: In one contract, Yahya marries Asma, a Muslim, and Roxana, a Majusi woman. What happens?
options: Asma's nikah stands; Roxana's is void
Both are void, as the contract was one
Both stand, as the contract was one
source: صح نكاح التي يحل له نكاحها وبطل نكاح الأخرى
ولا يجوز تزوج المجوسيات
cards.why: A Majusi woman is not allowed for him, so only her nikah is void. Asma's stands.

cards.ask: Which word completes it?
cards.ar: ويجوز تزوج ____ ولا يجوز تزوج المجوسيات
cards.source: ويجوز تزوج الكتابيات ولا يجوز تزوج المجوسيات
cards.why: الكتابيات: women of the Book may be married; Majusi women may not.

cards.title: An adult woman's consent
cards.ar: وينعقد نكاح المرأة الحرة البالغة العاقلة برضاها وإن لم يعقد عليها ولي عند أبي حنيفة بكر كانت أو ثيبا وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد: لا ينعقد إلا بولي
cards.en: A free, adult, sane woman's nikah is made by her own consent, for Abu Hanifa, even if no wali (guardian) contracts it for her. This is so whether she is a bikr (never married before) or a thayyib (married before). Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say it needs a wali.

cards.title: No forcing, and silence as a yes
cards.ar: ولا يجوز للولي إجبار البكر البالغة على النكاح وإذا استأذنها فسكتت أو ضحكت أو بكت فذلك إذن منها وإن أبت لم يزوجها
cards.en: A wali may not force an adult bikr to marry. If he asks her permission and she stays silent, laughs or cries, that is her permission. If she refuses, he may not marry her off.

cards.ask: Aisha, an adult bikr, is told by her father about a proposal from Hamza and asked if she agrees. She stays quiet. What does her silence mean?
options: He must ask her again until she speaks
cards.source: وإذا استأذنها فسكتت أو ضحكت أو بكت فذلك إذن منها
cards.why: For a bikr, silence, laughing or crying when asked counts as permission.

cards.ask: Fatima, an adult bikr, clearly says no to a proposal. Her father still wants it. May he marry her off?
options: No: if she refuses, he may not
Yes: a father can decide for a bikr
Yes, if the man is a good match
source: ولا يجوز للولي إجبار البكر البالغة على النكاح
وإن أبت لم يزوجها
cards.why: A wali cannot force an adult bikr. Her refusal stops the nikah.

cards.title: A thayyib must say it
cards.ar: وإذا استأذن الثيب فلا بد من رضاها بالقول
cards.en: When a thayyib (a woman married before) is asked, her consent must be spoken in words.

cards.ask: How does a thayyib consent? Complete it.
cards.ar: وإذا استأذن الثيب فلا بد من رضاها ____
cards.source: وإذا استأذن الثيب فلا بد من رضاها بالقول
cards.why: بالقول: in words. Silence is enough only for a bikr.

cards.ask: Khadija, a widow, is asked by her brother about a proposal. She only smiles. Has she consented?
options: No: a thayyib must agree in words
Yes: smiling counts as her permission
Yes, because she did not refuse
cards.source: فلا بد من رضاها بالقول
cards.why: Smiling is permission only from a bikr. A widow is a thayyib, so she must say it.

cards.title: Still counted a bikr
cards.ar: وإذا زالت بكارتها بوثبة أو حيضة أو جراح فهي في حكم الأبكار
cards.en: If a girl loses the physical sign of being a bikr through a jump, a heavy period or an injury, she is still treated as a bikr.

cards.ask: Hiba lost the physical sign of being a bikr through an injury. She is asked about a proposal and stays silent. What is her silence?
options: Her permission: she is still a bikr
Not enough: she must say it in words
cards.source: وإذا زالت بكارتها بوثبة أو حيضة أو جراح فهي في حكم الأبكار
cards.why: A jump, a heavy period or an injury leaves her a bikr, and a bikr's silence is her permission.

cards.title: If they disagree about her answer
cards.ar: وإذا قال الزوج: بلغك النكاح فسكت وقال: بل رددت فالقول قولها ولا يمين عليها ولا يستحلف في النكاح عند أبي حنيفة وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد: يستحلف فيه
cards.en: If the husband says "You heard of the nikah and stayed silent" and she says "No, I refused", her word is accepted and she does not have to swear an oath. For Abu Hanifa no oath is asked for in nikah. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say an oath may be asked for.

cards.ask: Ahmad says Sumayya stayed silent when told of the nikah. Sumayya says she refused at once. Whose word is accepted?
options: Ahmad's, if he swears an oath
cards.source: فالقول قولها ولا يمين عليها
cards.why: The word is hers, and she does not have to swear.
