cards.why: Two years at most and six months at least; no 'idda between dhimmis; under six months the child is not his. Her nikah is valid, but he waits until the birth.

cards.title: Food, clothing and a home
cards.ar: النفقة واجبة على زوجها مسلمة كانت أو كافرة
cards.en: Nafaqa (maintenance) is what a husband must provide for his wife: her food, her clothing and her home. It is due to her whether she is Muslim or not, once she has come to live in his home.

cards.title: Measured by them both
cards.ar: فعليه نفقتها وكسوتها وسكناها يعتبر ذلك لحالهما جميعا موسرا كان الزوج أو معسرا
cards.en: He owes her food, clothing and housing. How much is judged by the situation of both of them together, whether the husband is well off (musir) or short of money (mu'sir).

cards.ask: What does the husband owe his wife? Complete it.
cards.ar: فعليه نفقتها وكسوتها ____
cards.source: فعليه نفقتها وكسوتها وسكناها
cards.why: وسكناها: he owes her food, clothing and a home to live in.

cards.title: Waiting for the mahr, or leaving his home
cards.ar: فإن امتنعت من تسليم نفسها حتى يعطيها مهرها فلها النفقة وإن نشزت
cards.en: If she will not move to his home until he gives her the mahr (the marriage gift owed to her), she still gets maintenance, because she has that right. But if she becomes nashiza (leaves his home in defiance, without a right), she has no maintenance until she comes back.

cards.ask: Fatima's nikah is done, but she will not move into her husband's home until he pays the mahr due to her. Does she get maintenance meanwhile?
options: Yes: she is holding back for her right
No: she has not moved into his home yet
cards.source: فإن امتنعت من تسليم نفسها حتى يعطيها مهرها فلها النفقة
cards.why: Waiting for the mahr that is owed to her does not take away her maintenance.

cards.ask: After a quarrel, Huda leaves her husband's home without any right to, and stays away for two months. Does she get maintenance for those months?
options: No, not until she returns to his home
Yes: she is still his wife, so it is due
cards.source: نفقة لها حتى تعود إلى منزله
cards.why: A wife who leaves in defiance has no maintenance until she returns to his home.

cards.title: When one of them is young
cards.ar: وإن كانت صغيرة لا يستمتع بها فلا نفقة لها وإن سلمت نفسها إليه وإن كان الزوج صغيرا لا يقدر على الوطء والمرأة كبيرة فلها النفقة من ماله
cards.en: If the wife is still a young girl, too young for married life, she has no maintenance even if she is handed over to him. If the husband is a young boy, too young for married life, and the wife is grown up, she gets maintenance from his wealth.

cards.ask: Zaynab is grown up, but her husband is a young boy, too young for married life. Does she get maintenance?
options: Yes, from the boy's own wealth
No: he is too young for it
No, not until he is old enough to live with her
cards.source: فلها النفقة من ماله
cards.why: When the husband is too young and the wife is grown up, she gets maintenance from his wealth.

cards.title: Divorce and death
cards.ar: وإذا طلق الرجل امرأته فلها النفقة والسكنى في عدتها رجعيا كان أو بائنا ولا نفقة للمتوفى عنها زوجها
cards.en: If a man divorces his wife, she gets maintenance and a home during her 'idda (the waiting time after divorce), whether the divorce is raj'i (he may take her back) or ba'in (final). A widow gets no maintenance.

cards.title: When the separation is her wrongdoing
cards.ar: وكل فرقة جاءت من قبل المرأة بمعصية فلا نفقة لها وإن طلقها ثم ارتدت سقطت نفقتها وإن أمكنت ابن زوجها من نفسها إن كان بعد الطلاق فلها النفقة وإن كان قبل الطلاق فلا نفقة لها
cards.en: Any separation that comes from the wife by a sin leaves her no maintenance. If he divorced her and she then leaves Islam, her maintenance ends. Likewise, if she wrongly allows her husband's son to be intimate with her: if this is after the divorce she keeps her maintenance, but if it is before, she has none.

cards.ask: Sakina was divorced with a raj'i divorce. During her 'idda she leaves Islam. What happens to her maintenance?
cards.source: وإن طلقها ثم ارتدت سقطت نفقتها
cards.why: Leaving Islam after the divorce ends her maintenance, because the cause comes from her own wrongdoing.

cards.title: Away from home, or ill
cards.ar: وإذا حبست المرأة في دين أو غصبها رجل كرها فذهب بها أو حجت مع محرم فلا نفقة لها وإن مرضت في منزل الزوج فلها النفقة
cards.en: If she is held in prison for a debt, or a man takes her away by force, or she goes for Hajj with a mahram (a close relative she may not marry), she has no maintenance for that time. If she falls ill in her husband's home, she still gets it.

cards.ask: Does the wife get maintenance?
items: She is in her 'idda after a ba'in divorce
She left his home in defiance and has not returned
She has gone for Hajj with her brother
source: وإن مرضت في منزل الزوج فلها النفقة
فلها النفقة والسكنى في عدتها رجعيا كان أو بائنا
نفقة لها حتى تعود إلى منزله
أو حجت مع محرم فلا نفقة لها
ولا نفقة للمتوفى عنها زوجها
cards.why: Illness at home and the 'idda of divorce keep her maintenance. Leaving in defiance, Hajj with a mahram and widowhood do not.

lessons.title: Her servant, her home and her family
lessons.arabic: وعليه أن يسكنها في دار منفردة

cards.title: A servant
cards.ar: وتفرض على الزوج نفقة خادمها إذا كان موسرا ولا تفرض لأكثر من خادم واحد
cards.en: If the husband is well off, he must also pay for her servant's keep. But he is not made to pay for more than one servant.

cards.ask: Umar is wealthy. His wife has three servants and asks the judge to make him pay for all of them. What does the judge order?
options: The keep of one servant only
None: servants are her own affair
cards.source: وتفرض على الزوج نفقة خادمها إذا كان موسرا ولا تفرض لأكثر من خادم واحد
cards.why: A wealthy husband pays for her servant, but never for more than one.

cards.title: A home of her own
cards.ar: وعليه أن يسكنها في دار منفردة ليس فيها أحد من أهله إلا أن تختار ذلك وإن كان له ولد من غيرها فليس له أن يسكنه معها
cards.en: He must give her a home of her own, with none of his relatives living in it, unless she chooses that. If he has a child from another wife, he may not make that child live with her.

cards.title: Her parents and family
cards.ar: للزوج أن يمنع والديها وولدها من غيره وأهلها من الدخول عليها ولا يمنعهم من النظر إليها وكلامها أي وقت اختاروا
cards.en: The husband may stop her parents, her child from another husband, and her relatives from coming into the home. But he may not stop them from seeing her and speaking with her, at any time they choose.

cards.ask: Which of these are right about the wife's home?

options.text: She may refuse to share the house with his relatives
He may not make his son from another wife live with her
He may not stop her parents seeing and speaking with her
He may stop her parents from ever speaking with her
She must live with his family if he wishes

source: في دار منفردة ليس فيها أحد من أهله إلا أن تختار ذلك
وإن كان له ولد من غيرها فليس له أن يسكنه معها
ولا يمنعهم من النظر إليها وكلامها أي وقت اختاروا
cards.why: She has the right to a home without his relatives, unless she chooses otherwise, and without his child from another wife. Her family may always see her and speak with her.

cards.title: When he cannot pay
cards.ar: ومن أعسر بنفقة امرأته لم يفرق بينهما ويقال لها: استديني عليه
cards.en: If a husband cannot afford his wife's maintenance, they are not separated for that. She is told: borrow, and it becomes his debt.

cards.ask: Bilal has lost his work and cannot pay his wife's maintenance. She asks the judge to end the marriage. What does the judge do?
options: He cancels Bilal's duty to pay
cards.source: ومن أعسر بنفقة امرأته لم يفرق بينهما ويقال لها: استديني عليه
cards.why: Being unable to pay is no reason to separate them. She borrows, and the debt is on him.

cards.ask: Rashid is poor and does not have a servant to pay for. His wife says he must pay for one. Must he?
options: No: only a well-off husband pays it
Yes: a wife is always owed a servant
Yes: every husband must pay for one servant
cards.source: وتفرض على الزوج نفقة خادمها إذا كان موسرا
cards.why: The servant's keep is ordered only when the husband is well off.

lessons.title: When maintenance is owed or missed

cards.title: An absent husband
cards.ar: وإذا غاب الرجل وله مال في يد رجل وهو يعرف به وبالزوجية فرض القاضي في ذلك المال نفقة زوجة الغائب وأولاده الصغار ووالديه ويأخذ منها كفيلا بها ولا يقضى بنفقة في مال الغائب إلا لهؤلاء
cards.en: If a husband is away and someone holds his money, and that person admits it and admits the marriage, the judge orders maintenance from that money for his wife, his young children and his parents. He takes a guarantor (kafil) from her. No one else is given maintenance from an absent man's money.

cards.ask: Yasin is abroad. His friend holds his money and admits both the money and the marriage. Who can the judge give maintenance to from it?
options: His wife, his young children and his parents
Any poor relative of his, such as his brother
cards.source: فرض القاضي في ذلك المال نفقة زوجة الغائب وأولاده الصغار ووالديه
cards.why: From an absent man's money, maintenance is ordered only for his wife, his young children and his parents.

cards.title: If he becomes richer
cards.ar: وإذا قضى القاضي لها بنفقة الإعسار ثم أيسر فخاصمته تمم لها نفقة الموسر
cards.en: If the judge set her maintenance at the level of a poor man, and the husband then becomes well off, and she takes it to the judge, he raises it to the level of a well-off man.

cards.title: Months that went unpaid
cards.ar: وإذا مضت مدة لم ينفق الزوج عليها وطالبته بذلك فلا شيء لها إلا أن يكون القاضي فرض لها النفقة أو صالحت الزوج على مقدارها
cards.en: If time passes and he does not maintain her, and she asks for it later, she gets nothing for the past, unless the judge had already set her maintenance, or she had agreed an amount with her husband. If he dies after the judge's order while months were still unpaid, that unpaid maintenance falls away.

cards.ask: Ayesha's husband gave her nothing for three months. No judge had set an amount and they had never agreed one. She now asks for the three months. What does she get?
options: All three months, as he owed them
cards.source: فلا شيء لها إلا أن يكون القاضي فرض لها النفقة أو صالحت الزوج على مقدارها
cards.why: Past maintenance is owed only if a judge set it or the couple agreed an amount. Neither happened here.

cards.title: Paid in advance, then he dies
cards.ar: وإن أسلفها نفقة سنة ثم مات
cards.en: If he paid her a year's maintenance in advance and then died, nothing is taken back from her. Note: Muhammad says she keeps only what covers the time that passed, and the rest goes back to the husband.

cards.title: In al-Quduri's time: an enslaved husband or wife
cards.ar: وإذا تزوج العبد حرة فنفقتها دين عليه يباع فيها وإذا تزوج الرجل أمة فبوأها مولاها معه منزلا فعليه النفقة وإن لم يبوئها فلا نفقة لها
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time, if an enslaved man married a free woman, her maintenance was a debt on him, and he could be sold to pay it. If a man married a slave woman and her master gave her a home with her husband, he owed her maintenance; if not, he did not.

cards.ask: The judge set Mariam's maintenance at a poor man's level. Later her husband becomes rich, and she takes him back to the judge. What happens?
options: The judge raises it to a rich man's level
Nothing: the first order stands as it was
cards.source: ثم أيسر فخاصمته تمم لها نفقة الموسر
cards.why: Maintenance follows his means: when he becomes well off and she asks, it is raised to the level of a well-off man.

cards.title: The father alone
cards.ar: ونفقة الأولاد الصغار على الأب لا يشاركه فيها أحد كما لا يشاركه في نفقة الزوجة أحد
cards.en: The maintenance of young children is on their father, and no one shares it with him, just as no one shares with him the maintenance of his wife.

cards.title: Nursing the baby
cards.ar: فليس على أمه أن ترضعه ويستأجر له الأب من ترضعه عندها فإن استأجرها وهي زوجته أو معتدته لترضع ولدها لم يجز وإن انقضت عدتها فاستأجرها على إرضاعه جاز
cards.en: If the young child is a nursing baby, the mother is not made to nurse it; the father hires a woman to nurse it at her side. If he hires the mother herself while she is his wife or in her 'idda from him, the hiring is not valid. Once her 'idda is over, he may hire her.

cards.ask: Ali divorced Sumayya, and her 'idda is now over. He hires her for a wage to nurse their baby son. Is this hiring valid?
options: No: a mother can never be paid to nurse her own child
Only if no one else is available
cards.source: وإن انقضت عدتها فاستأجرها على إرضاعه جاز
cards.why: Once her 'idda is over, the father may hire her to nurse their child.

cards.title: The mother comes first
cards.ar: فإن قال الأب لا أستأجرها وجاء بغيرها فرضيت الأم بمثل أجر الأجنبية كانت الأم أحق به وإن التمست زيادة لم يجبر الزوج عليها
cards.en: If the father says, "I will not hire her," and brings another woman, but the mother is happy with the same wage as the stranger, the mother has more right to nurse the baby. If she asks for more, the father is not forced to pay it.

cards.ask: A father finds a nurse who will take 100 dirhams. The baby's mother, whose 'idda is over, offers to nurse for the same 100. Who has more right?
cards.source: فرضيت الأم بمثل أجر الأجنبية كانت الأم أحق به
cards.why: When the mother accepts the same wage as the stranger, she has more right to nurse her child.

cards.title: Even if their religion differs
cards.ar: ونفقة الصغير واجبة على أبيه وإن خالفه في دينه كما تجب نفقة الزوجة على الزوج وإن خالفته في دينه
cards.en: A young child's maintenance is due from the father even if their religion differs, just as a wife's maintenance is due from her husband even if her religion is different from his.

cards.ask: Which of these are right about a young child's maintenance and nursing?

options.text: The father pays it alone
The father must pay even if the child's religion differs from his
The mother is not forced to nurse the baby
The mother's family shares the cost
He may validly hire his own wife to nurse their baby

source: ونفقة الأولاد الصغار على الأب لا يشاركه فيها أحد
ونفقة الصغير واجبة على أبيه وإن خالفه في دينه
فليس على أمه أن ترضعه
فإن استأجرها وهي زوجته أو معتدته لترضع ولدها لم يجز
cards.why: The father alone pays, whatever the child's religion, and the mother is not forced to nurse. Hiring his own wife for it is not valid.

cards.ask: A divorced mother whose 'idda is over offers to nurse the baby, but asks for more than the nurse the father found. Must the father pay her higher wage?
options: No, he is not forced to
Yes: the mother always has more right
Yes, but only half of the extra
cards.source: وإن التمست زيادة لم يجبر الزوج عليها
cards.why: The mother comes first only at the same wage. If she asks for more, he is not forced to pay it.

cards.title: The mother has the most right
cards.ar: كتاب الحضانة وإذا وقعت الفرقة بين الزوجين فالأم أحق بالولد فإن لم تكن الأم فأم الأم أولى من أم الأب
cards.en: Hadana is the right to bring up and look after a young child. When husband and wife separate, the mother has the most right to the child. If there is no mother, the mother's mother comes before the father's mother.

cards.title: Who comes next
cards.ar: فإن لم تكن فأم الأب أولى من الأخوات فإن لم تكن جدة فلأخوات أولى من العمات والخالات وتقدم الأخت من الأب والأم ثم الأخت من الأم ثم الأخت من الأب ثم الخالات أولى من العمات
cards.en: After the grandmothers come the child's sisters, who come before aunts: first a full sister, then a sister through the mother, then a sister through the father. Then the mother's sisters (khalat), who come before the father's sisters ('ammat), each in the same order.

cards.ask: Put these in the order of their right to bring up the child.
source: فالأم أحق بالولد فإن لم تكن الأم فأم الأم أولى من أم الأب
وتقدم الأخت من الأب والأم ثم الأخت من الأم ثم الأخت من الأب ثم الخالات أولى من العمات وينزلن كذلك ثم العمات ينزلن كذلك
cards.why: Mother, then her mother, then the father's mother, then sisters (full, through the mother, through the father), then the mother's sisters, then the father's sisters.

cards.title: If she marries
cards.ar: وكل من تزوجت من هؤلاء سقط حقها إلا الجدة إذا كان زوجها الجد وإن لم تكن للصبي امرأة من أهله واختصم فيه الرجال فأولاهم به أقربهم تعصبيا
cards.en: Any of these women who marries loses her right, except a grandmother married to the child's grandfather. If the child has no woman in the family and the men dispute over him, the one with most right is the closest relative through the father's line.

cards.ask: After the divorce, little Hasan lives with his mother. She then marries another man. Hasan's mother's mother is alive. What happens to the mother's right?
options: It falls away, and her mother comes next
It passes to the father at once, as she remarried
source: وكل من تزوجت من هؤلاء سقط حقها
فإن لم تكن الأم فأم الأم أولى من أم الأب
cards.why: A woman who marries loses her right, so it moves on to the next in line: the mother's mother.

cards.title: Until what age
cards.ar: والأم والجدة أحق بالغلام حتى يأكل وحده ويلبس وحده ويستنجي وحده وبالجارية حتى تحيض ومن سوى الأم والجدة أحق بالجارية حتى تبلغ حدا تشتهى
cards.en: The mother and grandmother keep a boy until he can eat, dress and clean himself after the toilet on his own, and a girl until she reaches puberty. Other women keep a girl until she is old enough to be thought of for marriage.

cards.ask: Musa's son now eats, dresses and cleans himself all on his own. Until now the boy has lived with his divorced mother. Does her right over him continue?
options: No: he can now do these on his own
Yes, until he is an adult
Yes, until he reaches the age of ten
cards.source: والأم والجدة أحق بالغلام حتى يأكل وحده ويلبس وحده ويستنجي وحده
cards.why: The mother's right over a boy lasts until he can eat, dress and clean himself on his own.

cards.title: Other mothers
cards.ar: والأمة إذا أعتقها مولاها وأم الولد إذا أعتقت في الولد كالحرة وليس للأمة وأم الولد قبل العتق حق في الولد والذمية أحق بولدها المسلم ما لم يعقل الأديان ويخاف أن يألف الكفر
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time, an enslaved mother had no right of hadana until she was freed; once freed she was like a free woman. A dhimmi mother (a non-Muslim living under Muslim rule) has more right to her Muslim child until the child understands religion and there is a fear it will grow used to disbelief.

cards.title: Taking the child away
cards.ar: وإذا أرادت المطلقة أن تخرج بولدها من المصر فليس لها ذلك إلا أن تخرجه إلى وطنها وقد كان الزوج تزوجها فيه
cards.en: A divorced mother may not take the child out of the city, unless she takes it to her home town where the husband had married her.

cards.ask: Aisha was married in her home town of Basra and moved with her husband to Kufa. After the divorce she wants to take her little daughter back to Basra. May she?
options: Yes: it is her home town where he married her
No: she may never leave the city with the child
cards.source: إلا أن تخرجه إلى وطنها وقد كان الزوج تزوجها فيه
cards.why: She may take the child to her home town if that is where the husband married her.

lessons.title: Parents and relatives
lessons.arabic: وعلى الرجل أن ينفق على أبويه

cards.title: Parents and grandparents
cards.ar: وعلى الرجل أن ينفق على أبويه وأجداده وجداته إذا كانوا فقراء وإن خالفوه في دينه
cards.en: A man must maintain his parents and grandparents if they are poor, even if their religion differs from his.

cards.title: Different religions
cards.ar: ولا تجب النفقة مع اختلاف الدين إلا للزوجة والأبوين والأجداد والجدات والولد وولد الولد ولا يشارك الولد في نفقة أبويه أحد
cards.en: When the religion differs, maintenance is due only to a wife, parents, grandparents, children and grandchildren. And no one shares with a child the maintenance of his parents.

cards.ask: Hamid is Muslim. Which of these poor relatives, who are not Muslim, must he still maintain?

options.text: His father
His grandmother
His young son
His brother
His uncle

source: ولا تجب النفقة مع اختلاف الدين إلا للزوجة والأبوين والأجداد والجدات والولد وولد الولد
ولا تجب نفقتهم مع اختلاف الدين
cards.why: With a different religion, only wife, parents, grandparents, children and grandchildren are owed maintenance. Brothers and uncles are not.

cards.title: Other close relatives
cards.ar: والنفقة لكل ذي رحم محرم إذا كان صغيرا فقيرا أو كانت امرأة بالغة فقيرة أو كان ذكرا زمنا أو أعمى فقيرا ويجب ذلك على مقدار الميراث
cards.en: Maintenance is also due to every close relative he may never marry (dhu rahim mahram), if the relative is a poor child, a poor grown woman, or a poor man who is chronically disabled or blind. It is shared out in the same proportions as inheritance.

cards.title: Father two-thirds, mother one-third
cards.ar: وتجب نفقة الابنة البالغة والابن الزمن على أبويه أثلاثا: على الأب الثلثان وعلى الأم الثلث
cards.en: A grown daughter, or a son who is chronically disabled, is maintained by both parents in thirds: two-thirds from the father and one-third from the mother.

cards.ask: Sara is grown up, unmarried and poor. Both her parents are alive and able. Her maintenance costs 300 dirhams a month. How much does her father pay?
cards.source: على الأب الثلثان وعلى الأم الثلث
cards.why: The father pays two-thirds (200) and the mother one-third (100).

cards.title: When it is not due
cards.ar: ولا تجب نفقتهم مع اختلاف الدين ولا تجب على الفقير
cards.en: These other relatives are not owed maintenance when the religion differs, and it is not due from someone who is poor.

cards.ask: Khalid's adult brother is blind and poor, and they share the same religion. Khalid is well off. Must he maintain his brother?
options: Yes: a poor blind brother is owed it
No: only parents and children are owed it
cards.source: أو كان ذكرا زمنا أو أعمى فقيرا
cards.why: A brother is a close relative he may never marry, and a poor blind man is owed maintenance by such relatives.

lessons.title: An absent son's money, and those one owns

cards.title: An absent son's money
cards.ar: وإذا كان للابن الغائب مال فضي عليه بنفقة أبويه وإن باع أبوه متاعه في نفقته جاز عند أبي حنيفة وإن باع العقار لم يجز
cards.en: If a son is away and has money, the judge orders his parents' maintenance from it. If his father sells the son's goods (movable things) for his own keep, it is valid according to Abu Hanifa. If he sells the son's land or buildings, it is not valid.

cards.title: Who is holding the money
cards.ar: وإن كان للابن الغائب مال في يد أبويه فانفقا منه لم يضمنا وإن كان له مال في يد أجنبي فأنفق عليهما بغير إذن القاضي ضمن
cards.en: If the absent son's money is with his parents and they spend from it on themselves, they owe nothing back. If it is with a stranger who spends it on them without the judge's permission, the stranger must pay it back.

cards.ask: Idris is travelling. He left 1,000 dirhams with his poor parents, and they spend 200 on their food. Must they pay it back?
options: No: they spent on themselves from money in their hands
cards.source: وإن كان للابن الغائب مال في يد أبويه فانفقا منه لم يضمنا
cards.why: Parents who spend on themselves from their absent son's money in their own hands owe nothing.

cards.ask: Idris also left money with his neighbour Saleh. Without asking the judge, Saleh spends some of it on Idris's poor parents. What follows?
options: Nothing: it was spent on the parents
The parents must pay it back
cards.source: وإن كان له مال في يد أجنبي فأنفق عليهما بغير إذن القاضي ضمن
cards.why: A stranger who spends the money without the judge's permission must make it good.

cards.title: Unpaid months fall away
cards.ar: وإذا قضى القاضي للولد والوالدين وذوي الأرحام بالنفقة فمضت مدة سقطت إلا أن يأذن القاضي في الاستدانة عليه
cards.en: If the judge orders maintenance for children, parents or other relatives, and time passes without it being paid, it falls away, unless the judge allowed them to borrow against him.

cards.ask: The judge ordered Tahir to maintain his poor uncle, but did not let the uncle borrow against Tahir. Four months pass unpaid. Does Tahir owe the four months?
cards.source: فمضت مدة سقطت إلا أن يأذن القاضي في الاستدانة عليه
cards.why: The unpaid months fall away, because the judge had not allowed borrowing against him.

cards.title: In al-Quduri's time: those one owned
cards.ar: وعلى المولى أن ينفق على عبده وأمته فإن امتنع وكن لهما كسب اكتسبا وأنفقها على أنفسهما وإن لم يكن لهما كسب أجبر المولى على بيعهما
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time, a master had to provide for the people he owned. If he refused and they could earn, they worked and spent on themselves. If they could not earn, the master was forced to sell them to someone who would provide for them.

cards.ask: Which are right about maintenance from an absent son's money?

options.text: The judge may order parents' maintenance from an absent son's money
A stranger who spends it without the judge's permission must repay it
In al-Quduri's time, a master who refused to provide could be forced to sell
Unpaid relatives' maintenance is always owed later
Parents who spend from their son's money in their hands must repay it

source: وإذا كان للابن الغائب مال فضي عليه بنفقة أبويه
فأنفق عليهما بغير إذن القاضي ضمن
أجبر المولى على بيعهما
فمضت مدة سقطت
فانفقا منه لم يضمنا
cards.why: Parents can be maintained from his money, a stranger without permission repays, and a master who would not provide was forced to sell. Unpaid months fall away, and parents holding the money owe nothing.

cards.title: Who can free a slave
cards.ar: العتق يقع من الحر البالغ
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time there were slaves, and freeing them ('itq) was a great good deed. A slave is freed by a free, adult owner. The owner is called the mawla (master).

cards.title: Clear words free at once
cards.ar: أنت حر أو محرر أو قد حررتك أو أعتقتك فقد عتق نوى المولى العتق أو لم ينو وكذلك إذا قال: رأسك حر أو وجهك أو رقبتك
cards.en: If the master says to his slave "You are free", "You are freed", "I have freed you" or "I have set you free", the slave is free, whether the master meant it or not. These words are clear (sarih). The same if he says "Your head is free", or your face, or your neck: these stand for the whole person.

cards.ask: Bashir jokingly says to his slave, "I have freed you," without meaning it at all. Is the slave free?
options: Yes: clear words free whether meant or not
No: he did not intend it
Only if he repeats it three times
cards.source: أو أعتقتك فقد عتق نوى المولى العتق أو لم ينو
cards.why: Clear words like "I have freed you" free the slave even without the intention.

cards.title: Hinting words need an intention
cards.ar: ولو قال: لا ملك لي عليك ونوي به الحرية عتق وإن لم ينو لم يعتق وكذلك كنايات العتق وإن قال: لا سلطان لي عليك ونوى به العتق لم يعتق
cards.en: If he says "I have no ownership over you" and means freedom, the slave is free; if he did not mean it, he is not. All hinting words (kinayat) work this way: they need the intention (niyya). But "I have no authority (sultan) over you" does not free him, even if he meant freedom.

cards.ask: Hamid tells his slave Rafiq, "I have no authority over you," and he means to free him. Is Rafiq free?
options: Yes: he meant freedom by them
Yes, but only if two men heard it
cards.source: وإن قال: لا سلطان لي عليك ونوى به العتق لم يعتق
cards.why: Al-Quduri says "no authority over you" does not free the slave, even when freedom was meant.

cards.title: Calling him "my son" or "my brother"
cards.ar: وإن قال: هذا ابني وثبت على ذلك أو قال: هذا مولاي أو يا مولاي عتق وإن قال يا ابني أو يا أخي لم يعتق
cards.en: If he says "This is my son" and stands by it, or "This is my mawla", or calls him "O my mawla", the slave is free. But just calling out "O my son!" or "O my brother!" does not free him. Note: Abu Hanifa and his two students differ over a boy too old to be his son.

cards.ask: Calling across the market, a master shouts to his slave, "O my brother, come here!" Is the slave free?
options: No: "O my brother" does not free
Yes: he called him his brother
Yes, if the slave is older than him
cards.source: وإن قال يا ابني أو يا أخي لم يعتق
cards.why: Calling out "O my son" or "O my brother" does not free a slave.

cards.ask: One master says "You are like a free man." Another says "You are nothing but free." Which slave is freed?
cards.source: وإن قال لعبده أنت مثل الحر لم يعتق وإن قال ما أنت إلا حر عتق عليه
cards.why: "Like a free man" does not free, but "nothing but free" does.

cards.ask: Is the slave freed by these words?
items: "You are free", said without thinking of freedom
"I have no ownership over you", meaning freedom
"I have no ownership over you", meaning nothing
source: نوى المولى العتق أو لم ينو
رأسك حر
ونوي به الحرية عتق وإن لم ينو لم يعتق
وإن قال يا ابني أو يا أخي لم يعتق
cards.why: Clear words free without intention, a hint frees only with it, and "O my son" does not free.

cards.title: Freed, whatever the reason or state
cards.ar: ومن أعتق عبده لوجه الله تعالى أو للشيطان أو للصنم عتق وعتق المكره والسكران واقع
cards.en: Whoever frees his slave for the sake of Allah, or even for Shaytan or an idol, has freed him. Freeing by someone forced (mukrah) or drunk also counts.

cards.ask: Which of these slaves are now free?

options.text: A master forced at knifepoint says "You are free"
A drunk master says "I have freed you"
A master says "Your neck is free"
A master says "You are like a free man"
A master says "I have no authority over you", meaning freedom

source: وعتق المكره والسكران واقع
رقبتك
أنت مثل الحر لم يعتق
لا سلطان لي عليك ونوى به العتق لم يعتق
cards.why: Freeing under force or when drunk counts, and "your neck" stands for the person. "Like a free man" and "no authority" do not free.

cards.title: Owning a close relative
cards.ar: وإذا ملك الرجل ذا رحم محرم منه عتق عليه
cards.en: If a man comes to own a close relative he could never marry (dhu rahim mahram), such as his brother or his father, that relative is freed at once.

cards.ask: Umar buys a slave and then learns he is his own brother. What happens?
options: The brother is free at once
Umar must free him within a year
cards.source: وإذا ملك الرجل ذا رحم محرم منه عتق عليه
cards.why: A brother is a dhu rahim mahram, so he is freed as soon as Umar owns him.

cards.title: Freeing part of a slave
cards.ar: وإذا أعتق المولى بعض عبده عتق عليه ذلك البعض ويسعى في بقية قيمته لمولاه عند أبي حنيفة رحمه الله وقالا يعتق كله
cards.en: If a master frees part of his slave (say half), for Abu Hanifa that part is free and the slave works to earn the rest of his value for the master. This working to pay is called si'aya. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say the whole slave is free.

cards.ask: A master says, "A third of you is free." What follows, in Abu Hanifa's view?
options: That third is free; he earns the rest
The whole slave is free at once
Nothing, since a person cannot be split
cards.source: عتق عليه ذلك البعض ويسعى في بقية قيمته لمولاه
cards.why: For Abu Hanifa the freed part is free and the slave pays off the rest by si'aya.

cards.title: A slave owned by two partners
cards.ar: وإذا كان العبد بين شريكين فأعتق أحدهما نصيبه عتق فإن كان المعتق موسرا فشريكه بالخيار إن شاء أعتقه وإن شاء ضمن شريكه قيمة نصيبه وإن شاء استسعى العبد
cards.en: If two partners own a slave and one frees his share, that share is free. If the one who freed is well-off (musir), the other partner may choose: free his share too, make his partner pay him the value of his share, or have the slave work to earn it (si'aya).

cards.ask: Hasan and Khalid own a slave together. Hasan, who is well-off, frees his half. What may Khalid do (Abu Hanifa)?

options.text: Free his own half too
Make Hasan pay him the value of his half
Have the slave work to earn his half
Take back Hasan's freeing
Sell the whole slave

cards.source: إن شاء أعتقه وإن شاء ضمن شريكه قيمة نصيبه وإن شاء استسعى العبد
cards.why: With a well-off partner, Khalid has three choices: free, make Hasan pay, or si'aya. The freeing cannot be undone.

cards.title: When the freer is poor
cards.ar: وإن كان المعتق معسرا فالشريك بالخيار إن شاء أعتق نصيبه وإن شاء استسعى العبد وهذا عند أبي حنيفة رحمه الله وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد: ليس له إلا الضمان مع اليسار والسعاية مع الإعسار
cards.en: If the freer is poor (mu'sir), the partner may free his share or have the slave work for it. This is Abu Hanifa's view. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say he only has payment from a rich partner, or the slave's work when the partner is poor.

cards.ask: Now Hasan is poor when he frees his half. Which choices does Khalid have (Abu Hanifa)?
options: Free his half, or have the slave work for it
Make Hasan pay him, or free his half
cards.source: وإن كان المعتق معسرا فالشريك بالخيار إن شاء أعتق نصيبه وإن شاء استسعى العبد
cards.why: When the freer is poor, the partner may free or ask for si'aya, but not make the poor partner pay.

cards.title: Two men buy the son of one of them
cards.ar: وإذا اشترى رجلان ابن أحدهما عتق نصيب الأب ولا ضمان عليه وكذلك إذا ورثاه فالشريك بالخيار إن شاء أعتق نصيبه وإن شاء استسعى
cards.en: If two men buy a slave who is the son of one of them, the father's share is freed and the father owes nothing. The same if they inherit him. The other partner may free his share or ask for si'aya.

cards.title: Each partner says the other freed him
cards.ar: وإذا شهد كل واحد من الشريكين على الآخر بالحرية عتق كله وسعى العبد لكل واحد منهما في نصيبه موسرين كانا أو معسرين عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: If each partner claims the other freed the slave, the whole slave is free, and he works to pay each partner his share, rich or poor, says Abu Hanifa. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad make it depend on whether each partner is rich or poor.

cards.ask: Yahya and his friend Zayd buy a slave together. The slave is Yahya's son. What happens?
options: Yahya's half is free and he owes nothing
Yahya must pay Zayd the value of his half
Nothing changes until Yahya says "You are free"
cards.source: وإذا اشترى رجلان ابن أحدهما عتق نصيب الأب ولا ضمان عليه
cards.why: The father's share is freed by owning his son, with no payment due, and the partner has his two choices.

cards.title: Freeing tied to a condition
cards.ar: وإذا أضاف العتق إلى ملك أو شرط صح كما يصح في الطلاق
cards.en: Freeing can be tied to owning or to a condition, just like divorce. For example: "If I buy you, you are free", or "If you finish this work, you are free."

cards.title: A slave who comes over as a Muslim
cards.ar: وإذا خرج عبد من دار الحرب إلينا مسلما عتق
cards.en: Dar al-harb is a land at war with the Muslims. If a slave there becomes Muslim and comes over to the Muslim lands, he is free.

cards.ask: Ya'qub is a slave in a land at war with the Muslims. He becomes Muslim and crosses into the Muslim lands. What is his state?
options: He stays a slave of his old master
cards.source: وإذا خرج عبد من دار الحرب إلينا مسلما عتق
cards.why: A slave who comes over from dar al-harb as a Muslim is free.

cards.title: A pregnant slave woman
cards.ar: وإذا أعتق جارية حاملا عتق حملها وإن أعتق الحمل خاصة عتق ولم تعتق الأم
cards.en: If he frees a pregnant slave woman, her unborn child is freed with her. If he frees only the unborn child, the child is free but the mother is not.

cards.ask: A master says to his pregnant slave woman Rayhana, "The child in your womb is free." Who is free?
options: No one until the child is born
cards.source: وإن أعتق الحمل خاصة عتق ولم تعتق الأم
cards.why: Freeing only the unborn child frees the child, not the mother.

cards.title: Freeing for money
cards.ar: وإذا أعتق عبده على مال فقبل العبد عتق ولزمه المال
cards.en: If he frees his slave for a sum of money and the slave accepts, the slave is free at once and owes the money.

cards.title: "If you pay me a thousand"
cards.ar: ولو قال: إن أديت إلي ألفا فأنت حر صح وصار مأذونا فإن أحضر المال أجبر الحاكم المولى على قبضه وعتق العبد
cards.en: If he says "If you pay me a thousand, you are free", that is valid, and the slave becomes ma'dhun: allowed to trade to earn it. If he brings the money, the judge makes the master take it, and the slave is free.

cards.ask: Mubarak's master said, "If you pay me 1,000 dirhams, you are free." Mubarak brings the 1,000, but the master refuses to take it. What happens?
options: The judge makes the master take it, and Mubarak is free
The master may refuse, since it was only a promise
Mubarak must wait for the master's death
cards.source: فإن أحضر المال أجبر الحاكم المولى على قبضه وعتق العبد
cards.why: When the slave brings the money, the judge forces the master to take it, and the slave is free.

cards.title: Whose child is free
cards.ar: وولد الأمة من مولاها حر وولدها من زوجها مملوك لسيدها وولد الحرة من العبد حر
cards.en: A slave woman's child by her master is free. Her child by her husband belongs to her master. A free woman's child by a slave husband is free.

cards.ask: Is the child free?
items: A slave woman's child by her own master
A free woman's child by her slave husband
A slave woman's child by her husband
The unborn child when his pregnant mother is freed
source: وولد الأمة من مولاها حر وولدها من زوجها مملوك لسيدها وولد الحرة من العبد حر
عتق حملها
cards.why: Only the slave woman's child by her husband stays owned; the others are free.

cards.ask: Which statement matches al-Quduri?
options: A master may tie freeing to a condition, as in divorce
Freeing the unborn child also frees its mother
A slave who pays the agreed sum still needs the master's consent
source: وإذا أضاف العتق إلى ملك أو شرط صح كما يصح في الطلاق
ولم تعتق الأم
أجبر الحاكم المولى على قبضه
cards.why: Freeing may be tied to a condition. Freeing the unborn child does not free the mother, and the judge makes the master take the money.

lessons.title: Tadbir: free when the master dies

cards.title: What tadbir is
cards.ar: إذا قال المولى لمملوكه: إذا مت فأنت حر أو أنت حر عن دبر مني
cards.en: Tadbir is when a master says to his slave "When I die, you are free", or "You are free after me", or "I have made you a mudabbar". The slave is then a mudabbar: he will be free when his master dies.

cards.ask: Complete it.
cards.ar: أو قد دبرتك فقد صار ____
cards.source: أو قد دبرتك فقد صار مدبرا
cards.why: مدبرا: "I have made you a mudabbar" makes him a mudabbar, free at the master's death, not free now.

cards.title: What the master may do with him
cards.ar: لا يجوز بيعه ولا هبته وللمولى أن يستخدمه ويؤاجره وإن كانت أمة وطئها وله أن يزوجه
cards.en: A mudabbar may not be sold or given away. The master may still have him serve him, hire him out, and marry him off. If she is a slave woman, he may be with her as before.

cards.ask: May the master do this with his mudabbar?
items: Give him to a friend as a gift
cards.source: لا يجوز بيعه ولا هبته وللمولى أن يستخدمه ويؤاجره
cards.why: Selling and giving away are not allowed. Service, hiring out and marrying him off are.

cards.title: When the master dies
cards.ar: فإذا مات المولى عتق المدبر من ثلث ماله إن خرج من الثلث وإن لم يكن له مال غيره سعى في ثلثي قيمته وإن كان على المولى دين سعى في جميع قيمته لغرمائه
cards.en: When the master dies, the mudabbar is freed out of one third of what he leaves, if he fits in that third. If the mudabbar is all the master left, he works to pay two thirds of his value. If the master had debts, he works to pay his whole value to the creditors.

cards.ask: Sa'd dies leaving 3,000 dirhams and his mudabbar, who is worth 600. He has no debts. What does the mudabbar owe?
options: Nothing: he fits in the third
His whole value, 600, to the heirs
cards.source: عتق المدبر من ثلث ماله إن خرج من الثلث
cards.why: The estate is 3,600, so a third is 1,200. The mudabbar is worth 600, which fits, so he is simply free.

cards.ask: Sa'd dies leaving nothing but his mudabbar, worth 900, and no debts. How much must the mudabbar earn and pay?
cards.source: وإن لم يكن له مال غيره سعى في ثلثي قيمته
cards.why: One third (300) is freed by the bequest; he works to pay the other two thirds: 600.

cards.title: Her child, and tadbir with a condition
cards.ar: وولد المدبرة مدبر فإن علق التدبير بموته على صفة
cards.en: The child of a mudabbara (a woman given tadbir) is a mudabbar too. But if the master ties it to one kind of death, like "If I die of this illness", the slave is not a mudabbar and may be sold. If the master does die that way, the slave is freed just as a mudabbar is.

cards.ask: Ill in bed, Nasir tells his slave, "If I die of this illness, you are free." Nasir recovers. May he now sell the slave?
options: Yes: it is not a real tadbir
No: he is a mudabbar for ever
cards.source: فليس بمدبر ويجوز بيعه فإن مات المولى على الصفة التي ذكرها عتق كما يعتق المدبر
cards.why: A tadbir tied to "this illness" does not make him a mudabbar, so he may be sold. He would be freed only if the master died of it.

cards.ask: Which are true of a mudabbar (plain tadbir)?

options.text: His master may hire him out
A mudabbara's child is a mudabbar too
If his master dies in debt, he works to pay his whole value
His master may sell him if money runs short
He is free from the day of the tadbir

source: ويؤاجره
وولد المدبرة مدبر
وإن كان على المولى دين سعى في جميع قيمته لغرمائه
لا يجوز بيعه
cards.why: He may be hired out, his mother's tadbir passes to her child, and debts make him earn his full value. He cannot be sold and is not free until the death.

lessons.title: Istilad: the mother of the master's child

cards.title: Umm walad
cards.ar: إذا ولدت الأمة من مولاها فقد صارت أم ولد له لا يجوز بيعها ولا تمليكها وله وطؤها واستخدامها وإجارتها وتزويجها
cards.en: If a slave woman has a child by her master, she becomes his umm walad ("mother of a child"). She may not be sold or given to anyone. He may still be with her, have her serve, hire her out, and marry her to someone.

cards.ask: May the master do this with his umm walad?
items: Have her serve in his home
cards.source: لا يجوز بيعها ولا تمليكها وله وطؤها واستخدامها وإجارتها وتزويجها
cards.why: She may not be sold or handed to anyone, but service, hiring out and marrying her off are allowed.

cards.title: Whose child it is
cards.ar: ولا يثبت نسب ولدها إلا أن يعترف به المولى فإن جاءت بعد ذلك بولد ثبت نسبه بغير إقرار وإن نفاه انتفى بقوله
cards.en: Nasab is a child's family line. Her child is the master's only if he admits it. After that, a later child is his without him saying so, unless he denies it: then his word removes it.

cards.title: Free at his death
cards.ar: وإن زوجها فجاءت بولد فهو حكم أمه وإذا مات المولى عتقت من جميع المال ولا تلزمها السعاية للغرماء إن كان على المولى دين
cards.en: If he marries her to someone and she has a child, the child takes his mother's ruling. When the master dies she is free out of his whole estate, and she does not have to work for his creditors even if he had debts.

cards.ask: Nura is her master's umm walad. He dies owing large debts. Must Nura work to pay the creditors?
options: Yes: she works to pay her whole value
Yes: two thirds of her value
cards.source: وإذا مات المولى عتقت من جميع المال ولا تلزمها السعاية للغرماء
cards.why: Unlike a mudabbar, an umm walad is freed from the whole estate and owes no si'aya to creditors.

cards.ask: Idris married Salma, another man's slave woman, and they had a child. Later Idris buys Salma. What is she to him now?
options: An ordinary slave he may sell
source: وإذا وطئ أمة غيره بنكاح فولدت منه
إذا ولدت الأمة من مولاها فقد صارت أم ولد له
cards.why: A slave woman who had his child in marriage becomes his umm walad once he owns her.

cards.title: A father and his son's slave woman
cards.ar: وإذا وطئ الأب جارية ابنه فجاءت بولد فادعاه ثبت نسبه وصارت أم ولد له وعليه قيمتها وليس عليه عقرها ولا قيمة ولدها
cards.en: If a father is with his son's slave woman and she has a child he claims, the child is his and she becomes his umm walad. He owes his son her value, but not her 'uqr (a fair payment like a bride gift) and not the child's value. Note: a grandfather counts like this only once the father has died.

cards.ask: Zayd's father has a child by Zayd's slave woman and claims the child. What does the father owe Zayd?
options: Her value, her 'uqr and the child's value
cards.source: وعليه قيمتها وليس عليه عقرها ولا قيمة ولدها
cards.why: He owes her value; not her 'uqr and not the child's value.

cards.title: A slave woman owned by two
cards.ar: وإذا كانت الجارية بين شريكين فجاءت بولد فادعاه أحدهما ثبت نسبه منه وصارت أم ولد له وعليه نصف عقرها ونصف قيمتها وليس عليه شيء من قيمة ولدها
cards.en: If two partners own a slave woman and one of them claims her child, the child is his and she becomes his umm walad. He owes his partner half her 'uqr and half her value, but nothing for the child.

cards.ask: Ali and Hadi own a slave woman together. She has a child, and only Ali claims it. What does Ali owe Hadi?
options: Half her 'uqr and half her value
Her full value and the child's value
Nothing, since the child is his
cards.source: وعليه نصف عقرها ونصف قيمتها وليس عليه شيء من قيمة ولدها
cards.why: The one who claims owes his partner half her 'uqr and half her value, and nothing for the child.

cards.title: When both claim the child
cards.ar: وإذا ادعياه معا ثبت نسبه منهما وكانت الأم أم ولد لهما وعلى كل واحد منهما نصف العقر قصاصا بما له على الآخر ويرث الابن من كل واحد منهما ميراث ابن كامل وهما يرثان منه ميراث أب واحد
cards.en: If both claim him together, he is the son of both, and she is umm walad to both. Each owes the other half the 'uqr, so it cancels out. The son inherits a full son's share from each, and the two together inherit one father's share from him.

cards.ask: Two partners both claim the child of the slave woman they share. When the child later dies rich, how do they inherit from him?
options: Together they take one father's share
Each takes a full father's share
source: وعلى كل واحد منهما نصف العقر قصاصا بما له على الآخر ويرث الابن من كل واحد منهما ميراث ابن كامل وهما يرثان منه ميراث أب واحد
cards.why: They share a single father's share between them, while he inherits a full son's share from each.

cards.title: The slave woman of his mukatab
cards.ar: وإذا وطئ المولى جارية مكاتبه فجاءت بولد فادعاه: فإن صدقه المكاتب ثبت نسب الولد منه وكان عليه عقرها وقيمة ولدها ولا تصير أم ولد له وإن كذبه في النسب لم يثبت
cards.en: A mukatab is a slave with a contract to buy his freedom. If the master claims the child of his mukatab's slave woman and the mukatab agrees, the child is the master's, and he owes her 'uqr and the child's value, but she does not become his umm walad. If the mukatab denies it, the nasab is not proven.

cards.ask: Which statement matches al-Quduri?
options: An umm walad is freed from the whole estate when her master dies
An umm walad may be sold if the master needs money
The mukatab's slave woman becomes the master's umm walad
source: وإذا مات المولى عتقت من جميع المال
لا يجوز بيعها ولا تمليكها
ولا تصير أم ولد له
cards.why: She is freed from the whole estate. She may never be sold, and the mukatab's slave woman does not become his umm walad.

cards.title: What kitaba is
cards.ar: وإذا كاتب المولى عبده أو أمته على مال شرطه عليه وقبل العبد ذلك صار مكاتبا
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time a slave could buy his own freedom. Kitaba is a contract in which the master agrees to free his slave for a sum of money, and the slave accepts. The slave is then a mukatab.

cards.ask: What is kitaba?
options: A slave buying his freedom for money
A slave mother of his child
cards.source: وإذا كاتب المولى عبده أو أمته على مال شرطه عليه وقبل العبد ذلك صار مكاتبا
cards.why: In kitaba the master agrees to free the slave for a sum, and the slave accepts: he is then a mukatab.

cards.title: How the money is paid
cards.ar: ويجوز أن يشترط المال حالا ومؤجلا ومنجما وتجوز كتابة العبد الصغير إذا كان يعقل البيع والشراء
cards.en: The money may be due now, later, or in instalments (each instalment is a najm). A young slave can have a kitaba if he understands buying and selling.

cards.ask: Which of these kitaba contracts are valid?

options.text: 1,000 dirhams, paid now
1,000 dirhams, paid in ten monthly instalments
A boy of ten who understands buying and selling
A small child who cannot understand a sale
The master names a sum but the slave never accepts

source: ويجوز أن يشترط المال حالا ومؤجلا ومنجما
وتجوز كتابة العبد الصغير إذا كان يعقل البيع والشراء
وقبل العبد ذلك صار مكاتبا
cards.why: Cash, deferred or instalments are all fine, and a child who understands trade may contract. Without the slave's acceptance there is no kitaba.

cards.title: Out of his hand, still his
cards.ar: وإذا صحت الكتابة خرج المكاتب من يد المولى ولم يخرج من ملكه فيجوز له البيع والشراء والسفر ولا يجوز له التزويج إلا بإذن المولى ولا يهب ولا يصدق إلا بشيء اليسير ولا يتكفل
cards.en: Once the kitaba is valid, the mukatab leaves his master's control but is still owned by him. So he may buy, sell and travel. He may not marry without the master's permission, may not give gifts or charity except small amounts, and may not stand surety (kafala: promising to pay someone else's debt).

cards.ask: May a mukatab do this on his own?
items: Buy and sell in the market
Give a beggar a small coin
Give a friend a large gift
Promise to pay a friend's debt
source: فيجوز له البيع والشراء والسفر
ولا يجوز له التزويج إلا بإذن المولى ولا يهب ولا يصدق إلا بشيء اليسير ولا يتكفل
cards.why: Trade is open to him, and small charity. Marrying needs permission, and big gifts and surety are not allowed.

cards.title: His children
cards.ar: فإنه ولد له ولد من أمة له دخل في كتابته وكان حكمه كحكمه وكسبه له وإن زوج المولى عبده من أمته ثم كاتبهما فولدت منه ولدا دخل في كتابتها وكان كسبه لها
cards.en: If the mukatab has a child by his own slave woman, the child joins his kitaba, takes his ruling, and the child's earnings are his. If the master married his slave man to his slave woman and then gave both a kitaba, their child joins the mother's kitaba and his earnings are hers.

cards.title: The master must not wrong her
cards.ar: وإن وطئ المولى مكاتبته لزمه العقر وإن جنى عليها أو على ولدها لزمته الجناية وإن أتلف مالا لها غرمه
cards.en: A mukataba is a woman with a kitaba. If her master is with her, he owes her 'uqr (a fair payment like a bride gift). If he injures her or her child, he owes for the injury. If he destroys her property, he must pay for it.

cards.ask: Hind is a mukataba who weaves cloth. Her master breaks her loom, worth 50 dirhams. What follows?
options: Nothing: everything she has is his
He pays only once she is free
cards.source: وإن أتلف مالا لها غرمه
cards.why: Her property is her own during the kitaba, so the master must pay for what he destroys.

cards.title: Buying his relatives
cards.ar: وإذا اشترى المكاتب أباه أو أبنه دخل في كتابته وإن اشترى أم ولده دخل ولدها في الكتابة ولم يجز بيعها وإن اشترى ذا رحم محرم منه لا ولاد له لم يدخل في كتابته عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: If the mukatab buys his father or son, they join his kitaba. If he buys the mother of his child, the child joins the kitaba and he may not sell her. If he buys another close relative who is not a parent or child (say his brother), Abu Hanifa says he does not join the kitaba.

cards.ask: Salim, a mukatab, buys his own father. What happens to the father?
options: He is free at once, as a close relative
He is Salim's slave to sell
cards.source: وإذا اشترى المكاتب أباه أو أبنه دخل في كتابته
cards.why: A father or son bought by a mukatab joins his kitaba.

cards.ask: Which statement matches al-Quduri?
options: A mukatab's child by his own slave woman joins his kitaba
A mukatab may marry without asking his master
Once in a kitaba, a mukatab is no longer owned
source: دخل في كتابته وكان حكمه كحكمه
ولا يجوز له التزويج إلا بإذن المولى
ولم يخرج من ملكه
cards.why: The child joins his kitaba. He needs permission to marry and is still owned until he pays.

lessons.title: Failing to pay, dying, and faulty contracts

cards.title: The judge looks into it
cards.ar: وإذا عجز المكاتب عن نجم نظر الحاكم في حاله فإن كان له دين يقتضيه أو مال يقدم إليه ولم يعجل بتعجيزه وانتظر عليه اليومين والثلاثة
cards.en: If the mukatab cannot pay an instalment, the judge looks at his situation. If he has a debt to collect or money on its way, the judge does not rush to declare him unable, and waits two or three days.

cards.title: Ending the kitaba
cards.ar: وإن لم يكن له وجه وطلب المولى تعجيزه عجزه الحاكم وفسخ الكتابة عند أبي حنيفة رحمه الله
cards.en: If he has no way to pay and the master asks, the judge declares him unable and ends the kitaba (Abu Hanifa). Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say not until two instalments in a row are missed.

cards.ask: Mansur misses an instalment, but a caravan carrying his goods arrives in two days. The master asks the judge to end the kitaba now. What does the judge do?
cards.source: فإن كان له دين يقتضيه أو مال يقدم إليه ولم يعجل بتعجيزه وانتظر عليه اليومين والثلاثة
cards.why: With money on its way, the judge waits two or three days before declaring him unable.

cards.ask: Mansur has no way to pay, and at his master's request the judge ends his kitaba. Mansur has 300 dirhams he earned while a mukatab. Whose are they?
options: His master's: he is a slave again
Mansur keeps them as his own earnings
cards.source: وإذا عجز المكاتب عاد إلى أحكام الرق وكان ما في يده من الأكساب لمولاه
cards.why: Once declared unable, he is a slave again, and what he earned goes to his master.

cards.title: If the mukatab dies
cards.ar: وإن مات المكاتب وله مال لم تنفسخ الكتابة وقضيت كتابته من أكسابه وحكم بعتقه في آخر جزء من أجزاء حياته
cards.en: If the mukatab dies leaving money, the kitaba is not cancelled. It is paid from his earnings, and he is judged free in the very last moment of his life.

cards.title: A son left behind
cards.ar: وإن لم يترك وفاء وترك ولدا مولودا في الكتابة سعى في كتابة أبيه على نجومه وإذا أدى حكمنا بعتق أبيه قبل موته وعتق الولد وإن ترك ولدا مشترى في الكتابة قيل له: إما أن تؤدي الكتابة حالا وإلا رددت في الرق
cards.en: If he leaves too little but has a son born during the kitaba, the son works to pay on the same instalments. When he pays, the father is judged free before his death and the son is free. A son the mukatab bought during the kitaba is told: pay it all now, or go back to slavery.

cards.ask: Rashid, a mukatab, dies leaving nothing. His son Bilal was born during the kitaba. What happens?
options: Bilal pays on the same instalments
Bilal must pay everything at once or be a slave
The kitaba is cancelled and Bilal is a slave
cards.source: وترك ولدا مولودا في الكتابة سعى في كتابة أبيه على نجومه
cards.why: A son born in the kitaba carries on with the same instalments. Paying it frees his father before death, and himself.

cards.title: A faulty kitaba
cards.ar: وإذا كاتب المسلم عبده على خمر أو خنزير أو على قيمة نفسه فالكتابة فاسدة فإن أدى الخمر عتق ولزمه أن يسعى في قيمته ولا ينقص من المسمى ويزاد عليه
cards.en: If a Muslim gives his slave a kitaba for wine, pork, or "his own value", the kitaba is fasid (faulty). If the slave hands over the wine he is free, but he must earn and pay his value. It is never less than the named amount, and it may be more.

cards.title: An animal, and two slaves together
cards.ar: وإن كاتبه على حيوان غير موصوف فالكتابة جائزة وإذا كاتب عبديه كتابة واحدة
cards.en: A kitaba for an animal that is not described in detail is valid. If he gives two slaves one kitaba, each standing surety for the other, it is valid: whichever one pays, both are free, and the payer can claim half of what he paid from the other.

cards.ask: Is this kitaba valid?
source: وإن كاتبه على حيوان غير موصوف فالكتابة جائزة
على خمر أو خنزير أو على قيمة نفسه فالكتابة فاسدة
ويجوز أن يشترط المال حالا ومؤجلا ومنجما
cards.why: An undescribed animal and money are fine. Wine, pork and "your own value" make the kitaba faulty.

cards.ask: Two slaves, Bilal and Sa'id, have one kitaba of 2,000 dirhams. Bilal pays all 2,000. What follows?
options: Both are free; Bilal claims 1,000 from Sa'id
Both are free, and Bilal can claim nothing back
cards.source: جازت الكتابة وأيهما أدى عتقا ويرجع على شريكه بنصف ما أدى
cards.why: Whichever one pays frees both, and he claims back half of what he paid.

lessons.title: When the master frees, dies or changes the contract

cards.title: The master frees him
cards.ar: وإذا أعتق المولى مكاتبه عتق بعتقه وسقط عنه مال الكتابة
cards.en: If the master frees his mukatab, he is free and owes nothing more of the kitaba money.

cards.title: The master dies
cards.ar: وإذا مات مولى المكاتب لم تنفسخ الكتابة وقيل له: أد المال إلى ورثة المولى على نجومه فإن أعتقه أحد الورثة لم ينفذ عتقه وإن أعتقوه جميعا عتق وسقط عنه مال الكتابة
cards.en: If the master dies, the kitaba goes on: the mukatab pays the master's heirs on the same instalments. If only one heir frees him, that does not take effect. If all the heirs free him, he is free and owes nothing more.

cards.ask: Musa's master dies, leaving three sons. One son, out of kindness, says "You are free." What happens?
options: Nothing yet: one heir alone cannot free him
Musa is free and owes nothing
Musa is free but owes the other two sons
cards.source: فإن أعتقه أحد الورثة لم ينفذ عتقه وإن أعتقوه جميعا عتق
cards.why: One heir's freeing does not take effect; all of them together would free him.

cards.title: Kitaba with an umm walad
cards.ar: وإذا كاتب المولى أم ولده جاز وإن مات المولى سقط عنها مال الكتابة وإن ولدت مكاتبته منه فهي بالخيار: إن شاءت مضت على الكتابة وإن شاءت عجزت نفسها وصارت أم ولد له
cards.en: A master may give a kitaba to his umm walad. If he dies, she owes nothing more. If his mukataba has his child, she chooses: carry on with the kitaba, or give it up and become his umm walad.

cards.ask: A master gives his umm walad Zahra a kitaba of 1,000. She has paid 400 when he dies. What does she still owe?
options: The other 600, paid to his heirs
cards.source: وإذا كاتب المولى أم ولده جاز وإن مات المولى سقط عنها مال الكتابة
cards.why: An umm walad is freed by the master's death, so the rest of her kitaba money falls away.

cards.title: Kitaba with a mudabbara
cards.ar: وإذا كاتب مدبرته جاز فإن مات المولى ولا مال له كانت بالخيار بين أن تسعى في ثلثي قيمتها أو جميع مال الكتابة
cards.en: A master may give a kitaba to his mudabbara (promised freedom at his death). If he dies leaving nothing else, she chooses to pay either two thirds of her value or the whole kitaba sum.

cards.ask: Layla is a mudabbara with a kitaba of 900 dirhams. She is worth 600. Her master dies leaving nothing else. What may she pay?
cards.source: كانت بالخيار بين أن تسعى في ثلثي قيمتها أو جميع مال الكتابة
cards.why: She chooses between two thirds of her value (400) and the kitaba sum (900).

cards.title: Tadbir after kitaba
cards.ar: وإن دبر مكاتبته صح التدبير ولها الخيار: إن شاءت مضت على الكتابة وإن شاءت عجزت نفسها وصارت مدبرة
cards.en: If he gives tadbir to his mukataba, it is valid, and she chooses: carry on with the kitaba, or give it up and be a mudabbara. If she carries on and he dies leaving nothing else, she may pay two thirds of the kitaba sum or two thirds of her value (Abu Hanifa).

cards.title: The mukatab's own slave
cards.ar: وإذا أعتق المكاتب عبده على مال لم يجز وإن وهب على عوض لم يصح وإن كاتب عبده جاز
cards.en: A mukatab may not free his own slave for money, or give him away in return for payment. But he may give his slave a kitaba.

cards.ask: May a mukatab do this with his own slave?
items: Give him away in return for payment
source: وإذا أعتق المكاتب عبده على مال لم يجز
وإن وهب على عوض لم يصح وإن كاتب عبده جاز
cards.why: Only a kitaba is allowed; freeing for money and a gift for return are not.

cards.title: Whose wala' is the second slave's
cards.ar: فإن أدى الثاني قبل أن يعتق الأول فولاؤه للمولى وإن أدى بعد عتق المكاتب الأول فولاؤه له
cards.en: Wala' is the lasting tie between a freed slave and the one who freed him. If the second slave pays before the first mukatab is free, his wala' goes to the master. If he pays after, it goes to the first mukatab.

cards.ask: Ziyad, a mukatab, gave his slave Amr a kitaba. Amr finishes paying while Ziyad is still a mukatab. Who has Amr's wala'?
cards.source: فإن أدى الثاني قبل أن يعتق الأول فولاؤه للمولى
cards.why: Amr paid before Ziyad was free, so the wala' goes to the master.

lessons.title: Who has the wala'
lessons.arabic: إذا أعتق الرجل مملوكه فولاؤه له

cards.title: Wala' goes to the one who frees
cards.ar: إذا أعتق الرجل مملوكه فولاؤه له وكذلك المرأة تعتق
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time, wala' was the lasting tie between a freed slave and the person who freed him, a little like a family tie: it can bring inheritance. When a man frees his slave, the wala' is his. The same goes for a woman who frees a slave.

cards.title: A "no wala'" condition
cards.ar: فإن شرط أنه سائبه فالشرط باطل والولاء لمن أعتق
cards.en: If he frees him on condition that he is sa'iba (with no wala' to anyone), the condition is void, and the wala' still belongs to the one who freed.

cards.ask: Hind frees her slave and says, "On condition that no one has wala' over you." Who has his wala'?
options: No one, just as she said in her condition
cards.source: فإن شرط أنه سائبه فالشرط باطل والولاء لمن أعتق
cards.why: The sa'iba condition is void, and wala' belongs to whoever freed.

cards.title: Mukatab, mudabbar, umm walad, relative
cards.ar: وإذا أدى المكاتب عتق وولاؤه للمولى وكذلك إن عتق بعد موت المولى فولاؤه لورثة المولى فإن مات المولى عتق مدبره وأمهات أولاده وولاؤهم له ومن ملك ذا رحم محرم منه عتق عليه وولاؤه له
cards.en: When a mukatab pays, he is free and his wala' is the master's; if he becomes free after the master dies, it goes to the master's heirs. When the master dies, his mudabbar and his umm walads are freed and their wala' is his. Whoever owns a close relative he could never marry frees him, and the wala' is his.

cards.ask: Whose wala' belongs to the master who owned them?

options.text: A mukatab who finished paying
A mudabbar freed at the master's death
An umm walad freed at the master's death
A brother freed because the master bought him
A slave freed with the condition "no wala'": no one has it

source: وإذا أدى المكاتب عتق وولاؤه للمولى
عتق مدبره وأمهات أولاده وولاؤهم له
ومن ملك ذا رحم محرم منه عتق عليه وولاؤه له
فالشرط باطل
cards.why: All four are the master's. The "no wala'" condition is void, so that one is wrong too.

cards.ask: Tariq, a mukatab, makes his last payment a year after his master has died. Who has his wala'?
options: Tariq himself, as a free man
cards.source: وكذلك إن عتق بعد موت المولى فولاؤه لورثة المولى
cards.why: Freed after the master's death, his wala' goes to the master's heirs.

cards.title: A child of a slave father and a freed mother
cards.ar: وإذا تزوج عبد رجل أمة لآخر فأعتق مولى الأمة الأمة وهي حامل من العبد عتقت وعتق حملها وولاء الحمل لمولى الأم لا ينتقل عنه أبدا
cards.en: A slave man of one master marries a slave woman of another. Her master frees her while she is pregnant by him: she and the unborn child are free. The child's wala' belongs to the mother's master and never moves from him.

cards.title: The father's freedom pulls the wala'
cards.ar: فإن ولدت بعد عتقها لأكثر من ستة أشهر ولدا فولاؤه لمولى الأم فإن أعتق العبد جر ولاء ابنه وانتقل عن مولى الأم إلى مولى الأب
cards.en: If she gives birth more than six months after being freed, the child's wala' is first with the mother's master. But if the father is later freed, he "pulls" his son's wala', and it moves to the father's master.

cards.ask: Maryam was freed, and eight months later she had a son. Then the boy's slave father is freed by his master. Who now has the boy's wala'?
cards.source: فإن أعتق العبد جر ولاء ابنه وانتقل عن مولى الأم إلى مولى الأب
cards.why: Born over six months after her freedom, the boy was not in the womb when she was freed, so his father's freedom pulls the wala' to the father's master.

cards.ask: Now Maryam was already pregnant when she was freed. Later the slave father is freed. Who has the child's wala'?
options: The father's master, once he is freed
cards.source: وولاء الحمل لمولى الأم لا ينتقل عنه أبدا
cards.why: The child freed in the womb stays with the mother's master for ever.

cards.title: A non-Arab husband
cards.ar: ومن تزوج من العجم بمعتقه من العرب فولدت له أولاد فولاء أولادها لمواليها عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: If a non-Arab man (from the 'ajam) marries a freed woman from among the Arabs, Abu Hanifa says her children's wala' goes to her mawlas (those who freed her).

cards.ask: Which statement matches al-Quduri?
options: A woman who frees a slave has his wala'
A sa'iba condition removes the wala'
A child freed in the womb follows his father's wala'
source: وكذلك المرأة تعتق
فإن شرط أنه سائبه فالشرط باطل
وولاء الحمل لمولى الأم لا ينتقل عنه أبدا
cards.why: A woman who frees has wala' like a man. The sa'iba condition is void, and the child freed in the womb stays with the mother's master.

lessons.title: Inheriting by wala', and wala' by pact

cards.title: Wala' is a kind of 'asaba
cards.ar: وولاء العتاقة تعصيب فإن كان للمعتق عصبة من النسب فهو أولى منه وإن لم يكن له عصبة من النسب فميراثه للمعتق
cards.en: 'Asaba are a person's relatives through the male line who take what is left of an inheritance. Wala' works like that. If the freed person has 'asaba by blood, they come first. If he has none, the one who freed him inherits.

cards.ask: Faraj, a freed slave, dies. He leaves a son, and the man who freed him is still alive. Who takes the inheritance?
options: The one who freed him, before the son
cards.source: فإن كان للمعتق عصبة من النسب فهو أولى منه
cards.why: A blood 'asaba like a son comes before the freer.

cards.title: Sons, not daughters
cards.ar: فإن مات المولى ثم مات المعتق فميراثه لبني المولى دون بناته وليس للنساء من الولاء إلا ما أعتقن أو أعتق من أعتقن أو كاتبن أو كاتب من كاتبن
cards.en: If the freer dies first and then the freed man dies, the freed man's estate goes to the freer's sons, not his daughters. Women have wala' only over those they freed, or whom their freed ones freed, or those they gave a kitaba, or whom their mukatab gave a kitaba.

cards.ask: Umar freed Salim. Umar died, leaving a son and a daughter. Now Salim dies with no relatives. Who inherits from Salim?
options: Umar's son and daughter, two to one
cards.source: فإن مات المولى ثم مات المعتق فميراثه لبني المولى دون بناته
cards.why: Wala' passes to the freer's sons, not his daughters.

cards.ask: Over whom can a woman have wala'?

options.text: A slave she freed herself
A slave freed by the man she freed
A slave she gave a kitaba
A slave freed by her father
A slave freed by her husband

cards.source: وليس للنساء من الولاء إلا ما أعتقن أو أعتق من أعتقن أو كاتبن أو كاتب من كاتبن
cards.why: Women have wala' only through their own freeing or kitaba, or that of those they freed or gave a kitaba. Not through a father or husband.

cards.title: The nearest takes it
cards.ar: إذا ترك المولى ابنا أولاد ابن آخر فميراث المعتق للابن دون بني البن والولاء للكبر
cards.en: If the freer left a son, and grandsons from another son who died, the freed man's estate goes to the son, not the grandsons. Wala' goes to the nearest in degree (al-kubr).

cards.ask: Hasan freed a slave. Hasan left one living son, Ali, and two grandsons from his son who died before him. The freed man now dies. Who inherits?
options: Ali and the two grandsons, equally
cards.source: فميراث المعتق للابن دون بني البن والولاء للكبر
cards.why: The son is nearer in degree than the grandsons, so he alone takes it.

cards.title: Wala' by pact
cards.ar: وإذا أسلم رجل على يد رجل ووالاه على أن يرثه ويعقل عنه أو أسلم على يد غيره ووالاه فالولاء صحيح وعقله على مولاه فإن مات ولا وارث له فميراثه للمولى وإن كان له وارث فهو أولى منه
cards.en: If a man becomes Muslim at another's hands, or anyone's, and makes a pact (muwalat) that this mawla will inherit from him and pay his blood money ('aql), the wala' is valid, and his blood money falls on the mawla. If he dies with no heir, the mawla inherits; an heir comes first.

cards.title: Moving to another mawla
cards.ar: وللمولى أن ينتقل عنه بولائه إلى غيره ما لم يعقل عنه فإذا عقل عنه لم يكن له أن يتحول بولائه إلى غيره وليس لمولى العتاقة أن يوالي أحد
cards.en: He may move his wala' to someone else, as long as the mawla has not yet paid blood money for him. Once the mawla has paid, he cannot move. A freed slave (who already has the wala' of freeing) may not make a pact with anyone.

cards.ask: Kamal made a pact of wala' with Yusuf. Last year Yusuf paid blood money for something Kamal did by mistake. Can Kamal now move his wala' to someone else?
options: No: Yusuf has already paid for him
Yes: he may move whenever he likes
Yes, if he pays Yusuf back
cards.source: فإذا عقل عنه لم يكن له أن يتحول بولائه إلى غيره
cards.why: After the mawla has paid blood money for him, he may no longer move his wala'.

cards.ask: Who inherits in each case?
items: A man with a pact of wala' dies with no heir
A man with a pact of wala' dies leaving a daughter
A freed man with no relatives dies after his freer did; the freer left a son
A freed man with no blood 'asaba dies; his freer is alive
source: فإن مات ولا وارث له فميراثه للمولى وإن كان له وارث فهو أولى منه
فميراثه لبني المولى
وإن لم يكن له عصبة من النسب فميراثه للمعتق
cards.why: With no heir, the mawla inherits; a real heir comes first. If the freer has died, it goes to his sons, not to him.

cards.title: Five kinds
cards.ar: القتل على خمسة أوجه: عمد وشبه عمد وخطإ وما أجزي مجرى الخطإ والقتل بسبب
cards.en: Al-Quduri sorts killing into five kinds: deliberate ('amd), like-deliberate (shibh 'amd), mistake (khata'), what is treated like a mistake, and killing by a cause (bi-sabab).

cards.title: Deliberate killing
cards.ar: فالعمد: ما تعمد ضربه بسلاح أو ما أجزي مجرى السلاح في تفريق الأجزاء كالمحدد من الخشب والحجر والنار وموجب ذلك المأثم
cards.en: 'Amd is deliberately striking with a weapon, or with something that cuts like one: sharpened wood or stone, or fire. It brings sin and qawad (also called qisas: the killer's life is taken in return, by the ruler's court), unless the victim's family forgive. There is no kaffara (an act to make up for it) in it.

cards.ask: Tariq deliberately stabs Salim with a knife, and Salim dies. What follows?
options: Kaffara and blood money from Tariq's relatives
source: ما تعمد ضربه بسلاح
إلا أن يعفو الأولياء
cards.why: A knife is a weapon used on purpose, so it is 'amd: qisas, unless the family (the awliya') forgive.

cards.title: Like-deliberate
cards.ar: وشبه العمد عند أبي حنيفة: أن يتعمد الضرب بما ليس بسلاح ولا ما أجري مجرى السلاح
cards.en: Shibh 'amd is deliberately striking with something that is not a weapon and does not cut like one, something that does not usually kill. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say a huge rock or a huge piece of wood makes it 'amd.

cards.title: What shibh 'amd brings
cards.ar: وموجب ذلك على القولين والمأثم والكفارة ولا قود وفيه دية مغلظة على العاقلة
cards.en: Shibh 'amd brings sin and kaffara, but no qawad. There is a heavier blood money (diya mughallaza), paid by the killer's 'aqila: the group of his people who share in paying blood money.

cards.ask: In a quarrel Hamza deliberately hits a man with a small stick, which does not usually kill, and the man dies. Which kind of killing is it?
options: Khata': diya, and no sin at all
source: أن يتعمد ضربه بما لا يقتل غالبا
ولا قود وفيه دية مغلظة على العاقلة
cards.why: Striking on purpose with what does not usually kill is shibh 'amd: no qawad, but heavy diya on the 'aqila, and kaffara.

cards.title: Mistake
cards.ar: والخطأ على وجهين: خطأ في القصد وهو: أن يرمي شخصا يظنه صيدا فإذا هو آدمي وخطأ في الفعل وهو: أن يرمي غرضا فيصيب آدميا وموجب ذلك: الكفارة والدية على العاقلة ولا مأثم فيه
cards.en: Khata' is of two kinds. A mistake in aim: shooting at a figure he thinks is game, and it is a person. A mistake in the act: shooting at a target and hitting a person. It brings kaffara, and diya (blood money) on the 'aqila, but no sin.

cards.title: Like a mistake, and by a cause
cards.ar: وما أجري مجرى الخطإ: مثل النائم ينقلب على رجل فيقتله فحكمه حكم الخطإ وأما القتل بسبب: كحافر البئر وواضع الحجر في غير ملكه وموجبه إذا تلف فيه آدمي: الدية على العاقلة ولا كفارة فيه
cards.en: Treated like a mistake: a sleeper rolls onto a man and kills him; the ruling is that of a mistake. Killing by a cause: someone digs a well or puts a stone where it is not his property, and a person dies by it. That brings diya on the 'aqila, but no kaffara.

cards.ask: Bakr leaves a big stone on a road that is not his land. At night a man trips on it and dies. What follows?
options: Diya on Bakr's 'aqila, but no kaffara
Qisas on Bakr, unless the family forgive
cards.source: وواضع الحجر في غير ملكه وموجبه إذا تلف فيه آدمي: الدية على العاقلة ولا كفارة فيه
cards.why: This is killing by a cause: diya on the 'aqila, but no kaffara.

cards.ask: Is there kaffara in this killing?
items: A hunter shoots at what he thinks is a deer, and it is a man
An archer misses his target and hits a man
A man hits another on purpose with a small stick
A man stabs another on purpose
A man digs a well in the road and someone falls in
source: وموجب ذلك: الكفارة والدية على العاقلة
والمأثم والكفارة ولا قود
إلا أن يعفو الأولياء ولا كفار
الدية على العاقلة ولا كفارة فيه
cards.why: Mistake and shibh 'amd bring kaffara. 'Amd has qisas instead, and killing by a cause has no kaffara.

cards.ask: In which of these kinds is the diya paid by the 'aqila?

options.text: Shibh 'amd
Khata' (mistake)
A sleeper rolling onto someone
Killing by a cause, like a well
'Amd (deliberate)

source: وفيه دية مغلظة على العاقلة
الكفارة والدية على العاقلة
فحكمه حكم الخطإ
الدية على العاقلة ولا كفارة فيه
cards.why: All but 'amd put the diya on the 'aqila. 'Amd brings qisas unless the family forgive.

lessons.title: Who is killed in qisas for whom
lessons.arabic: والقصاص واجب بقتل كل محقون الدم

cards.title: Whose killing brings qisas
cards.ar: والقصاص واجب بقتل كل محقون الدم على التأبيد إذا قتل عمدا
cards.en: Qisas (taking the killer's life in return) is due for deliberately killing anyone whose blood is protected for ever (mahqun al-dam): a person the law always protects.

cards.title: Lives are equal
cards.ar: ويقتل الحر بالحر والحر بالعبد والمسلم بالذمي
cards.en: A free man is killed in qisas for a free man, and for a slave. A Muslim is killed for a dhimmi (a non-Muslim living under Muslim rule), but not for a musta'min (a non-Muslim visitor on a safe-conduct). A man is killed for a woman, an adult for a child, a healthy man for a blind or crippled one.

cards.ask: Is there qisas for this deliberate killing?
items: A free man kills a slave
A healthy man kills a blind man
A Muslim kills a musta'min visitor
source: ويقتل الحر بالحر والحر بالعبد والمسلم بالذمي
ولا يقتل والمسلم بالمستأمن
ويقتل الرجل بالمرأة والكبير بالصغير والصحيح بالأعمى والزمن
cards.why: Free and slave, Muslim and dhimmi, man and woman, healthy and blind are equal here. A musta'min's blood is not protected for ever, so there is no qisas for him.

cards.title: When there is no qisas
cards.ar: ولا يقتل الرجل بابنه ولا بعبده ولا مدبره ولا مكاتبه ولا بعبد ولده ومن ورث قصاصا على أبيه سقط
cards.en: A man is not killed for his son, his own slave, mudabbar or mukatab, or his son's slave. If someone inherits a right of qisas against his own father, it falls away.

cards.ask: Is there qisas for this deliberate killing?
items: A master kills his own slave
A man kills his son's slave
A man kills his own mukatab
An adult kills someone else's child
source: ولا يقتل الرجل بابنه ولا بعبده ولا مدبره ولا مكاتبه ولا بعبد ولده
والكبير بالصغير
cards.why: A man is not killed for his son, his own slave, mudabbar or mukatab, or his son's slave. An adult is killed for a child.

cards.ask: Yasir's father killed Yasir's mother on purpose. Yasir is her heir, so the right of qisas passes to him. What happens to it?
options: Qisas falls away; he cannot claim it
Yasir may ask for qisas against his father
It passes to the ruler to carry out
cards.source: ومن ورث قصاصا على أبيه سقط
cards.why: A right of qisas inherited against one's father falls away.

cards.ask: How is qisas carried out? Complete it.
cards.ar: ولا يستوفى القصاص إلا ____
cards.source: ولا يستوفى القصاص إلا بالسيف
cards.why: بالسيف: qisas is carried out only with the sword.

cards.title: When a mukatab is killed
cards.ar: وإذا قتل المكاتب عمدا وليس له وارث إلا المولى وترك وفاء فله القصاص فإن ترك وفاء ووارثه غير المولى فلا قصاص لهم وإن اجتمعوا مع المولى
cards.en: A mukatab is a slave buying his freedom by instalments (kitaba). If he is killed deliberately, leaving enough to pay, and his master is his only heir, the master has qisas. If he leaves enough but has other heirs, there is no qisas for them, even if they join with the master.

cards.ask: A mukatab is killed deliberately. He left enough money to pay his kitaba, and his only heir is his master. Who may ask for qisas?
cards.source: وليس له وارث إلا المولى وترك وفاء فله القصاص
cards.why: With the master as his only heir, the master has the right of qisas.

cards.title: A pledged slave
cards.ar: وإذا قتل عبد الرهن لم يجب القصاص حتى يجتمع الراهن والمرتهن
cards.en: Rahn is a pledge: something handed over as security for a debt. If a slave held in pledge is killed, qisas is not due until both the one who pledged him and the one holding the pledge agree.

cards.ask: Which statement matches al-Quduri?
options: An adult is killed in qisas for a child
A Muslim is never killed in qisas for a dhimmi
A father is killed in qisas for his son
source: والكبير بالصغير
والمسلم بالذمي
ولا يقتل الرجل بابنه
cards.why: The adult is killed for the child, and the Muslim for the dhimmi. A father is not killed for his son.

cards.title: A wound that kills, and cut limbs
cards.ar: ومن جرح رجلا عمدا فلم يزل صاحب فراش حتى مات فعليه القصاص ومن قطع يد غيره عمدا من المفصل قطعت يده وكذلك الرجل ومارن الأنف والأذن
cards.en: Qisas means the same harm is done back. Whoever wounds a man on purpose, and the man stays in bed until he dies, owes qisas. Whoever cuts off another's hand on purpose at the joint has his hand cut. The same for a foot, the soft part of the nose (marin), and the ear.

cards.title: The eye
cards.ar: ومن ضرب عين رجل فقلعها فلا قصاص عليه وإن كانت قائمة فذهب ضوؤها فعليه القصاص
cards.en: If someone strikes a man's eye and knocks it out, there is no qisas (it cannot be matched exactly). If the eye stays but its sight is lost, there is qisas: the striker's sight is taken with a heated mirror while wet cotton guards his face.

cards.ask: Nabil strikes Imran's eye on purpose. The eye stays in place, but Imran can no longer see with it. Is there qisas?
options: No: only a knocked-out eye has qisas
cards.source: وإن كانت قائمة فذهب ضوؤها فعليه القصاص
cards.why: Lost sight in an eye that remains can be matched, so there is qisas. A knocked-out eye has none.

cards.title: Teeth, head wounds and bones
cards.ar: وفي السن القصاص وفي كل شجة يمكن فيها المماثلة القصاص ولا قصاص في عظم إلا في السن وليس فيما دون النفس شبه عمد إنما هو عمد أو خطأ
cards.en: There is qisas for a tooth, and for every head wound (shajja) that can be matched exactly. There is no qisas for a bone, except a tooth. For injuries less than a life there is no shibh 'amd: it is either deliberate or a mistake.

cards.ask: A deliberate injury between two free Muslim men. Is there qisas?
items: Cutting off the hand at the wrist
Breaking a bone in the leg
source: قطعت يده وكذلك الرجل ومارن الأنف والأذن
وفي السن القصاص
ولا قصاص في عظم إلا في السن
فقلعها فلا قصاص عليه
cards.why: A cut at a joint, a tooth and an ear can be matched exactly. A broken bone and a knocked-out eye cannot.

cards.title: Between whom
cards.ar: ولا قصاص بين الرجل والمرأة فيما دون النفس ولا بين الحر والعبد ولا بين العبدين ويجب القصاص في الأطراف بين المسلم والكافر
cards.en: For injuries less than a life, there is no qisas between a man and a woman, a free man and a slave, or two slaves. But there is qisas for limbs between a Muslim and a non-Muslim.

cards.ask: Khalid deliberately cuts off a woman's hand at the wrist. Is his hand cut in qisas?
options: No: not between a man and a woman
Yes: a hand for a hand, at the joint
cards.source: ولا قصاص بين الرجل والمرأة فيما دون النفس
cards.why: Below a life, al-Quduri allows no qisas between a man and a woman.

cards.title: When the hands are not alike
