cards.en: In al-Quduri's time, a slave and a free person were the same in this: the hand is cut for both.

cards.title: How it is proved
cards.ar: ويجب القطع بإقراره مرة واحدة أو بشهادة شاهدين
cards.en: Cutting becomes due by the thief's confessing once, or by the testimony of two witnesses.

cards.ask: Complete: how many times must a thief confess?
cards.ar: ويجب القطع بإقراره ____ أو بشهادة شاهدين
cards.source: ويجب القطع بإقراره مرة واحدة
cards.why: مرة واحدة: one confession is enough for theft, unlike zina, which needs four.

cards.title: Stealing as a group
cards.ar: وإذا اشترك جماعة في سرقة فأصاب كل واحد منهم عشرة دراهم قطع وإن أصابه أقل من ذلك لم يقطع
cards.en: If several people steal together, the stolen money is divided between them. If each one's share reaches ten dirhams, all are cut. If a share is less, no one is cut.

cards.ask: Three men steal 24 dirhams together. What is the ruling?
cards.source: فأصاب كل واحد منهم عشرة دراهم قطع وإن أصابه أقل من ذلك لم يقطع
cards.why: 24 ÷ 3 = 8 dirhams each, which is less than ten, so none of them is cut.

cards.ask: Four people steal 40 dirhams from a house together. What is the ruling?
options: All four are cut: each share is 10
No cutting: they were a group
Only the one who held the money
cards.source: وإذا اشترك جماعة في سرقة فأصاب كل واحد منهم عشرة دراهم قطع
cards.why: 40 ÷ 4 = 10 dirhams each. Each share reaches the nisab, so all are cut.

cards.ask: Cut, or not?
items: An adult steals 12 dirhams from a locked house
A slave steals 10 dirhams from a hirz
A thief confesses once to stealing 20 dirhams from a hirz
source: إذا سرق العاقل البالغ عشرة
وإن أصابه أقل من ذلك لم يقطع
والعبد والحر في القطع سواء
ويجب القطع بإقراره مرة واحدة
cards.why: A sane adult who takes ten dirhams from a hirz is cut, slave or free, and one confession is enough. A child is not cut, and 7.5 each is under the nisab.

lessons.title: Things with no cutting
lessons.arabic: ولا يقطع فيما يوجد تافها مباحا

cards.title: Common, free things
cards.ar: ولا يقطع فيما يوجد تافها مباحا في دار الإسلام كالخشب والقصب والحشيس والسمك والطير والصيد
cards.en: There is no cutting for things that are common and free for anyone to take in Muslim lands, like wood, reeds, grass, fish, birds and game.

cards.title: Things that go off quickly
cards.ar: وكذلك فيما يسرع إليه الفساد كالفواكه الرطبة واللبن واللحم والبطيخ والفاكهة على الشجر والزرع الذي لم يحص
cards.en: Nor for things that spoil quickly, like fresh fruit, milk, meat and melons, nor for fruit still on the tree or crops not yet harvested.

cards.ask: Bashir steals melons worth 20 dirhams from a locked store. Is his hand cut?
options: Yes: they are worth more than ten
Yes, because the store was locked
cards.source: كالفواكه الرطبة واللبن واللحم والبطيخ
cards.why: Things that go off quickly, such as melons, bring no cutting, whatever their price.

cards.title: Drinks, birds and the Mushaf
cards.ar: ولا قطع في الأشربة المطربة
cards.en: There is no cutting for intoxicating drinks, nor for birds, nor for a Mushaf (a copy of the Qur'an) even if decorated with silver or gold, nor for a gold cross, nor for chess or backgammon sets.

cards.ask: Someone steals a Mushaf with a gold-decorated cover worth 100 dirhams. Is the hand cut?
options: No: there is no cutting for a Mushaf
Yes: the gold is worth more than ten dirhams
Yes, but only if the gold is removed
cards.source: ولا في الطيور ولا في السرقة المصحف وإن كان عليه حلية
cards.why: There is no cutting for a Mushaf, even with decoration on it.

cards.title: Stealing a person
cards.ar: ولا قطع على سارق الصبي الحر وإن كان عليه حلي ولا قطع في سرقة العبد الكبير ويقطع في سرقة العبد الصغير
cards.en: No cutting for kidnapping a free child, even wearing jewellery, since a free person is not property. In al-Quduri's time, taking a grown slave brought no cutting, but taking a small slave child did.

cards.ask: A man carries off a free child wearing a gold necklace worth 200 dirhams. Is his hand cut?
options: No: a free child is not property
Yes: the necklace is worth over ten
Yes, if the child is under seven
cards.source: ولا قطع على سارق الصبي الحر وإن كان عليه حلي
cards.why: There is no cutting for taking a free child, even one wearing jewellery.

cards.title: Books, dogs and instruments
cards.ar: ولا قطع في الدفاتر كلها إلا في دفاتر الحساب ولا قطع في سرقة الكلب ولا فهد ولا دف ولا طبل ولا مزمار
cards.en: No cutting for books of any kind, except account books. Nor for a dog, a cheetah, a tambourine, a drum or a flute.

cards.ask: Cut, or no cutting?
source: ولا في السرقة المصحف وإن كان عليه حلية
واللبن واللحم
إلا في دفاتر الحساب
ولا قطع في سرقة الكلب
ولا طبل
cards.why: Account books bring cutting. A Mushaf, fresh meat, a drum and a dog do not.

cards.title: Precious woods
cards.ar: ويقطع في الساج والقنا والآبنوس والصندل وإذا اتخذ من الخشب أوان أو أبواب قطع فيها
cards.en: But the hand is cut for precious woods: teak, cane, ebony and sandalwood. And if ordinary wood is made into dishes or doors, there is cutting for them.

cards.ask: Ordinary firewood brings no cutting. Musa steals a wooden door worth 30 dirhams. What is the ruling?
options: Cut: wood made into a door counts
No cutting: it is only wood
No cutting, since a door is fixed
cards.source: وإذا اتخذ من الخشب أوان أو أبواب قطع فيها
cards.why: Once wood is made into dishes or doors, there is cutting for it.

cards.title: Not theft in the hadd sense
cards.ar: ولا قطع على خائن ولا خائنة ولا نباش ولا منتهب ولا مختلس
cards.en: No cutting for a kha'in (one who betrays something trusted to him), a nabbash (grave robber), a muntahib (one who seizes openly by force) or a mukhtalis (one who snatches and runs). Theft for the hadd means taking secretly.

cards.ask: A shop owner leaves his till money with his helper, Sami. Sami keeps 50 dirhams of it for himself. Is Sami's hand cut?
options: Yes: it is over ten dirhams
cards.source: ولا قطع على خائن ولا خائنة
cards.why: The money was trusted to him. Betraying a trust is a sin, but there is no cutting for it.

cards.ask: Cut, or no cutting?
items: A grave robber (nabbash) takes a shroud
A snatcher (mukhtalis) grabs a purse and runs
source: ويقطع في الساج والقنا والآبنوس والصندل
أو أبواب قطع فيها
ولا نباش ولا منتهب ولا مختلس
cards.why: Precious woods and things made of wood bring cutting. A grave robber and a snatcher do not take secretly from a hirz, so they are not cut.

lessons.title: Shared property, family and the hirz

cards.title: Public or shared money
cards.ar: ولا يقطع السارق من بيت المال ولا من مال للسارق فيه شركة
cards.en: No cutting for stealing from bayt al-mal (the public treasury), since every Muslim has a share in it, nor from property the thief partly owns.

cards.ask: Hamid steals 100 dirhams from the bayt al-mal. Is his hand cut?
options: No: he has a share in it
Yes: it is far above ten dirhams
cards.source: ولا يقطع السارق من بيت المال
cards.why: Every Muslim has a share in the public treasury, so there is no cutting.

cards.title: Close family
cards.ar: سرق من أبويه أو ولده أو ذي رحم محرم منه لم يقطع
cards.en: No cutting for stealing from one's parents, children, or any dhu rahim mahram: a close relative one may never marry, like a brother, sister, aunt or uncle. Family go into each other's homes freely.

cards.title: Spouses and others
cards.ar: وكذلك إذا سرق أحد الزوجين من الآخر أو العبد من سيده أو من امرأة سيده أو زوج سيدته والمولى من مكاتبه والسارق من المغنم
cards.en: The same for a husband or wife stealing from the other; and in al-Quduri's time a slave from his master or the master's spouse, or a master from his mukatab (a slave buying his freedom). And none for stealing from the maghnam: war spoils not yet shared out.

cards.ask: Ali steals 50 dirhams from his uncle's (his mother's brother's) house. Is his hand cut?
options: No: he is a close mahram
Yes: it is a different household
Yes: an uncle is not a parent
cards.source: أو ذي رحم محرم منه لم يقطع
cards.why: A maternal uncle is a dhu rahim mahram, so there is no cutting.

cards.title: Two kinds of hirz
cards.ar: والحرز على ضربين: حرز لمعنى فيه كالبيوت والدور وحرز بالحافظ
cards.en: A hirz is of two kinds: a place that protects by itself, like houses and buildings; and protection by a guard watching over the property.

cards.ask: A hirz is of how many kinds?
cards.source: والحرز على ضربين
cards.why: Two: a place that protects by itself, and protection by a guard.

cards.ask: Which of these are the two kinds of hirz?

options.text: A place that protects by itself, like a house
A public bath
A guard watching over the property
A building people may enter

source: والحرز على ضربين: حرز لمعنى فيه كالبيوت والدور وحرز بالحافظ
ولا قطع على من سرق من حمام أو من بيت أذن للناس في دخوله
cards.why: A hirz is a place like a house, or a guard. A public bath, or a building people are let into, is not a hirz against them.

cards.title: Guarded property
cards.ar: فمن سرق شيئا من حرز أو غير حرز وصاحبه عنده يحفظه وجب عليه القطع
cards.en: So whoever steals from a hirz, or from an open place while the owner is right there watching it, is cut.

cards.ask: In an open market, Yasir's bag sits on the ground and he sits beside it watching. A man takes it, worth 30 dirhams. Is his hand cut?
options: No: it was in the open
No: there were no walls around it
cards.source: أو غير حرز وصاحبه عنده يحفظه وجب عليه القطع
cards.why: A guard makes a hirz, even in an open place.

cards.title: Open to the public
cards.ar: ولا قطع على من سرق من حمام أو من بيت أذن للناس في دخوله
cards.en: No cutting for stealing from a public bath, or any building that people are allowed to enter. Being let in means it is not a hirz against them.

cards.ask: During the day, a man steals clothes worth 20 dirhams from the changing room of a public bath. Is his hand cut?
options: Yes: it is over ten dirhams
cards.source: ولا قطع على من سرق من حمام
cards.why: A public bath is open to everyone, so it is not a hirz against them.

cards.ask: Cut, or not?
items: A wife steals from her husband
Steals from a stranger's locked house
Steals a bag whose owner sits guarding it
Steals from a building open to customers
source: ولا يقطع السارق من بيت المال
وكذلك إذا سرق أحد الزوجين من الآخر
حرز لمعنى فيه كالبيوت والدور
وصاحبه عنده يحفظه
أو من بيت أذن للناس في دخوله
cards.why: A locked house or a guarded bag is a hirz. Public money, a spouse's property and a place open to people are not.

lessons.title: Inside the hirz: guests, helpers and reaching in

cards.title: Things in the mosque
cards.ar: ومن سرق من المسجد متاعا وصاحبه عنده قطع
cards.en: Whoever steals belongings in the mosque while their owner is beside them is cut. The owner is guarding them.

cards.title: The guest
cards.ar: ولا قطع على الضيف إذا سرق ممن أضافه
cards.en: No cutting for a guest who steals from his host. He was invited in, so the house was not a hirz against him.

cards.ask: Karim invites Omar to dinner. Omar takes 30 dirhams from Karim's room. Is Omar's hand cut?
options: Yes: it is over ten dirhams
Yes: he took it from a closed room
cards.source: ولا قطع على الضيف إذا سرق ممن أضافه
cards.why: A guest was let in, so there is no cutting, though he must return it.

cards.title: Passing it out
cards.ar: وإذا نقب اللص البيت فدخل فأخذ المال وناوله آخر خارج البيت فلا قطع عليهما
cards.en: Naqb is breaking a hole through a wall. If a thief breaks in, takes the money and hands it to someone outside, neither is cut: the one inside did not carry it out, and the one outside did not enter.

cards.title: Throwing it out
cards.ar: وإن ألقاه في الطريق ثم خرج فأخذه قطع وكذلك إن حمله على حمار فساقه فأخرجه
cards.en: But if he throws it into the road, then comes out and picks it up, he is cut. The same if he loads it on a donkey and drives it out.

cards.ask: Cut, or not?
items: Hands the money to a friend waiting outside
Throws it into the road, then picks it up
Loads it on a donkey and drives it out
source: وناوله آخر خارج البيت فلا قطع عليهما
وإن ألقاه في الطريق ثم خرج فأخذه قطع
وكذلك إن حمله على حمار فساقه فأخرجه
cards.why: If he gets it out himself, by throwing it or by a donkey, he is cut. Handing it to another outside brings no cutting for either.

cards.title: A group inside
cards.ar: وإذا دخل الحرز جماعة فتولى بعضهم الأخذ قطعوا جميعا
cards.en: If a group enters the hirz together and only some of them actually take the things, all of them are cut.

cards.ask: Three men break into a house together. Only Zaid picks up the goods, worth 60 dirhams; the others keep watch inside. Who is cut?
cards.source: وإذا دخل الحرز جماعة فتولى بعضهم الأخذ قطعوا جميعا
cards.why: All of them entered the hirz, and each share is 20 dirhams, so all are cut.

cards.title: Reaching in
cards.ar: ومن نقب البيت وأدخل يده فيه فأخذ شيئا لم يقطع وإذا أدخل يده في صندوق الصيرفي أو في كم غيره فأخذ المال قطع
cards.en: If he breaks a hole and only reaches his hand in to take something, he is not cut. But if he puts his hand into a money-changer's box, or into someone's sleeve (where people kept money then), and takes the money, he is cut.

cards.ask: In a crowd, Hisham slips his hand into a man's sleeve and takes 15 dirhams. What is the ruling?
options: No cutting: he did not enter anywhere
No cutting: it was in a crowd
cards.source: أو في كم غيره فأخذ المال قطع
cards.why: Putting a hand into someone's sleeve and taking the money brings cutting.

cards.ask: Which are true of theft from inside the hirz?

options.text: A guest who steals from his host is not cut
Reaching through a hole in the wall brings no cutting
A group that enters together are all cut
Things in a mosque can never bring cutting
Handing the money to someone outside brings cutting for both

source: ولا قطع على الضيف
ومن نقب البيت وأدخل يده فيه فأخذ شيئا لم يقطع
قطعوا جميعا
ومن سرق من المسجد متاعا وصاحبه عنده قطع
فلا قطع عليهما
cards.why: Guest, reaching in and the group rule are as stated. A guarded item in a mosque brings cutting, and handing it out brings none.

cards.title: The right hand
cards.ar: وتقطع يمين السارق من الزند وتحسم
cards.en: The thief's right hand is cut off at the wrist (zand), and the wound is sealed (hasm), for example with hot oil, so that he does not bleed to death.

cards.title: A second and third time
cards.ar: فإن سرق ثانيا قطعت رجله اليسرى فإن سرق ثالثا لم يقطع وخلد في السجن حتى يتوب
cards.en: If he steals a second time, his left foot is cut. If he steals a third time, nothing more is cut; he is kept in prison until he repents.

cards.ask: Put in order what happens to a thief who steals again and again.
steps: He is kept in prison until he repents
cards.source: وتقطع يمين السارق من الزند وتحسم فإن سرق ثانيا قطعت رجله اليسرى فإن سرق ثالثا لم يقطع وخلد في السجن حتى يتوب
cards.why: First the right hand, then the left foot, then prison until he repents.

cards.title: If he is already disabled
cards.ar: وإذا كان السارق أشل اليد اليسرى أو أقطع أو مقطوع الرجل اليمنى لم يقطع
cards.en: If the thief's left hand is paralysed or missing, or his right foot is cut off, his right hand is not cut. Cutting would leave him unable to use his body at all.

cards.ask: A thief whose left hand is paralysed steals 20 dirhams from a hirz. Is his right hand cut?
options: No: he would have no useful hand
His left foot is cut instead
cards.source: وإذا كان السارق أشل اليد اليسرى
cards.why: With a paralysed left hand, the right is not cut, or he would have no useful hand.

cards.title: The owner must demand it
cards.ar: ولا يقطع السارق إلا أن يحضر المسروق منه فيطالب بالسرقة فإن وهبها من السارق أو باعها إياه أو نقصت قيمتها من النصاب لم يقطع
cards.en: The thief is not cut unless the person stolen from comes and claims it. If he gives it to the thief as a gift, or sells it to him, or its value falls below the nisab, there is no cutting.

cards.ask: After the trial, but before the cutting, the owner says to the thief, "Keep it, it is a gift." What happens?
options: He must pay its price instead
cards.source: فإن وهبها من السارق أو باعها إياه أو نقصت قيمتها من النصاب لم يقطع
cards.why: Once the owner gives it to him, there is no cutting.

cards.title: Stealing the same thing again
cards.ar: فقطع فيها وردها ثم عاد فسرقها وهي بحالها لم يقطع فإن تغيرت عن حالها مثل أن كان غزلا
cards.en: If he is cut for something, returns it, and later steals the same thing again unchanged, he is not cut again. But if it has changed, for example yarn that was woven into cloth, he is cut.

cards.ask: Nadir stole yarn and was cut. The yarn was returned and woven into cloth. Later Nadir steals the cloth. What is the ruling?
options: He is cut: it has changed
Not cut: it is the same thing
Not cut: he has already been punished
cards.source: فإن تغيرت عن حالها مثل أن كان غزلا
cards.why: Yarn turned into cloth counts as a changed thing, so he is cut again.

cards.title: Giving it back
cards.ar: وإذا قطع السارق والعين قائمة في يده ردها وإن كانت هالكة لم يضمن
cards.en: If, after the cutting, he still has the stolen thing, he returns it. If it was destroyed, he does not have to pay for it.

cards.ask: A man is accused of stealing a horse. He says, "It is mine," but has no proof. What happens to the cutting?
options: He is cut, since he has no proof
The judge decides by drawing lots
cards.source: وإذا ادعى السارق أن العين المسروقة ملكه سقط القطع عنه
cards.why: His claim creates a doubt, so the cutting falls away even without proof.

cards.ask: Which are true of cutting for theft?

options.text: The hand is cut at the wrist
A third theft brings prison, not cutting
If the stolen thing was destroyed, he does not pay for it after the cutting
The thief is cut even if the owner never claims it
The left hand is cut first

source: وتقطع يمين السارق من الزند
فإن سرق ثالثا لم يقطع وخلد في السجن
وإن كانت هالكة لم يضمن
إلا أن يحضر المسروق منه فيطالب بالسرقة
cards.why: Right hand at the wrist, prison the third time, and no payment for a destroyed item. The owner must claim it, and it is the right hand first.

cards.title: Caught before doing anything
cards.ar: وإذا خرج جماعة ممتنعين أو واحد يقدر على الامتناع فقصدوا قطع الطريق فأخذوا قبل أن يأخذوا مالا ولا قتلوا نفسا حبسهم الإمام حتى يحدثوا توبة
cards.en: Qat' al-tariq is highway robbery: armed people strong enough to resist, or one person who can, set out to attack travellers. If they are caught before taking any money or killing anyone, the imam imprisons them until they show repentance.

cards.title: If they took money
cards.ar: وإن أخذوا مال مسلم أو ذمي والمأخوذ إذا قسم على جماعتهم أصاب كل واحد منهم عشرة دراهم فصاعدا أو ما قيمته ذلك قطع الإمام أيديهم وأرجلهم من خلاف
cards.en: If they take money from a Muslim or a dhimmi (a non-Muslim living under Muslim rule), and each one's share is at least ten dirhams, the imam cuts their hands and feet on opposite sides: the right hand and the left foot.

cards.ask: A band of 5 robbers stop a traveller and take 40 dirhams. Nobody is hurt. Are their hands and feet cut?
cards.source: أصاب كل واحد منهم عشرة دراهم فصاعدا
cards.why: 40 ÷ 5 = 8 dirhams each, below ten, so this hadd is not due.

cards.title: If they killed
cards.ar: وإن قتلوا ولم يأخذوا مالا قتلهم الإمام حدا فإن عفا الأولياء عنهم لم يلتفت إلى عفوهم
cards.en: If they killed but took no money, the imam puts them to death as a hadd. If the victim's family (awliya) forgive them, the forgiveness is not counted, because a hadd is Allah's right.

cards.ask: Highway robbers killed a traveller but took nothing. The traveller's family say, "We forgive them." What happens?
options: They are still put to death
They pay the diya instead of death
cards.source: فإن عفا الأولياء عنهم لم يلتفت إلى عفوهم
cards.why: This is a hadd, so the family's forgiveness does not stop it.

cards.title: If they killed and took money
cards.ar: وإن قتلوا وأخذوا المال فالإمام بالخيار: إن شاء قطع أيديهم وأرجلهم من خلاف وقتلهم وصلبهم وإن شاء قتلهم وإن شاء صلبهم
cards.en: If they both killed and took money, the imam may choose: cut their hands and feet on opposite sides and then put them to death and crucify them (salb), or just put them to death, or just crucify them.

cards.ask: Complete: for how long may one be left crucified?
cards.ar: ولا يصلب أكثر من ____ أيام
cards.source: ولا يصلب أكثر من ثلاثة أيام
cards.why: ثلاثة: no more than three days.

cards.title: A child, insane or relative among them
cards.ar: فإن كان فيهم صبي أو مجنون أو ذو رحم محرم من المقطوع عليه سقط الحد عن الباقين وصار القتل إلى الأولياء: إن شاؤوا قتلوا وإن شاؤا عفوا
cards.en: If there is a child, an insane person, or a close mahram relative of the victim among the robbers, the hadd falls away from all the rest. The killing then becomes the family's right: they may demand retaliation or forgive.

cards.ask: A band robs and kills a traveller. One of the robbers is the traveller's own brother. What is the ruling?
options: The hadd applies to all but the brother
cards.source: أو ذو رحم محرم من المقطوع عليه سقط الحد عن الباقين وصار القتل إلى الأولياء
cards.why: A mahram relative among them drops the hadd for all. The family then decide.

cards.title: If only one did it
cards.ar: وإن باشر الفعل واحد أجري الحد على جماعتهم
cards.en: If only one of them actually did the killing or taking, the hadd still applies to all of them, since they acted as one band.

cards.ask: What does the imam do with highway robbers?
items: Caught before taking or killing anything
source: حبسهم الإمام حتى يحدثوا توبة
قطع الإمام أيديهم وأرجلهم من خلاف
وإن قتلوا ولم يأخذوا مالا قتلهم الإمام حدا
وإن قتلوا وأخذوا المال فالإمام بالخيار
cards.why: The book gives four cases: prison, cutting from opposite sides, death, or the imam's choice when they did both.

cards.ask: Which are true of highway robbery?

options.text: Robbers caught before doing anything are imprisoned until they repent
Taking money brings cutting the right hand and left foot
If one robber does it, the hadd falls on the whole band
The victim's family may forgive a robber who killed
A child among them makes no difference to the rest

source: حبسهم الإمام حتى يحدثوا توبة
قطع الإمام أيديهم وأرجلهم من خلاف
وإن باشر الفعل واحد أجري الحد على جماعتهم
لم يلتفت إلى عفوهم
فإن كان فيهم صبي أو مجنون
cards.why: Prison until repentance, cutting from opposite sides, and the whole band shares the hadd. The family's forgiveness does not stop the hadd, and a child among them drops it for all.

cards.title: Trained hunting animals
cards.ar: يجوز الاصطياد بالكلب المعلم والفهد والبازي وسائر الجوارح المعلمة
cards.en: It is allowed to hunt with a trained dog, a cheetah (fahd), a hawk (bazi), and any other trained jawarih: animals and birds of prey that catch game.

cards.title: A trained dog
cards.ar: وتعليم الكلب: أن يترك الأكل ثلاث مرات
cards.en: A dog counts as trained when it leaves the catch without eating from it three times. That shows it is catching for its owner, not for itself. A hawk counts as trained when it comes back when called.

cards.ask: When does a hawk count as trained?
options: When it comes back when you call it
When it leaves the catch uneaten three times
When it has caught ten birds
cards.source: وتعليم البازي: أن يرجع إذا دعوته
cards.why: A hawk's training is that it returns when called. Leaving the catch uneaten is the test for a dog.

cards.title: Sending it with Bismillah
cards.ar: وذكر اسم الله تعالى عليه عند إرساله فأخذ الصيد وجرحه فمات حل أكله
cards.en: If he sends his trained dog, hawk or falcon and says Allah's name (Bismillah) as he sends it, and it catches the game, wounds it, and it dies, the game is halal (lawful) to eat.

cards.title: If the animal eats from it
cards.ar: وإن أكل منه الكلب لم يؤكل وأن أكل منه البازي أكل
cards.en: If the dog eats from the catch, it may not be eaten: the dog caught it for itself. If a hawk eats from it, it may still be eaten.

cards.ask: Bilal sends his trained dog with Bismillah. It catches a rabbit and eats part of it. May Bilal eat the rest?
options: No: the dog ate from it
Yes, if he says Bismillah again
cards.source: وإن أكل منه الكلب لم يؤكل
cards.why: When a dog eats from the catch, it is not eaten. (A hawk eating from it would be different.)

cards.title: If it is still alive
cards.ar: وإذا أدرك المرسل الصيد حيا وجب عليه أن يذكيه فإن ترك تذكيته حتى مات لم يؤكل وإن خنقه الكلب ولم يجرحه لم يؤكل
cards.en: If the hunter reaches the game while it is still alive, he must slaughter it properly (dhakat). If he leaves it until it dies, it is not eaten. If the dog strangles it without wounding it, it is not eaten either.

cards.ask: Yusuf's trained dog catches a deer and kills it by pressing on its neck, with no wound. May it be eaten?
options: No: it was strangled, not wounded
cards.source: وإن خنقه الكلب ولم يجرحه لم يؤكل
cards.why: The animal must die from a wound. A strangled catch is not eaten.

cards.title: Another dog joins in
cards.ar: وإن شاركه كلب غير معلم أو كلب مجوسي أو كلب لم يذكر اسم الله تعالى عليه لم يؤكل
cards.en: If an untrained dog, a Majusi's dog (a Majusi is a fire-worshipper), or a dog sent without Bismillah joins in the catch, it is not eaten.

cards.ask: Hamza's trained dog chases a gazelle, and a stray untrained dog joins in. Together they bring it down. May it be eaten?
options: No: an untrained dog shared in it
cards.source: وإن شاركه كلب غير معلم
cards.why: When an untrained dog takes part, the catch may not be eaten.

cards.ask: Which of these catches may be eaten?

options.text: A hawk sent with Bismillah wounds a bird, which dies
A hawk eats a little of its catch
A trained dog eats from the catch
He reached it alive but left it to die
A dog sent without Bismillah helped

source: وأن أكل منه البازي أكل
فأخذ الصيد وجرحه فمات حل أكله
وإن أكل منه الكلب لم يؤكل
فإن ترك تذكيته حتى مات لم يؤكل
أو كلب لم يذكر اسم الله تعالى عليه لم يؤكل
cards.why: A wound and Bismillah make it halal, and a hawk eating from it is fine. A dog eating, leaving it to die, or a dog sent without Bismillah make it unlawful.

lessons.title: Hunting with arrows
lessons.arabic: وإذا رمى الرجل سهما إلى صيد

cards.title: Shooting with Bismillah
cards.ar: وإذا رمى الرجل سهما إلى صيد فسمى عند الرمي أكل ما أصاب إذا جرحه السهم فمات وإن أدركه حيا ذكاه
cards.en: If a man shoots an arrow at game and says Bismillah as he shoots, he may eat what he hits, if the arrow wounds it and it dies. If he reaches it alive, he slaughters it.

cards.title: Searching for it
cards.ar: وإن وقع السهم فتحامل حتى غاب عنه ولم يزل في طلبه حتى أصابه ميتا أكل وإن قعد عن طلبه ثم أصابه ميتا لم يؤكل
cards.en: If the arrow hits and the animal struggles away out of sight, and he keeps searching until he finds it dead, it is eaten. If he stops searching and later finds it dead, it is not eaten: something else may have killed it.

cards.ask: Adam shoots a deer with Bismillah. It runs off. He sits down to rest for a few hours, then finds it dead. May he eat it?
options: Yes, if his arrow is still in it
cards.source: وإن قعد عن طلبه ثم أصابه ميتا لم يؤكل
cards.why: Because he stopped searching, he cannot be sure his arrow killed it.

cards.title: Where it falls
cards.ar: صيدا فوقع في الماء فمات لم يؤكل وكذلك إن وقع على سطح أو جبل ثم تردى منه إلى الأرض لم يؤكل وإن وقع على الأرض ابتداء أكل
cards.en: If the game falls into water and dies, it is not eaten, since it may have drowned. The same if it lands on a roof or mountain and then tumbles down. If it falls straight onto the ground, it is eaten.

cards.title: Blunt weapons
cards.ar: وما أصاب المعراض بعرضه لم يؤكل وإن جرحه أكل ولا يؤكل ما أصابته
cards.en: A mi'rad is a heavy shaft with no sharp head. If it hits with its flat side, the game is not eaten; if it cuts it, it is eaten. Nor is game eaten that dies from a bunduqa, a clay pellet that kills by force, not by cutting.

cards.ask: Eaten, or not?
items: Shot, then fell into a river and died
Shot, landed on a roof and rolled to the ground
Shot, fell straight to the ground
Hit by the flat side of a mi'rad
source: فوقع في الماء فمات لم يؤكل
وكذلك إن وقع على سطح أو جبل ثم تردى منه إلى الأرض لم يؤكل
وإن وقع على الأرض ابتداء أكل
وما أصاب المعراض بعرضه لم يؤكل وإن جرحه أكل
cards.why: Falling straight to the ground or a cutting wound is fine. Water, a fall from height, or a blow from the flat side may be what killed it.

cards.title: Cutting off a part
cards.ar: وإذا رمى إلى صيد فقطع عضوا منه أكل ولا يؤكل العضو وإن قطعه أثلاثا والأكثر مما يلي العجز أكل وإن كان الأكثر مما يلي الرأس أكل الأكثر ولا يؤكل الأقل
cards.en: If his shot cuts off a limb, the animal is eaten but not the cut-off limb. If it cuts the animal into thirds, with the bigger part on the tail side, all is eaten. If the bigger part is on the head side, the bigger part is eaten and the smaller is not.

cards.ask: Rami's arrow cuts a leg off a rabbit, and then the rabbit dies from the wound. What may be eaten?
options: The rabbit, but not the cut-off leg
All of it, the cut-off leg included
None of it, since a limb came off
cards.source: فقطع عضوا منه أكل ولا يؤكل العضو
cards.why: The animal is eaten; the limb that came off while it was alive is not.

cards.title: Two hunters
cards.ar: ومن رمى صيدا فأصابه ولم يثخنه ولم يخرجه من حيز الإمتناع فرماه آخر فقتله فهو للثاني ويؤكل
cards.en: If one man hits an animal but does not wound it enough to stop it escaping, and a second man shoots and kills it, it belongs to the second, and it is eaten. But if the first had already disabled it, it is not eaten, and the second pays the first its value.

cards.ask: Ziyad's arrow wounds a deer so badly it cannot run. Then Karim shoots and kills it. What is the ruling?
options: Not eaten, and Karim pays Ziyad its value
Karim owns it and it is eaten
Ziyad owns it, and Karim owes him nothing
cards.source: وإن كان الأول أثخنه فرماه الثاني فقتله لم يؤكل والثاني ضامن بقيمته للأول غير ما نقصته جراحته
cards.why: Once Ziyad had caught it by disabling it, it should have been slaughtered. Karim's shot killed it, so it is not eaten, and he pays Ziyad its value, less what Ziyad's wound had already taken off.

cards.ask: Which are true of hunting with arrows?

options.text: Game that falls straight to the ground is eaten
Game that falls into water and dies is not eaten
He must keep searching for wounded game
Game killed by a clay pellet is eaten
A cut-off limb is eaten too

source: وإن وقع على الأرض ابتداء أكل
فوقع في الماء فمات لم يؤكل
ولم يزل في طلبه حتى أصابه ميتا أكل
ولا يؤكل العضو
cards.why: Game that falls straight down is eaten, not what dies in water, and he must keep searching. A pellet does not cut, and the cut-off limb is not eaten.

cards.title: What may be hunted
cards.ar: ويجوز اصطياد ما يؤكل لحمه من الحيوان وما لا يؤكل
cards.en: It is allowed to hunt animals whose meat is eaten, and also ones whose meat is not eaten, for example for their skins.

cards.title: Whose slaughter is halal
cards.ar: وذبيحة المسلم والكتابي حلال ولا تؤكل ذبيحة المجوسي والمرتد والوثني والمحرم
cards.en: What a Muslim or a kitabi (a Jew or Christian) slaughters is halal. What a Majusi, a murtadd or an idol-worshipper slaughters is not eaten, nor game slaughtered by a muhrim (someone in ihram). In Hajj the book lets a muhrim slaughter his sheep or camel.

cards.ask: Is the animal they slaughter halal?
items: A man in ihram, with a deer he hunted
cards.source: وذبيحة المسلم والكتابي حلال ولا تؤكل ذبيحة المجوسي والمرتد والوثني والمحرم
cards.why: Muslims and the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) may slaughter. A Majusi and an idol-worshipper may not, and game slaughtered by a muhrim is not eaten.

cards.title: Saying Bismillah
cards.ar: وإن ترك الذابح التسمية عمدا فالذبيحة ميتة لا تؤكل وإن تركها ناسيا أكلت
cards.en: Tasmiya is saying Allah's name at slaughter. If the slaughterer leaves it out on purpose, the animal is mayta (like an animal that died by itself) and is not eaten. If he forgot, it is eaten.

cards.ask: Ibrahim slaughters a sheep and forgets to say Bismillah. May it be eaten?
options: Only if he says it afterwards
cards.source: وإن تركها ناسيا أكلت
cards.why: Leaving the tasmiya by mistake does not make the meat unlawful. Leaving it on purpose would.

cards.title: The four vessels
cards.ar: والعروق التي تقطع في الذكاة أربعة: الحلقوم والمريء والودجان فإذا قطعها حل الأكل وإن قطع أكثرها فكذلك عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: Slaughter is at the throat and the top of the chest. Four vessels are cut: the windpipe, the food pipe and the two jugular veins. Cutting all four makes it halal, and for Abu Hanifa cutting most of them is enough. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad required the windpipe, the food pipe and one jugular.

cards.ask: A butcher's knife cuts three of the four vessels, any three. Following Abu Hanifa, is the animal halal?
options: Yes: most of them were cut
No: all four must be cut
Only if he cuts the fourth afterwards
source: والذبح في الحلق واللبة
وإن قطع أكثرها فكذلك عند أبي حنيفة
cards.why: For Abu Hanifa, cutting most of the four vessels counts like cutting all of them.

cards.title: What to slaughter with
cards.ar: ويجوز الذبح بالليطة والمروة وبكل شيء أنهر الدم إلا السن القائم والظفر القائم
cards.en: Slaughter is allowed with a sharp strip of reed (lita), a sharp stone (marwa), or anything that makes the blood flow, except a tooth or a nail still in the mouth or on the finger.

cards.ask: Which may be used to slaughter?

options.text: A sharp stone
A sharp strip of reed
A knife
A tooth still in the mouth
A fingernail still on the finger

cards.source: ويجوز الذبح بالليطة والمروة وبكل شيء أنهر الدم إلا السن القائم والظفر القائم
cards.why: Anything that makes the blood flow is allowed, except a tooth or nail still attached.

cards.title: Sharpen the knife
cards.ar: ويستحب أن يحد الذابح شفرته ومن بلغ بالسكين النخاع أو قطع الرأس كره له ذلك وتؤكل ذبيحته
cards.en: It is mustahabb (recommended) to sharpen the knife, to be kind to the animal. Cutting down to the spinal cord or cutting the head off is makruh (disliked), but the animal is still eaten.

cards.ask: Saad cuts a goat from the back of its neck, and it dies before he reaches the four vessels. May it be eaten?
options: No: it died before the vessels were cut
Yes: it is only makruh to cut from behind
cards.source: وإن ذبح الشاة من قفاها فإن بقيت حية قطع العروق جاز ويكره وإن ماتت قبل قطع العروق لم تؤكل
cards.why: From the back is makruh; it is allowed only if the animal was still alive when the vessels were cut.

cards.ask: Which of these animals may be eaten?
options: A Muslim forgot Bismillah and used a sharp stone
It was a deer a man in ihram hunted and slaughtered
A Muslim left out Bismillah on purpose to save time
It was cut with a tooth still in the mouth
source: وإن تركها ناسيا أكلت
والمحرم
وإن ترك الذابح التسمية عمدا فالذبيحة ميتة لا تؤكل
إلا السن القائم
cards.why: Forgetting the tasmiya is forgiven and a sharp stone is fine. Game slaughtered by a muhrim, leaving Bismillah on purpose, and an attached tooth all make it unlawful.

lessons.title: Nahr, and animals that run wild

cards.title: Tame game and wild livestock
cards.ar: وما استأنس من الصيد فذكاته الذبح وما توحش من النعم فذكاته العقر والجرح
cards.en: A wild animal that has become tame must be slaughtered normally. Na'am (farm animals: camels, cattle, sheep) that have run wild can be made halal by 'aqr: wounding them anywhere, as in hunting.

cards.ask: Ahmad's cow escapes into the forest and runs wild. Nobody can catch it. He shoots it with an arrow, saying Bismillah, and it dies. May it be eaten?
options: Yes: wounding is its slaughter now
No: a cow must be slaughtered at the throat
Only if it is caught alive
cards.source: وما توحش من النعم فذكاته العقر والجرح
cards.why: A farm animal that has run wild is treated like game, so a wound makes it halal.

cards.ask: A deer has lived tame in Huda's garden for years. Can it be made halal by shooting it?
options: No: tame game must be slaughtered
Yes: a deer is game, so shooting is fine
Yes, if it is far away
cards.source: وما استأنس من الصيد فذكاته الذبح
cards.why: Game that has become tame is slaughtered like a farm animal.

cards.title: Camels: nahr
cards.ar: والمستحب في الإبل النحر فإن ذبحها جاز ويكره
cards.en: Nahr is stabbing at the base of the neck. For camels nahr is mustahabb. If he slaughters a camel at the throat instead, it is allowed but makruh.

cards.title: Cattle and sheep: dhabh
cards.ar: والمستحب في البقر والغنم الذبح فإن نحرهما جاز ويكره
cards.en: For cattle, sheep and goats, dhabh (cutting the throat) is mustahabb. Nahr on them is allowed but makruh.

cards.ask: Which way is mustahabb?
source: والمستحب في الإبل النحر
والمستحب في البقر والغنم الذبح
cards.why: Nahr is for camels; dhabh for cattle, sheep and goats.

cards.title: An unborn young
cards.ar: ومن نحر ناقة أو ذبح بقرة أو شاة فوجد في بطنها جنينا ميتا لم يؤكل أشعر أو لم يشعر
cards.en: If he slaughters a camel, cow or sheep and finds a dead janin (unborn young) inside, the janin is not eaten, whether or not it had grown hair.

cards.ask: Ali slaughters a cow and finds a dead calf inside it, fully formed with hair. May the calf be eaten?
options: No: a dead janin is not eaten
Yes, because it had grown hair
cards.source: فوجد في بطنها جنينا ميتا لم يؤكل أشعر أو لم يشعر
cards.why: A dead janin is not eaten, with hair or without.

cards.ask: Which of these is true?
options: A camel cut at the throat is allowed, but makruh
A sheep killed by nahr may not be eaten at all
A runaway cow can never be made halal by an arrow
A dead janin with hair may be eaten
source: فإن ذبحها جاز ويكره
فإن نحرهما جاز ويكره
وما توحش من النعم فذكاته العقر والجرح
لم يؤكل أشعر أو لم يشعر
cards.why: Using the other method is allowed but makruh, for camels and for sheep. A runaway cow is made halal by wounding, and a dead janin is never eaten.

lessons.title: Which animals may be eaten
lessons.arabic: ولا يجوز أكل كل ذي ناب من السباع

cards.title: Fangs and claws
cards.ar: ولا يجوز أكل كل ذي ناب من السباع وكل ذي مخلب من الطير
cards.en: It is not allowed to eat any wild beast with fangs that it hunts with (like lions and wolves), or any bird with talons (like eagles and hawks). But there is no harm in the crop crow, which eats grain.

cards.ask: Complete: which crow may not be eaten?
cards.ar: ولا يؤكل الأبقع الذي يأكل ____
cards.source: ولا يؤكل الأبقع الذي يأكل الجيف
cards.why: الجيف: the piebald crow that eats dead animals is not eaten. The crop crow, which eats grain, is fine.

cards.title: Disliked
cards.ar: ويكره أكل الضبع والضب والحشرات كلها
cards.en: Eating the hyena, the dabb (a desert lizard) and all insects and small crawling creatures is makruh.

cards.ask: Allowed, makruh, or not allowed?
source: ولا يجوز أكل كل ذي ناب من السباع وكل ذي مخلب من الطير
بغراب الزرع
ويكره أكل الضبع والضب والحشرات كلها
cards.why: Fanged beasts and taloned birds are not allowed; the hyena and insects are makruh. The crop crow, which eats grain, is fine.

cards.title: Donkeys, mules and horses
cards.ar: ولا يجوز أكل لحم الحمر الأهلية والبغال ويكره لحم الفرس عند أبي حنيفة ولا بأس بأكل الأرنب
cards.en: Eating the meat of tame donkeys and of mules is not allowed. Abu Hanifa held horse meat to be makruh. There is no harm in eating rabbit.

cards.ask: Allowed, makruh, or not allowed?
source: ولا يجوز أكل لحم الحمر الأهلية والبغال
بأكل الأرنب
ويكره أكل الضبع والضب
cards.why: Tame donkeys and mules are not allowed, the dabb is makruh, and there is no harm in rabbit.

cards.title: Slaughtering what is not eaten
cards.ar: وإذا ذبح ما لا يؤكل لحمه طهر لحمه وجلده إلا الآدمي والخنزير فإن الذكاة لا تعمل فيهما
cards.en: If an animal that is not eaten is slaughtered, its meat and skin become tahir (ritually clean), though still not eaten. This is not so for a human or a pig: slaughter has no effect on them.

cards.ask: A wolf is slaughtered properly with Bismillah. What is the ruling on its skin?
options: It stays impure, like a pig's skin
It may now be eaten with the meat
cards.source: وإذا ذبح ما لا يؤكل لحمه طهر لحمه وجلده
cards.why: Slaughter makes the skin of an uneaten animal clean, except for a pig or a human.

cards.title: Sea creatures
cards.ar: ولا يؤكل من حيوان الماء إلا السمك ويكره أكل الطافي منه ولا بأس بأكل الجريث والمارماهي
cards.en: Of the creatures of the water, only fish are eaten. Eating tafi, a fish that died by itself and floats on the water, is makruh. There is no harm in the jirrith and the marmahi, kinds of eel-like fish.

cards.ask: Following al-Quduri, may a crab caught from the sea be eaten?
options: No: of water creatures only fish are eaten
Yes: everything from the sea is halal
cards.source: ولا يؤكل من حيوان الماء إلا السمك
cards.why: Only fish are eaten from the water, and a crab is not a fish.

cards.title: Locusts
cards.ar: ويجوز أكل الجراد ولا ذكاة له
cards.en: Locusts may be eaten, and they need no slaughter.

cards.ask: Which of these may be eaten without being makruh?

options.text: Locusts, without slaughter
A rabbit
A fish caught alive
A floating fish that died by itself
A mule

source: ويجوز أكل الجراد ولا ذكاة له
بأكل الأرنب
إلا السمك
ويكره أكل الطافي منه
والبغال
cards.why: Locusts, rabbit and fish are fine. A floating dead fish is makruh, and a mule is not allowed.

cards.title: Who must sacrifice
cards.ar: الأضحية واجبة على كل حر مسلم مقيم موسر في يوم الأضحى عن نفسه وولده الصغار
cards.en: The udhiya is the animal sacrificed for Eid al-Adha. It is wajib (required) for every free Muslim who is muqim (at home, not travelling) and musir (well-off), on the day of Eid al-Adha, for himself and for his young children.

cards.ask: Who must give the udhiya?

options.text: A Muslim
Someone who is well-off
Someone at home, not travelling
A poor person
A traveller

source: الأضحية واجبة على كل حر مسلم مقيم موسر
وليس على الفقير والمسافر أضحية
cards.why: It is on a free Muslim who is at home and well-off. The poor and travellers do not have to.

cards.title: A sheep, or a share
cards.ar: يذبح عن كل واحد منهم شاة أو يذبح بدنة أو بقرة عن سبعة
cards.en: He slaughters a sheep for each person, or a badana (camel) or a cow for seven people together.

cards.ask: Yusuf and six friends are all well-off and at home. Can they share one cow as the udhiya for all seven?
options: Yes: a cow is for seven
No: a cow counts for only three
cards.source: أو يذبح بدنة أو بقرة عن سبعة
cards.why: A camel or a cow can be shared by seven people.

cards.title: Not on the poor or the traveller
cards.ar: وليس على الفقير والمسافر أضحية
cards.en: There is no udhiya due from the poor or from the traveller.

cards.ask: Karim is well-off, but he is on a long journey during the days of Eid al-Adha. Is the udhiya wajib on him?
options: Yes, when he gets home a month later
cards.source: وليس على الفقير والمسافر أضحية
cards.why: The udhiya is only on someone muqim. A traveller does not owe it.

cards.title: When it begins
cards.ar: ووقت الأضحية يدخل بطلوع الفجر من يوم النحر إلا أنه لا يجوز لأهل الأمصار الذبح حتى يصلي الإمام صلاة العيد فأما أهل السواد فيذبحون بعد الفجر
cards.en: Its time begins at dawn on yawm al-nahr (the day of sacrifice, 10 Dhul Hijjah). But people of the amsar (towns and cities) may not slaughter until the imam has prayed the Eid prayer. People of the countryside slaughter after dawn.

cards.ask: Bilal lives in a city. On Eid morning, after dawn but before the Eid prayer, he slaughters his udhiya. Is it valid?
options: No: the Eid prayer comes first
Yes: dawn on Eid day has come
Yes, if he prays the Eid later
cards.source: إلا أنه لا يجوز لأهل الأمصار الذبح حتى يصلي الإمام صلاة العيد
cards.why: Town people must wait for the Eid prayer. Only the countryside may slaughter straight after dawn.

cards.title: Three days
cards.ar: وهي جائزة في ثلاثة أيام: يوم النحر ويومان بعده
cards.en: It can be done on three days: the day of sacrifice and the two days after it.

cards.ask: On how many days may the udhiya be slaughtered?
cards.source: وهي جائزة في ثلاثة أيام: يوم النحر ويومان بعده
cards.why: The day of sacrifice and the two days after it: three.

cards.ask: Which of these udhiyas is valid?
options: A villager slaughters after dawn on Eid day
A city man slaughters at dawn, before the Eid prayer
A man slaughters on the fourth day of Eid
Eight neighbours share one cow as their udhiya
source: فأما أهل السواد فيذبحون بعد الفجر
حتى يصلي الإمام صلاة العيد
وهي جائزة في ثلاثة أيام
أو بقرة عن سبعة
cards.why: Country people may slaughter after dawn. The city man was early, the fourth day is too late, and a cow is for seven at most.

cards.title: Defects that rule it out
cards.ar: ولا يضحي بالعمياء والعوراء والعرجاء التي لا تمشي إلى المنسك ولا العجفاء
cards.en: An animal may not be sacrificed if it is blind, one-eyed, so lame it cannot walk to the place of slaughter, or 'ajfa' (very thin and weak).

cards.title: Ears and tail
cards.ar: ولا تجزئ مقطوعة الأذن والذنب ولا التي ذهب أكثر أذنها فإن بقي الأكثر من الأذن والذنب جاز
cards.en: One whose ear or tail is cut off does not count, nor one that has lost most of its ear. If most of the ear and tail are left, it is fine.

cards.ask: Does this animal count as an udhiya?
items: A sheep with its tail cut off
A goat that has lost a small part of one ear
source: والعوراء
ولا العجفاء
ولا تجزئ مقطوعة الأذن والذنب
فإن بقي الأكثر من الأذن والذنب جاز
cards.why: One eye, great thinness and a cut-off tail rule it out. If most of the ear is still there, it counts.

cards.title: Defects that do not matter
cards.ar: ويجوز أن يضحى بالجماء والخصي والجرباء والثولاء
cards.en: It is allowed to sacrifice one that has no horns, one that is castrated, one with mange (a skin disease), and one that is thawla' (acts crazed).

cards.ask: Allowed for the udhiya?
items: A cow too lame to walk to the place of slaughter
source: ولا يضحي بالعمياء
ويجوز أن يضحى بالجماء والخصي والجرباء والثولاء
والعرجاء التي لا تمشي إلى المنسك
cards.why: Blindness and lameness that stops it walking to the slaughter rule it out. No horns, castration and mange do not.

cards.title: The age
cards.ar: والأضحية من الإبل والبقر والغنم يجزئ من ذلك كله الثني فصاعدا إلا الضمان فإن الجذع منه يجزئ
cards.en: The udhiya is from camels, cattle, sheep and goats. A thani (an animal that has reached its full set age) or older counts, for all of them. The exception is the da'n (sheep): a jadha', a younger sheep, also counts.

cards.ask: Hamza has a young sheep, a jadha', not yet a thani. Can he sacrifice it?
options: Yes: for sheep a jadha' counts
No: every animal must be a thani
Only if it is a fat jadha' ram
cards.source: إلا الضمان فإن الجذع منه يجزئ
cards.why: For every kind a thani is needed, except sheep, where a jadha' is enough.

cards.title: The meat
cards.ar: ويأكل من لحم الأضحية ويطعم الأغنياء والفقراء ويدخر ويستحب أن لا ينقص الصدقة من الثلث
cards.en: He eats from the meat, feeds the rich and the poor, and may store some. It is mustahabb (recommended: rewarded, not required) that what he gives in charity is not less than a third.

cards.ask: Musa's udhiya gives 30 kg of meat. Following the mustahabb way, at least how much should he give in charity?
cards.source: ويستحب أن لا ينقص الصدقة من الثلث
cards.why: A third of 30 kg is 10 kg. The rest he may eat, give to anyone, or store.

cards.title: The skin
cards.ar: ويتصدق بجلدها أو يعمل منه آلة تستعمل في البيت
cards.en: He gives the skin in charity, or makes something from it that is used at home, like a water skin or a mat.

cards.title: Who slaughters it
cards.ar: والأفضل أن يذبح أضحيته بيده إن كان يحسن الذبح ويكره أن يذبحها الكتابي
cards.en: It is best to slaughter one's own udhiya by hand, if he knows how to do it well. It is makruh (disliked) for a kitabi (a Jew or Christian) to slaughter it for him.

cards.ask: Ali and Omar each bring a sheep. By mistake, Ali slaughters Omar's and Omar slaughters Ali's. What is the ruling?
options: Both count, and neither owes anything
Each pays the other the price of a sheep
cards.source: وإذا غلط رجلان فذبح كل واحد منهما أضحية الآخر أجزأ عنهما ولا ضمان عليهما
cards.why: When two men slaughter each other's udhiya by mistake, both count and there is nothing to pay.

cards.ask: Which are true of the udhiya?

options.text: He may eat from his own udhiya
He may make a household item from the skin
It is best to slaughter it himself, if he slaughters well
A goat with no horns cannot be used
A blind animal is fine if it is fat

source: ويأكل من لحم الأضحية
أو يعمل منه آلة تستعمل في البيت
والأفضل أن يذبح أضحيته بيده إن كان يحسن الذبح
ويجوز أن يضحى بالجماء
ولا يضحي بالعمياء
cards.why: He may eat from it, use the skin at home, and should slaughter it himself if he can. A hornless animal is fine, and a blind one is never allowed.

cards.title: Three kinds
cards.ar: الأيمان على ثلاثة أضرب: يمين غموس ويمين منعقدة ويمين لغو
cards.en: An oath (yamin) is when you swear, for example "By Allah, I will...". Al-Quduri says there are three kinds: the ghamus oath, the mun'aqida (binding) oath and the laghw (slip) oath.

cards.ask: How many kinds of oath does al-Quduri name?
cards.source: الأيمان على ثلاثة أضرب
cards.why: Three: the ghamus, the binding and the slip oath.

cards.ask: Which of these are the kinds of oath al-Quduri names?

options.text: The ghamus oath
The written oath
The binding (mun'aqida) oath
The laghw (slip) oath
The silent oath

cards.source: الأيمان على ثلاثة أضرب: يمين غموس ويمين منعقدة ويمين لغو
cards.why: His three kinds are the ghamus, the binding and the slip oath. The other two are not on his list.

cards.title: The ghamus oath
cards.ar: فاليمين الغموس هي: الحلف على أمر ماض يتعمد الكذب فيه فهذه اليمين يأثم بها صاحبها ولا كفارة فيها إلا الاستغفار
cards.en: The ghamus oath is swearing about something in the past while lying on purpose. The person sins. There is no kaffara for it (a kaffara is an act, like feeding the poor, that makes up for a broken oath). The only way out is istighfar: asking Allah's forgiveness.

cards.ask: Khalid swears "By Allah, I paid you yesterday", knowing that he did not. What does he owe?
options: A sin, and only asking Allah's forgiveness
A kaffara: feeding or clothing ten poor people
Nothing at all: it is a slip oath
cards.source: فهذه اليمين يأثم بها صاحبها ولا كفارة فيها إلا الاستغفار
cards.why: He lied on purpose about the past, so this is a ghamus oath. He sins, and only istighfar is left for him, not a kaffara.

cards.title: The binding oath
cards.ar: واليمين المنعقدة: هي الحلف على الأمر المستقبل أن يفعله أو لا يفعله فإذا حنث في ذلك لزمته الكفارة
cards.en: The mun'aqida (binding) oath is swearing about the future: that you will do something, or will not. If you break it (this is called hinth), you must pay the kaffara.

cards.title: The slip oath
cards.ar: واليمين اللغو: أن يحلف على أمر ماض وهو يظن أنه
cards.en: The laghw (slip) oath is swearing about something in the past, truly thinking it is so, when in fact it is not. Al-Quduri says: we hope Allah will not hold the person to account for it.

cards.ask: Amina swears "By Allah, Zayd has arrived", truly believing it. In fact he had not arrived. What kind of oath is this?
options: A ghamus oath: she has sinned
A binding oath: she owes a kaffara
source: واليمين اللغو: أن يحلف على أمر ماض وهو يظن أنه
فهذه نرجو أن لا يؤاخذ الله بها صاحبها
cards.why: She swore about the past and believed it was true, so it is a laghw oath, and al-Quduri hopes she is not held to account.

cards.ask: Which kind of oath is it?
items: "By Allah, I didn't take it", when he knows he did
"By Allah, I will visit you tomorrow"
"By Allah, the shop was open", truly thinking so, but it was shut
"By Allah, I was at home last night", a deliberate lie
source: الحلف على أمر ماض يتعمد الكذب فيه
هي الحلف على الأمر المستقبل أن يفعله أو لا يفعله
أن يحلف على أمر ماض وهو يظن أنه
cards.why: A deliberate lie about the past is ghamus, and an honest mistake about the past is laghw. Any oath about the future is binding.

cards.title: Meaning it or not
cards.ar: والقاصد في اليمين والمكره والناسي سواء ومن فعل المحلوف عليه مكرها أو ناسيا سواء
cards.en: An oath counts the same whether the person meant it, was forced (mukrah) to say it, or said it by mistake. And if he does the thing he swore not to do, it counts the same if he was forced or had forgotten.

cards.ask: Umar swore not to drink coffee this week. Then he forgot and drank a cup. Has he broken his oath?
options: No: he forgot, so it doesn't count
Only if he drinks a second cup
cards.source: ومن فعل المحلوف عليه مكرها أو ناسيا سواء
cards.why: Doing the thing you swore against counts the same when forgotten, so he has broken the oath and owes a kaffara.

cards.ask: Which are true of the kinds of oath?

options.text: A ghamus oath has no kaffara, only asking forgiveness
Breaking a binding oath means paying the kaffara
An oath said under force still counts
A laghw oath is about the future
A ghamus oath is about the future

source: ولا كفارة فيها إلا الاستغفار
فإذا حنث في ذلك لزمته الكفارة
والقاصد في اليمين والمكره والناسي سواء
cards.why: Ghamus has only istighfar, a broken binding oath needs a kaffara, and a forced oath counts. Ghamus and laghw are both about the past.

lessons.title: Words that make an oath
lessons.arabic: واليمين بالله تعالى أو باسم من أسمائه

cards.title: By Allah or His names
cards.ar: واليمين بالله تعالى أو باسم من أسمائه كالرحمن والرحيم
cards.en: An oath is made by swearing by Allah, or by one of His names, such as al-Rahman (the Most Merciful) or al-Rahim (the Most Kind).

cards.title: By His qualities
cards.ar: أو بصفة من صفات ذاته كعزة الله وجلالته وكبريائه إلا قوله: وعلم الله فإنه لا يكون يمينا
cards.en: It is also an oath to swear by a quality of Allah's own being, like His might, majesty or greatness. But saying "By the knowledge of Allah" is not an oath.

cards.ask: Yusuf says: "By the knowledge of Allah, I will not go." Is this an oath?
options: No: that phrase is the book's exception
Yes: knowledge is a quality of Allah
Yes: any quality of Allah makes an oath
cards.source: إلا قوله: وعلم الله فإنه لا يكون يمينا
cards.why: Al-Quduri names "By the knowledge of Allah" as the exception: it is not an oath.

cards.title: Qualities of action, and other things
cards.ar: وإن حلف بصفة من صفات الفعل كغضب الله وسخطه لم يكن حالفا
cards.en: Swearing by a quality of Allah's action, like His anger or displeasure, is not an oath. Swearing by anything other than Allah, like the Prophet, the Qur'an or the Kaaba, is not an oath either.

cards.ask: Is it an oath?
source: واليمين بالله تعالى أو باسم من أسمائه
كعزة الله وجلالته وكبريائه
كغضب الله وسخطه لم يكن حالفا
ومن حلف بغير الله لم يكن حالفا كالنبي والقرآن والكعبة
cards.why: Allah, His names and the qualities of His being make an oath. His anger (a quality of action) and the Kaaba, which is not Allah, do not.

cards.title: Letters of swearing
cards.ar: وحروف القسم: الواو كقوله: والله والباء كقوله: بالله والتاء كقوله: تالله وقد تضمر الحروف فيكون حالفا كقوله: الله لا أفعل كذا
cards.en: In Arabic you swear with a letter: wa (wallahi), bi (billahi) or ta (tallahi). The letter can also be left out, as in "Allahi, I won't do it", and it is still an oath. Abu Hanifa said that "wa haqqi Allah" (by the right of Allah) is not an oath.

cards.ask: The letter can be left out. Complete the example.
cards.ar: وقد تضمر الحروف فيكون حالفا كقوله: ____ لا أفعل كذا
cards.source: وقد تضمر الحروف فيكون حالفا كقوله: الله لا أفعل كذا
cards.why: الله: saying "Allah, I won't do it" with no letter is still an oath.

cards.ask: How many letters of swearing does al-Quduri name?
cards.source: وحروف القسم: الواو كقوله: والله والباء كقوله: بالله والتاء كقوله: تالله
cards.why: Three: wa, bi and ta.

cards.ask: Which of these are al-Quduri's letters of swearing?

options.text: Wa, as in wallahi
La
Bi, as in billahi
Fa
Ta, as in tallahi

cards.source: وحروف القسم: الواو كقوله: والله والباء كقوله: بالله والتاء كقوله: تالله
cards.why: The letters of swearing are wa, bi and ta. La and fa are not among them.

cards.title: "I swear", "I bear witness"
cards.ar: وإذا قال: أقسم أو أقسم بالله أو أحلف بالله أو أشهد أو أشهد بالله فهو حالف
cards.en: Saying "I swear", "I swear by Allah", "I bear witness" or "I bear witness by Allah" is an oath. So is "By Allah's covenant", "I owe a vow (nadhr)", or "If I do it, I am a Jew, a Christian or a disbeliever".

cards.ask: Hasan says: "I swear (uqsimu) I won't go out today." He did not say "by Allah". Is it an oath?
options: Yes: "I swear" alone is an oath
Only if he also says "I bear witness"
cards.source: وإذا قال: أقسم أو أقسم بالله
cards.why: Al-Quduri lists "I swear" on its own as an oath.

cards.title: Not an oath
cards.ar: وإن قال: علي غضب الله أو سخطه أو أنا زان أو شارب خمر أو آكل ربا فليس بحالف
cards.en: Saying "Allah's anger be on me", or "(if I do it) I am a fornicator, a wine-drinker, or one who eats riba" is not an oath. (Riba is interest: taking extra money on a loan, which Islam forbids.)

cards.ask: Is it an oath?
items: "If I do it, I am a Christian"
"If I do it, Allah's anger be on me"
"If I do it, I am a wine-drinker"
source: وكذلك قوله: وعهد الله وميثاقه وعلي نذر أو نذر الله وإن فعلت كذا فأنا يهودي أو نصراني أو كافر فهو يمين
علي غضب الله أو سخطه أو أنا زان أو شارب خمر أو آكل ربا فليس بحالف
cards.why: Allah's covenant, "I am a Christian if..." and "I bear witness by Allah" are oaths. "Allah's anger on me" and "I am a wine-drinker" are not.

lessons.title: The kaffara for a broken oath

cards.title: Freeing a slave
cards.ar: وكفارة اليمين: عتق رقبة يجزئ فيها ما يجزئ في
cards.en: The kaffara (making up) for a broken oath has choices. In al-Quduri's time, the first was freeing a slave, and the same slaves count as in the kaffara for zihar (a forbidden way a husband once spoke to his wife).

cards.title: Clothing or feeding ten
cards.ar: وإن شاء كسا عشرة مساكين كل واحد ثوبا فما زاد وأذناه ما تجزئ فيه الصلاة وإن شاء أطعم عشرة مساكين كالإطعام في كفارة الظهار
cards.en: Or, if he likes, he clothes ten poor people, each with a garment or more; the least is clothing you could pray in. Or, if he likes, he feeds ten poor people, the same way as feeding in the zihar kaffara.

cards.ask: How many poor people does he clothe or feed for a broken oath?
cards.source: وإن شاء أطعم عشرة مساكين
cards.why: Al-Quduri says ten poor people, for both clothing and feeding.

cards.title: Fasting three days
cards.ar: فإن لم يقدر على أحد الأشياء الثلاثة صام ثلاثة أيام متتابعات
cards.en: Only if he cannot do any of the three (freeing, clothing, feeding) does he fast, for three days in a row.

cards.ask: Imran broke his oath. He cannot afford to free a slave, clothe or feed ten poor people. What must he do?
options: Fast three days in a row
Fast three days, with gaps allowed
cards.source: صام ثلاثة أيام متتابعات
cards.why: When none of the three is possible, he fasts three days, one after the other.

cards.title: Not before breaking it
cards.ar: فإن قدم الكفارة على الحنث لم يجزه
cards.en: If he pays the kaffara before he breaks the oath, it does not count.

cards.ask: Saad swore not to enter his cousin's house, but he plans to. He feeds ten poor people first and then enters. Is his kaffara done?
options: No: it came before he broke the oath
Yes: he fed ten poor people as required
Yes, but he must also fast three days
cards.source: فإن قدم الكفارة على الحنث لم يجزه
cards.why: He paid before he broke the oath, so it does not count. He owes the kaffara after breaking it.

cards.title: An oath to do wrong
cards.ar: ومن حلف على معصية مثل أن لا يصلي أو لا يكلم أباه أو ليقتلن فلانا فينبغي أن يحنث ويكفر عن يمينه
cards.en: If someone swears to do a sin, like not praying, not speaking to his father, or killing someone, he should break the oath and pay the kaffara.

cards.ask: Tariq angrily swore never to speak to his father again. What should he do?
options: Break it, speak to him, and pay the kaffara
Keep the oath, and never speak to his father
Speak to him and only ask forgiveness
cards.source: فينبغي أن يحنث ويكفر عن يمينه
cards.why: Not speaking to his father is a sin, so he should break the oath and pay its kaffara.

cards.title: A non-Muslim's oath
cards.ar: وإذا حلف الكافر ثم حنث في حال الكفر أو بعد إسلامه فلا حنث عليه
cards.en: If a non-Muslim swears and then breaks it, whether before or after becoming Muslim, it does not count as breaking an oath.

cards.ask: Which are true of the kaffara for an oath?

options.text: The kaffara can be clothing ten poor people
Fasting is only for someone who cannot do the other three
A kaffara paid before breaking the oath doesn't count
The fast is ten days
A non-Muslim who swore and broke it after Islam owes a kaffara

source: وإن شاء كسا عشرة مساكين
فإن لم يقدر على أحد الأشياء الثلاثة صام ثلاثة أيام متتابعات
فإن قدم الكفارة على الحنث لم يجزه
فلا حنث عليه
cards.why: Clothing ten is one choice, fasting comes only when the others are impossible, and early kaffara doesn't count. The fast is three days, and a non-Muslim's oath has no breaking.

lessons.title: Making things haram on yourself, and vows
lessons.arabic: ومن نذر نذرا مطلقا فعليه الوفاء به

cards.title: Calling your own thing haram
cards.ar: ومن حرم على نفسه شيئا مما يملكه لم يصر محرما لعينه
cards.en: If someone declares something he owns haram (forbidden) for himself, it does not really become haram. But if he then uses it, he owes the kaffara of an oath.

cards.ask: Layla says "This cake is haram for me", then eats it. What happens?
options: She owes the kaffara of an oath
She has sinned and must only ask forgiveness
source: لم يصر محرما لعينه
استباحه كفارة يمين
cards.why: The cake did not become haram, but by eating it after her words she owes an oath's kaffara.

cards.title: "Everything halal is haram for me"
cards.ar: فإن قال: كل حلال علي حرام فهو على الطعام والشراب إلا أن ينوي غير ذلك
cards.en: If he says "Everything halal is haram for me", it is taken to mean food and drink, unless he meant something else.

cards.ask: Rashid says "Everything halal is haram for me", without meaning anything in particular. What does it cover?
cards.source: فهو على الطعام والشراب إلا أن ينوي غير ذلك
cards.why: With no particular intention, it is understood to be about food and drink.

cards.title: Keeping a vow
cards.ar: ومن نذر نذرا مطلقا فعليه الوفاء به
cards.en: A nadhr is a vow: promising Allah to do a good deed. If someone makes a plain vow with no condition, he must fulfil it.

cards.ask: Huda vows: "I will fast three days for Allah", with no condition. What must she do?
options: Nothing, unless she adds a condition
cards.source: ومن نذر نذرا مطلقا فعليه الوفاء به
cards.why: A plain vow must be fulfilled.

cards.title: A vow with a condition
cards.ar: وإن علق نذره بشرط فوجد الشرط فعليه الوفاء بنفس النذر
cards.en: If he ties his vow to a condition ("If this happens, I will...") and the condition happens, he must fulfil the vow itself.

cards.title: Abu Hanifa's later view
cards.ar: وروي أن أبا حنيفة رجع عن ذلك وقال: إذا قال: إن فعلت كذا فعلي حجة أو صوم سنة أو صدقة ما أملكه أجزأه من ذلك كفارة يمين وهو قول محمد
cards.en: Note: it is reported that Abu Hanifa later changed his view. If someone says "If I do such-and-such, I owe a Hajj, a year of fasting, or giving away all I own", an oath's kaffara is enough for him. This is also Muhammad's view.

cards.ask: What does he owe?
items: Says "My car is haram for me", then drives it
Says "This bread is haram for me", then eats it
Vows a day's fast, with no condition
Vows "If I recover, I'll give 10 dirhams in charity", and recovers
source: وعليه أن استباحه كفارة يمين
ومن نذر نذرا مطلقا فعليه الوفاء به
فوجد الشرط فعليه الوفاء بنفس النذر
cards.why: Using something you called haram costs an oath's kaffara. A plain vow, or a conditional vow whose condition happens, must be fulfilled.

cards.title: "I won't enter a house"
cards.ar: لا يدخل بيتا فدخل الكعبة أو المسجد أو البيعة أو الكنيسة لم يحنث
cards.en: Oaths are understood by how people normally speak. A bayt is a house to live in. So if someone swears not to enter a bayt and then enters the Kaaba, a mosque, a synagogue or a church, he has not broken his oath.

cards.ask: Musa swore "By Allah, I won't enter a house today". Then he went into the mosque to pray. Has he broken his oath?
options: No: a mosque is not a house
Yes: he went into a building
Yes, unless he stayed outside the prayer hall
cards.source: لا يدخل بيتا فدخل الكعبة أو المسجد
cards.why: Entering a mosque does not break an oath about entering a house.

cards.title: Reciting in prayer
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يتكلم فقرأ في الصلاة لم يحنث
cards.en: If someone swears not to speak, and then recites Qur'an in his prayer, he has not broken the oath.

cards.ask: Ziyad swore not to say a word all afternoon. He then prayed Asr and recited the Fatiha. What is the ruling?
cards.source: ومن حلف لا يتكلم فقرأ في الصلاة لم يحنث
cards.why: Al-Quduri says reciting in the prayer does not break an oath not to speak.

cards.title: Taking it off at once
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يلبس ثوبا وهو لابسه فنزعه في الحال لم يحنث وكذا إذا حلف لا يركب هذه الدابة وهو راكبها فنزل في الحال وإن لبث ساعة حنث
cards.en: If someone wearing a garment swears not to wear it, and takes it off at once, he has not broken the oath. The same goes for swearing not to ride an animal while on it, and getting off at once. If he stays on for a while, he has broken it.

cards.ask: Bilal, riding his camel, swears not to ride this camel. He stays on it for an hour. What is the ruling?
options: Broken: he stayed on for a while
Not broken: he was already riding
Not broken, as long as he gets off later
cards.source: وإن لبث ساعة حنث
cards.why: He did not get off at once, so staying on counts as riding.

cards.title: Already inside
cards.ar: وإن حلف لا يدخل هذه الدار وهو فيها لم يحنث بالقعود حتى يخرج ثم يدخل
cards.en: If someone inside a house (dar) swears not to enter it, sitting there does not break it. Only going out and coming back in does.

cards.ask: Nur is sitting in her aunt's house when she swears not to enter it. She stays sitting there all evening. What is the ruling?
options: Not broken: sitting there is not entering
Broken: she stayed inside the house all evening
Broken, unless she leaves at once
cards.source: وإن حلف لا يدخل هذه الدار وهو فيها لم يحنث بالقعود حتى يخرج ثم يدخل
cards.why: Sitting inside is not entering. Only going out and coming back in would break it.

cards.title: A ruined house
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يدخل دارا فدخل دارا خرابا لم يحنث
cards.en: If he swears not to enter "a house" (dar, any house) and enters a ruined one, he has not broken it.

cards.title: "This house" after it falls
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يدخل هذه الدار فدخلها بعد ما انهدمت وصارت صحراء حنث ولو حلف لا يدخل هذا البيت فدخله بعد ما انهدم لم يحنث
cards.en: But if he swore not to enter "this dar" (a particular house with its yard), then entered it after it fell down into open ground, he has broken it. If he swore not to enter "this bayt" (this roofed room) and entered after it collapsed, he has not.

cards.ask: Broken or not?
items: Swore not to enter "this dar"; entered after it became open ground
Swore not to ride this horse while on it; stayed on an hour
Swore not to enter "a dar"; entered a ruined one
Swore not to enter "this bayt"; entered after it collapsed
Wearing a coat, swore not to wear it; took it off at once
source: فدخلها بعد ما انهدمت وصارت صحراء حنث
وإن لبث ساعة حنث
فدخل دارا خرابا لم يحنث
فدخله بعد ما انهدم لم يحنث
فنزعه في الحال لم يحنث
cards.why: "This dar" stays itself even as open ground, and staying on counts as riding. A ruin is not "a dar", a fallen bayt is no bayt, and taking a coat off at once is not wearing it.

lessons.title: When people and things change
lessons.arabic: ومن حلف لا يكلم زوجة فلان

cards.title: Someone's wife
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يكلم زوجة فلان فطلقها فلان ثم كلمها حنث
cards.en: If someone swears not to speak to a certain man's wife, and the man then divorces her, speaking to her afterwards still breaks the oath.

cards.ask: Faris swore not to speak to Hamid's wife. Hamid later divorced her, and Faris spoke to her. What is the ruling?
options: Not broken: she is no longer Hamid's wife
Broken only if he knew of the divorce
cards.source: فطلقها فلان ثم كلمها حنث
cards.why: Al-Quduri says he has broken the oath, even after the divorce.

cards.title: Someone's slave or house, once sold
cards.ar: ولو حلف لا يكلم عبد فلان أو لا يدخل دار فلان فباع عبده وداره ثم كلم العبد ودخل الدار لم يحنث
cards.en: If he swears not to speak to a man's slave (in al-Quduri's time) or not to enter a man's house, and the man sells them, speaking to that slave or entering that house afterwards does not break it.

cards.ask: Nabil swore not to enter Hamza's house. Hamza sold the house, and Nabil then went in. What is the ruling?
options: Not broken: it is no longer Hamza's house
Broken: it is the same building
Broken if Nabil pointed at it
cards.source: أو لا يدخل دار فلان فباع عبده وداره ثم كلم العبد ودخل الدار لم يحنث
cards.why: After the sale, the house no longer belongs to Hamza, so entering it does not break the oath.

cards.title: The same person, the same thing
cards.ar: وإن حلف لا يكلم صاحب هذا الطيلسان فباعه ثم كلمه حنث وكذلك إن حلف لا يكلم هذا الشاب فكلمه بعد ما صار شيخا حنث أو لا يأكل لحم هذا الحمل فصار كبشا فأكله حنث
cards.en: If he swears not to speak to "the owner of this taylasan" (a scarf worn over the shoulders), and the owner sells it, speaking to him still breaks it. So does speaking to "this young man" after he grows old, or eating "this lamb" after it grows into a ram.

cards.ask: Idris swore not to speak to "the owner of this shawl". The owner sold the shawl, and Idris spoke to him. What is the ruling?
options: Broken: he is still the same man
Not broken: he no longer owns the shawl
Not broken, unless Idris knew the man
cards.source: وإن حلف لا يكلم صاحب هذا الطيلسان فباعه ثم كلمه حنث
cards.why: Al-Quduri rules that he has broken the oath: selling the shawl does not change who the man is.

cards.title: Palm trees and dates
cards.ar: وإن حلف لا يأكل من هذه النخلة فهو على ثمرها وإن حلف لا يأكل من هذا البسر فصار رطبا فأكله لم يحنث وإن حلف لا يأكل بسرا فأكل رطبا لم يحنث
cards.en: Swearing not to eat from "this palm tree" means its fruit. Busr are unripe dates and rutab are ripe, fresh dates. If he swears not to eat "this busr" and eats it after it ripens into rutab, or swears not to eat busr and eats rutab, he has not broken the oath.

cards.ask: Hani swore not to eat "this busr" (these unripe dates). He waited until they ripened into rutab, then ate them. What is the ruling?
options: Broken: they are the same dates
Broken, unless he waited a month
cards.source: وإن حلف لا يأكل من هذا البسر فصار رطبا فأكله لم يحنث
cards.why: Once busr has become rutab, eating it does not break an oath about "this busr".

cards.title: Dates starting to ripen
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يأكل رطبا فأكل بسرا مذنبا حنث عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: If he swears not to eat rutab, and eats busr that has started ripening at the tip, Abu Hanifa says he has broken it.

cards.title: Meat and fish
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يأكل لحما فأكل السمك لم يحنث
cards.en: If he swears not to eat meat (lahm) and eats fish, he has not broken it.

cards.ask: Adil swore not to eat meat (lahm) this week. At dinner he ate grilled fish. What is the ruling?
options: Broken: fish is a kind of meat
Broken, unless the fish was small
cards.source: ومن حلف لا يأكل لحما فأكل السمك لم يحنث
cards.why: Al-Quduri says eating fish does not break an oath not to eat meat.

cards.title: Drinking from the Tigris
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يشرب من دجله فشرب منها بإناء لم يحنث حتى يكرع منها كرعا في قول أبي حنيفة ومن حلف لا يشرب من ماء دجلة فشرب منها بإناء حنث
cards.en: The Tigris (Dijla) is a river in Iraq. Abu Hanifa says that if he swears not to drink "from the Tigris", drinking from it with a cup does not break it, only drinking straight from the river. If he swears not to drink "from the water of the Tigris", a cup does break it.

cards.ask: Broken or not?
items: Swore not to speak to "this young man"; spoke to him when old
Swore not to eat "this lamb"; ate it once it was a ram
Swore not to drink "the water of the Tigris"; drank it from a cup
Swore not to eat "this busr"; ate it once it was rutab
Swore not to enter Ali's house; entered after Ali sold it
source: فكلمه بعد ما صار شيخا حنث
فصار كبشا فأكله حنث
ومن حلف لا يشرب من ماء دجلة فشرب منها بإناء حنث
فصار رطبا فأكله لم يحنث
فباع عبده وداره ثم كلم العبد ودخل الدار لم يحنث
cards.why: A person or animal pointed at stays the same as it grows, and the water of the Tigris is the same in a cup. Busr that became rutab, and a house that was sold, are different.

lessons.title: Wheat, flour, speaking and the doorway
lessons.arabic: ومن حلف لا يأكل من هذه الحنطة

cards.title: Wheat and its bread
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يأكل من هذه الحنطة فأكل من خبزها لم يحنث
cards.en: If someone swears not to eat "from this wheat" and eats bread made from it, he has not broken the oath.

cards.title: Flour and its bread
cards.ar: من خبزه حنث ولو استفه كما هو لم يحنث
cards.en: But if he swears not to eat "from this flour" and eats bread made from it, he has broken it. If he swallows the dry flour as it is, he has not, since people don't usually eat flour that way.

cards.ask: Sami swore not to eat from this sack of wheat. His mother ground it and baked bread, and he ate it. What is the ruling?
options: Broken only if he ate the whole loaf
cards.source: ومن حلف لا يأكل من هذه الحنطة فأكل من خبزها لم يحنث
cards.why: For wheat, eating its bread does not break the oath. (For flour, it would.)

cards.title: Speaking to someone asleep
cards.ar: ولو حلف لا يكلم فلانا فكلمه وهو بحيث يسمع إلا أنه نائم حنث
cards.en: If he swears not to speak to someone, then speaks to him close enough to be heard, but the person is asleep, he has broken it.

cards.title: Permission he didn't know of
cards.ar: وإن حلف لا يكلمه إلا بإذنه فأذن له ولم يعلم بالأذن حتى كلمه حنث
cards.en: If he swears not to speak to someone without that person's permission, and permission is given but he does not know about it before speaking, he has broken it.

cards.ask: Jamal swore not to speak to Tariq without Tariq's permission. Tariq told someone "He may speak to me", but Jamal never heard this. Jamal spoke to him. What is the ruling?
options: Broken: he didn't know of the permission
Not broken, if Tariq didn't mind
cards.source: فأذن له ولم يعلم بالأذن حتى كلمه حنث
cards.why: Permission he did not know about doesn't help him, so he has broken the oath.

cards.title: The governor's oath
cards.ar: وإذا استحلف الوالي رجلا ليعلمه بكل داعر دخل البلد فهذا على حال ولايته خاصة
cards.en: If a governor makes a man swear to tell him of every da'ir (troublemaker) who comes to town, the oath lasts only while that governor is in office.

cards.ask: The governor made Hisham swear to report every troublemaker who enters the city. The governor was later removed. Must Hisham still report to him?
options: No: the oath was only for his time in office
Yes, to whoever is the new governor
cards.source: فهذا على حال ولايته خاصة
cards.why: The oath is tied to his governorship and ends with it.

cards.title: The slave's animal
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يركب دابة فلان فركب دابة عبده لم يحنث
cards.en: If he swears not to ride a certain man's animal and rides the animal of that man's slave (in al-Quduri's time), he has not broken it.

cards.title: Roof and hallway
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يدخل هذه الدار فوقف على سطحها أو دخل دهليزها حنث
cards.en: If he swears not to enter this house, and stands on its roof or enters its entrance hall, he has broken it.

cards.ask: Ayyub swore not to enter this house. He stood inside the arch of the doorway, so that if the door were shut he would be outside. What is the ruling?
options: Broken: he was in the doorway
Broken, like standing on the roof
source: وإن وقف في طاق الباب
إذا أغلق الباب كان خارجا لم يحنث
cards.why: If shutting the door would leave him outside, he has not entered, so he has not broken it.

cards.ask: Broken or not?
items: Swore not to eat this flour; ate bread made from it
Swore not to enter this house; stood on its roof
Swore not to speak to Ali; spoke to him while he slept nearby
Swore not to eat this flour; swallowed it dry
Swore not to ride Ali's animal; rode his slave's animal
source: من خبزه حنث ولو استفه كما هو لم يحنث
فوقف على سطحها أو دخل دهليزها حنث
إلا أنه نائم حنث
فركب دابة عبده لم يحنث
cards.why: Flour's bread, the roof, and speaking within hearing all break it. Dry flour and the slave's animal do not.

lessons.title: What words mean: food, agents, sitting

cards.title: Roast
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يأكل الشواء فهو على اللحم دون الباذنجان والجزر
cards.en: Words in an oath mean what people usually mean by them. "Roast" means roasted meat, not roasted aubergine or carrots.

cards.title: Cooked food
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يأكل الطبيخ فهو على ما يطبخ من اللحم
cards.en: "Cooked food" (tabikh) means meat that is cooked.

cards.ask: Yasir swore not to eat roast. At a barbecue he ate grilled aubergine. What is the ruling?
options: Broken only if he ate a lot
cards.source: فهو على اللحم دون الباذنجان والجزر
cards.why: "Roast" is about meat only, so aubergine does not break it.

cards.title: Heads
cards.ar: على ما يكبس في التنانير ويباع في المصر
cards.en: If he swears not to eat "heads", it means the heads that are baked in ovens and sold in town (like sheep's heads), not every head.

cards.title: Bread
cards.ar: على ما يعتاد أهل البلد أكله خبزا فإن أكل خبز القطائف أو خبز الأرز بالعراق لم يحنث
cards.en: "Bread" means what the people of that town normally eat as bread. So eating qata'if (a sweet pancake) or rice bread in Iraq does not break it.

cards.ask: In Iraq, Rami swore not to eat bread. He ate some rice bread. What is the ruling?
cards.source: فإن أكل خبز القطائف أو خبز الأرز بالعراق لم يحنث
cards.why: Bread means the town's usual bread, and al-Quduri names rice bread in Iraq as not counting.

cards.title: Using an agent to sell
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يبيع أو لا يشتري أولا يؤاجر فوكل بذلك لم يحنث
cards.en: If he swears not to sell, buy or rent out, and then appoints a wakil (an agent who acts for him) to do it, he has not broken the oath.

cards.title: Using an agent to marry
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يتزوج أو لا يطلق
cards.en: But if he swears not to marry, or not to divorce, or not to free a slave, and then appoints an agent to do it, he has broken it.

cards.ask: He swore not to do it, then had an agent do it. Broken or not?
items: An agent sells his car for him
An agent buys a phone for him
An agent rents out his flat for him
source: ومن حلف لا يبيع أو لا يشتري أولا يؤاجر فوكل بذلك لم يحنث
ومن حلف لا يتزوج أو لا يطلق
cards.why: For marrying and divorcing, an agent's act counts as his own. For selling, buying and renting, it does not.

cards.title: Sitting on the ground
cards.ar: ومن حلف لا يجلس على الأرض فجلس على بساط أو حصير لم يحنث
cards.en: If he swears not to sit on the ground, and sits on a carpet or a mat, he has not broken it.

cards.ask: Hadi swore not to sit on a bed. He sat on a bed with a blanket spread on it. What is the ruling?
options: Broken: it is still the bed
Not broken: he sat on the blanket
Not broken, unless the bed was his
cards.source: ومن حلف لا يجلس على سرير فجلس على سرير فوقه بساط حنث وإن جعل فوقه سريرا فجلس عليه لم يحنث
cards.why: A blanket on a bed is still sitting on the bed. Only another bed on top would change it.

cards.ask: Which of these break the oath?

options.text: Swore not to sleep on a mattress; slept on it with a sheet on top
Swore not to divorce; had an agent divorce for him
Swore not to eat roast; ate roast lamb
Swore not to sleep on a mattress; slept on another mattress laid on top
Swore not to sit on the ground; sat on a mat

source: وإن حلف لا ينام على فراش فنام عليه
وإن جعل فوقه فراشا آخر لم يحنث
ومن حلف لا يتزوج أو لا يطلق
فهو على اللحم
فجلس على بساط أو حصير لم يحنث
cards.why: A sheet doesn't change the mattress, divorce by an agent counts, and roast lamb is roast. A second mattress on top, or a mat on the ground, makes it something else.

lessons.title: In sha Allah, time words, permission
lessons.arabic: ومن حلف بيمين وقال: إن شاء الله

cards.title: Saying in sha Allah
cards.ar: ومن حلف بيمين وقال: إن شاء الله متصلا بيمينه فلا حنث عليه
