cards.en: When a right is proved and its owner asks for his debtor to be jailed, the judge does not rush to jail him. He first orders him to pay. If he refuses, he jails him.

cards.ask: The court has proved that Nabil owes Faisal 400 dirhams. Faisal says: "Jail him now!" What does the judge do first?
cards.source: لم يعجل بحبسه وأمره بدفع ما عليه فإن امتنع حبسه
cards.why: He first orders him to pay, and only jails him if he refuses.

cards.title: Which debts
cards.ar: في كل دين لزمه بدلا عن مال حصل في يده كثمن المبيع وبدل القرض أو التزمه بعقد كالمهر والكفالة
cards.en: He is jailed for any debt he owes in return for property that came into his hands, like the price of something he bought or a loan, or a debt he took on by a contract, like a mahr or a kafala (standing as guarantor for someone).

cards.title: "I am poor"
cards.ar: ولا يحبسه فيما سوى ذلك إذا قال: إني فقير إلا أن يثبت غريمه أن له مالا
cards.en: For other debts, if he says "I am poor", he is not jailed, unless the creditor proves he has money.

cards.ask: Zayd bought a horse and has not paid its price. He refuses to pay and says: "I am poor." Can he be jailed?
options: Yes: it is a debt for a horse he received
No: he says he is poor
Only if the horse has died
cards.source: في كل دين لزمه بدلا عن مال حصل في يده كثمن المبيع
cards.why: The price of a thing he bought is a debt for property he received, so he can be jailed.

cards.title: How long
cards.ar: ويحبسه شهرين أو ثلاثة ثم يسأل عنه فإن لم يظهر له مال خلى سبيله ولا يحول بينه وبين غرمائه
cards.en: He jails him for two or three months, then asks about him. If no money of his comes to light, he lets him go. But he does not stop his creditors from following him to get their money.

cards.ask: How long is he jailed before the judge asks about him? Complete it.
cards.ar: ويحبسه ____ ثم يسأل عنه
cards.source: ويحبسه شهرين أو ثلاثة ثم يسأل عنه
cards.why: شهرين أو ثلاثة: two or three months, then the judge asks about him.

cards.title: A wife's keep, and a father
cards.ar: ويحبس الرجل في نفقة زوجته ولا يحبس والد في دين ولده إلا إذا امتنع من الإنفاق عليه
cards.en: A man can be jailed for not paying his wife's nafaqa (her food, clothing and housing). A father is not jailed for a debt he owes his child, unless he refuses to spend on the child's keep.

cards.ask: Ibrahim borrowed 1,000 dirhams from his grown-up son and has not paid it back. Can the son have him jailed for it?
options: No: a father is not jailed for a debt to his child
cards.source: ولا يحبس والد في دين ولده
cards.why: A father is not jailed for a debt to his child. Only refusing to spend on the child's keep would change that.

cards.ask: Which are true?

options.text: A man can be jailed for not paying his wife's nafaqa
After release, the creditors may still follow him
The judge orders payment before jailing
A debtor who says "I am poor" is always freed
He stays in jail until he dies if no money is found

source: ويحبس الرجل في نفقة زوجته
ولا يحول بينه وبين غرمائه
وأمره بدفع ما عليه
فإن لم يظهر له مال خلى سبيله
cards.why: Nafaqa can bring jail, payment is ordered first, and creditors may follow him after release. If no money appears he is let go, not kept forever.

lessons.title: Women judges, letters between judges, deputies

cards.title: A woman as judge
cards.ar: ويجوز قضاء المرأة في كل شيء إلا في الحدود والقصاص
cards.en: A woman may judge in everything except hudud and qisas.

cards.ask: Judge Khadija hears a dispute about the sale of a house. Is her ruling valid?
options: Yes: a woman may judge except in hudud and qisas
Only if a man agrees with her
cards.source: ويجوز قضاء المرأة في كل شيء إلا في الحدود والقصاص
cards.why: A woman may judge in everything except hudud and qisas, so her ruling on a sale is valid.

cards.title: A letter from one judge to another
cards.ar: ويقبل كتاب القاضي إلى القاضي في الحقوق إذا شهد به عنده فإن شهدوا على خصم حكم بالشهادة وكتب بحكمه وإن شهدوا بغير حضرة خصم لم يحكم وكتب بالشهادة ليحكم بها المكتوب إليه
cards.en: When witnesses testify before a judge about a right, he can write to a judge in another town. If they testified with the opponent present, he rules and writes his ruling. If the opponent was not there, he does not rule, but writes down the testimony so the judge who receives the letter can rule on it.

cards.title: Witnesses to the letter
cards.ar: ولا يقبل الكتاب إلا بشهادة رجلين أو رجل وامرأتين
cards.en: The letter is only accepted with two men, or a man and two women, as witnesses. The judge reads it to them, seals it before them and hands it over. The receiving judge accepts it only with the opponent present; then he opens it, reads it to him and makes him do what it says.

cards.ask: Put the journey of a judge's letter in order.
steps: The judge reads the letter to the witnesses
He seals it in front of them
They testify to the other judge, with the opponent present
The other judge opens it and reads it to the opponent
cards.source: ويجب أن يقرأ الكتاب عليهم ليعوفوا ما فيه ثم يختمه بحضرتهم ويسلمه إليهم فإذا وصل إلى القاضي لم يقبله إلا بحضرة الخصم فإن شهدوا أنه كتاب فلان القاضي سلمه إلينا في مجلس حكمه وقرأه علينا وختمه فضه القاضي وقرأه على الخصم وألزمه ما فيه
cards.why: He reads it to them, seals it, hands it over; they testify before the other judge with the opponent there; then he opens and reads it.

cards.title: Not in hudud, and deputies
cards.ar: ولا يقبل كتاب القاضي إلى القاضي في الحدود والقصاص وليس للقاضي أن يستخلف على القضاء إلا أن يفوض ذلك إليه
cards.en: A judge's letter is not accepted in hudud and qisas. And a judge may not appoint a deputy to judge in his place, unless the ruler gave him that power.

cards.ask: Judge Salih wants to travel and appoints his student to judge while he is away. The ruler never gave him the power to do this. Is it allowed?
options: No: he was not given that power
Yes: a judge may always appoint a deputy
Yes, if the student is learned
cards.source: وليس للقاضي أن يستخلف على القضاء إلا أن يفوض ذلك إليه
cards.why: A judge may not appoint a deputy unless that power was given to him.

cards.title: Another judge's ruling, and an absent party
cards.ar: وإذا رفع القاضي حكم حاكم أمضاه إلا أن يخالف الكتاب أو السنة أو الإجماع أو يكون قولا لا دليل عليه ولا يقضي القاضي على غائب إلا أن يحضر من يقوم مقامه
cards.en: When another judge's ruling is brought to a judge, he carries it out, unless it goes against the Qur'an, the Sunna or ijma' (the agreement of the scholars), or is a view with no evidence at all. And a judge does not rule against someone absent, unless someone who stands in his place is present.

cards.ask: A ruling by an earlier judge is brought to Judge Anas. It clearly goes against the ijma'. What does Anas do?
options: He does not carry it out
He must carry it out anyway
He sends it back to the earlier judge
cards.source: إلا أن يخالف الكتاب أو السنة أو الإجماع
cards.why: A judge carries out another's ruling unless it goes against the Qur'an, the Sunna or ijma'.

cards.ask: Can a judge's letter be accepted for this?
source: ويقبل كتاب القاضي إلى القاضي في الحقوق
ولا يقبل كتاب القاضي إلى القاضي في الحدود والقصاص
cards.why: Letters are accepted for rights such as debts and prices, but not for hudud and qisas.

cards.title: Two people choose a judge
cards.ar: وإذا حكم رجلان رجلا ليحكم بينهما ورضيا بحكمه جاز إذا كان بصفة الحاكم
cards.en: Tahkim means two people choose a man to judge between them (an arbiter) and agree to his ruling. It is allowed if he has the qualities of a judge.

cards.title: Who cannot be an arbiter
cards.ar: ولا يجوز تحكيم الكافر والعبد والذمي والمحدود في القذف والفاسق والصبي
cards.en: These may not be chosen as arbiter: a kafir (non-Muslim), a slave (in al-Quduri's time), a dhimmi, one given the hadd for qadhf, a fasiq (an openly sinful person), and a child.

cards.ask: Two Muslims want to choose an arbiter. Whom may they NOT choose?

options.text: A 12-year-old boy
A man known for open sins
A man punished for qadhf
An upright, free, adult Muslim man

cards.source: ولا يجوز تحكيم الكافر والعبد والذمي والمحدود في القذف والفاسق والصبي
cards.why: A child, a fasiq and one punished for qadhf cannot be arbiters. An upright, free, adult Muslim can.

cards.title: Pulling out, and the judge's review
cards.ar: ولكل واحد من المحكمين أن يرجع ما لم يحكم عليهما فإذا حكم لزمهما وإذا رفع حكمه إلى القاضي فوافق مذهبه أمضاه وإن خالفه أبطله
cards.en: Either of the two may pull out until the arbiter has ruled. Once he rules, it binds them both. If his ruling is brought to the judge, the judge carries it out if it agrees with his own view, and cancels it if not.

cards.ask: Ali and Hasan choose Umar to settle their dispute. Before Umar rules, Hasan says: "I don't want this any more." May he pull out?
options: No: once chosen, it is final
cards.source: ولكل واحد من المحكمين أن يرجع ما لم يحكم عليهما
cards.why: Each may pull out as long as the arbiter has not yet ruled.

cards.ask: Umar ruled between Ali and Hasan. The ruling is then brought to the judge, whose own view is different. What does the judge do?
cards.source: وإن خالفه أبطله
cards.why: If the arbiter's ruling goes against the judge's view, the judge cancels it.

cards.title: Not in hudud, qisas, or the 'aqila
cards.ar: ولا يجوز التحكيم في الحدود والقصاص وإن حكما في دم خطإ فقضى الحاكم على العاقلة بالدية لم ينفذ حكمه
cards.en: Arbitration is not allowed in hudud and qisas. If two people choose an arbiter over an accidental killing and he makes the 'aqila (the relatives who share in paying blood money) pay the diya, his ruling does not take effect.

cards.ask: After an accidental killing, the two sides choose an arbiter, who rules that the killer's 'aqila must pay the diya. Does this ruling take effect?
options: No: his ruling against the 'aqila does not take effect
Yes, since both sides chose him
Yes, if the diya is small
cards.source: فقضى الحاكم على العاقلة بالدية لم ينفذ حكمه
cards.why: His ruling against the 'aqila does not take effect.

cards.title: Proof and refusing an oath
cards.ar: ويجوز أن يسمع البينة ويقضي بالنكول
cards.en: The arbiter may hear proof from witnesses, and may rule on nukul (when the person who should swear an oath refuses to).

cards.title: Ruling for his own family
cards.ar: وحكم الحاكم لأبويه وولده وزوجته باطل
cards.en: A ruling by the arbiter in favour of his own parents, child or wife is void.

cards.ask: Two neighbours choose Salman as arbiter. One of them is Salman's wife, and he rules in her favour. What is the ruling?
options: Valid if he swears he was fair
cards.source: وحكم الحاكم لأبويه وولده وزوجته باطل
cards.why: A ruling for his wife is void.

cards.ask: Can this be settled by an arbiter?
source: ولا يجوز التحكيم في الحدود والقصاص
فقضى الحاكم على العاقلة بالدية لم ينفذ حكمه
وإذا حكم رجلان رجلا ليحكم بينهما ورضيا بحكمه جاز
cards.why: Money disputes like sales and debts can go to an arbiter. Hudud, qisas and the 'aqila's diya cannot.

lessons.title: The divider, and dividing inherited land

cards.title: A divider for the people
cards.ar: ينبغي للإمام أن ينصب قاسما
cards.en: Qisma means dividing shared property between its owners. The imam (ruler) should appoint a qasim (divider), paid from the bayt al-mal (public treasury), to divide between people free of charge. If he does not, he appoints a divider who takes a fee.

cards.title: What the divider must be
cards.ar: ويجب أن يكون عدلا مأمونا عالما بالقسمة ولا يجبر القاضي الناس على قاسم واحد ولا يترك القسام يشتركون
cards.en: The divider must be upright, trustworthy and know how to divide. The judge does not force people to use only one divider, and he does not let the dividers join together (so they could not push up their fees).

cards.ask: Which are true about the divider?

options.text: He must be upright and trustworthy
He must know how to divide
If not paid by the treasury, he may take a fee
Everyone must use the same one divider
The dividers should join together

source: ويجب أن يكون عدلا مأمونا عالما بالقسمة
فإن لم يفعل نصب قاسما بالأجرة
ولا يجبر القاضي الناس على قاسم واحد ولا يترك القسام يشتركون
cards.why: He must be upright, trustworthy and skilled, and may be paid a fee. People are not forced onto one divider, and dividers may not join together.

cards.ask: The judge tells the town: "Only Hamid may divide your land, no one else." Is this right?
options: Yes: the judge picks the divider
cards.source: ولا يجبر القاضي الناس على قاسم واحد
cards.why: The judge does not force people to use one divider.

cards.title: Who pays the fee
cards.ar: وأجر القسمة على عدد الرؤوس عند أبي حنيفة وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد: على قدر الأنصاء
cards.en: Abu Hanifa says the divider's fee is shared by head: each partner pays the same. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say each pays by the size of his share.

cards.ask: Two partners share a field: one owns three quarters, the other a quarter. As al-Quduri gives Abu Hanifa's ruling, how is the divider's fee paid?
options: The bigger owner pays it all
The one who asked pays it all
cards.source: وأجر القسمة على عدد الرؤوس عند أبي حنيفة
cards.why: Abu Hanifa makes the fee shared by head: each partner pays the same.

cards.title: Inherited land: Abu Hanifa asks for proof
cards.ar: لم يقسمها عند أبي حنيفة حتى يقيموا
cards.en: If partners holding a house or farmland say they inherited it from someone, Abu Hanifa says the judge does not divide it until they prove his death and the number of heirs. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say he divides it on their word, and records that he did so.

cards.title: Other cases
cards.ar: وإذا كان المال المشترك ما سوى العقار وادعوا أنه ميراث قسمه في قولهم جميعا وإن ادعوا في العقار اشتروه قسمه بينهم وإن ادعوا الملك ولم يذكروا كيف انتقل قسمه بينهم
cards.en: 'Aqar means land and buildings. If the shared property is not 'aqar and they say it is inherited, the judge divides it, by all three scholars. If they say they bought the 'aqar, he divides it. If they just say they own it, without saying how it came to them, he divides it too.

cards.ask: Three brothers bring 60 sheep and say they inherited them from their father. They ask the judge to divide them. What does he do?
options: Refuses until they prove the death and the heirs
cards.source: وإذا كان المال المشترك ما سوى العقار وادعوا أنه ميراث قسمه في قولهم جميعا
cards.why: Sheep are not 'aqar, so all three scholars agree he divides them.

cards.ask: Two friends say: "We bought this house together." They ask the judge to divide it. What does he do?
options: Asks for proof of a death
cards.source: وإن ادعوا في العقار اشتروه قسمه بينهم
cards.why: If they say they bought the 'aqar, he divides it between them.

cards.ask: Partners hold a piece of land. They say "It is ours" but do not say how they got it. What does the judge do?
cards.source: وإن ادعوا الملك ولم يذكروا كيف انتقل قسمه بينهم
cards.why: If they claim ownership without saying how it came to them, he divides it.

cards.title: When each can use his share
cards.ar: وإذا كان كل واحد من الشركاء ينتفع بنصيبه قسم بطلب أحدهم
cards.en: If every partner can still make use of his share after dividing, the property is divided when any one of them asks.

cards.title: When a small share is useless
cards.ar: وإن كان أحدهم ينتفع والآخر يستضر لقلة نصيبه فإن طلب صاحب الكثير قسم وإن طلب صاحب القليل لم يقسم وإن كان كل واحد يستضر لم يقسمها إلا بتراضيها
cards.en: If one can use his share but the other is harmed because his share is too small to use, then: if the owner of the big share asks, it is divided; if the owner of the small share asks, it is not. If dividing harms every one of them, it is only divided if they all agree.

cards.ask: Bilal owns one tenth of a small shop, and Ahmad owns the rest. Bilal's tenth would be useless on its own. Bilal asks for the shop to be divided. Is it?
options: No: the owner of the small share asked
Only if Ahmad pays a fee
cards.source: وإن طلب صاحب القليل لم يقسم
cards.why: When the owner of the small share asks, it is not divided.

cards.ask: Same shop: this time Ahmad, who owns nine tenths, asks for it to be divided. Is it?
options: Yes: the owner of the big share asked
No: Bilal's tenth would be useless
cards.source: فإن طلب صاحب الكثير قسم
cards.why: When the owner of the big share asks, it is divided.

cards.title: Goods of one kind
cards.ar: ويقسم العروض إذا كانت من صنف واحد ولا يقسم الجنسان بعضهما في بعض
cards.en: 'Urud (goods) are divided when they are all of one kind. Two different kinds are not divided one against the other (for example, all the wheat to one and all the cloth to the other).

cards.title: Slaves, jewels, bathhouses, wells and mills
cards.ar: وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد: يقسم الرقيق ولا يقسم حمام ولا بئر ولا رحى إلا أن يتراضى الشركاء
cards.en: A bathhouse, a well or a mill is not divided unless the partners all agree. Note: Abu Hanifa says slaves (in his time) and jewels are not divided, as they differ so much; Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say slaves are divided.

cards.ask: How can this shared property be divided?
items: A big field where every share is still useful
A heap of wheat of one kind
source: وإذا كان كل واحد من الشركاء ينتفع بنصيبه قسم بطلب أحدهم
ولا يقسم حمام ولا بئر ولا رحى إلا أن يتراضى الشركاء
ويقسم العروض إذا كانت من صنف واحد
cards.why: Things every partner can still use, and goods of one kind, are divided on request. A well, a bathhouse and a mill need everyone's agreement.

cards.title: An absent heir
cards.ar: وإذا حضر وارثان وأقاما البينة على الوفاة وعدد الورثة والدار في أيديهم ومعهم وارث غائب قسمها القاضي بطلب الحاضرين وينصب للغائب وكيلا يقبض نصيبه
cards.en: If two heirs come with proof of the death and the number of heirs, and the house is in their hands, but another heir is away, the judge divides it when the present heirs ask. He appoints a wakil (agent) to take the absent heir's share for him.

cards.title: Buyers, and one heir alone
cards.ar: وإن كانوا مشترين لم يقسم مع غيبة أحدهم وإن كان العقار في يد الوارث الغائب لم يقسم وإن حضر وارث واحد لم يقسم
cards.en: If they are buyers, not heirs, it is not divided while one of them is away. And it is not divided if the land is in the absent heir's hands, or if only one heir comes.

cards.ask: Two of three heirs come with proof of their father's death and the number of heirs. The house is in their hands; the third heir is abroad. What does the judge do?
options: Divides it; an agent takes his share
Waits until the third heir returns
Gives the whole house to the two of them
cards.source: قسمها القاضي بطلب الحاضرين وينصب للغائب وكيلا يقبض نصيبه
cards.why: He divides it at the present heirs' request and appoints an agent to take the absent one's share.

cards.ask: Three men bought a house together. One is away on a journey. The other two ask the judge to divide it. What does he do?
options: Divides it between the two present
cards.source: وإن كانوا مشترين لم يقسم مع غيبة أحدهم
cards.why: For buyers, the judge does not divide while one of them is absent.

lessons.title: How the divider divides
lessons.arabic: وينبغي للقاسم: أن يصور ما يقسمه

cards.title: Several houses
cards.ar: وإذا كانت دور مشتركة في مصر واحد قسمت كل دار على حدتها في قول أبي حنيفة رحمه الله وقالا: إن كان الأصلح لهم قسمة بعضها في بعض قسمها
cards.en: If partners share several houses in one town, Abu Hanifa says each house is divided on its own. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say that if it is better for the partners, some houses may be given against others.

cards.title: A house and a shop
cards.ar: وإن كانت دار وضيعة أو دار وحانوت قسم كل واحد على حدته
cards.en: If they share a house and farmland, or a house and a shop, each one is divided on its own.

cards.ask: Two sisters share a house and a shop. One says: "I'll take the house, you take the shop." How does the divider divide them?
options: Each one is divided on its own
House to one sister, shop to the other
He sells both and splits the money
cards.source: أو دار وحانوت قسم كل واحد على حدته
cards.why: A house and a shop are each divided on their own.

cards.title: Drawing, measuring and separating
cards.ar: وينبغي للقاسم: أن يصور ما يقسمه ويعدله ويذرعه ويقوم البناء ويفرز كل نصيب عن الباقي بطريقة وشربه حتى لا يكون لنصيب بعضهم بنصيب الآخر تعلق
cards.en: The divider should draw a plan of what he divides, make the shares equal, measure it, value the buildings, and separate each share with its own path and water supply, so that no share depends on another.

cards.title: Naming the shares and drawing lots
cards.ar: والذي يليه بالثاني والثالث وعلى هذا ثم يخرج القرعة فمن خرج اسمه أولا فله السهم الأول ومن خرج ثانيا فله السهم الثاني
cards.en: Then he names one share "the first", the next "the second", then "the third", and so on. Then he draws lots (qur'a): whoever's name comes out first gets the first share, and whoever's comes out second gets the second.

cards.ask: Put the divider's work in order.
steps: Draw a plan of the land
Measure it and value the buildings
Separate each share with its own path and water
Name the shares first, second, third
source: أن يصور ما يقسمه ويعدله ويذرعه ويقوم البناء ويفرز كل نصيب عن الباقي بطريقة وشربه
ثم يلقب نصيبا بالأول
ثم يخرج القرعة
cards.why: He draws, measures and values, separates each share, names the shares, and finally draws lots.

cards.title: No money added
cards.ar: ولا يدخل في القسمة الدراهم والدنانير إلا بتراضيهم
cards.en: Dirhams and dinars (money) are not added into the division to even out the shares, unless the partners all agree.

cards.title: A path or water channel through another's share
cards.ar: أو طريق لم يشترط في القسمة: فإن أمكن صرف الطريق والمسيل عنه فليس له أن يستطرق ويسيل في نصيب الآخر وإن لم يمكن فسخت القسمة
cards.en: After dividing, one partner may find his water channel or path runs through the other's share, and this was not agreed in the division. If the path or channel can be moved away, he may not use the other's share for it. If it cannot be moved, the division is cancelled.

cards.ask: After dividing, Kamil's only path to the street runs through Nasir's share. Nothing was agreed about it, and there is no other way to make a path. What happens?
cards.source: وإن لم يمكن فسخت القسمة
cards.why: If the path cannot be moved away, the division is cancelled.

cards.title: Upper and lower floors
cards.ar: وإن كان سفل لا علو له وعلو لا سفل له وسفل له علو قوم كل واحد على حدته وقسم بالقيمة ولا معتبر بغير ذلك
cards.en: If there is a ground floor with nothing above it, an upper floor with nothing below it (owned without the ground floor), and a ground floor with an upper floor on it, each is valued on its own and they are divided by value. Nothing else counts.

cards.ask: The shares are not quite equal, so the divider decides to give one partner some extra dirhams to balance them. The partners did not agree to this. Is it allowed?
options: Yes: it makes the shares fair
cards.source: ولا يدخل في القسمة الدراهم والدنانير إلا بتراضيهم
cards.why: Money is only brought into a division if the partners all agree.

cards.title: The dividers as witnesses
cards.ar: وإذا اختلف المتقاسمون فشهد القاسمان قبلت شهادتهما
cards.en: If the partners disagree about the division and the two dividers testify about it, their testimony is accepted.

cards.ask: After dividing, Habib and Murad argue about where the line between their shares is. The two men who did the dividing testify about it. Is their testimony accepted?
options: Yes: the dividers' testimony is accepted
No: they did the job, so they cannot testify
Only if they took no fee
cards.source: فشهد القاسمان قبلت شهادتهما
cards.why: The two dividers' testimony is accepted.

cards.title: Claiming a mistake after receiving
cards.ar: فإن ادعى أحدهما الغلط وزعم أن مما أصابه شيئا في يد صاحبه وقد أشهد على نفسه بالاستيفاء لم يصدق على ذلك إلا ببينة
cards.en: If one claims there was a mistake, saying part of what he should have got is in his partner's hands, but he already had it witnessed that he received his full share, he is not believed without proof.

cards.title: "I received it all", then "only some"
cards.ar: وإن قال: استوفيت حقي ثم قال: أخذت بعضه فالقول قول خصمه مع يمينه
cards.en: If he said "I received my full right" and later says "I only took some of it", then his partner's word counts, with his oath.

cards.ask: Yunus said: "I have received my whole share." A week later he says: "Actually I only got part of it." His partner denies this. Whose word counts?
cards.source: فالقول قول خصمه مع يمينه
cards.why: After saying he received his full right, the partner's word counts, with his oath.

cards.title: Both swear, and it is cancelled
cards.ar: ولم يشهد على نفسه بالاستيفاء وكذبه شريكه تحالفا وفسخت القسمة
cards.en: If he says "My share reaches as far as this spot, but you did not hand it to me", and he never had it witnessed that he received his share, and his partner says he is lying, then they both swear (tahaluf) and the division is cancelled.

cards.ask: Rami says: "My share goes up to the palm tree, but you never gave me that strip." He never declared that he received his share. His partner says he is wrong. What happens?
options: Both swear; the division is undone
Rami gets the strip on his word
The partner keeps it without an oath
cards.source: تحالفا وفسخت القسمة
cards.why: Without a declaration of receiving, and with the partner denying, both swear and the division is cancelled.

cards.title: When part of a share turns out to belong to someone else
cards.ar: وإن استحق بعض نصيب أحدهما بعينه لم تفسخ القسمة عند أبي حنيفة ورجع بحصة ذلك من
cards.en: If a specific part of one partner's share turns out to belong to someone else, Abu Hanifa says the division is not cancelled: he claims back the matching amount from his partner's share. Note: Abu Yusuf says the division is cancelled.

cards.ask: After the division, what happens?
items: He declared he received it all, then claims a mistake
He said "I got my full right", then "only some"
He never declared receiving, says a strip was not handed over, partner denies
source: وقد أشهد على نفسه بالاستيفاء لم يصدق على ذلك إلا ببينة
فالقول قول خصمه مع يمينه
تحالفا وفسخت القسمة
cards.why: A declared receipt needs proof to undo; "all" then "some" goes to the partner's oath; no declaration plus denial means both swear and it is cancelled.

cards.ask: Hakim had it witnessed that he received his full share. Now he says a room that should be his is in his partner's hands, but he has no witnesses. Is he believed?
options: Yes: both swear and it is cancelled
cards.source: لم يصدق على ذلك إلا ببينة
cards.why: Since he declared he received his share, he is not believed without proof.

cards.title: What counts as coercion
cards.ar: الإكراه يثبت حكمه إذا حصل ممن يقدر على إيقاع ما توعد به سلطانا كان أو لصا
cards.en: Ikrah (coercion) means forcing someone with threats. It has its rulings when it comes from someone able to carry out his threat, whether he is a ruler or a robber.

cards.ask: A robber holding a knife, who could easily use it, tells Adam: "Sign this or I'll kill you." Does this count as coercion?
options: Yes: he can carry it out
No: he has not hurt Adam yet
No: a robber's threats do not count
cards.source: ممن يقدر على إيقاع ما توعد به سلطانا كان أو لصا
cards.why: Coercion counts when the threat comes from someone able to carry it out, ruler or robber.

cards.title: Forced to sell, buy, admit or rent
cards.ar: وإذا أكره الرجل على بيع ماله أو على شراء سلعة أو على أن يقر لرجل بألف أو يؤاجر داره - وأكره على ذلك بالقتل أو بالضرب الشديد أو بالحبس المديد
cards.en: Say a man is forced to sell his property, buy goods, admit he owes someone 1,000, or rent out his house, and the threat is killing, a severe beating or a long imprisonment.

cards.title: He has the choice
cards.ar: فباع أو اشترى فهو بالخيار: إن شاء أمضى البيع وإن شاء فسخه
cards.en: If he sold or bought under that threat, he has the choice (khiyar): he may let the sale stand, or cancel it.

cards.ask: Under threat of a severe beating, Rafiq sold his house to Jalal. Later he is safe. What is the sale's status?
options: Rafiq chooses: keep it or cancel it
It is final and cannot be undone
It is void and nothing can make it valid
cards.source: فهو بالخيار: إن شاء أمضى البيع وإن شاء فسخه
cards.why: A coerced seller has the choice to let the sale stand or cancel it.

cards.ask: In the book's words, which threats make a forced sale coercion?

options.text: A threat to kill him
A threat of a severe beating
A threat of long imprisonment
"I'll be upset with you"
"I won't invite you to dinner"

cards.source: وأكره على ذلك بالقتل أو بالضرب الشديد أو بالحبس المديد
cards.why: The book names killing, a severe beating and long imprisonment. Being upset or not inviting him are not threats of harm.

cards.title: Taking the price
cards.ar: وإن كان قبض الثمن طوعا فقد أجاز البيع وإن كان قبضه مكرها فليس بإجازة وعليه رده إن كان قائما في يده
cards.en: If he later takes the price willingly, he has approved the sale. If he was forced to take it too, that is not approval, and if he cancels he must give the price back, if he still has it.

cards.ask: Rafiq was forced to sell his house. A month later, free and safe, he happily collects the price from the buyer. Can he still cancel the sale?
options: Yes, if he returns half the price
cards.source: وإن كان قبض الثمن طوعا فقد أجاز البيع
cards.why: Taking the price willingly counts as approving the sale.

cards.title: If the item is destroyed
cards.ar: وإن هلك المبيع في يد المشتري وهو غير مكره ضمن قيمته وللمكره أن يضمن المكره إن شاء
cards.en: If the thing sold is destroyed while with the buyer, and the buyer was not forced, the buyer pays its value. And the one who was forced may, if he wishes, make the one who forced him pay instead.

cards.ask: Sami was forced to sell his camel. The buyer, who was not forced, has it, and it dies. Sami cancels the sale. Who can Sami claim the camel's value from?
options: Only the judge who heard it
source: وإن هلك المبيع في يد المشتري وهو غير مكره ضمن قيمته
وللمكره أن يضمن المكره إن شاء
cards.why: The willing buyer owes its value, and the forced seller may choose to claim from the coercer instead.

cards.ask: A ruler threatens to imprison Tahir for years unless he admits he owes Fadi 1,000 dirhams. Tahir admits it. What does this coerced admission count as?
cards.source: أو على أن يقر لرجل بألف
cards.why: Being forced to admit a debt under threat of long imprisonment is coercion like being forced to sell.

lessons.title: Forced to eat the forbidden, or to say words of kufr
lessons.arabic: ومن أكره على أن يأكل الميتة

cards.title: Carrion and wine
cards.ar: ومن أكره على أن يأكل الميتة أو يشرب الخمر - وأكره على ذلك بحبس أو ضرب أو يد لم يحل له إلا أن يكره بما يخاف منه على نفسه أو على عضو من أعضائه
cards.en: If someone is forced to eat mayta (meat of an animal that died without proper slaughter) or drink wine, with a threat of prison or a beating, it is still not allowed for him, unless the threat makes him fear for his life or for a limb.

cards.title: Then he must not hold out
cards.ar: فإذا خاف ذلك وسعه أن يقدم على ما أكره عليه ولا يسعه أن يصبر على ما توعد به فإن صبر حتى أوقعوا به ولم يأكل فهو آثم
cards.en: If he fears that, he may do what he is forced to, and he may not hold out against the threat. If he holds out until they carry it out and he did not eat, he is sinful.

cards.ask: Captors tell Harun: "Eat this carrion or we will kill you", and he truly fears they will. He refuses, and they harm him. What is his position?
cards.source: فإن صبر حتى أوقعوا به ولم يأكل فهو آثم
cards.why: When he fears for his life, he must eat. Holding out until they harm him is a sin.

cards.ask: Harun is threatened only with a short spell in prison unless he drinks wine. Is it allowed for him to drink?
options: No: only fear for his life or a limb allows it
Yes: any threat makes it allowed
cards.source: بحبس أو ضرب أو يد لم يحل له إلا أن يكره بما يخاف منه على نفسه أو على عضو من أعضائه
cards.why: Prison or a beating is not enough; only fear for his life or a limb makes it allowed.

cards.title: Forced to say words of kufr
cards.ar: وإن أكره على الكفر بالله عز وجل أو سب النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام: بقيد أو حبس أو ضرب لم يكن ذلك إكراها حتى يكره بأمر يخاف منه على نفسه أو على عضو من أعضائه
cards.en: Kufr means disbelief. If someone is forced to say words of kufr, or to insult the Prophet, peace be upon him, with chains, prison or a beating, that is not coercion, until he is threatened with something that makes him fear for his life or a limb.

cards.title: His heart at peace with faith
cards.ar: فإذا خاف ذلك وسعه أن يظهر ما أمروه به ويوري فإذا أظهر ذلك وقلبه مطمئن بالإيمان فلا إثم عليه وإن صبر حتى قتل ولم يظهر الكفر ذلك كان مأجورا
cards.en: If he fears that, he may say outwardly what they order, while meaning something else in his mind (tawriya). If he says it while his heart is at peace with iman (faith), he has no sin. But if he holds firm until he is killed and does not say the words of kufr, he is rewarded.

cards.ask: Under a real threat of death, Yahya says the words of kufr his captors demand, while his heart stays firm in faith. Is he sinful?
options: No: his heart stayed firm in faith
Yes: the words of kufr are a sin
Only if he does not repeat his shahada later
cards.source: فإذا أظهر ذلك وقلبه مطمئن بالإيمان فلا إثم عليه
cards.why: If he says it while his heart is at peace with faith, there is no sin on him.

cards.ask: Under a real threat of death, he holds firm and is harmed. Is he sinful or rewarded?
items: He refused to say words of kufr, and was killed
source: فإن صبر حتى أوقعوا به ولم يأكل فهو آثم
وإن صبر حتى قتل ولم يظهر الكفر ذلك كان مأجورا
cards.why: Holding out over food or drink is a sin. Holding firm against words of kufr until killed is rewarded.

lessons.title: Forced to destroy, kill, divorce or free

cards.title: Destroying someone's property
cards.ar: وإن أكره على إتلاف مال مسلم لأمر يخاف منه على نفسه أو على عضو من أعضائه وسعه أن يفعل ذلك ولصاحب المال أن يضمن المكره
cards.en: If someone is forced, with a threat that makes him fear for his life or a limb, to destroy a Muslim's property, he may do it. The owner of the property can make the one who forced him pay.

cards.ask: Under a real threat of death, Wasim is forced by a gang leader to smash Karim's shop window. Who does Karim claim the damage from?
cards.source: ولصاحب المال أن يضمن المكره
cards.why: The owner may make the one who did the forcing pay.

cards.title: Forced to kill
cards.ar: وإن أكره بقتل على قتل لم يسعه أن يقدم عليه ويصبر حتى يقتل فإن قتله كان آثما والقصاص على الذي أكرهه إن كان القتل عمدا
cards.en: If someone is threatened with death unless he kills another person, he may not do it. He must hold out, even until he is killed. If he does kill, he is sinful, and the qisas falls on the one who forced him, if the killing was deliberate.

cards.ask: A tyrant tells Hamid: "Kill this man, or I will kill you." What must Hamid do?
options: Refuse, even if he is killed
Kill the man, since his own life is threatened
Kill him, but pay diya afterwards
cards.source: لم يسعه أن يقدم عليه ويصبر حتى يقتل
cards.why: Being forced by death threats never makes killing another person allowed. He must hold out.

cards.title: Divorce and freeing under coercion
cards.ar: وإن أكرهه على طلاق امرأته أو أعتق عبده ففعل وقع ما أكره عليه ويرجع على الذي أكرهه بقيمة العبد وبنصف مهر المرأة إن كان الطلاق قبل الدخول
cards.en: If he is forced to divorce his wife, or (in al-Quduri's time) to free his slave, and he does it, it takes effect. He then claims from the one who forced him the slave's value, and half the mahr if the divorce was before consummation.

cards.ask: Murad is forced to divorce his wife before the marriage was consummated. Her mahr is 4,000 dirhams. How much can he claim from the man who forced him?
options: Nothing: the divorce did not happen
cards.source: وبنصف مهر المرأة إن كان الطلاق قبل الدخول
cards.why: The divorce happens, and he claims half the mahr: half of 4,000 is 2,000.

cards.title: Zina under coercion
cards.ar: وإن أكرهه على الزنا وجب عليه الحد عند أبي حنيفة إلا أن يكرهه السلطان
cards.en: If a man is forced into zina, Abu Hanifa says the hadd is due on him, unless it was the ruler who forced him. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say the hadd is not due.

cards.title: Forced to leave Islam
cards.ar: وإذا أكره على الردة لم تبن امرأته منه
cards.en: Ridda means leaving Islam. If a man is forced into words of ridda, his wife is not separated from him.

cards.ask: Under a real threat of death, Ziyad is forced to say words of ridda, while his heart stays firm in faith. What happens to his marriage?
cards.source: وإذا أكره على الردة لم تبن امرأته منه
cards.why: Coerced ridda does not separate a man from his wife.

lessons.title: Jihad: a duty on the community

cards.title: A shared duty
cards.ar: الجهاد فرض على الكفاية إذا قام به فريق من الناس سقط عن الباقين وإن لم يقم به أحد أثم جميع الناس بتركه
cards.en: Kitab al-Siyar is the classical law of war and of the Muslim state, as al-Quduri wrote it. Jihad here means fighting in a war led by the Muslim ruler. It is fard kifaya (a duty on the community as a whole): if enough people carry it out, the rest are free of it. If nobody does, everyone is sinful.

cards.ask: What kind of duty is jihad? Complete it.
cards.ar: الجهاد فرض ____
cards.source: الجهاد فرض على الكفاية
cards.why: على الكفاية: it is a duty on the community, so when some carry it out the rest are free of it.

cards.ask: The ruler has sent an army that is enough for the task. Hamza, a farmer, stays at home on his farm. Is he sinful?
options: No: a group is doing it, so he is free
Yes: every man must go every time
Yes, unless he pays someone to go in his place
cards.source: إذا قام به فريق من الناس سقط عن الباقين
cards.why: A group is doing it, so the duty has dropped from Hamza and the others.

cards.title: Fighting the enemy state
cards.ar: وقتال الكفار واجب وإن لم يبدؤونا
cards.en: In this classical law of states at war, fighting the enemy (the non-Muslim lands at war with the Muslim state) is a duty on the community, even if they did not start the fighting.

cards.title: Who it is not on
cards.ar: ولا يجب الجهاد على صبي ولا عبد ولا امرأة ولا أعمى ولا مقعد ولا أقطع
cards.en: Jihad is not required of a child, a woman, a blind person, someone who cannot walk (muq'ad), or someone missing a hand or foot (aqta'). In al-Quduri's time there were also slaves, and it was not required of a slave either.

cards.ask: In normal times, who is jihad NOT required of?

options.text: A 12-year-old boy
A woman
A healthy, free adult man
A blind man
A man who cannot walk

cards.source: ولا يجب الجهاد على صبي ولا عبد ولا امرأة ولا أعمى ولا مقعد ولا أقطع
cards.why: The book lists the child, the slave, the woman, the blind, the one who cannot walk and the one missing a limb. A healthy free adult man is not on the list.

cards.title: When the enemy attacks a town
cards.ar: وإن هجم العدو على بلد وجب على جميع المسلمين الدفع تخرج المرأة بغير إذن زوجها والعبد بغير إذن المولى
cards.en: If an enemy attacks a town, defending it becomes a duty on all the Muslims there. A woman goes out without needing her husband's permission, and in al-Quduri's time a slave went out without his master's permission.

cards.ask: An enemy army attacks the town where Aisha lives. Her husband is away and cannot be asked. Does she need his permission to help defend it?
options: No: in an attack she goes without it
Yes: a wife always needs his permission
cards.source: تخرج المرأة بغير إذن زوجها
cards.why: When the enemy attacks a town, defence is on everyone, and a woman goes out without her husband's permission.

cards.ask: The ruler gathers an army for a campaign far away; no one is attacking the town. Musa is blind. Must he go?
options: No: jihad is not required of the blind
Yes: it is a duty on everyone
source: ولا أعمى
إذا قام به فريق من الناس سقط عن الباقين
cards.why: It is a shared duty in normal times, and the book says it is not required of a blind person.

cards.title: First, the invitation
cards.ar: وإذا دخل المسلمون دار الحرب فحاصروا مدينة أو حصنا دعوهم إلى الإسلام فإن أجابوهم كفوا عن قتالهم
cards.en: Dar al-harb means "the land of war": lands at war with the Muslim state. If a Muslim army there surrounds (besieges) a city or fort, they first invite its people to Islam. If they accept, the fighting stops.

cards.title: Second, the jizya
cards.ar: وإن امتنعوا دعوهم إلى أداء الجزية فإن بذلوها فلهم ما للمسلمين وعليهم ما عليهم
cards.en: If they refuse, they are invited to pay the jizya: a yearly tax paid by non-Muslims living under the Muslim state, in return for its protection. If they agree, they have the rights the Muslims have and the duties the Muslims have.

cards.ask: What are they invited to second? Complete it.
cards.ar: وإن امتنعوا دعوهم إلى أداء ____
cards.source: وإن امتنعوا دعوهم إلى أداء الجزية
cards.why: الجزية: if they refuse Islam, they are invited to pay the jizya.

cards.ask: Put the steps at a besieged city in the book's order
steps: If they refuse, invite them to pay the jizya
If they refuse, seek Allah's help and fight
source: دعوهم إلى الإسلام
وإن امتنعوا دعوهم إلى أداء الجزية
وإن أبوا استعانوا بالله تعالى عليهم وحاربوهم
cards.why: Islam first, then the jizya, and only if both are refused is there fighting.

cards.title: When the invitation is required
cards.ar: ولا يجوز أن يقاتل من لم تبلغه دعوة الإسلام إلا بعد أن يدعوهم ويستحب أن يدعو من بلغته الدعوة ولا يجب ذلك
cards.en: People who have never heard the message of Islam may not be fought until they have been invited. For people who have already heard it, inviting them again is recommended (mustahabb) but not required.

cards.ask: An army reaches a fort whose people have never heard of Islam. The commander wants to attack at once. Is that allowed?
options: No: they must be invited first
Yes, if the fort is strong
cards.source: ولا يجوز أن يقاتل من لم تبلغه دعوة الإسلام إلا بعد أن يدعوهم
cards.why: Those who have never heard the message may not be fought until they are invited.

cards.title: Siege warfare
cards.ar: وإن أبوا استعانوا بالله تعالى عليهم وحاربوهم ونصبوا عليهم المجانيق وحرقوهم وأرسلوا عليهم الماء وقطعوا أشجارهم وأفسدوا زروعهم
cards.en: If they refuse both, the army asks for Allah's help and fights them. The book lists the siege methods of its time: catapults (manjaniq), fire, sending water against them, and cutting down their trees and crops.

cards.title: Aiming only at the enemy
cards.ar: ولا بأس برميهم وإن كان فيهم مسلم أسير أو تاجر وإن تترسوا بصبيان المسلمين أو بالأسارى لم يكفوا عن رميهم ويقصدون بالرمي الكفار
cards.en: They may shoot at the enemy even if a Muslim prisoner or trader is among them. If the enemy hide behind Muslim children or prisoners as shields, the army does not stop, but they must aim only at the enemy fighters.

cards.ask: Enemy soldiers in a fort put Muslim prisoners in front of them as shields. What does the book say?
options: They keep shooting, aiming only at the enemy
They must stop the fighting completely
They may aim at anyone in the fort
source: لم يكفوا عن رميهم ويقصدون بالرمي الكفار
cards.why: They do not stop, but their aim must be the enemy fighters only.

cards.ask: An army reaches a city whose people already know the message of Islam well. The commander does not invite them again before offering the jizya. Did he do wrong?
options: No: a second invitation is only recommended
Yes: the invitation is required before every fight
Yes: he had to skip the jizya and fight
cards.source: ويستحب أن يدعو من بلغته الدعوة ولا يجب ذلك
cards.why: For people who have already heard the message, inviting again is only recommended.

lessons.title: Limits in war and peace treaties

cards.title: Women and the Quran with the army
cards.ar: ولا بأس بإخراج النساء والمصاحف مع المسلمين إذا كان عسكرا عظيما يؤمن عليه ويكره إخراج ذلك في سرية لا يؤمن عليها
cards.en: Women and copies of the Quran (mushaf) may go with a large army that is safe. Taking them with a small raiding party (sariyya) that cannot be kept safe is disliked (makruh).

cards.ask: A small raiding party of 20 riders sets out, and it cannot be kept safe. Should they take a copy of the Quran with them?
options: No: it is disliked with a small, unsafe party
Yes: it is always good to carry the Quran along
Only if a woman carries it
cards.source: ويكره إخراج ذلك في سرية لا يؤمن عليها
cards.why: Taking it with a small party that is not safe is disliked.

cards.title: Permission to fight
cards.ar: ولا تقاتل المرأة إلا بإذن زوجها ولا العبد إلا بإذن سيده إلا أن يهجم العدو
cards.en: A woman does not fight without her husband's permission, and in al-Quduri's time a slave did not fight without his master's, unless the enemy attacks.

cards.ask: Sumayya wants to join an ordinary campaign, but her husband says no. The enemy is not attacking. May she go to fight?
options: Yes: fighting in jihad needs no one's permission
Yes, if her brother goes too
cards.source: ولا تقاتل المرأة إلا بإذن زوجها
cards.why: Outside an attack, a woman fights only with her husband's permission.

cards.title: Who must not be harmed
cards.ar: وينبغي للمسلمين أن لا يغدروا ولا يغلوا ولا يمثلوا ولا يقتلوا امرأة أو شيخا فانيا ولا صبيا ولا أعمى ولا مقعدا إلا أن يكون هؤلاء ممن له رأي في الحرب أو تكون المرأة ملكة ولا يقتلوا مجنونا
cards.en: Muslims must not betray a promise (ghadr), not secretly take from the spoils (ghulul), and not mutilate. They must not kill a woman, a very old man, a child, a blind person or someone who cannot walk, unless that person plans the war or the woman is a queen. They must not kill an insane person.

cards.ask: What must Muslims never do? Complete it.
cards.ar: وينبغي للمسلمين أن لا ____ ولا يغلوا
cards.source: وينبغي للمسلمين أن لا يغدروا ولا يغلوا
cards.why: يغدروا: Muslims must never betray a promise.

cards.ask: Who must the army NOT kill?

options.text: A child
An old man who plans the enemy's battles
A very old man who takes no part
A woman who takes no part
An insane person

source: ولا يقتلوا امرأة أو شيخا فانيا ولا صبيا
إلا أن يكون هؤلاء ممن له رأي في الحرب
ولا يقتلوا مجنونا
cards.why: Women, the very old, children and the insane are protected. The exception is someone who plans the war.

cards.title: Peace treaties
cards.ar: وإذا رأى الأمام أن يصالح أهل الحرب أو فريقا منهم وكان في ذلك مصلحة للمسلمين فلا بأس به وإن صالحهم مدة ثم رأى أن نقض الصلح أنفع نبذ إليهم وقاتلهم
cards.en: The ruler (imam) may make a peace treaty (sulh) with the enemy, or some of them, when it is good for the Muslims. If he later sees that ending it is better, he must first openly tell them it is over (nabdh). Only then may he fight.

cards.title: If they betray first
cards.ar: وإن بدؤوا بخيانة قاتلهم ولم ينبذ إليهم إذا كان ذلك باتفاقهم
cards.en: If the other side betray the treaty first, and they agreed on it together, the ruler may fight them without first announcing that the treaty is over.

cards.ask: A ruler made a five-year peace treaty. After two years he sees that ending it is better for the Muslims. The other side have kept it. What must he do first?
options: Openly tell them the treaty is over
Nothing: he may attack at once
Wait until the five years end
cards.source: ثم رأى أن نقض الصلح أنفع نبذ إليهم وقاتلهم
cards.why: He must first announce to them that the treaty has ended (nabdh); a surprise attack would be a betrayal.

cards.title: Slaves who come over
cards.ar: وإذا خرج عبيدهم إلى عسكر المسلمين فهم أحرار
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time, if slaves of the enemy escaped and came over to the Muslim army, they became free.

cards.ask: During a war, the enemy break their treaty by a plan they all agreed on. Must the ruler announce the end of the treaty before fighting?
options: Yes: he must always announce it first
Yes, and then wait one more year
cards.source: وإن بدؤوا بخيانة قاتلهم ولم ينبذ إليهم إذا كان ذلك باتفاقهم
cards.why: When they start the betrayal by agreement, he may fight without announcing it.

cards.title: Using what they find
cards.ar: ويأكلوا ما وجدوه من الطعام ويستعملون الحطب ويدهنون بالدهن ويقاتلون بما يجدونه من السلاح
cards.en: In enemy land, the army may feed their animals and eat the food they find, use firewood, use oil, and fight with weapons they find, all before the spoils are divided.

cards.title: But not sell it
cards.ar: ولا يجوز أن يبيعوا من ذلك شيئا
cards.en: They may not sell any of it or keep it as their own wealth. It is for use only.

cards.ask: In enemy land, before the spoils are divided: allowed or not?
items: Fighting with a sword found there
Selling some of the food found there
source: ويأكلوا ما وجدوه من الطعام ويستعملون الحطب ويدهنون بالدهن ويقاتلون بما يجدونه من السلاح
ولا يجوز أن يبيعوا من ذلك شيئا
cards.why: Food, firewood, oil and weapons may be used, but nothing may be sold.

cards.title: Someone there accepts Islam
cards.ar: ومن أسلم منهم أحرز بإسلامه نفسه وأولاد الصغار وكل مال هو في يده أو وديعة في يد مسلم أو ذمي
cards.en: If someone in enemy land accepts Islam, his Islam protects himself, his young children, and all wealth in his hand or left as a deposit with a Muslim or a dhimmi (a non-Muslim citizen of the Muslim state).

cards.title: What his Islam does not protect
cards.ar: فإن ظهرنا على الدار فعقاره فيء وزوجته فيء وحملها فيء وأولاده فيء
cards.en: If the Muslims later take that land, his land and buildings become fay' (taken by the state). In the law of al-Quduri's time, his wife, her unborn child and his older children were counted the same way.

cards.ask: Harith, living in enemy land, becomes Muslim. He has a horse in his hand and owns a farm there. Later the Muslims take the land. What stays his?
options: The horse, but not the farm
The farm, but not the horse
source: وكل مال هو في يده
فعقاره فيء
cards.why: Wealth in his hand is protected by his Islam, but his land becomes fay'.

cards.title: No weapons to the enemy
cards.ar: ولا ينبغي أن يباع السلاح من أهل الحرب ولا يجهز إليهم ولا يفدون بالأسارى عند أبي حنيفة وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد: يفادى بهم أسارى المسلمين ولا يجوز المن عليهم
cards.en: Weapons must not be sold to the enemy or sent to them. Enemy prisoners are not set free in exchange for Muslim prisoners, says Abu Hanifa. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say they may be exchanged for Muslim prisoners. Letting them go for nothing (mann) is not allowed.

cards.title: After a conquest
cards.ar: وإذا فتح الإمام بلدا عنوة فهو بالخيار: إن شاء قسمه بين الغانمين وإن شاء أقر أهله عليه ووضع عليهم الخراج وهو في الأسارى بالخيار: إن شاء قتلهم وإن شاء استرقهم وإن شاء تركهم أحرارا ذمة للمسلمين
cards.en: If the ruler takes a town by force ('anwa), he chooses: divide its land among the fighters, or leave its people on it and set kharaj (a land tax) on them. For prisoners of war, the law of al-Quduri's time gave the ruler a choice: execution, slavery, or leaving them free as dhimmis under the Muslims.

cards.ask: A ruler takes a city by force. What may he do with its land?
options: Either: divide it, or set kharaj on it
He must divide it among all the fighters
He must leave it with its people, under kharaj
cards.source: فهو بالخيار: إن شاء قسمه بين الغانمين وإن شاء أقر أهله عليه ووضع عليهم الخراج
cards.why: The book gives the ruler a choice between the two.

cards.ask: After the conquest, the ruler wants to send the prisoners back to the land of war. Is this allowed?
options: No; he may instead leave them free as dhimmis
Yes: setting them free is always allowed
Yes, if they promise not to fight
source: ولا يجوز أن يردهم إلى دار الحرب
وإن شاء تركهم أحرارا ذمة للمسلمين
cards.why: He may not return them to the land of war, but leaving them free as dhimmis is one of his choices.

cards.ask: Which of these does the book allow?
options: Fighting with a sword found in enemy land
Selling food found in enemy land
source: ويقاتلون بما يجدونه من السلاح
ولا ينبغي أن يباع السلاح من أهل الحرب
cards.why: Using weapons found there is allowed; selling the food, or selling weapons to the enemy, is not.

lessons.title: Spoils on the way, and safe conduct
lessons.arabic: وإذا أمن رجل حر أو امرأة

cards.title: Animals they cannot bring back
cards.ar: وإذا أراد العود معهم مواش فلم يقدروا على نقلها إلى دار الإسلام ذبحوها وحرقوها ولا يعقرونها ولا يتركونها
cards.en: Dar al-Islam is the land under the Muslim state. If the army is going home with animals it cannot take along, they slaughter them and burn them so the enemy cannot use them. They do not cripple them, and they do not leave them behind.

cards.title: No dividing in enemy land
cards.ar: ولا يقسم غنيمة في دار الحرب حتى يخرجها إلى دار الإسلام والردء والمقاتل في العسكر سواء
cards.en: Ghanima is the spoils taken in battle. It is not divided in enemy land until it is brought to dar al-Islam. The back-up soldiers (rid') who guard and support count the same as those who fought.

cards.ask: Bilal guarded the camp as back-up while Khalid fought in the battle. How do their shares compare?
cards.source: والردء والمقاتل في العسكر سواء
cards.why: The back-up soldier and the fighter in the army are equal.

cards.title: Late arrivals and the army market
cards.ar: وإذا لحقهم المدد في دار الحرب قبل أن يخرجوا الغنيمة إلى دار الإسلام شاركوهم فيها ولا حق لأهل سوق العسكر في الغنيمة إلا أن يقاتلوا
cards.en: If reinforcements join the army in enemy land before the spoils are brought home, they share in them. The traders of the army's market have no right to the spoils unless they fight.

cards.ask: Does this person share in the spoils?
items: A back-up soldier guarding the camp
Reinforcements who arrive before the spoils leave enemy land
A trader in the army market who did not fight
A trader in the army market who fought
source: والردء والمقاتل في العسكر سواء
شاركوهم فيها ولا حق لأهل سوق العسكر في الغنيمة إلا أن يقاتلوا
cards.why: Back-up soldiers and early reinforcements share. Market traders share only if they fight.

cards.title: Giving aman (safe conduct)
cards.ar: وإذا أمن رجل حر أو امرأة كافرا أو جماعة أو أهل حصن أو مدينة صح أمانهم ولم يجز لأحد من المسلمين قتلهم إلا أن يكون في ذلك مفسدة فينبذ إليهم الإمام
cards.en: Aman is a promise of safety. If a free Muslim man or woman gives aman to an enemy person, a group, or the people of a fort or city, it is valid, and no Muslim may kill them. If it causes harm, the ruler openly ends it.

cards.title: Whose aman does not count
cards.ar: ولا يجوز أمان ذمي ولا أسير ولا تاجر يدخل عليهم ولا يجوز أمان العبد عند أبي حنيفة إلا أن يأذن له مولاه في القتال وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد: يصح أمانة
cards.en: The aman of a dhimmi, of a Muslim held prisoner by the enemy, or of a trader who went into their land is not valid. In al-Quduri's time, Abu Hanifa said a slave's aman was not valid unless his master let him fight. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say it is valid.

cards.ask: Whose aman to an enemy soldier is valid?

options.text: A dhimmi
A free Muslim man in the army
A Muslim held prisoner by the enemy
A free Muslim woman in the army
A Muslim trader who went into their land

source: وإذا أمن رجل حر أو امرأة
ولا يجوز أمان ذمي ولا أسير ولا تاجر يدخل عليهم
cards.why: A free Muslim man or woman can give aman. A dhimmi, a prisoner and a trader inside their land cannot.

cards.ask: Fatima, a free Muslim woman, gives aman to an enemy soldier. Umar wants to kill him anyway. May he?
options: Yes: a woman's aman does not count
Yes, if the ruler did not hear it
cards.source: صح أمانهم ولم يجز لأحد من المسلمين قتلهم
cards.why: A free woman's aman is valid, so no Muslim may kill him.

cards.ask: The army has spoils in enemy land. Some soldiers want to divide them there and then. What does the book say?
options: Wait until the spoils reach dar al-Islam
Give them all to the fighters, none to the back-up
cards.source: ولا يقسم غنيمة في دار الحرب حتى يخرجها إلى دار الإسلام
cards.why: The spoils are not divided in enemy land; they are brought home first.

cards.title: Taken by one enemy from another
cards.ar: وإذا غلب الترك على الروم فسبوهم وأخذوا أموالهم ملكوها فإن غلبنا على الترك حل لنا من ذلك
cards.en: The book gives an example from its time. If the Turks defeat the Byzantines (Rum) and take their wealth, the Turks own it. If the Muslims then defeat the Turks, that wealth becomes lawful for the Muslims.

cards.title: Muslim property taken in a raid
cards.ar: وإذا غلبوا على أموالنا فأحرزوها بدارهم ملكوها فإن ظهر عليها المسلمون فوجدوها قبل القسمة فهي لهم بغير شيء وإن وجدوها بعد القسمة أخذوها بالقيمة
cards.en: If the enemy take Muslims' property and bring it into their own land, they own it. If Muslims later win it back, the old owners take it free if they find it before the spoils are divided. After the division, they may take it back by paying its value, if they want to.

cards.ask: Raiders took Salim's camel into their land. The Muslim army wins it back, and Salim finds it before the spoils are divided. What must he pay?
cards.source: فوجدوها قبل القسمة فهي لهم بغير شيء
cards.why: Found before the division, it goes back to him free.

cards.ask: This time Salim only finds his camel after the spoils were divided, and it went to Anas. What can Salim do?
options: Take it back by paying its value
Take it back for nothing, as it is still his
cards.source: وإن وجدوها بعد القسمة أخذوها بالقيمة
cards.why: After the division, he may take it by paying its value.

cards.title: Bought by a trader
cards.ar: وإن دخل دار الحرب تاجر فاشترى ذلك وأخرجه إلى دار الإسلام فمالكه بالخيار: إن شاء أخذه بالثمن الذي اشتراه به التاجر وإن شاء ترك
cards.en: If a trader goes into enemy land, buys that property and brings it back, the old owner chooses: take it for the price the trader paid, or leave it.

cards.ask: Ammar, a trader, buys Salim's stolen camel in enemy land for 50 dirhams and brings it home. What can Salim do?
options: Take it for 50 dirhams, or leave it
Take it for its full market value only
cards.source: إن شاء أخذه بالثمن الذي اشتراه به التاجر وإن شاء ترك
cards.why: He may pay the trader's price, 50 dirhams, or leave it.

cards.title: What they can never own
cards.ar: ولا يملك علينا أهل الحرب بالغلبة مدبرينا ومكاتبنا وأمهات أولادنا وأحرارنا ونملك عليهم جميع ذلك
cards.en: By capture, the enemy never become owners of free Muslims. In al-Quduri's time this also covered three kinds of slaves who were on the way to freedom: the mudabbar (promised freedom at the master's death), the mukatab (buying his freedom by contract) and the umm walad (a slave woman who had her master's child).

cards.title: A runaway and a stray animal
cards.ar: وإذا أبق عبد لمسلم فدخل إليهم فأخذوه لم يملكوه عند أبي حنيفة وإن ند
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time, if a Muslim's slave ran away into their land and they took him, they did not own him, according to Abu Hanifa. But if a camel strays into their land and they take it, they own it.

cards.ask: If the enemy take it into their land, do they own it?
items: Money taken from Muslims in a raid
A camel that wandered into their land
source: وإذا غلبوا على أموالنا فأحرزوها بدارهم ملكوها
إليهم فأخذوه ملكوه
مدبرينا ومكاتبنا وأمهات أولادنا وأحرارنا
cards.why: Property and a stray camel become theirs. Free people, and those on the way to freedom, never do.

cards.ask: Complete it: the Muslims can own all of that from the enemy.
cards.ar: ونملك عليهم ____ ذلك
cards.source: ونملك عليهم جميع ذلك
cards.why: جميع: the Muslims can own all of it from them, though the enemy cannot own these from the Muslims.

lessons.title: Handling the spoils
lessons.arabic: ولا يجوز بيع الغنائم قبل القسمة

cards.title: No pack animals
cards.ar: وإذا لم يكن للإمام حمولة يحمل عليها الغنائم قسمها بين الغانمين قسمة إيداع ليحملوها إلى دار الإسلام ثم يرتجعها فيقسمها
cards.en: If the ruler has no animals to carry the spoils, he hands them out among the fighters for safe-keeping only, so they carry them home. Then he takes them back and divides them properly.

cards.title: No selling first
cards.ar: ولا يجوز بيع الغنائم قبل القسمة
cards.en: The spoils may not be sold before they are divided.

cards.ask: The ruler has no pack animals, so he gives Rami a bag of spoils to carry home. On the way, Rami sells some of it. Was that allowed?
options: No: it was given only for carrying
Yes: it was his share of the spoils
Yes, if he sold it to a Muslim
source: قسمة إيداع ليحملوها إلى دار الإسلام
ولا يجوز بيع الغنائم قبل القسمة
cards.why: The bag was only for safe-keeping until home, and the spoils may not be sold before they are divided.

cards.title: A soldier who dies
cards.ar: ومن مات من الغانمين في دار الحرب فلا حق له في الغنيمة ومن مات منهم بعد إخراجها إلى دار الإسلام فنصيبه لورثته
cards.en: A soldier who dies in enemy land has no right to the spoils. If he dies after they are brought to dar al-Islam, his share goes to his heirs.

cards.ask: Yasir and Hasan fought in the same army. Yasir died in enemy land; Hasan died after the spoils reached home. Whose heirs get his share?
source: ومن مات من الغانمين في دار الحرب فلا حق له في الغنيمة
فنصيبه لورثته
cards.why: Dying in enemy land loses the right. Dying after the spoils are home passes the share to the heirs.

cards.title: What salab is
cards.ar: والسلب: ما على المقتول من ثيابه وسلاحه ومركبه
cards.en: Salab is what the fallen enemy fighter had: his clothes, his weapons and his mount.

cards.title: Nafl: an extra reward
cards.ar: ولا بأس أن ينقل الإمام في حال القتال ويحرض بالنفل على القتال فيقول: من قتل قتيلا فله سلبه أو يقول لسرية: قد جعلت لكم الربع بعد الخمس
cards.en: Nafl is an extra reward the ruler promises during the fighting to encourage it. He may say: "Whoever defeats an enemy fighter gets his salab", or tell a raiding party: "You get a quarter, after the fifth is taken out."

cards.ask: During the battle, the ruler tells a raiding party: "You get a quarter, after the fifth is taken out." May he promise this?
options: Yes: it is a nafl to encourage fighting
No: the spoils must all be shared equally
No: only the fifth may ever be promised
cards.source: أو يقول لسرية: قد جعلت لكم الربع بعد الخمس
cards.why: During the fighting the ruler may promise a nafl, such as a quarter after the fifth, to spur the army on.

cards.title: Once the spoils are secured
cards.ar: بعد إحراز الغنيمة إلا من الخمس وإذا لم يجعل السلب للقاتل فهو من جملة الغنيمة والقاتل وغيره فيه سواء
cards.en: After the spoils are secured, any extra reward can only come from the fifth (khumus). If the ruler did not promise the salab to the fighter, it is part of the spoils, and he is equal to everyone else in it.

cards.ask: The ruler made no promise about salab. In battle, Ali defeats an enemy fighter. Who gets the fighter's sword and horse?
options: They go into the spoils, shared by all
Ali alone: the fighter's salab is always his
cards.source: وإذا لم يجعل السلب للقاتل فهو من جملة الغنيمة والقاتل وغيره فيه سواء
cards.why: Without the ruler's promise, the salab is part of the spoils, and Ali is equal to the others in it.

cards.title: After leaving enemy land
cards.ar: وإذا خرج المسلمون من دار الحرب لم يجز أن يعلفوا من الغنيمة ولا يأكلوا منها ومن فضل معه علف أو طعام
cards.en: Once the Muslims leave enemy land, they may no longer feed their animals or eat from the spoils. Fodder or food a soldier has left over goes back into the spoils.

cards.ask: Which are true of the spoils?

options.text: With no pack animals, fighters may carry the spoils for safe-keeping
The spoils may be sold before they are divided
Salab includes the fighter's weapons and mount
After leaving enemy land, soldiers may keep eating from the spoils
A soldier who dies after the spoils reach home leaves his share to his heirs

source: قسمة إيداع ليحملوها إلى دار الإسلام
ولا يجوز بيع الغنائم قبل القسمة
والسلب: ما على المقتول من ثيابه وسلاحه ومركبه
لم يجز أن يعلفوا من الغنيمة ولا يأكلوا منها
فنصيبه لورثته
cards.why: Carrying for safe-keeping, salab and the heirs' share are right. Selling before division and eating after leaving are not allowed.

lessons.title: Dividing the spoils and the fifth

cards.title: The fifth and the four fifths
cards.ar: ويقسم الإمام الغنيمة: فيخرج خمسها ويقسم أربعة أخماسها بين الغانمين: للفارس سهما وللراجل سهم عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: The ruler takes out one fifth (the khumus) and divides the other four fifths among the fighters. For Abu Hanifa, a horseman gets two shares and a foot soldier one. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say the horseman gets three.

cards.ask: An army's spoils are worth 1,000 dirhams. How much is the fifth (khumus)?
cards.source: فيخرج خمسها ويقسم أربعة أخماسها بين الغانمين
cards.why: One fifth of 1,000 is 200; the other 800 go to the fighters.

cards.title: Which animals count
cards.ar: ولا يسهم إلا لفرس واحد والبراذين والعتاق سواء ولا يسهم لراحلة ولا بغل
cards.en: A share is given for one horse only, even if a man has more. Non-Arab horses (baradhin) and pure Arab horses ('itaq) count the same. No share is given for a riding camel or a mule.

cards.title: How he entered counts
cards.ar: ومن دخل دار الحرب فارسا فنفق فرسه استحق سهم فارس ومن دخل راجلا فاشترى فرسا استحق سهم راجل
cards.en: What counts is how he entered enemy land. If he entered on a horse and it died, he still gets a horseman's share. If he entered on foot and then bought a horse, he gets a foot soldier's share.

cards.ask: Sa'd rode into enemy land on his horse, and it died on the way. Ubayd walked in and bought a horse there. Who gets a horseman's share?
cards.source: ومن دخل دار الحرب فارسا فنفق فرسه استحق سهم فارس ومن دخل راجلا فاشترى فرسا استحق سهم راجل
cards.why: It depends on how each one entered: Sa'd entered as a horseman, Ubayd on foot.

cards.title: A gift instead of a share
cards.ar: ولا يسهم لمملوك ولا امرأة ولا ذمي ولا صبي ولكن يرضخ لهم على حسب ما يراه الإمام
cards.en: No full share is given to a woman, a dhimmi, a child, or in al-Quduri's time a slave. Instead they get a smaller gift (radkh), as much as the ruler sees fit.

cards.ask: Umm Sulaym helped the army by nursing the wounded. What does she get from the spoils?
options: A gift (radkh) as the ruler sees fit
cards.source: ولا يسهم لمملوك ولا امرأة ولا ذمي ولا صبي ولكن يرضخ لهم على حسب ما يراه الإمام
cards.why: A woman gets no full share, but she is given a radkh.

cards.title: Who receives the fifth
cards.ar: وأما الخمس فيقسم على ثلاثة أسهم: سهم لليتامى وسهم للمساكين وسهم لأبناء السبيل يدخل فقراء ذوي القربى فيهم ويقدمون ولا يدفع إلى أغنيائهم شيء
cards.en: The fifth is split into three: one for orphans, one for the poor, and one for travellers in need. The poor among the Prophet's relatives (dhawu al-qurba) are included in these and come first. Their rich ones get nothing from it.

cards.title: The Prophet's share
cards.ar: وما ذكر الله تعالى في الخمس فإنما هو لافتتاح الكلام تبركا باسمه وسهم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سقط بموته كما سقط الصفي
cards.en: Allah's name in the ayah of the fifth opens the words for blessing; it is not a separate share. The Prophet's share ﷺ ended with his death, like his safi (a chosen item from the spoils). His relatives received theirs in his time for their support, and after him because of poverty.

cards.ask: Who receives from the fifth today, by the book?

options.text: Orphans
Rich relatives of the Prophet ﷺ
The poor
Travellers in need
Poor relatives of the Prophet ﷺ

source: سهم لليتامى وسهم للمساكين وسهم لأبناء السبيل يدخل فقراء ذوي القربى فيهم ويقدمون ولا يدفع إلى أغنيائهم شيء
cards.why: Orphans, the poor and travellers, with the poor relatives first. The rich relatives get nothing.

cards.title: Raids without permission
cards.ar: وإذا دخل الواحد أو الاثنان إلى دار الحرب مغيرين بغير إذن الإمام فأخذوا شيئا لم يخمس وإن دخل جماعة لها منعة وأخذوا شيئا خمس وإن لم يأذن لهم الإمام
cards.en: If one or two men raid enemy land without the ruler's permission and take something, no fifth is taken from it. If a group with real strength (man'a) does it, a fifth is taken, even without the ruler's permission.

cards.ask: Two men raid enemy land without the ruler's permission and take 100 sheep. Is a fifth taken from them?
options: No: two raiders without permission pay no fifth
cards.source: وإذا دخل الواحد أو الاثنان إلى دار الحرب مغيرين بغير إذن الإمام فأخذوا شيئا لم يخمس
cards.why: One or two raiders without permission are not taxed a fifth.

lessons.title: Traders and visitors with safe conduct
lessons.arabic: وإذا دخل المسلم دار الحرب تاجرا

cards.title: A Muslim trader in their land
cards.ar: وإذا دخل المسلم دار الحرب تاجرا فلا يحل له أن يتعرض لشيء من أموالهم ولا من دمائهم
cards.en: If a Muslim enters enemy land as a trader, under their promise of safety, he must not touch any of their property or harm any of them.

cards.title: If he betrays them
cards.ar: وإن غدر بهم وأخذ شيئا وخرج به ملكه ملكا محظورا ويؤمر أن يتصدق به
cards.en: If he betrays them, takes something and brings it out, he owns it in a forbidden way, and he is told to give it away in charity.

cards.ask: Tariq trades in enemy land under their safe conduct and secretly takes 30 dinars. Back home, what is he told to do?
options: Hand a fifth to the ruler and keep the rest
cards.source: ملكه ملكا محظورا ويؤمر أن يتصدق به
cards.why: He owns it in a forbidden way and is told to give it in charity.

cards.title: A visitor from the land of war
cards.ar: وإذا دخل الحربي إلينا مستأمنا لم يمكن أن يقيم في دارنا سنة ويقول له الإمام: إن أقمت تمام السنة وضعت عليك الجزية فإن أقام أخذ منه الجزية وصار ذميا ولم يترك أن يرجع إلى دار الحرب
cards.en: A musta'min is someone from the land of war who enters Muslim land with a promise of safety. He is not allowed to stay a full year. The ruler tells him: "If you stay the whole year, I will set jizya on you." If he stays, he pays jizya, becomes a dhimmi, and may not go back.

cards.ask: Nikolas came with a promise of safety. The ruler warned him, and he stayed a full year. What now?
options: He becomes a dhimmi and may not go back
He must leave for the land of war at once
cards.source: فإن أقام أخذ منه الجزية وصار ذميا ولم يترك أن يرجع إلى دار الحرب
cards.why: After the full year he pays jizya and becomes a dhimmi, and is not allowed to go back.

cards.title: What he leaves behind
cards.ar: وما في دار الإسلام من ماله على خطر فإن أسر أو قتل سقطت ديونه وصارت الوديعة فيئا
cards.en: If he goes back to the land of war and leaves a deposit with a Muslim or a dhimmi, or a debt they owe him, his property here is at risk. If he is later captured or killed, the debts owed to him drop, and the deposit becomes fay' (state property).

cards.title: Gained without fighting
cards.ar: وما أوجف عليه المسلمون من أموال أهل الحرب بغير قتال يصرف مصالح المسلمين كما يصرف الخراج
cards.en: Wealth the Muslims gain from the enemy without fighting is spent on the public good of the Muslims, the same way as the kharaj (land tax).

cards.ask: Where does it go?
items: Spoils taken in battle, after the fifth
Wealth the enemy hand over without fighting
source: ويقسم أربعة أخماسها بين الغانمين
من أموال أهل الحرب بغير قتال يصرف مصالح المسلمين كما يصرف الخراج
cards.why: Battle spoils go to the fighters (after the fifth). Wealth gained without fighting is spent like kharaj, on the public good.

cards.ask: A musta'min goes home and leaves 100 dirhams on deposit with Umar. Later he is killed in war. What happens to the deposit?
options: It is sent to his family in the land of war
source: وترك وديعة عند مسلم أو ذمي
فإن أسر أو قتل سقطت ديونه وصارت الوديعة فيئا
cards.why: If he is captured or killed, the deposit becomes fay'.

cards.title: The land of the Arabs
cards.ar: ما بين العذيب إلى أقصى حجر باليمن بمهرة إلى حد الشام
cards.en: Two kinds of farmland pay two kinds of tax. Ushr land pays ushr: a tenth of its crops, as zakat. Kharaj land pays kharaj: a land tax. All the land of the Arabs is ushr land. It runs from al-'Udhayb to the far edge of Yemen at Mahra, up to the border of Syria (al-Sham).

cards.title: The Sawad of Iraq
cards.ar: والسواد كلها أرض خراج وهي: ما بين العذيب إلى عقبة حلوان ومن العلث إلى عبادان
cards.en: The Sawad is the rich farmland of Iraq. All of it is kharaj land: from al-'Udhayb to the pass of Hulwan, and from al-'Alth to 'Abbadan.

cards.ask: Which kind of land is the Sawad, the farmland of Iraq?
cards.source: والسواد كلها أرض خراج
cards.why: Al-Quduri says all of the Sawad is kharaj land.

cards.title: Its people own it
cards.ar: وأرض السواد مملوكه لأهلها: يجوز بيعهم لها وتصرفهم فيها
cards.en: The land of the Sawad belongs to its people. They may sell it and use it as owners.

cards.ask: What may the people of the Sawad do with their land? Complete it.
cards.ar: يجوز ____ لها وتصرفهم فيها
cards.source: يجوز بيعهم لها وتصرفهم فيها
cards.why: بيعهم: they own it, so they may sell it.

cards.title: The general rule
cards.ar: وكل أرض أسلم أهلها عليها أو فتحت عنوة وقسمت بين الغانمين فهي أرض عشر وكل أرض فتحت عنوة وأقر عليها فهي أرض خراج
cards.en: Any land whose people became Muslim while on it, or that was taken by force and divided among the fighters, is ushr land. Any land taken by force whose people were left on it is kharaj land.

cards.ask: Ushr land or kharaj land?
items: Land whose people became Muslim on it
Land taken by force and divided among the fighters
Land taken by force, its people left on it
source: وكل أرض أسلم أهلها عليها أو فتحت عنوة وقسمت بين الغانمين فهي أرض عشر
وكل أرض فتحت عنوة وأقر عليها فهي أرض خراج
والسواد كلها أرض خراج
cards.why: Islam on the land, or division among the fighters, makes it ushr land. Leaving the people on conquered land makes it kharaj land.

cards.title: Reviving dead land
cards.ar: إحياء الموات ومن أحيا أرضا مواتا فهي عند أبي يوسف معتبرة بحيزها: فإن كانت من حيز أرض الخارج فهي خراجية وإن كانت من حيز أرض العشر فهي عشرية والبصرة عنده عشرية بإجماع الصحابة رضي الله عنهم
cards.en: Ihya al-mawat means bringing "dead" land (unused land that no one owns) to life by farming it. Note: Abu Yusuf judges it by the area it lies in: near kharaj land it is kharaj, near ushr land it is ushr. For him Basra is ushr land, by the agreement of the Companions.

cards.title: Muhammad's view
cards.ar: وقال محمد: إن أحياها ببئر حفرها أو عين استخرجها أو ماء دجله أو الفرات أو الأنهار العظام التي لا يملكها أحد فهي عشرية وإن أحياها بماء الأنهار التي احتفرها الأعاجم مثل نهر الملك ونهر يزدجرد فهي خراجية
cards.en: Note: Muhammad judges it by its water. Watered from a well he dug, a spring he opened, the Tigris, the Euphrates or another great river no one owns, it is ushr land. Watered from canals the Persians dug, like Nahr al-Malik and Nahr Yazdajird, it is kharaj land.

cards.ask: A ruler takes a town by force and leaves its people on their land. What kind of land is it now?
cards.source: وكل أرض فتحت عنوة وأقر عليها فهي أرض خراج
cards.why: Land taken by force with its people left on it is kharaj land.

cards.ask: The people of a valley become Muslim while living on their land, with no fighting. What kind of land is it?
cards.source: وكل أرض أسلم أهلها عليها
cards.why: Land whose people became Muslim on it is ushr land.

cards.title: What 'Umar set
cards.ar: والخراج الذي وضعه عمر رضي الله عنه على أهل السواد من كل جريب يبلغه الماء قفيز هاشمي وهو الصاع ودرهم ومن جريب الرطبة خمسة
cards.en: A jarib is a measure of land. The kharaj 'Umar set on the Sawad: from each jarib that water reaches, one Hashimi qafiz of grain (a sa') and one dirham. From each jarib of ratba (fresh fodder like alfalfa), five dirhams. From each jarib of close-planted vines or palms, ten dirhams.

cards.ask: Hisham has 3 jaribs of close-planted vines in the Sawad. How much kharaj in dirhams?
cards.source: ومن جريب الكرم المتصل والنخل المتصل عشرة
cards.why: Ten dirhams a jarib for vines: 3 x 10 = 30.

cards.ask: Huda has 2 jaribs of ratba (fresh fodder). How much kharaj?
cards.source: ومن جريب الرطبة خمسة
cards.why: Five dirhams a jarib: 2 x 5 = 10.

cards.title: Other crops
cards.ar: وما سوى ذلك من الأصناف يوضع عليها بحسب الطاقة فإن لم تطق ما وضع عليها نقصهم الإمام
cards.en: Other kinds of crops are taxed by what the land can bear. If it cannot bear what was set, the ruler lowers it.

cards.title: When the crop is lost
cards.ar: وإن غلب الماء على أرض الخراج أو انقطع عنها أو اصطلم الزرع آفة فلا خراج عليهم وإن عطلها صاحبها فعليه الخراج
cards.en: If water floods kharaj land, or its water is cut off, or a disaster destroys the crop, no kharaj is due. But if the owner simply leaves it unused, he still owes the kharaj.

cards.ask: Is kharaj due this year?
items: The water supply was cut off
The owner left the land unused
cards.source: وإن غلب الماء على أرض الخراج أو انقطع عنها أو اصطلم الزرع آفة فلا خراج عليهم وإن عطلها صاحبها فعليه الخراج
cards.why: Loss the owner cannot help removes it. Leaving the land idle does not.

cards.title: A Muslim and kharaj land
cards.ar: ومن أسلم من أهل الخراج أخذ منه الخراج على حاله ويجوز أن يشتري المسلم أرض الخراج من الذمي ويؤخذ منه الخراج ولا عشر في الخارج من أرض الخراج
cards.en: If an owner of kharaj land becomes Muslim, he still pays the kharaj. A Muslim may buy kharaj land from a dhimmi and then pays the kharaj on it. There is no ushr on crops from kharaj land as well.

cards.ask: Mundhir owns kharaj land but chooses to leave it unfarmed this year. Does he owe kharaj?
options: Yes: leaving it idle does not remove the kharaj
cards.source: وإن عطلها صاحبها فعليه الخراج
cards.why: Leaving it unused by choice does not remove the kharaj.

cards.ask: Yahya, a Muslim, buys kharaj land from a dhimmi and grows wheat on it. What does he pay on it?
source: ويجوز أن يشتري المسلم أرض الخراج من الذمي ويؤخذ منه الخراج
ولا عشر في الخارج من أرض الخراج
cards.why: He pays the kharaj, and there is no ushr on crops from kharaj land.

cards.title: Two kinds of jizya
cards.ar: والجزية على ضربين: جزية توضع بالتراضي والصلح فتقدر بحسب ما يقع عليه الاتفاق
cards.en: There are two kinds of jizya. The first is set by a peace agreement both sides accept; its amount is whatever they agreed.

cards.title: Jizya set by the ruler
cards.ar: وجزية يبتدئ الإمام وضعها إذا غلب الكفار وأقرهم على أملاكهم فيضع على الغني الظاهر الغني في كل سنة ثمانية وأربعين درهما يأخذ منه في كل شهر أربعة دراهم
cards.en: The second is set by the ruler when he wins and leaves the people with their property. A clearly rich man pays 48 dirhams a year (4 a month). A man of middle means pays 24 (2 a month). A poor man who can work pays 12 (1 a month).

cards.ask: Elias is clearly rich, and the ruler set his jizya. How much does he pay in a year?
cards.source: فيضع على الغني الظاهر الغني في كل سنة ثمانية وأربعين درهما
cards.why: A clearly rich man pays 48 dirhams a year, taken at 4 a month.

cards.ask: Thomas is of middle means. How much is taken from him each month?
cards.source: وعلى المتوسط الحال أربعة وعشرين درهما في كل شهر درهمين
cards.why: Middle means: 24 dirhams a year, which is 2 a month.

cards.title: Who it is set on
cards.ar: وتوضع الجزية على أهل الكتاب والمجوس وعبدة الأوثان من العجم ولا توضع على عبدة الأوثان من العرب ولا على المرتدين
cards.en: Jizya is set on the People of the Book (Jews and Christians), the Magians (Zoroastrians), and idol-worshippers who are not Arabs. It is not set on Arab idol-worshippers or on apostates (those who leave Islam).

cards.title: Who never pays it
cards.ar: ولا جزية على امرأة ولا صبي ولا زمن ولا أعمى ولا فقير غير معتمل ولا الرهبان الذين لا يخالطون الناس
cards.en: No jizya is due from a woman, a child, someone chronically ill or disabled (zamin), a blind person, a poor man who cannot work, or monks who live apart from people.

cards.ask: Who owes no jizya?

options.text: A woman
A child
A poor man who is able to work
A blind man
A monk who lives apart from people

source: ولا جزية على امرأة ولا صبي ولا زمن ولا أعمى ولا فقير غير معتمل ولا الرهبان الذين لا يخالطون الناس
وعلى الفقير المعتمل اثني عشر درهما
cards.why: Only the poor man who cannot work is exempt; a poor man who can work pays 12 dirhams.

cards.title: Becoming Muslim, and years that pile up
cards.ar: ومن أسلم وعليه جزية سقطت عنه وإن اجتمع حولان تداخلت الجزية
cards.en: If someone who owes jizya becomes Muslim, it is dropped. If two years (hawl, a full year) pile up unpaid, they merge into one, so only one year's jizya is taken.

cards.ask: Yuhanna, a poor man who works, did not pay jizya for two years. How much is taken from him?
source: وإن اجتمع حولان تداخلت الجزية
وعلى الفقير المعتمل اثني عشر درهما
cards.why: Two years merge into one, and his rate is 12 dirhams.
