cards.ask: Thomas, of middle means, owes this year's jizya and then becomes Muslim before paying. What does he pay?
cards.source: ومن أسلم وعليه جزية سقطت عنه
cards.why: Jizya owed is dropped when he becomes Muslim.

cards.title: Places of worship
cards.ar: ولا يجوز إحداث بيعة ولا كنيسة في دار الإسلام وإذا انهدمت الكنائس البيع القديمة أعادوها
cards.en: In this classical law, new churches and synagogues (bi'a and kanisa) were not built in the Muslim lands. Old ones that fell down could be rebuilt.

cards.ask: An old church in a dhimmi neighbourhood falls down in an earthquake. May its people rebuild it?
options: Yes: old ones that fall down are rebuilt
No: a fallen church may never be rebuilt
Only with half its old size
cards.source: وإذا انهدمت الكنائس البيع القديمة أعادوها
cards.why: The book says old ones that collapse may be rebuilt.

cards.title: Being distinguished
cards.ar: ويؤخذ أهل الذمة بالتميز عن المسلمين في زيهم ومراكبهم وسروجهم وقلانسهم ولا يركبون الخيل ولا يحملون السلاح
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time, dhimmis were required to look different from Muslims in their clothes, mounts, saddles and caps. They did not ride horses or carry weapons.

cards.title: What does not end the covenant
cards.ar: ومن امتنع من أداء الجزية أو قتل مسلما أو سب النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام أو زنى بمسلمة لم ينقض عهده
cards.en: The covenant ('ahd) is the agreement that makes someone a dhimmi. It is not ended if he refuses to pay jizya, kills a Muslim, insults the Prophet ﷺ, or commits zina (unlawful relations) with a Muslim woman. The covenant stays.

cards.ask: A dhimmi refuses to pay his jizya. Has his covenant ended?
options: No: only joining the land of war or fighting ends it
cards.source: ومن امتنع من أداء الجزية
cards.why: Refusing the jizya does not end the covenant; only joining the land of war or fighting does.

cards.title: What does end it
cards.ar: ولا ينتقض العهد إلا بأن يلحق بدار الحرب أو يغلبوا على موضع فيحاربونا
cards.en: The covenant ends only if he goes over to the land of war, or if they take over a place and fight the Muslims.

cards.ask: When does the covenant end? Complete it.
cards.ar: ولا ينتقض العهد إلا بأن يلحق بدار ____
cards.source: ولا ينتقض العهد إلا بأن يلحق بدار الحرب
cards.why: الحرب: only joining the land of war, or seizing a place and fighting, ends it.

cards.ask: Does it end the dhimmi's covenant?
items: Going over to the land of war
Taking over a town and fighting the Muslims
source: ومن امتنع من أداء الجزية أو قتل مسلما
لم ينقض عهده ولا ينتقض العهد إلا بأن يلحق بدار الحرب أو يغلبوا على موضع فيحاربونا
cards.why: Only joining the enemy, or seizing a place and fighting, ends it. The other wrongs do not.

cards.ask: Some dhimmis want to build a brand-new church in a Muslim city. What does al-Quduri say?
options: It is allowed if they pay double jizya
cards.source: ولا يجوز إحداث بيعة ولا كنيسة في دار الإسلام
cards.why: The book does not allow building new ones in dar al-Islam, only rebuilding old ones.

cards.title: Leaving Islam
cards.ar: وإذا ارتد المسلم عن الإسلام
cards.en: Ridda means leaving Islam, and a murtadd is someone who does. In this classical law, Islam is offered back to him. If he has a doubt (shubha), it is explained and cleared up for him.

cards.title: Three days
cards.ar: ثلاثة أيام فإن أسلم وإلا قتل
cards.en: He is held for three days to think. If he returns to Islam, that is the end of it. If not, the ruling in this classical law is execution.

cards.ask: What does the book say happens first, before any sentence?

options.text: Islam is offered back to him
He is fined
His doubts are explained
He is held for three days
He is sent out of the country

source: وإذا ارتد المسلم عن الإسلام
فإن كانت له شبهة كشفت له
ثلاثة أيام فإن أسلم
cards.why: Islam is offered, his doubt is cleared up, and he is held three days.

cards.title: Acting before the offer
cards.ar: فإن قتله قاتل قبل عرض الإسلام عليه كره له ذلك ولا شيء على القاتل
cards.en: If someone kills him before Islam is offered to him, that is disliked (makruh), and the book says the killer owes nothing.

cards.title: A woman who leaves Islam
cards.ar: فأما المرأة إذا ارتدت فلا تقتل ولكن تحبس حتى تسلم
cards.en: A woman who leaves Islam is not executed. She is held in custody until she returns to Islam.

cards.ask: What happens to a woman who leaves Islam? Complete it.
cards.ar: فأما المرأة إذا ارتدت فلا تقتل ولكن ____ حتى تسلم
cards.source: فأما المرأة إذا ارتدت فلا تقتل ولكن تحبس حتى تسلم
cards.why: تحبس: she is held until she returns to Islam, not executed.

cards.ask: A man leaves Islam because of a doubt about a hadith. What does the book say comes first?
options: Islam is offered and his doubt explained
An immediate sentence, with no offer or delay
He is held for three months first
source: عرض عليه
فإن كانت له شبهة كشفت له
cards.why: Islam is offered back, and his doubt is cleared up for him, before anything else.

cards.ask: Which of these does the book say about a man who leaves Islam?
options: He is held for three days
He is held for three months
cards.source: ثلاثة أيام فإن أسلم
cards.why: He is held for three days so that he may return.

cards.title: His property waits
cards.ar: ويزول ملك المرتد عن أمواله بردته زوالا مراعى فإن أسلم عادت على حالها
cards.en: When someone leaves Islam, his ownership of his wealth is put on hold (suspended). If he returns to Islam, it all goes back to him as it was.

cards.title: If he dies an apostate
cards.ar: وإن مات أو قتل على ردته انتقل ما كان اكتسبه في حال الإسلام إلى ورثته المسلمين وكان ما اكتسبه في حال ردته فيئا
cards.en: If he dies or is killed without returning, what he earned while a Muslim passes to his Muslim heirs. What he earned after leaving Islam becomes fay' (state property).

cards.ask: He died without returning. Where does it go?
items: A shop he bought while a Muslim
Wages he earned while a Muslim
Money he earned after leaving Islam
Profit from trading after leaving Islam
source: انتقل ما كان اكتسبه في حال الإسلام إلى ورثته المسلمين
وكان ما اكتسبه في حال ردته فيئا
cards.why: Earnings from his time as a Muslim go to his heirs; earnings after leaving Islam become fay'.

cards.title: If he goes to the land of war
cards.ar: فإن لحق بدرا الحرب مرتدا وحكم الحاكم بلحاقه عتق مدبروه وأمهات أولاده وحلت الديون التي عليه ونقل ما اكتسبه في حال الإسلام إلى ورثته المسلمين
cards.en: If he goes over to the land of war and a judge rules that he has gone, it is treated like his death. His debts fall due at once, and what he earned as a Muslim passes to his heirs. Note: in al-Quduri's time his mudabbars and umm walads (slaves promised freedom) also became free.

cards.title: Which wealth pays which debts
cards.ar: وتقضى الديون التي لزمته في حال الإسلام مما اكتسبه في حال الإسلام وما لزمه من الديون في حال ردته مما اكتسبه في حال ردته
cards.en: Debts from his time as a Muslim are paid from what he earned as a Muslim. Debts from after he left Islam are paid from what he earned after.

cards.ask: Before leaving Islam, Rafiq borrowed 100 dirhams. A judge rules that he has gone to the land of war. From which wealth is the 100 paid?
options: What he earned as a Muslim
What he earned after leaving Islam
cards.source: وتقضى الديون التي لزمته في حال الإسلام مما اكتسبه في حال الإسلام
cards.why: Debts from his Muslim time are paid from what he earned as a Muslim.

cards.title: His deals are on hold
cards.ar: وما باعه أو اشتراه أو تصرف فيه من أمواله في حال ردته موقوف: فإن أسلم صحت عقوده وإن مات أو قتل أو لحق بدار الحرب بطلت
cards.en: What he sells, buys or does with his wealth after leaving Islam is on hold (mawquf). If he returns to Islam, his contracts are valid. If he dies, is killed or goes to the land of war, they are void.

cards.ask: After leaving Islam, Kamal sells his house. A month later he returns to Islam. Is the sale valid?
options: Yes: his return makes it valid
No: it was void from the start
Only if the buyer agrees again
cards.source: فإن أسلم صحت عقوده
cards.why: His deals were on hold; returning to Islam makes them valid.

cards.title: Coming back after the ruling
cards.ar: وإن عاد المرتد بعد الحكم بلحاقه إلى دار الإسلام مسلما فما وجده في يد ورثته من ماله بعينه أخذه
cards.en: If he comes back to the Muslim lands as a Muslim after the judge's ruling, he takes back any of his own property he finds still in his heirs' hands.

cards.ask: After the ruling, Rafiq returns as a Muslim. His heir still has his horse but has sold his sword. What can Rafiq take back?
options: The horse and the sword's price
cards.source: فما وجده في يد ورثته من ماله بعينه أخذه
cards.why: He takes back what he finds itself in the heirs' hands: the horse.

cards.ask: A woman leaves Islam and, while in that state, sells her jewellery. Is the sale valid?
options: No: it is on hold, like a man's
cards.source: في مالها في حال ردتها جاز تصرفها
cards.why: The book says a woman's dealings with her wealth during ridda are valid, unlike a man's.

lessons.title: Banu Taghlib, public funds and rebels

cards.title: The Christians of Banu Taghlib
cards.ar: ونصارى بني تغلب يؤخذ من أموالهم ضعف ما يؤاخذ من المسلمين من الزكاة ويؤخذ من نسائهم ولا يؤخذ من صبيانهم
cards.en: Banu Taghlib were an Arab Christian tribe. From their wealth, double the zakat a Muslim pays is taken. It is taken from their women too, but not from their children.

cards.ask: A Muslim with 40 sheep pays 1 sheep in zakat. Yuhanna of Banu Taghlib has 40 sheep. How many are taken?
cards.source: يؤخذ من أموالهم ضعف ما يؤاخذ من المسلمين من الزكاة
cards.why: Double what a Muslim pays: 2 x 1 = 2 sheep.

cards.title: How public funds are spent
cards.ar: وما جباه الإمام من الخراج ومن أموال بني تغلب وما أهداه أهل الحرب إلى الإمام والجزية تصرف في مصالح المسلمين فتسد منها الثغور وتبنى القناطر والجسور ويعطى قضاة المسلمين وعلماؤهم منه ما يكفيهم ويدفع منه أرزاق المقاتلة وذراريهم
cards.en: Kharaj, Banu Taghlib's payments, gifts from the enemy to the ruler, and jizya are spent on the public good: guarding the frontiers, building bridges, paying judges and scholars enough to live on, and paying the soldiers and their families.

cards.ask: What do these public funds pay for?

options.text: Guarding the frontiers
Building bridges
A gift to the ruler's rich friends
Judges and scholars
Soldiers and their families

cards.source: فتسد منها الثغور وتبنى القناطر والجسور ويعطى قضاة المسلمين وعلماؤهم منه ما يكفيهم ويدفع منه أرزاق المقاتلة وذراريهم
cards.why: Frontiers, bridges, judges and scholars, and soldiers and their families: all for the public good.

cards.title: Muslim rebels (bughat)
cards.ar: إذا تغلب قوم من المسلمين على بلد وخرجوا عن طاعة الإمام دعاهم إلى العود إلى الجماعة وكشف عن شبهتهم ولا يبدؤهم بالقتال حتى يبدؤوا
cards.en: Kitab al-Bughat is about bughat: a group of Muslims who take over a town and rebel against the ruler. He first calls them back to the community and clears up their doubt. He does not start fighting them until they start.

cards.title: When they have a group behind them
cards.ar: فإن بدؤوا قاتلهم حتى يفرق جمعهم فإن كانت لهم فئة أجهز على جريحهم واتبع موليهم وإن لم يكن لهم فئة لم يجهز على جريحهم ولم يتبع موليهم
cards.en: If they start, he fights them until their group breaks up. If they have a fi'a (a larger group to fall back to), their wounded may be finished off and those who flee may be chased. If not, their wounded are left and those who flee are not chased.

cards.ask: A rebel group with no larger group to return to is broken up, and its men run away. Should the ruler's army chase them?
options: No: they have no group to go back to
Yes: fleeing rebels are always chased
cards.source: وإن لم يكن لهم فئة لم يجهز على جريحهم ولم يتبع موليهم
cards.why: With no fi'a behind them, those who flee are not chased.

cards.title: Their families and property
cards.ar: ولا تسبى لهم ذرية ولا يغنم لهم مال ولا بأس أن يقاتلوا بسلاحهم إن احتاج المسلمون إليه ويحبس الإمام أموالهم ولا يردها عليهم ولا يقسمها حتى يتوبوا فيردها
cards.en: Rebels are still Muslims. Their families are not taken captive, and their wealth is not taken as spoils. Their weapons may be used if needed. The ruler holds their wealth, neither returning nor dividing it, until they repent, and then he gives it back.

cards.ask: With the rebels' things: allowed or not?
items: Holding their wealth until they repent
cards.source: ولا تسبى لهم ذرية ولا يغنم لهم مال ولا بأس أن يقاتلوا بسلاحهم إن احتاج المسلمون إليه ويحبس الإمام أموالهم
cards.why: Their weapons may be used and their wealth held, but their families and wealth are never treated as spoils.

cards.title: Taxes the rebels took
cards.ar: وما جناه أهل البغي من البلاد التي غلبوا عليها من الخراج والعشر لم يأخذه الإمام ثانيا فإن كانوا صرفوه في حقه أجزأ من أخذ منه وإن لم يكونوا صرفوه في حقه أفتى أهله فيما بينهم وبين الله تعالى أن يعيدوا ذلك
cards.en: If the rebels collected kharaj and ushr in the towns they held, the ruler does not collect it a second time. If they spent it where it should go, it counts. If not, the people are told that, between them and Allah, they should pay it again.

cards.ask: Rebels held a town for a year and collected its kharaj, spending it where it should go. The ruler takes the town back. Must the people pay that year's kharaj again?
options: Yes: the ruler collects it again
cards.source: لم يأخذه الإمام ثانيا فإن كانوا صرفوه في حقه أجزأ من أخذ منه
cards.why: The ruler does not collect it again, and since it was spent properly, it counts.

cards.title: Silk for men and women
cards.ar: لا يحل للرجال لبس الحرير ويحل للنساء ولا بأس بتوسده عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: Kitab al-Hazr wal-Ibaha is about what is disallowed and what is allowed. Wearing silk is not allowed for men, and is allowed for women. For Abu Hanifa there is no harm in using silk as a pillow. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say that is disliked.

cards.ask: What may men not wear? Complete it.
cards.ar: لا يحل للرجال لبس ____ ويحل للنساء
cards.source: لا يحل للرجال لبس الحرير ويحل للنساء
cards.why: الحرير: silk is not allowed for men to wear, but is allowed for women.

cards.ask: Fatima wears a silk dress to a family wedding. Is it allowed?
options: Yes: silk is allowed for women
No: silk is for no one
Only if it is mixed with cotton
cards.source: ويحل للنساء
cards.why: Silk is allowed for women.

cards.title: Brocade in battle
cards.ar: ولا بأس بلبس الديباج في الحرب عندهما ويكره عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: Dibaj is a thick silk brocade. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad see no harm in wearing it in battle; Abu Hanifa says it is disliked.

cards.title: Mixed cloth
cards.ar: ولا بأس بلبس الملحم إذا كان سداه إبرسما ولحمته قطنا أو خزا
cards.en: Woven cloth has long threads (the warp, sada) and cross threads (the weft, luhma). Cloth whose warp is silk and whose weft is cotton or khazz (a silk-and-wool fabric) is fine to wear.

cards.ask: Yusuf buys a shirt whose long threads are silk and whose cross threads are cotton. May he wear it?
options: Yes: silk warp with cotton weft is allowed
No: it has silk in it
cards.source: ولا بأس بلبس الملحم إذا كان سداه إبرسما ولحمته قطنا
cards.why: Silk warp with a cotton weft is allowed.

cards.ask: May a man wear it?
items: Cloth with silk warp and cotton weft
Cloth with silk warp and khazz weft
source: لا يحل للرجال لبس الحرير
إذا كان سداه إبرسما ولحمته قطنا أو خزا
cards.why: Pure silk is not allowed for men; silk warp with cotton or khazz weft is.

cards.ask: Which of these is NOT allowed?
options: A man wearing a silk robe
A woman wearing a silk scarf
A man wearing cloth with silk warp and cotton weft
source: لا يحل للرجال لبس الحرير ويحل للنساء
ولا بأس بلبس الملحم
cards.why: A man may not wear silk; women may, and the mixed cloth is fine.

cards.title: Jewellery for men
cards.ar: ولا يجوز للرجال التحلي بالذهب والفضة إلا الخاتم والمنطقة وحلية السيف من الفضة
cards.en: Men may not wear gold or silver jewellery, except a silver ring, a silver belt (mintaqa) and silver decoration on a sword.

cards.ask: Which may a man wear?

options.text: A silver ring
A gold necklace
A belt with silver on it
A silver bracelet
A sword with silver decoration

cards.source: ولا يجوز للرجال التحلي بالذهب والفضة إلا الخاتم والمنطقة وحلية السيف من الفضة
cards.why: Only the ring, the belt and the sword decoration, all of silver.

cards.title: Women and children
cards.ar: ويجوز للنساء التحلي بالذهب والفضة ويكره أن يلبس الصبي الذهب والحرير
cards.en: Women may wear gold and silver jewellery. It is disliked to dress a boy in gold or silk.

cards.ask: Umar's parents dress him, aged 6, in a silk shirt with a gold chain. What does the book say?
options: It is fine: he is a child
cards.source: ويكره أن يلبس الصبي الذهب والحرير
cards.why: Dressing a boy in gold and silk is disliked.

cards.title: Gold and silver vessels
cards.ar: ولا يجوز الأكل والشرب والادهان والتطيب في آنية الذهب والفضة للرجال والنساء ولا بأس باستعمال آنية الزجاج والبلور والعقيق
cards.en: Eating, drinking, oiling oneself or putting on perfume from gold or silver vessels is not allowed, for men and for women. Vessels of glass, crystal and agate are fine.

cards.ask: May you drink from it?
source: في آنية الذهب والفضة للرجال والنساء
ولا بأس باستعمال آنية الزجاج والبلور والعقيق
cards.why: Gold and silver vessels are not allowed; glass, crystal and agate are.

cards.ask: Zaynab drinks from a silver cup at a party. Is it allowed because she is a woman?
options: No: the vessel rule is for men and women
Yes: silver is allowed for women
cards.source: ولا يجوز الأكل والشرب والادهان والتطيب في آنية الذهب والفضة للرجال والنساء
cards.why: Women may wear silver, but eating and drinking from silver vessels is forbidden for both.

cards.title: Silver-plated things
cards.ar: ويجوز الشرب في الإناء المفضض عند أبي حنيفة والركوب على السرج المفضض والجلوس على السرير المفضض
cards.en: Note: for Abu Hanifa, it is allowed to drink from a vessel with silver plating on it, ride on a silver-plated saddle and sit on a silver-plated bed.

cards.title: The mushaf and the mosque
cards.ar: ويكره التعشير في المصحف
cards.en: It is disliked to add marks for every tenth verse (ta'shir) in a mushaf (a copy of the Quran), and dots. But there is no harm in decorating a mushaf, or carving and gilding a mosque with gold paint.

cards.ask: Which of these does the book allow?
options: Gilding a mosque with gold paint
A man wearing a gold ring
A woman eating from a gold plate
source: ولا بأس بتحلية المصحف ونقش المسجد وزخرفته بماء الذهب
إلا الخاتم والمنطقة وحلية السيف من الفضة
cards.why: Gilding a mosque is allowed. A man's ring must be silver, and no one eats from gold vessels.

cards.title: Eunuch servants
cards.ar: ويكره استخدام الخصيان
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time some rulers kept eunuchs (men who had been castrated) as servants. Using them as servants is disliked.

cards.title: Animals
cards.ar: ولا بأس بخصاء البهائم
cards.en: There is no harm in castrating animals, for example to make them calmer, or in breeding donkeys with horses to get mules.

cards.ask: Rashid, a farmer, has his young bull castrated so it is calmer to work with. Is this allowed?
options: Yes: there is no harm in it
No: it is disliked, like eunuch servants
cards.source: ولا بأس بخصاء البهائم
cards.why: The book says there is no harm in castrating animals.

cards.title: Whose word is accepted
cards.ar: ويجوز أن يقبل في الهدية والإذن قول الصبي والعبد ويقبل في المعاملات قول الفاسق
cards.en: For a gift (hadiya) or permission to come in (idhn), you may accept the word of a child, and in al-Quduri's time of a slave. In everyday dealings (mu'amalat), like buying and selling, even the word of a fasiq (someone known for sinning) is accepted.

cards.ask: A 9-year-old boy knocks: "My father sent you this plate of dates as a gift." May you accept it on his word?
options: Yes: a child's word is accepted for a gift
No: a child's word is not accepted
Only if an adult comes too
cards.source: ويجوز أن يقبل في الهدية والإذن قول الصبي
cards.why: A child's word is accepted for a gift.

cards.title: Matters of religion
cards.ar: ولا يقبل في أخبار الديانات إلا قول العدل
cards.en: In news about religious matters, such as whether water is pure or meat is halal, only the word of an 'adl (an upright, trustworthy Muslim) is accepted.

cards.ask: Is his word enough on its own?
items: A child: "My mum says you may come in"
A fasiq trader: "I am selling this for my brother"
An upright man: "This water is impure"
source: ويجوز أن يقبل في الهدية والإذن قول الصبي والعبد ويقبل في المعاملات قول الفاسق
ولا يقبل في أخبار الديانات إلا قول العدل
cards.why: Gifts, permission and dealings accept a child's or fasiq's word. Religious matters need an upright person.

cards.ask: A man known for lying tells Bilal, "This meat is halal." What does the book say about his word?
options: Not accepted: he is not upright
Accepted, if he swears by Allah
cards.source: ولا يقبل في أخبار الديانات إلا قول العدل
cards.why: Whether meat is halal is a religious matter, so only an upright person's word counts.

cards.ask: In buying and selling, whose word is accepted? Complete it.
cards.ar: ويقبل في المعاملات قول ____
cards.source: ويقبل في المعاملات قول الفاسق
cards.why: الفاسق: in dealings, even a fasiq's word is accepted.

lessons.title: Looking: men and women
lessons.arabic: ولا يجوز أن ينظر الرجل من الأجنبية

cards.title: A woman who is not family
cards.ar: ولا يجوز أن ينظر الرجل من الأجنبية إلا إلى وجهها وكفيها وإن كان لا يأمن الشهوة لا ينظر إلى وجهها إلا لحاجة
cards.en: An ajnabiyya is a woman who is not his wife and not his close family. A man may look only at her face and hands. If he cannot be sure he will not feel desire, he does not look even at her face, unless there is a need.

cards.ask: What may a man look at of a woman who is not family? Complete it.
cards.ar: ولا يجوز أن ينظر الرجل من الأجنبية إلا إلى وجهها ____
cards.source: إلا إلى وجهها وكفيها
cards.why: وكفيها: her face and her hands.

cards.title: The judge and the witness
cards.ar: يحكم عليها وللشاهد إذا أراد الشهادة عليها النظر إلى وجهها وإن خاف أن يشتهي
cards.en: A judge giving a ruling about her, and a witness giving testimony about her, may look at her face even if he fears desire, because there is a need.

cards.title: The doctor
cards.ar: ويجوز للطبيب أن ينظر إلى موضع المرض منها
cards.en: A doctor may look at the place of the illness or injury.

cards.ask: Who may look at a woman for a real need, by the book?

options.text: A judge giving a ruling about her
A shopkeeper chatting with her
A witness giving testimony about her
A doctor checking her injury
A curious neighbour

source: وللشاهد إذا أراد الشهادة عليها النظر إلى وجهها وإن خاف أن يشتهي
ويجوز للطبيب أن ينظر إلى موضع المرض منها
cards.why: The judge, the witness and the doctor have a need. Chatting or curiosity is not a need.

cards.title: Men with men
cards.ar: وينظر الرجل من الرجل إلى جميع بدنه إلا ما بين سرته إلى ركبته
cards.en: A man may look at all of another man's body except between his navel and his knee.

cards.title: Women
cards.ar: ويجوز للمرأة أن تنظر من الرجل إلى ما ينظر الرجل إليه منه وتنظر المرأة من المرأة إلى ما يجوز للرجل أن ينظر إليه من الرجل
cards.en: A woman may look at a man where a man may look at a man. A woman may look at another woman where a man may look at another man: everything except between the navel and the knee.

cards.ask: May they look?
items: A man at another man's back
A man at another man's thigh
A woman at another woman's arms
A woman at what is between another woman's navel and knee
source: إلا ما بين سرته إلى ركبته
وتنظر المرأة من المرأة إلى ما يجوز للرجل أن ينظر إليه من الرجل
cards.why: Everything is allowed except between the navel and the knee, for men with men and women with women.

cards.ask: Huda has hurt her ankle, and the only doctor is a man, Dr Karim. May he look at the injury?
options: Yes: it is the place of the illness
No: a man may only see her face and hands
cards.source: ويجوز للطبيب أن ينظر إلى موضع المرض منها
cards.why: A doctor may look at the place of the illness.

cards.ask: Ahmad wants to look at the face of a woman he does not know. He cannot be sure he will not feel desire, and there is no need. May he?
options: No: not without a need, if he may feel desire
Yes: the face is always allowed
cards.source: وإن كان لا يأمن الشهوة لا ينظر إلى وجهها إلا لحاجة
cards.why: Without being safe from desire, he does not look even at her face unless there is a need.

cards.title: Husband and wife
cards.ar: وينظر الرجل من أمته التي تحل له وزوجته إلى فرجها
cards.en: A husband may look at all of his wife's body. In al-Quduri's time the same applied to a slave woman lawful to her master.

cards.title: Mahram women
cards.ar: وينظر الرجل من ذوات محارمه إلى الوجه والرأس والصدر والساقين والعضدين ولا ينظر إلى ظهرها وبطنها
cards.en: A mahram is a close relative he can never marry, like his mother, sister or aunt. He may look at her face, head, chest, shins and upper arms, but not her back or belly.

cards.ask: May he look at it?
cards.source: وينظر الرجل من ذوات محارمه إلى الوجه والرأس والصدر والساقين والعضدين ولا ينظر إلى ظهرها وبطنها
cards.why: Face, head, chest, shins and upper arms are allowed; the back and belly are not.

cards.title: Touching
cards.ar: ولا بأس أن يمس ما جاز أن ينظر إليه منها
cards.en: There is no harm in him touching what he may look at of his mahram, like kissing his mother's head.

cards.ask: Khalid kisses his mother's head when he comes home. Is this allowed?
options: Yes: he may touch what he may look at
No: touching a woman is never allowed
cards.source: ولا بأس أن يمس ما جاز أن ينظر إليه منها
cards.why: The head is something he may look at, so he may touch it.

cards.title: In al-Quduri's time: another man's slave
cards.ar: إلى ما يجوز أن ينظر إليه من ذوات محارمه ولا بأس بأن يمس ذلك إذا أراد الشراء وإن خاف أن يشتهي
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time, a man could look at another man's slave woman as he looks at his mahram, and touch those same parts when examining her before buying.

cards.title: A eunuch is like any man
cards.ar: والخصي في النظر إلى الأجنبية كالفحل
cards.en: A eunuch is like any other man when it comes to looking at women who are not his family.

cards.ask: Masrur is a eunuch servant in a palace, in al-Quduri's time. May he look at the hair of an unrelated woman?
options: No: he is like any other man
Only if she is a servant too
source: والخصي في النظر إلى الأجنبية كالفحل
ولا يجوز للمملوك أن ينظر من سيدته إلا إلى ما يجوز للأجنبي أن ينظر إليه منها
cards.why: A eunuch counts as a man, and so does a male slave with his mistress: like a stranger, only her face and hands.

cards.title: 'Azl
cards.ar: ويعزل عن أمته بغير إذنها ولا يعزل عن زوجته إلا بإذنها
cards.en: 'Azl is withdrawal, a way of avoiding pregnancy. A husband may not do it without his wife's permission. In al-Quduri's time, a master did not need his slave woman's permission.

cards.ask: Hamid wants to practise 'azl, but his wife has not agreed. May he?
options: Yes, after one year of marriage
cards.source: ولا يعزل عن زوجته إلا بإذنها
cards.why: With his wife, 'azl needs her permission.

cards.ask: Which may a man look at of his sister?
cards.source: إلى الوجه والرأس والصدر والساقين والعضدين
cards.why: The shins are on the book's list; the back and belly are not.

cards.title: Hoarding
cards.ar: ويكره الاحتكار في أقوات الآدميين والبهائم إذا كان ذلك في بلد يضر الاحتكار بأهله
cards.en: Ihtikar (hoarding) is buying up food and holding it back so the price rises. It is disliked for the food of people and of animals, in a town where the hoarding harms its people.

cards.ask: Hoarding what is disliked? Complete it.
cards.ar: ويكره الاحتكار في أقوات ____
cards.source: ويكره الاحتكار في أقوات الآدميين
cards.why: الآدميين: hoarding people's food is disliked.

cards.title: What is not hoarding
cards.ar: ومن احتكر غلة ضيعته أو ما جلبه من بلد آخر فليس بمحتكر
cards.en: Storing the crops of your own land, or what you brought in from another town, is not hoarding.

cards.ask: Nuh stores all the wheat from his own farm to sell later in the year. Is he a hoarder?
options: No: it is his own land's crop
Yes: he is holding back food
Only if he sells it dearly
cards.source: ومن احتكر غلة ضيعته أو ما جلبه من بلد آخر فليس بمحتكر
cards.why: Crops of his own land do not count as hoarding.

cards.ask: Hoarding or not?
items: Buying up the town's barley in a shortage to sell later
Storing food you brought from another town
Buying up animal fodder where it harms the town
source: ويكره الاحتكار في أقوات الآدميين والبهائم إذا كان ذلك في بلد يضر الاحتكار بأهله
ومن احتكر غلة ضيعته أو ما جلبه من بلد آخر فليس بمحتكر
cards.why: Buying up local food that harms people is hoarding. Your own crop, or food brought from elsewhere, is not.

cards.title: Fixing prices
cards.ar: ولا ينبغي للسلطان أن يسعر على الناس
cards.en: Tas'ir is when the ruler sets the prices people must sell at. The book says the ruler should not do it.

cards.ask: A governor orders every baker to sell bread at one price he chooses. What does the book say?
options: The ruler should not fix prices
It is fine for bread only
cards.source: ولا ينبغي للسلطان أن يسعر على الناس
cards.why: The ruler should not set prices for people.

cards.title: Weapons and grape juice
cards.ar: ويكره بيع السلاح في أيام الفتنة ولا بأس ببيع العصير ممن يعلم أنه يتخذه خمرا
cards.en: Selling weapons in times of fitna (fighting between Muslims) is disliked. The book says there is no harm in selling grape juice even to someone known to make wine from it.

cards.ask: Hasan sells fresh grape juice to a man who he knows makes wine. What does al-Quduri say?
options: There is no harm in it
It is disliked, like selling weapons
cards.source: ولا بأس ببيع العصير ممن يعلم أنه يتخذه خمرا
cards.why: The book says there is no harm in selling the juice; it is the buyer who makes the wine.

cards.ask: During fighting between Muslim groups in his city, Amr wants to sell swords. What does the book say?
options: There is no harm in it
cards.source: ويكره بيع السلاح في أيام الفتنة
cards.why: Selling weapons in times of fitna is disliked.

lessons.title: What a will is, and its limits

cards.title: Recommended, not required
cards.ar: الوصية غير واجبة وهي مستحبة
cards.en: A wasiyya (will) is when someone says that part of their wealth should go to a person or a good cause after they die. Making one is not wajib (required). It is mustahabb (recommended), and best for less than a third.

cards.title: Three limits
cards.ar: ولا تجوز الوصية لوارث إلا أن يجيزها الورثة ولا يجوز الوصية بما زاد على الثلث ولا للقاتل
cards.en: A will has three limits. It cannot be: 1) for a warith (someone who already inherits from you), unless the other heirs agree, 2) for more than a third of your wealth, 3) for the person who killed you. A Muslim and a non-Muslim may leave wills to each other.

cards.ask: The heirs do not agree to more. Which of these wills are NOT allowed?

options.text: 1,000 to his son, who is an heir
Half his wealth to a poor neighbour
Any amount to the man who killed him
A third to a Christian friend
A quarter to the mosque

source: ولا تجوز الوصية لوارث
إلا أن يجيزها الورثة ولا يجوز الوصية بما زاد على الثلث ولا للقاتل
ويجوز أن يوصي المسلم للكافر والكافر للمسلم
cards.why: A will cannot go to an heir, beyond a third, or to the killer. A third to a non-Muslim and a quarter to the mosque are fine.

cards.ask: Umar's will gives 1,000 dirhams to his own son Hamza, on top of Hamza's inheritance. After Umar dies, his other heirs do not agree. Does the will stand?
options: No: a will for an heir needs the other heirs to agree
Yes: a father may always give his son more
Yes, because 1,000 is less than a third
cards.source: ولا تجوز الوصية لوارث إلا أن يجيزها الورثة
cards.why: Hamza is an heir, so the will for him only stands if the other heirs agree. They did not.

cards.ask: Saad leaves 9,000 dirhams. His will gives 4,000 to a poor neighbour, and his heirs do not agree to more. How much can the neighbour get?
cards.source: ولا يجوز الوصية بما زاد على الثلث
cards.why: A will cannot go past a third. A third of 9,000 is 3,000.

cards.title: Accepting comes after death
cards.ar: وقبول الوصية بعد الموت فإن قبلها الموصى له في حال الحياة أو ردها فذلك باطل
cards.en: The musa lahu (the person the will is for) accepts the gift after the death. If he accepts it or turns it down while the person making the will is still alive, that counts for nothing.

cards.title: Owned by accepting
cards.ar: والموصى به يملك بالقبول إلا في مسألة وهي: أن يموت الموصي ثم يموت الموصى له قبل القبول فيدخل الموصى به في ملك ورثته
cards.en: The thing left in the will becomes his when he accepts it. There is one exception: if the musi (the one making the will) dies, and then the musa lahu dies before he could accept, the gift goes into the ownership of the musa lahu's heirs.

cards.ask: Hasan's will leaves a horse to Ali. While Hasan is alive, Ali says "I don't want it." After Hasan dies, Ali says "I accept." Who gets the horse?
options: Ali: his refusal in Hasan's life was void
Hasan's heirs: Ali had already refused it
Nobody: the will was cancelled by it
source: فإن قبلها الموصى له في حال الحياة أو ردها فذلك باطل
والموصى به يملك بالقبول
cards.why: Refusing during life counts for nothing. Ali accepted after the death, so the horse is his.

cards.ask: Hasan dies, and his will leaves a horse to Ali. A week later Ali dies too, before he had said he accepts. Who gets the horse?
cards.source: أن يموت الموصي ثم يموت الموصى له قبل القبول فيدخل الموصى به في ملك ورثته
cards.why: This is the one exception: Hasan died first, then Ali died before accepting, so the horse goes to Ali's heirs.

cards.title: Whose will does not count
cards.ar: ولا تصح وصية الصبي والمكاتب وإن ترك وفاء
cards.en: A will made by a child is not valid. Nor is a will by a mukatab (in al-Quduri's time, a slave with a contract to buy his own freedom), even if he left enough to pay off his contract.

cards.title: Taking a will back
cards.ar: ويجوز للموصي الرجوع عن الوصية فإن صرح بالرجوع أو فعل ما يدل على الرجوع كان رجوعا ومن جحد الوصية لم يكن رجوعا
cards.en: The person who made a will may take it back. Saying so clearly, or doing something that shows he took it back, counts. But simply denying that he ever made the will does not count as taking it back.

cards.ask: Which are true of wills?

options.text: A Muslim may leave a will to a Christian neighbour
It is recommended to leave less than a third
Saying clearly "I take it back" cancels a will
Denying he ever made the will cancels it
A 10-year-old's will is valid
Making a will is wajib (required)

source: ويجوز أن يوصي المسلم للكافر والكافر للمسلم
ويستحب أن يوصي الإنسان بدون الثلث
ومن جحد الوصية لم يكن رجوعا
ولا تصح وصية الصبي
الوصية غير واجبة
cards.why: A Muslim and a non-Muslim may leave wills to each other, less than a third is recommended, and a clear taking back counts. Denying is not taking back, a child's will is not valid, and a will is not wajib.

cards.title: Refusing to his face
cards.ar: وإذا أوصى إلى رجل فقبل الوصي في وجه الموصي فردها في غير وجهه فليس برد وإن ردها في وجهه فهو رد
cards.en: A wasi (executor) is the person chosen to carry out the will after the death. If he accepts the job in front of the person making the will, and then refuses it behind his back, that is not a refusal. If he refuses it to his face, it is a refusal.

cards.ask: Khalid names Yasir as his wasi, and Yasir accepts in front of him. Later, at the market, Yasir tells friends "I won't do it", while Khalid is not there. Is Yasir free of the job?
options: No: refusing behind his back is not a refusal
Yes: he refused it clearly in front of witnesses
cards.source: فقبل الوصي في وجه الموصي فردها في غير وجهه فليس برد
cards.why: Yasir accepted to Khalid's face and refused behind his back, so that is not a refusal. He is still the wasi.

cards.title: An unfit executor
cards.ar: ومن أوصى إلى عبد أو كافر أو فاسق أخرجهم القاضي من الوصية
cards.en: If someone names as wasi a slave (in al-Quduri's time), a non-Muslim, or a fasiq (someone who openly sins), the qadi (judge) removes them from the job and puts others in their place.

cards.ask: Hakim names his neighbour, a man known for openly sinning, as his wasi. What does the judge do?
options: He removes him and puts another in his place
He keeps him, since the dead man chose him himself
He adds a helper to work with him
cards.source: أخرجهم القاضي من الوصية ونثب غيرهم
cards.why: A fasiq wasi is removed by the judge, who puts someone else in his place.

cards.title: His own slave
cards.ar: ومن أوصى إلى عبد نفسه وفي الورثة كبار لم تصح الوصية
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time: if a man names his own slave as wasi, and some of his heirs are adults, the appointment is not valid.

cards.title: An executor who cannot cope
cards.ar: ومن أوصى إلى من يعجز عن القيام بالوصية
cards.en: If the wasi is not able to manage the job on his own, the judge adds another person to work with him.

cards.ask: What happens with this wasi?
items: An honest wasi too weak to manage alone
The man's own slave, with adult heirs (in al-Quduri's time)
source: أخرجهم القاضي من الوصية
ومن أوصى إلى من يعجز عن القيام بالوصية
ومن أوصى إلى عبد نفسه وفي الورثة كبار لم تصح الوصية
cards.why: A non-Muslim or a fasiq is removed, a weak wasi gets a helper, and his own slave with adult heirs is not valid.

cards.title: Two executors
cards.ar: ومن أوصى إلى اثنين لم يجز لأحدهما أن يتصرف عند أبي حنيفة ومحمد دون صاحبه
cards.en: If two people are named as wasi, one of them may not act without the other. This is the view of Abu Hanifa and Muhammad.

cards.title: What one may do alone
cards.ar: إلا من شراء كفن الميت وتجهيزه وطعام الصغار وكسوتهم ورد وديعة بعينها وقضاء دين وتنفيذ وصية بعينها وعتق عبد بتعينه والخصومة في حقوق الميت
cards.en: Except for these, which one may do alone: buying the kafan (burial cloth) and preparing the body, food and clothes for the young children, returning a particular item held in trust, paying a debt, carrying out a particular named gift, freeing a named slave (in al-Quduri's time), and going to court for the dead man's rights.

cards.ask: Ruqayya named Imran and Musa together as her executors. Musa is away. Which may Imran do on his own?

options.text: Buy her burial cloth
Buy winter clothes for her young children
Pay back a debt she owed
Return a ring a friend left with her in trust
Sell her house
Trade with the children's money

cards.source: إلا من شراء كفن الميت وتجهيزه وطعام الصغار وكسوتهم ورد وديعة بعينها وقضاء دين
cards.why: The burial cloth, the children's clothes, paying a debt and returning a trust are on the list. Selling the house and trading are not, so they need both executors.

cards.ask: Which of these matches al-Quduri?
options: A wasi who refused behind his back is still the wasi
A fasiq wasi stays in the job, since the dead man chose him
One of two executors may sell the dead man's house alone
source: فردها في غير وجهه فليس برد
أخرجهم القاضي من الوصية
لم يجز لأحدهما أن يتصرف
cards.why: Refusing behind his back is not a refusal. A fasiq is removed by the judge, and one of two executors cannot sell alone.

lessons.title: When wills share the third
lessons.arabic: ومن أوصى لرجل بثلث ماله ولآخر بثلث ماله

cards.title: A third to each of two
cards.ar: ومن أوصى لرجل بثلث ماله ولآخر بثلث ماله فلم تجز الورثة فالثلث بينهما نصفان
cards.en: If a will gives a third to one man and a third to another, and the heirs do not agree to more, the one third is split between them in halves.

cards.title: A third and a sixth
cards.ar: وإن أوصى لأحدهما بالثلث وللآخر بالسدس فالثلث بينهما أثلاثا
cards.en: If it gives one a third and the other a sixth, the third is split between them in thirds: two parts to the one given a third and one part to the one given a sixth.

cards.ask: Mansur leaves 1,800 dirhams. His will gives a third to Zayd and a sixth to Bakr. The heirs do not agree to more. What does each get?
cards.source: وإن أوصى لأحدهما بالثلث وللآخر بالسدس فالثلث بينهما أثلاثا
cards.why: The third is 600, split in thirds: two parts (400) to Zayd and one part (200) to Bakr.

cards.title: All the wealth and a third
cards.ar: وإن أوصى لأحدهما بجميع ماله وللآخر بثلث ماله فلم تجز الورثة فالثلث بينهما على أربعة أسهم عند أبي يوسف ومحمد وقال أبو حنيفة: الثلث بينهما نصفان
cards.en: If it gives one man all his wealth and the other a third, and the heirs do not agree, Abu Hanifa says the third is split between them in halves. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad split it into four parts.

cards.title: When debts swallow the wealth
cards.ar: ومن أوصى وعليه دين يحيط بماله لم تجز الوصية إلا أن يبرئ الغرماء الدين
cards.en: If he makes a will while he owes debts as big as all his wealth, the will does not go ahead, unless the people he owes let him off the debt.

cards.ask: Rashid owns 8,000 dirhams and owes 10,000. His will gives 1,000 to the mosque. The people he owes do not let him off. What happens to the will?
options: The mosque gets a third of 8,000
cards.source: ومن أوصى وعليه دين يحيط بماله لم تجز الوصية
cards.why: His debt is more than all his wealth, so the will does not go ahead unless the debt is forgiven.

cards.title: "My son's share" or "like it"
cards.ar: ومن أوصى بنصيب ابنه فالوصية باطلة وإن أوصى بمثل نصيب ابنه جازت فإن كان له ابنان فللموصى له الثلث
cards.en: A will of "my son's share" is void, because that share belongs to the son. But a will of "the same as my son's share" is valid. If he has two sons, the person in the will gets a third.

cards.ask: Hashim has two sons and no other heirs. His will gives his nephew "the same as one son's share". What does the nephew get?
cards.source: وإن أوصى بمثل نصيب ابنه جازت فإن كان له ابنان فللموصى له الثلث
cards.why: "The same as" a son's share is valid. With two sons, the nephew gets a third.

cards.title: "A share" of my wealth
cards.ar: ومن أوصى بسهم من ماله فله أخس سهام الورثة إلا أن ينقص من السدس فيتم له السدس
cards.en: A will of "a sahm (share) of my wealth" gives him the smallest share any heir gets. But if that is less than a sixth, it is made up to a sixth.

cards.ask: And a will of "a part" of my wealth? Complete it.
cards.ar: وإن أوصى بجزء من ماله قيل للورثة: أعطوه ____
cards.source: وإن أوصى بجزء من ماله قيل للورثة: أعطوه ما شئتم
cards.why: ما شئتم: for "a part" (juz'), the heirs are told to give him whatever they wish.

cards.ask: Which are true of wills that share the third?

options.text: A will of "my son's share" is void
Two wills of a third each, not agreed, split the third in halves
A will of "a share" never gives less than a sixth
A will still goes ahead when debts cover all the wealth
A will of "a part" always means a third

source: ومن أوصى بنصيب ابنه فالوصية باطلة
فالثلث بينهما نصفان
إلا أن ينقص من السدس فيتم له السدس
لم تجز الوصية إلا أن يبرئ الغرماء الدين
قيل للورثة: أعطوه ما شئتم
cards.why: "My son's share" is void, two thirds split the third in halves, and a sahm is at least a sixth. Debts covering everything stop the will, and for "a part" the heirs give what they wish.

lessons.title: Last illness, and duties to Allah

cards.title: Gifts in the last illness
cards.ar: ومن أعتق عبدا في مرضه أو باع وحابى أو وهب فذلك كله جائز يعتبر من الثلث ويضرب به مع أصحاب الوصايا
cards.en: In his final illness, a man may free a slave (in al-Quduri's time), sell something with muhabat (cheaply, as a favour), or give a gift. All of it is valid, but it is counted from the third, and it shares the third with the people named in his wills.

cards.ask: Jamil, in the illness he later dies of, gives his cousin 5,000 dirhams. He owns 6,000 in all, and his heirs do not agree to more. How is the gift treated?
options: Counted from the third: valid up to 2,000
Valid in full: a gift is not a will
Void: gifts in illness do not count
cards.source: أو وهب فذلك كله جائز يعتبر من الثلث
cards.why: A gift in the last illness is valid but counted from the third. A third of 6,000 is 2,000.

cards.title: A cheap sale and a freeing
cards.ar: فإن حابى ثم أعتق بالمحاباة أولى عند أبي حنيفة وإن أعتق ثم حابى فهما سواء
cards.en: If both do not fit in the third: for Abu Hanifa, if he sold cheaply first and then freed a slave, the cheap sale comes first. If he freed first and then sold cheaply, they are equal. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say the freeing comes first in both cases.

cards.title: Duties to Allah come first
cards.ar: ومن أوصى بوصايا من حقوق الله تعالى قدمت الفرائض منها قدمها الموصي أو آخرها مثل الحج والزكاة والكفارات وما ليس بواجب قدم منه ما قدمه الموصي
cards.en: If a will has several things owed to Allah, the fard (obligatory) ones come first, whether he named them first or last: like Hajj, zakat and kaffarat (expiations for broken oaths and similar). Among the ones that are not wajib, what he named first comes first.

cards.ask: Bakr's will says: "First, 100 dirhams as voluntary charity. Then, pay the zakat I missed." The third is not enough for both. Which comes first?
options: The charity: he named it first
cards.source: قدمت الفرائض منها قدمها الموصي أو آخرها
cards.why: Zakat is fard, so it comes first even though he named it second.

cards.title: A Hajj for him
cards.ar: ومن أوصى بحجة الإسلام أحجوا عنه رجلا من بلده يحج عنه راكبا فإن لم تبلغ الوصية النفقة أحجوا عنه من حيث تبلغ
cards.en: If he leaves a will for Hajjat al-Islam (the Hajj every Muslim owes once), they send a man from his own city to make Hajj for him, riding. If the money is not enough from there, they send someone from wherever the money is enough.

cards.ask: Idris of Kufa leaves money in his will for his Hajj. It is not enough for a trip from Kufa, but it is enough from a town closer to Makkah. What do they do?
options: Send someone from where the money is enough
Cancel the will, since it cannot reach from Kufa
Make the heirs add the rest
cards.source: فإن لم تبلغ الوصية النفقة أحجوا عنه من حيث تبلغ
cards.why: If the money does not reach from his city, the Hajj is made from wherever it does reach.

cards.title: Dying on the way
cards.ar: ومن خرج من بلده حاجا فمات في الطريق وأوصى أن يحج عنه حج عنه من بلده عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: If a man sets out from his city for Hajj, dies on the way, and leaves a will for a Hajj for him, Abu Hanifa says the Hajj is made for him from his own city.

cards.ask: Tariq of Basra sets out for Hajj and dies halfway. His will asks for a Hajj for him. Where does the person making it start, for Abu Hanifa?
cards.source: فمات في الطريق وأوصى أن يحج عنه حج عنه من بلده عند أبي حنيفة
cards.why: For Abu Hanifa, the Hajj is made for him from his own city, Basra.

cards.ask: Which are true of wills and duties to Allah?

options.text: Hajj, zakat and kaffarat in a will come before voluntary gifts
Voluntary gifts in a will go in the order he named them
A gift in the last illness is counted from the third
A gift in the last illness is taken from all the wealth
The Hajj for him must be made on foot

source: مثل الحج والزكاة والكفارات وما ليس بواجب قدم منه ما قدمه الموصي
يعتبر من الثلث
يحج عنه راكبا
cards.why: Fard duties come first and voluntary ones go in his order. A gift in the last illness comes from the third, and the Hajj is made riding.

cards.title: My neighbours
cards.ar: ومن أوصى لجيرانه فهم الملاصقون عند أبي حنيفة
cards.en: If a will is "for my neighbours", Abu Hanifa says that means the ones whose homes touch his.

cards.ask: Salim's will leaves 600 dirhams "for my neighbours". Who shares it, for Abu Hanifa?
options: The families whose houses touch Salim's
Everyone who prays in his mosque
cards.source: فهم الملاصقون عند أبي حنيفة
cards.why: For Abu Hanifa, the neighbours are those whose homes are joined to his.

cards.title: My in-laws
cards.ar: ومن أوصى لأصهاره فالوصية لكل ذي رحم محرم من امرأته ومن أوصى لأختانه فالختن كل ذات رحم محرم منه
cards.en: A will "for my ashar" (in-laws through my wife) is for every close relative of his wife whom she could never marry, like her father or brother. For his akhtan (in-laws through the women of his own family), the book links them to every close woman relative of his whom he could never marry.

cards.ask: Umar's will gives 300 dirhams "to my ashar". Who is it for?
cards.source: ومن أوصى لأصهاره فالوصية لكل ذي رحم محرم من امرأته
cards.why: Ashar are every close mahram relative of his wife.

cards.title: My relatives
cards.ar: ومن أوصى لأقربائه فالوصية للأقرب فالأقرب من كل ذي رحمه محرم منه ولا يدخل فيهم الوالدان والولد ويكون للإثنين فصاعدا
cards.en: A will "for my relatives" goes to the nearest, then the next nearest, from his close mahram relatives (relatives he could never marry). His parents and children are not counted among them. It is for two or more people.

cards.ask: Who can be counted among "my relatives" in a will?

options.text: His brother
His sister
His father's sister
His father
His daughter

source: من كل ذي رحمه محرم منه ولا يدخل فيهم الوالدان والولد
cards.why: Brothers, sisters and aunts are close mahram relatives. Parents and children are not counted.

cards.title: Paternal and maternal uncles
cards.ar: وإذا أوصى بذلك وله عمان وخالان فالوصية لعميه عند أبي حنيفة وإن كان له عم وخالان فللعم النصف وللخالين النصف
cards.en: For Abu Hanifa: if he has two 'amms (father's brothers) and two khals (mother's brothers), the will for his relatives goes to the two 'amms. If he has one 'amm and two khals, the 'amm gets half and the two khals share half. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say it is for everyone descended from his furthest ancestor in Islam.

cards.ask: Faisal's will leaves 600 dirhams "to my relatives". His only close relatives are one 'amm and two khals. What do they get, for Abu Hanifa?
options: 300 to the 'amm, 300 to the two khals
600 to the 'amm, nothing to the khals
cards.source: وإن كان له عم وخالان فللعم النصف وللخالين النصف
cards.why: With one 'amm and two khals, the 'amm takes half (300) and the two khals share the other half (300).

cards.ask: Same will, but Faisal has two 'amms and two khals. Who gets the 600, for Abu Hanifa?
cards.source: وله عمان وخالان فالوصية لعميه عند أبي حنيفة
cards.why: With two 'amms and two khals, the will is for the two 'amms, since there are two of them.

cards.ask: Which of these matches al-Quduri?
options: A will for "my relatives" does not include his father or son
A will for "my neighbours" is for the whole street
A will for "my ashar" is for his own cousins
source: ولا يدخل فيهم الوالدان والولد
فهم الملاصقون
فالوصية لكل ذي رحم محرم من امرأته
cards.why: Parents and children are not counted as relatives. Neighbours are those whose homes touch his, and ashar are his wife's mahram relatives.

lessons.title: When the wealth or the people change

cards.title: Part of the gift is lost
cards.ar: ومن أوصى لرجل بثلث دراهمه أو ثلث غنمه فهلك ثلثا ذلك وبقي ثلثه وهو يخرج من ثلث ما بقي من ماله فله جميع ما بقي
cards.en: A will gives someone a third of his dirhams, or a third of his sheep. Then two thirds of them are lost and one third is left. If what is left fits inside a third of the rest of his wealth, the person gets all that is left.

cards.title: But clothes are different
cards.ar: وإن أوصى بثلث ثيابه فهلك ثلثاها وبقي ثلثها وهو يخرج من ثلث ما بقي من ماله لم يستحق إلا ثلث ما بقي من الثياب
cards.en: If the will is a third of his clothes, and two thirds of them are lost, he only gets a third of the clothes that are left, even if they would fit in the third.

cards.ask: Nasir's will gives Bilal a third of his 90 sheep. Before Nasir dies, 60 sheep die, and 30 are left. The 30 fit easily in a third of Nasir's other wealth. How many does Bilal get?
options: 10: a third of what is left
cards.source: ومن أوصى لرجل بثلث دراهمه أو ثلث غنمه فهلك ثلثا ذلك وبقي ثلثه وهو يخرج من ثلث ما بقي من ماله فله جميع ما بقي
cards.why: With dirhams or sheep, if the third that is left fits in the third of the wealth, he gets all of it: 30 sheep.

cards.ask: Nasir's will gives Bilal a third of his 45 robes. 30 robes are lost, and 15 are left. How many does Bilal get?
options: 5: a third of what is left
cards.source: لم يستحق إلا ثلث ما بقي من الثياب
cards.why: With clothes, he only gets a third of what is left: a third of 15 is 5.

cards.title: Cash and money owed to him
cards.ar: ومن أوصى لرجل بألف درهم وله مال عين ودين فإن خرجت الألف من ثلث العين دفعت إلى الموصى له
cards.en: A will gives someone 1,000 dirhams. The dead man has 'ayn (cash in hand) and dayn (money others owe him). If 1,000 fits inside a third of the cash, it is paid to him.

cards.ask: Will: 1,000 dirhams to Hamid. The dead man has 6,000 in cash, and people owe him 2,000. What does Hamid get?
options: 500 now, the rest as debts come in
Nothing until the debts are paid
cards.source: فإن خرجت الألف من ثلث العين دفعت إلى الموصى له
cards.why: A third of 6,000 is 2,000, so the 1,000 fits in a third of the cash and is paid to him.

cards.title: When the cash is not enough
cards.ar: وإن لم تخرج دفع إليه ثلث العين وكلما خرج شيء من الدين أخذ ثلثه حتى يستوفي الألف
cards.en: If it does not fit, he is paid a third of the cash. Then every time some of the owed money comes in, he takes a third of it, until he has his 1,000.

cards.ask: Will: 1,000 dirhams to Hamid. The dead man has 1,500 in cash, and people owe him 3,000. What does Hamid get now?
options: 500 now, then a third of each debt paid in
1,000 now, all taken from the cash
Nothing now, only once all the debts are paid
cards.source: وإن لم تخرج دفع إليه ثلث العين وكلما خرج شيء من الدين أخذ ثلثه حتى يستوفي الألف
cards.why: 1,000 does not fit in a third of 1,500 (500). So he gets 500 now and a third of each debt as it comes in, until he reaches 1,000.

cards.title: When one of the two has died
cards.ar: ومن أوصى لزيد وعمرو بثلث ماله فإذا عمرو ميت فالثلث كله لزيد وإن قال: ثلث مالي بين زيد وعمرو وزيد ميت كان لعمرو نصف الثلث
cards.en: If he says "a third of my wealth to Zayd and Amr", and Amr turns out to be already dead, the whole third goes to Zayd. But if he says "a third of my wealth is between Zayd and Amr", and Zayd is dead, Amr gets only half of the third.

cards.ask: Bilal owns 3,000 dirhams. His will says "a third of my wealth is between Zayd and Amr", but Zayd had already died. What does Amr get?
cards.source: وإن قال: ثلث مالي بين زيد وعمرو وزيد ميت كان لعمرو نصف الثلث
cards.why: With the word "between", Amr gets half of the third. The third is 1,000, so he gets 500.

cards.ask: Nuh writes a will of a third of his wealth when he owns 3,000 dirhams. By his death he owns 6,000. How much does the will give?
options: 2,000: a third of what he owns at death
1,000: a third of what he had when he wrote it
cards.source: ومن أوصى بثلث ماله له ثم اكتسب مالا استحق الموصى له ثلث ما يملكه عند الموت
cards.why: The third is counted on what he owns when he dies. A third of 6,000 is 2,000.

cards.title: For an unborn child
cards.ar: وتجوز الوصية للحمل وبالحمل إذا وضع لأقل من ستة أشهر من يوم الوصية
cards.en: A will may be for a haml (a baby not yet born), or give away an unborn young, if it is born less than six months after the day of the will. And a will of a jariya (slave woman) except the baby she carries is valid with its exception.

cards.ask: Yahya's will gives 500 dirhams "to the baby Fatima is carrying". The baby is born five months after the will. Is it valid?
options: Yes: it was born within six months
No: the baby was not born yet when he wrote it
Only if the baby is a boy
cards.source: وتجوز الوصية للحمل وبالحمل إذا وضع لأقل من ستة أشهر من يوم الوصية
cards.why: A will for an unborn child is valid when it is born less than six months from the day of the will. Five months is less.

cards.title: A child born before accepting
cards.ar: ومن أوصى لرجل بجارية فولدت بعد موت الموصي قبل أن يقبل الموصى له ولدا ثم قبل وهما يخرجان من الثلث فهما للموصى له
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time: a will gives a man a jariya (a slave woman). After the death, and before he accepts, she gives birth. Then he accepts. If mother and child both fit within the third, both are his.

cards.ask: In al-Quduri's time: Ali's will gives Umar a slave woman. After Ali dies, before Umar accepts, she has a baby. Umar then accepts, and both fit in the third. Who owns the baby?
options: Ali's heirs, since it was born after his death
No one until a judge decides
cards.source: ثم قبل وهما يخرجان من الثلث فهما للموصى له
cards.why: When mother and child both fit within the third, both belong to the one the will is for.

cards.title: If they do not both fit
cards.ar: وإن لم يخرجا من الثلث ضرب بالثلث وأخذ ما يخصه منهما جميعا في قول أبو يوسف ومحمد وقال أبو حنيفة: يأخذ ذلك من الأم فإن فضل شيء أخذه من الولد
cards.en: If they do not both fit in the third: Abu Hanifa says he takes his third from the mother first, and anything left over from the child. Note: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad say he takes his part from both of them together.

cards.title: A will of service or of living in a house
cards.ar: وتجوز الوصية بخدمة عبده وسكنى داره سنين معلومة وتجوز بذلك أبدا
cards.en: A will may give someone the service of a slave (in al-Quduri's time), or the right to live in a house, for a set number of years or forever.

cards.ask: Zahir's will lets his nephew live in his house forever. Is that valid?
options: Yes: it can be for set years or forever
No: it must be for a set number of years
No: a will can only give away property
cards.source: وتجوز بذلك أبدا
cards.why: A will to live in a house may be for a set number of years, or forever.

cards.title: If the slave is all he had
cards.ar: فإن خرجت رقبة العبد من الثلث سلم إليه للخدمة وإن كان لا مال له غيره خدم الورثة يومين والموصى له يوما
cards.en: If the slave's value fits in the third, he is handed over for service. If the dead man had no other wealth, the slave serves the heirs two days and the person in the will one day.

cards.ask: In al-Quduri's time: a will gives Karim the service of a slave, and the slave is all the dead man owned. How is the service shared?
options: Two days for the heirs, one day for Karim
One day for the heirs, two days for Karim
cards.source: وإن كان لا مال له غيره خدم الورثة يومين والموصى له يوما
cards.why: With no other wealth, the heirs get two days and Karim one: Karim's third, the heirs' two thirds.

cards.title: When the receiver dies
cards.ar: فإن مات الموصى له عاد إلى الورثة وإن مات الموصى له في حياة الموصى بطلت الوصية
cards.en: If the person who was given the service dies, it goes back to the heirs. If he dies while the man who made the will is still alive, the will is cancelled.

cards.title: "His children" and "his heirs"
cards.ar: وإذا أوصى لولد فلان فالوصية بينهم: الذكر والأنثى فيه سواء ومن أوصى لورثة فلان فالوصية بينهم: للذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين
cards.en: A will "for the children of so-and-so" is shared equally between the boys and the girls. A will "for the heirs of so-and-so" is shared like inheritance: a male gets as much as two females.

cards.ask: A will gives 900 dirhams "to the heirs of Khalid". Khalid's heirs are two sons and one daughter. What does each get?
cards.source: ومن أوصى لورثة فلان فالوصية بينهم: للذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين
cards.why: For heirs, a male gets two parts and a female one: 5 parts of 180. Each son gets 360, the daughter 180.

cards.ask: Now the will gives 900 dirhams "to the children of Khalid", who are two sons and one daughter. What does each get?
cards.source: وإذا أوصى لولد فلان فالوصية بينهم: الذكر والأنثى فيه سواء
cards.why: For "children", boys and girls are equal: 900 shared by three is 300 each.

cards.ask: Which are true of special cases in wills?

options.text: A will of a jariya, leaving out the baby she carries, is valid with the exception (in al-Quduri's time)
A will to live in a house can be forever
If the receiver dies before the man who made the will, the will is cancelled
A will for an unborn child is valid however late it is born
"The children of so-and-so" share like inheritance, two to one

source: ومن أوصى لرجل بجارية إلا حملها صحت الوصية والاستثناء
وتجوز بذلك أبدا
وإن مات الموصى له في حياة الموصى بطلت الوصية
إذا وضع لأقل من ستة أشهر
الذكر والأنثى فيه سواء
cards.why: The exception of the unborn is valid, service or living can be forever, and the will is cancelled if the receiver dies first. The unborn must be born within six months, and children share equally.

cards.title: The ten men
cards.ar: المجمع على توريثهم من الذكور عشرة: الابن وابن الابن وإن سفل والأب والجد أب الأب وإن علا والأخ وابن الأخ والعم وابن العم والزوج ومولى النعمة
cards.en: Fara'id is the knowledge of who inherits and how much. All agree that ten men inherit: the son; the son's son, however far down; the father; the father's father, however far up; the brother; the brother's son; the 'amm (father's brother); the 'amm's son; the husband; and the freer (mawla al-ni'ma, in al-Quduri's time).

cards.ask: How many men are agreed heirs? Complete it.
cards.ar: المجمع على توريثهم من الذكور ____
cards.source: المجمع على توريثهم من الذكور عشرة
cards.why: عشرة: ten men are agreed to inherit.

cards.ask: Which of these are among the ten men who are agreed heirs?

options.text: The son's son
The daughter's son
The father's father
The 'amm's son
The khal (mother's brother)
The husband

cards.source: المجمع على توريثهم من الذكور عشرة: الابن وابن الابن وإن سفل والأب والجد أب الأب وإن علا والأخ وابن الأخ والعم وابن العم والزوج ومولى النعمة
cards.why: The son's son, father's father, 'amm's son and husband are on the list. The daughter's son and the khal are not.

cards.title: The seven women
cards.ar: ومن الإناث سبع: البنت وبنت الابن والأم والجدة والأخت والزوجة ومولاة النعمة
cards.en: And seven women: 1) the daughter, 2) the son's daughter, 3) the mother, 4) the grandmother, 5) the sister, 6) the wife, 7) the mawlat al-ni'ma (the woman who freed the dead person, in al-Quduri's time).

cards.ask: Which of these are among the seven women who are agreed heirs?

options.text: The son's daughter
The grandmother
The wife
The mother
The daughter's daughter
The khala (mother's sister)

cards.source: ومن الإناث سبع: البنت وبنت الابن والأم والجدة والأخت والزوجة ومولاة النعمة
cards.why: The son's daughter, grandmother, wife and mother are on the list. The daughter's daughter and the khala are not.

cards.ask: How many women are agreed heirs?
cards.source: ومن الإناث سبع: البنت وبنت الابن والأم والجدة والأخت والزوجة ومولاة النعمة
cards.why: Seven, against ten men.

cards.title: Four who do not inherit
cards.ar: ولا يرث أربعة: المملوك والقاتل من المقتول والمرتد وأهل الملتين
cards.en: Four do not inherit: 1) a slave (in al-Quduri's time), 2) a killer, from the person he killed, 3) a murtadd (someone who left Islam), 4) people of two different religions, from each other.

cards.ask: How many kinds of people does the book say do not inherit?
cards.source: ولا يرث أربعة: المملوك والقاتل من المقتول والمرتد وأهل الملتين
cards.why: Four: the slave, the killer, the murtadd and people of two religions.

cards.ask: Which of these does the book say do not inherit?

options.text: A killer, from the one he killed
A murtadd
A wife
A slave, in al-Quduri's time
A son's son
People of two religions, from each other

source: ولا يرث أربعة: المملوك والقاتل من المقتول والمرتد وأهل الملتين
وابن الابن وإن سفل
والزوجة
cards.why: The four who do not inherit are the slave, the killer, the murtadd and people of two religions. The wife and the son's son are agreed heirs.

cards.ask: Fahd wrongly kills his father. Fahd's brother Salim is also alive. Does Fahd inherit from his father?
options: No: a killer does not inherit
Yes, but only half a son's share
cards.source: والقاتل من المقتول
cards.why: The killer does not inherit from the person he killed, so everything goes to Salim.

cards.ask: Maryam, a Muslim, dies. Her only brother is a Christian. Does he inherit from her?
options: No: they are of two religions
Yes: a brother is one of the ten men
Yes, if she said so in her will
cards.source: وأهل الملتين
cards.why: People of two different religions do not inherit from each other.

cards.ask: Does this relative inherit?
items: A son who is a slave (in al-Quduri's time)
source: الابن وابن الابن وإن سفل والأب والجد أب الأب
ولا يرث أربعة: المملوك والقاتل من المقتول والمرتد
cards.why: The son's son, father's father and brother's son are among the ten. A slave and a murtadd do not inherit.

cards.ask: Which of these matches al-Quduri?
options: The daughter's son is not one of the ten
The husband is not one of the ten agreed men
The wife is not one of the seven women
source: والأخ وابن الأخ والعم وابن العم والزوج ومولى النعمة
والزوجة ومولاة النعمة
cards.why: The ten men are the son's line, the father's line, brothers, 'amms and their sons, the husband and the freer. The daughter's son is not among them, while the husband and the wife are.

lessons.title: The fixed shares: half, quarter, eighth, two thirds
lessons.arabic: والفروض المحدودة في كتاب الله تعالى ستة

cards.title: Six fixed shares
cards.ar: والفروض المحدودة في كتاب الله تعالى ستة: النصف والربع والثمن والثلثان والثلث والسدس
cards.en: The furud (fixed shares) named in the Book of Allah are six: 1) a half, 2) a quarter, 3) an eighth, 4) two thirds, 5) a third, 6) a sixth.

cards.ask: Which are among the six fixed shares?

options.text: A half
An eighth
Two thirds
A sixth
A fifth
A tenth

cards.source: ستة: النصف والربع والثمن والثلثان والثلث والسدس
cards.why: The six are a half, a quarter, an eighth, two thirds, a third and a sixth. There is no fifth or tenth.

cards.ask: How many fixed shares are named in the Book of Allah?
cards.source: والفروض المحدودة في كتاب الله تعالى ستة: النصف
cards.why: Six: a half, a quarter, an eighth, two thirds, a third and a sixth.

cards.title: The half
cards.ar: فالنصف من الأب والأم والأخت من الأب إذا لم تكن أخت لأب وأم والزوج إذا لم يكن للميت ولد
cards.en: The half goes to a full sister; to a sister from the father only, when there is no full sister; and to the husband, when his wife leaves no child and no son's child. A single daughter also takes a half, as a later lesson shows.

cards.title: The quarter and the eighth
cards.ar: والربع: فرض الزوج مع الولد أو ولد الابن والزوجات إذا لم يكن للميت ولد ولا ولد ابن والثمن: فرض الزوجات مع الولد وولد الابن
cards.en: The quarter is for the husband when there is a child or a son's child, and for the wife (or wives) when there is no child and no son's child. The eighth is for the wife (or wives) when there is a child or a son's child.

cards.ask: Hind dies, leaving her husband Zayd and their son. What is Zayd's share?
cards.source: والربع: فرض الزوج مع الولد
cards.why: A husband gets a quarter when there is a child. The son takes the rest.

cards.ask: Ahmad dies, leaving his wife and a daughter. What is the wife's share?
cards.source: والثمن: فرض الزوجات مع الولد وولد الابن
cards.why: A daughter is a child, and a wife with a child gets an eighth.

cards.ask: Ahmad dies with no children or grandchildren, leaving his wife and his brother. What is the wife's share?
cards.source: والزوجات إذا لم يكن للميت ولد ولا ولد ابن
cards.why: With no child and no son's child, the wife gets a quarter. The brother takes the rest.

cards.title: Two thirds
cards.ar: والثلثان: لكل اثنين فصاعدا ممن فرضه النصف إلا الزوج
cards.en: Two thirds is for two or more of the people whose share alone would be a half, except the husband. So two sisters share two thirds, where one alone would get a half.

cards.ask: Layla dies with no children and no parents. She leaves two full sisters and her 'amm. What do the two sisters get together?
cards.source: والثلثان: لكل اثنين فصاعدا ممن فرضه النصف
cards.why: One full sister would get a half, so two of them share two thirds. The 'amm takes the rest.

cards.ask: What is the share?
items: A husband with a son's daughter
source: والزوج إذا لم يكن للميت ولد
والربع: فرض الزوج مع الولد أو ولد الابن والزوجات إذا لم يكن للميت ولد ولا ولد ابن
والثمن: فرض الزوجات مع الولد
cards.why: A husband gets a half with no child and a quarter with one. A wife gets a quarter with no child and an eighth with one.

cards.title: The mother's third
cards.ar: والثلث: للأم إذا لم يكن للميت ولد ولا ولد ابن ولا اثنان من الإخوة والأخوات فصاعدا
cards.en: The mother gets a third when the dead person has no child, no son's child, and not two or more brothers or sisters.

cards.ask: Sami dies young, with no children and no brothers or sisters. He leaves his mother and father. What is his mother's share?
cards.source: والثلث: للأم إذا لم يكن للميت ولد ولا ولد ابن
cards.why: No child and no two siblings, so the mother gets a third. The father takes the rest.

cards.title: A third of what is left
cards.ar: ويفرض لها في مسألتين - وهما: زوج وأبوان وامرأة وأبوان - ثلث ما يبقى بعد فرض الزوج أو الزوجة
cards.en: In two cases the mother gets a third of what is left, not a third of everything: a husband with both parents, and a wife with both parents. First the husband's or wife's share is taken out, then the mother gets a third of the rest, and the father the remainder.

cards.ask: Amina dies with no children, leaving her husband, her mother and her father, and 600 dirhams. What does her mother get?
options: 100: a third of what is left
200: a third of the whole estate
source: زوج وأبوان
ثلث ما يبقى بعد فرض الزوج أو الزوجة
والزوج إذا لم يكن للميت ولد
cards.why: The husband takes half (300). The mother gets a third of the 300 left, which is 100, and the father the other 200.

cards.ask: Yusuf dies with no children, leaving his wife, mother and father, and 1,200 dirhams. What does his mother get?
source: وامرأة وأبوان
ثلث ما يبقى بعد فرض الزوج أو الزوجة
cards.why: The wife takes a quarter (300). The mother gets a third of the 900 left, which is 300, and the father 600.

cards.title: The mother's other children
cards.ar: وهو لكل اثنين فصاعدا من ولد الأم: ذكورهم وإناثهم فيه سواء
cards.en: The third is also for two or more walad al-umm (half-brothers and half-sisters through the mother only). The males and females among them get equal parts.

cards.ask: The third of an estate is 300 dirhams. It goes to the dead man's half-brother and half-sister from his mother. What does each get?
options: 200 to the brother, 100 to the sister
cards.source: من ولد الأم: ذكورهم وإناثهم فيه سواء
cards.why: Among the mother's children, males and females are equal: 150 each.

cards.title: The sixth: seven cases
cards.ar: والسدس: فرض سبعة: لكل واحد من الأبوين مع الولد أو ولد الابن وللأم مع الإخوة والأخوات من أي جهة كانوا وللجدات وللجد مع الولد أو ولد الابن ولبنات الابن مع البنت وللأخوات لأب مع الأخت لأب وأم وللواحد من ولد الأم
cards.en: The sixth is for seven: each parent, with a child or son's child; the mother, with brothers or sisters of any kind; the grandmothers; the grandfather, with a child or son's child; son's daughters, with one daughter; sisters from the father, with a full sister; and a single child of the mother.

cards.ask: For how many heirs is the sixth the fixed share?
cards.source: والسدس: فرض سبعة
cards.why: The book says the sixth is the share of seven.

cards.ask: Who gets a sixth here?

options.text: A father, when the dead man has a son
A son's daughter, along with one daughter
One half-brother through the mother
A grandmother
A mother, with no children and no siblings
A husband, when there is a child

source: لكل واحد من الأبوين مع الولد
ولبنات الابن مع البنت
وللواحد من ولد الأم
وللجدات
cards.why: The father with a child, a son's daughter with a daughter, one maternal sibling and the grandmother get a sixth. The mother here gets a third, and the husband a quarter.

cards.ask: Khadija dies, leaving one daughter, one son's daughter, and her 'amm. What does the son's daughter get?
cards.source: ولبنات الابن مع البنت
cards.why: The daughter gets a half, and the son's daughter a sixth with her, making two thirds. The 'amm takes the rest.

cards.ask: Ibrahim dies with no children, leaving his mother, his father and two brothers. What is his mother's share?
options: A third of what is left
source: وللأم مع الإخوة والأخوات من أي جهة كانوا
ولا اثنان من الإخوة والأخوات فصاعدا
cards.why: Two brothers bring the mother down to a sixth, even though the brothers themselves get nothing because of the father.

cards.title: Blocked by a closer one
cards.ar: وتسقط الجدات بالأم والجد والإخوة والأخوات بالأب
cards.en: Some heirs "fall" (get nothing) because a closer heir is there. The grandmothers fall when the mother is alive. The grandfather and the brothers and sisters fall when the father is alive.

cards.ask: Hasan dies, leaving his father, his mother, a brother, and his father's father. Who gets nothing?
options: Only the brother; the grandfather inherits
cards.source: والجد والإخوة والأخوات بالأب
cards.why: The father is alive, so the grandfather and the brother both fall.

cards.title: The mother's children fall by four
cards.ar: ويسقط ولد الأم بأربعة: بالولد وولد الابن والأب والجد
cards.en: Half-siblings through the mother fall with four: 1) a child, 2) a son's child, 3) the father, 4) the grandfather.

cards.ask: By how many relatives do the mother's children fall?
cards.source: ويسقط ولد الأم بأربعة: بالولد وولد الابن والأب والجد
cards.why: Four: a child, a son's child, the father and the grandfather.

cards.ask: A half-brother through the mother is left with this relative. Which of these make him fall?

options.text: A son
Only the mother
The father
The father's father
Only a husband
A son's daughter

cards.source: ويسقط ولد الأم بأربعة: بالولد وولد الابن والأب والجد
cards.why: A child, a son's child, the father and the grandfather make him fall. The mother or a husband do not.

cards.title: When daughters fill two thirds
cards.ar: وإذا استكمل البنات الثلثين سقطت بنات الابن إلا أن يكون بإزائهن أو أسفل منهن ابن ابن فيعصبهن
cards.en: When the daughters have taken the full two thirds, the son's daughters fall, unless there is a son's son at their level or lower. He makes them 'asaba with him: heirs who share what is left over after the fixed shares.

cards.ask: Rabi'a dies, leaving two daughters, a son's daughter, and her 'amm. What does the son's daughter get?
options: Nothing: the daughters filled two thirds
A share of the two thirds with the daughters
cards.source: وإذا استكمل البنات الثلثين سقطت بنات الابن
cards.why: The two daughters take the full two thirds, and there is no son's son, so the son's daughter falls.

cards.ask: Rabi'a leaves 900 dirhams: two daughters, a son's daughter, and a son's son. What do the son's son and son's daughter get?
source: إلا أن يكون بإزائهن أو أسفل منهن ابن ابن فيعصبهن
والفاضل عن فرض البنات لبني الابن وأخواتهم للذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين
cards.why: The daughters take two thirds (600). The son's son makes his sister 'asaba, and the 300 left is shared two to one: 200 and 100.

cards.title: When full sisters fill two thirds
cards.ar: وإذا استكمل الأخوات لأب وأم الثلثين سقطت الأخوات لأب إلا أن يكون معهن أخ لهن فيعصبهن
cards.en: In the same way, when full sisters have taken two thirds, the sisters from the father only fall, unless they have a brother with them who makes them 'asaba.

cards.ask: Zaynab dies with no children or parents. She leaves two full sisters, one half-sister from her father, and an 'amm. Does the half-sister inherit?
cards.source: وإذا استكمل الأخوات لأب وأم الثلثين سقطت الأخوات لأب
cards.why: The full sisters took two thirds and the half-sister has no brother with her, so she falls.

cards.ask: What does the son's son do for the son's daughters? Complete it.
cards.ar: سقطت بنات الابن إلا أن يكون بإزائهن أو أسفل منهن ابن ابن ____
cards.source: إلا أن يكون بإزائهن أو أسفل منهن ابن ابن فيعصبهن
cards.why: فيعصبهن: he makes them 'asaba, so they share what is left with him instead of falling.

cards.title: Who is nearest
cards.ar: باب أقرب العصبات وأقرب العصبات البنون ثم بنوهم ثم الأب ثم الجد ثم بنو الأب وهم الإخوة ثم بنو الجد وهم الأعمام ثم بنوا أب الجد
cards.en: The 'asaba are the relatives who take what is left after the fixed shares, or everything if there are none. The nearest are the sons, then their sons, then the father, then the grandfather, then the father's sons (the brothers), then the grandfather's sons (the 'amms), then the sons of the grandfather's father.

cards.ask: Put the 'asaba in order, nearest first.
cards.source: وأقرب العصبات البنون ثم بنوهم ثم الأب ثم الجد ثم بنو الأب وهم الإخوة ثم بنو الجد وهم الأعمام ثم بنوا أب الجد
cards.why: Sons, their sons, the father, the grandfather, the brothers, the 'amms, then the great-grandfather's sons.

cards.ask: Bashir dies, leaving only a brother and an 'amm. Who takes everything?
cards.source: ثم بنو الأب وهم الإخوة ثم بنو الجد وهم الأعمام
cards.why: The brothers come before the 'amms, so the brother takes it all.

cards.title: Full before half
cards.ar: وإذا استوى بنو أب في الدرجة فأولاهم من كان لأب وأم
cards.en: When they are at the same level, the one related through both father and mother comes before the one related through the father only.

cards.ask: Jabir dies, leaving a full brother and a half-brother from his father. Who inherits?
cards.source: فأولاهم من كان لأب وأم
cards.why: Both are brothers, at the same level, so the full brother comes first and takes it all.

cards.title: Sharing with sisters
cards.ar: والابن وابن الابن والإخوة يقاسمون أخواتهم للذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين ومن عداهم من العصبات ينفرد بالميراث ذكورهم دون إناثهم
cards.en: The son, the son's son and the brothers share with their sisters, a male getting as much as two females. For the other 'asaba, only the males inherit, not their sisters.

cards.ask: Usama dies, leaving one son and one daughter, and 900 dirhams. What does each get?
cards.source: والابن وابن الابن والإخوة يقاسمون أخواتهم للذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين
cards.why: A son shares with his sister, a male getting two parts: 3 parts of 300, so 600 and 300.

cards.ask: Uthman's only relatives are the son and the daughter of his 'amm. Who inherits as 'asaba?
cards.source: ومن عداهم من العصبات ينفرد بالميراث ذكورهم دون إناثهم
cards.why: Only sons, son's sons and brothers share with their sisters. Among the 'amm's children, only the male inherits.

cards.title: When there is no 'asaba by blood
cards.ar: وإذا لم يكن عصبة من النسب فالعصبة هو المولى المعتق ثم أقرب عصبة المولى
cards.en: In al-Quduri's time: if there is no 'asaba by family, the 'asaba is the man who freed the dead person from slavery, and then that man's nearest 'asaba.

cards.ask: Which are true of the 'asaba?

options.text: The father comes before the grandfather
A brother shares with his sister, two to one
A full brother comes before a half-brother from the father
An 'amm comes before a brother
An 'amm's daughter shares with her brother, two to one

source: ثم الأب ثم الجد
والإخوة يقاسمون أخواتهم للذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين
فأولاهم من كان لأب وأم
ينفرد بالميراث ذكورهم دون إناثهم
cards.why: The father is before the grandfather, brothers share with sisters, and the full brother comes first. Brothers are before 'amms, and an 'amm's daughter does not share as 'asaba.

lessons.title: Reducing shares, and what is left over

cards.title: The mother reduced
cards.ar: باب الحجب وتحجب الأم من الثلث إلى السدس بالولد أو بأخوين
cards.en: Hajb is when one heir reduces or blocks another's share. The mother is brought down from a third to a sixth by a child, or by two brothers.

cards.ask: Rania dies, leaving her mother, a daughter and an 'amm. What is the mother's share?
cards.source: وتحجب الأم من الثلث إلى السدس بالولد
cards.why: A daughter is a child, and a child brings the mother down to a sixth.

cards.title: What is left after the daughters or sisters
cards.ar: والفاضل عن فرض البنات لبني الابن وأخواتهم للذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين والفاضل عن فرض الأختين من الأب والأم للإخوة والأخوات من الأب للذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين
cards.en: What is left after the daughters' share goes to the son's sons and their sisters, a male getting as much as two females. What is left after two full sisters' share goes to the brothers and sisters from the father, a male getting as much as two females.

cards.title: One daughter
cards.ar: فللبنت النصف والباقي لبني الابن وأخواتهم للذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين وكذلك الفاضل عن فرض الأخت من الأب والأم لبني الأب وبنات الأب للذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين
